articleTitle: Estimation of Scattering and Attenuation of a Random Distribution of Metallic Wires Using Radiative Transfer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a formulation for electromagnetic waves propagating through a lossy random medium. A model for such a random medium is proposed. Our medium is modeled as free space containing a volume fraction of perfectly conducting electrical wires of various geometries. The conductors are assumed to be distributed uniformly and randomly throughout the medium, and are assumed to be roughly the size of a wavelength of the propagating wave. Propagation of this wave through the medium is modeled using radiative transfer. The phase and Stokes matrices are calculated using the Method of Moments, and these are used to compute the extinction matrix of the medium for various geometries of the conductors and for various volume fractions. The mathematical formulation of vector radiative transfer, also, the statistical behavior o the extinction matrices are given for this medium.

articleTitle: Scaled PT -Symmetric Coherent Perfect Absorber (CPA)- Laser
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reducing threshold gain of lasers and radiating harmonic oscillators has been a long desired goal. In this paper, we introduce a novel scaled parity-time (gPT)-symmetric metasurfaces, with imbalanced gain and loss, to realize low-threshold laser and coherent perfect absorber (CPA). Moreover, we theoretically show that in the same structure, the lasing and coherent perfect absorption modes can be switched by properly phasing two excitation sources.

articleTitle: Sensing the Defect Response of Cranial Vault using Resistively Loaded Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes the resistively loaded dipole antenna for sensing the defect response. The developed antenna characterized in terms of short pulse radiating aspects. The calculated fidelity factor is 0.6 and 0.97 for conventional dipole and resistively loaded dipole antenna, respectively. The healing stages can be monitored by looking at the changes of the reflected pulse using proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-band Single/Dual-beam Slot Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this letter, a dual-band dual-beam microstrip antenna is investigated. The proposed antenna consists of a rectangular ground plane, a V-shape feed probe and a double slots radiating patch. By adjusting the size of them, a dual-band antenna can be obtained. In the low frequency band, the antenna can radiate one radiation beam. In the high frequency band, the antenna can achieve two symmetrical radiation beams. An antenna prototype is fabricated and measured for validation. Good agreement between the simulated and measured results is observed. The antenna operating frequency ranges are 3.6 ~ 3.9 GHz in the low frequency band and 4.8 ~ 5.3 GHz in the high frequency band with VSWR less than 2. At 3.8 GHz, the antenna radiate one beam with 7.9 dBi realized gain. At 5.0 GHz, it exhibits two radiation beams directed at -40°and 40°with 5.8 dBi and 5.7 dBi realized gain.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Three- Dimensional Scattering from a buried object under a Dielectric Rough Surface using the Characteristic Basis Function Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Characteristic Basis Function Method (CBFM) is adapted to analyze the problem of electromagnetic scattering from a 3-D object buried under a 2-D dielectric rough surface. A current-based physical optics (PO) method, called Modified Equivalent Current Approximation (MECA), is used for efficient derivation of the Characteristic Basis Functions (CBFs) for the dielectric body. The interaction between the rough surface and the object is rigorously taken into account to derive accurate solutions for the electric and magnetic current densities on the rough surface. In addition, the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) is implemented to expedite the generation of the reduced matrix. Finally, scattered fields in the far zone are calculated by using the method of azimuthal angular averaging. The proposed approach is demonstrated to be accurate and efficient. Moreover, it is well-suited for applications when the solution for multiple excitations is required.

articleTitle: Dual-band Notched Ultra-Wideband Microstrip Antenna with Integrated Bluetooth band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of ultra-wide band microstrip antenna with dual-band notched at WiMAX and WLAN bands is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a patch antenna, three gradual steps connected to the end of the feed line and a partial ground plane with a trapezoidal slit. Two U-shaped slots were etched on the antenna to reject the WLAN band with a sharp rejection at the start of the band. A coupled C-shaped resonator was placed along the microstrip feed line to reject the WiMAX band. Also, the antenna supports the Bluetooth operating band. The fabricated antenna operates from 2.05 GHz to 14.01 GHz except at the notched WiMAX and WLAN bands. There is a good agreement between the simulated and the experimental results.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Radiation Efficiency Improvement of a Miniature Narrow Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates two ways to improve the radiation efficiency of an electrically small antenna loaded by a capacitor. The first one consists in enlarging the antenna strip width in order to lower its loss resistance. The second one focus on optimizing the loading capacitor used to lower the resonant frequency by mixing a discrete and a coplanar twin strip capacitors. The two studied parameters have a strong impact on the radiation efficiency as the antenna is electrically small.

articleTitle: Dual-Circular Polarized Antenna Lattice with Odd Number of Radiating Elements and Integrated Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of an integrated 5 × 5 antenna lattice featuring dual-circular polarization has been presented. The described antenna array is composed of 25 radiating elements arranged in 5 rows and 5 columns and fed in series along both × and Y axes, except the center element which is separately fed by four feeding lines. To provide appropriate signals feeding these linear subarrays a compact feeding network based on quadrature directional couplers has been integrated at the center of the antenna array. The proposed concept has been verified by measurements of an antenna array operating at the center frequency 5.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Effect of the Surface Roughness of the Water and Ice Boundary on Lake Icepack Thickness Measurement Using Wideband Autocorrelation Radiometry
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wideband autocorrelation radiometry (WiBAR) is a new method to remotely measure the vertical extent of low loss layered media such as dry snowpack and freshwater lake icepack. This technique measures the pack thickness by sensing the microwave propagation time Tdelay of multi-path microwave emission of the pack. The presence of a surface roughness can affect the ability of this technique to measure the Tdelay correctly. In this paper, the effect of the surface roughness is discussed, and it is shown that the surface roughness can be measured for lake icepack by understanding the surface roughness effect.

articleTitle: Deep-Sub-Wavelength Magnetoquasistatic Indoor Navigation Sensor–2D Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent progress in magneto quasi static (MQS) field-based techniques have enabled effective sensor techniques for accurate position sensing in indoor environments. Key to the technique is the ability to measure and invert MQS field couplings from an external active device to an internal active device. Due to use of low-frequency MQS couplings, the technique enables accurate field inversions within a few skin-depths into an indoor environment. We demonstrate 2D position tracking for a mobile MQS receiver device in a large indoor house environment with through-the-wall coupling, and analyze the error in data collected.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Dual-Polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Array with Resistance Ring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar dual-polarized ultra wideband phased array with wide scan and low profile is proposed in this work. The design of the array is based on the concept of tightly coupled dipole array. However, this work employs a novel structure on antenna and balun which enables simple fabrication. Moreover, a resistance ring is involved to achieve a 0.095λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> profile since the ring with SMD resistors weakens the ground effect. The array with 6:1 bandwidth exhibits an active VSWR<;3.0 at broadside and VSWR<;3.5 at =45° in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: 3D LTE Coverage Prediction for Residential District by Ray Tracing Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The deployment of the Long-Term Evolution (LTE) base stations significantly impacts the quality of communication and the cost of the operator. This paper focuses on predicting the power coverage for LTE microcell base stations at 2.6 GHz. We reconstruct the 3D environment model of a realistic residential district and conduct extensive ray-tracing simulations for different heights and different receiver locations in the same region. The results provide numerical analysis on how the buildings and heights impact the propagation within and surrounding the building, and therefore, guide the deployment of the base stations in typical residential districts.

articleTitle: Use of Dielectric Nanoparticles for Designing High-Reflection Coatings and Dielectric Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we investigate the use of high-index nanoparticles as a possible solution for realizing ultra-thin dielectric mirrors working at a desired frequency of the optical spectrum. First, exploiting the Mie theory for spherical scatterers, we will show that it is possible engineering the optical response of a high-index nanoparticle and maximizing the difference between its forward and backward scattering. Then, we will show that, when such optimized nanoparticles are arranged in a proper lattice, they behave as perfect optical mirrors with 20 % fractional bandwidth. A possible realistic implementation, based on crystalline silicon, is also proposed and checked with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Focal Intensity Distribution Manipulation with Huygens Metamirror
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Huygens metasurface is new type of two-dimension metasurface composed of crossed electric and magnetic dipoles. Due to the outstanding merits, the proposed reflective Huygens metasurface is designed with 2π reflection phase range on condition that the reflection amplitude keeps above 0.99, and a multi-focus imaging Huygens metamirror is fist proposed. Compared with traditional imaging, Huygens metamirror can tailor the microwave to specified points, no matter the focal location, focal number or even the focal intensity distribution, adding a new degree of freedom to imaging manipulation. Our research offers a new method to the multi-focus imaging at microwave band and the Huygens metamirror offers the potential for applications in antenna and imaging system.

articleTitle: Fast Direct Equivalence Principle Algorithm for Multi-scale Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Equivalence principle algorithm is proposed to integrated with hierarchical matrix based fast direct solver in order to solve deep multi-scale problem accurately and efficiently. Additionally, model order reduction techniques are applied to the equivalence principle algorithm to further reduce the computational complexities.

articleTitle: Bow Tie Antenna with Metamaterial Loading for Selective Directivity and Improved Gain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a bow tie antenna with and without metamaterial loading operating from 1.2 GHz to 1.45 GHz. Five layers, each consisting of a 4×5 array of split ring resonators (SRR)and modified split ring resonators (SRR)on a FR-4 substrate is placed around the antenna. The directivity in the E-plane is increased by a factor of two compared to the H-plane. The gain at 1.32 GHz for the antenna with SRR and modified SRR is equal to 2.84 dB and 2.82 dB respectively, compared to 1.77 dB of a bow tie antenna without metamaterial loading.

articleTitle: Fast Solution of Volume-Surface Integral Equations for the Analysis of Interconnect Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic analysis for interconnect structures is formulated by volume-surface integral equations (VSIEs) in integral equation approach. The VSIEs are usually solved by the method of moments (MoM) with the basis functions requiring conforming meshes. We propose a different scheme to discretize the VSIEs by combining the traditional MoM for the SIEs and a point-matching method for the VIEs. For electrically large problems, we incorporate the scheme with the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) to accelerate the solution. A typical numerical example is presented to demonstrate the scheme and its effectiveness has been verified.

articleTitle: Second-mode Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Based on Complementary Plasmonic Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) are supported by plasmonic meta material with arrays of complementary symmetric grooves. In comparison with the slotline-based complementary SSPP structure, the proposed structure has a different second-mode dispersion relation which indicates improved operating bandwidth. High-efficiency and broadband excitation and propagation of second-mode SSPPs are achieved by a smooth transition using a linear tapered coplanar waveguide with complementary gradient grooves. The transition is of seamless connection with conventional microwave circuits and simple geometry for easy and low-cost fabrication. The numerical simulations show that the proposed structure has significant potentials in developing plasmonic integrate circuits at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Drift-Free Range, Velocity, and Acceleration Sensing via Magnetoquasistatic Field Couplings
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate and discuss a technique to enable drift-free wireless sensing of range, velocity, and acceleration of a mobile device by measurements of the magnetoquasistatic field couplings between the device and a base sensor or anchor node.

articleTitle: Influence of Ionospheric Scintillation on GNSS Satellite Constellation Geometry
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ionospheric scintillation is a serious concern for GPS users under low latitude regions. Under extreme cases, scintillation may lead to a full disruption of the receiver operation. This work presents a statistical analysis of ionospheric scintillation data measured by receivers belonging to CIGALA/CALIBRA network throughout Brazil. The main objective is to investigate how ionospheric irregularities may affect the GPS satellites available in the sky and consequently impact on positioning accuracy. The results show that a user near the crest of the equatorial ionization anomaly will be susceptible to such phenomenon and users in this region can be seriously harmed.

articleTitle: Monolithic Stereolithography 3-D Printed Microwave Passive Waveguide Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a systematic overview of recently reported stereolithography 3-D printed passive waveguide devices operating at microwave/millimeter-wave frequencies. Typically, these devices are prototyped monolithically, i.e., as a single part, with the use of low-density photosensitive resins, and are then surface-metallized by appropriately employing copper coating techniques such as electroplating and electroless plating. Such devices are free of either assembly or post fabrication tuning, which effectively shortens the processing cycle. The structural highlights, fabrication techniques, and RF performance of these devices will be discussed.

articleTitle: High-Power and Widely-Tunable Evanescent-Mode Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new high-power and widely-tunable cavity-backed slot antenna is introduced and experimentally investigated in this work. The proposed antenna is composed of a tunable evanescent-mode cavity resonator with a radiating slot on its back wall. The antenna tuning is based on a piezoelectric actuator which changes the resonator gap size in the range of 15-170 μm, Considering minimum return loss of 10 dB, a prototype fabricated antenna was successfully tuned over the frequency range of 1.8-2.6 GHz, representing about 36% tunability. The simulated antenna gain at 2.4 GHz is about 5.4 dBi while the antenna can potentially handle high powers up to 100 W.

articleTitle: Study of A Water- Immersed Orbital Angular Momentum Circular Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new method that can significantly improve the microwave biological imaging resolution is provided by means of water-immersed orbital angular momentum (OAM) circular antenna array. Considering the microwave penetration depth and the reflection at the interface between tissue and environment, 2.45GHz is selected as the central frequency of the OAM circular antenna array which is assumed to be immersed in water. Some important simulation results of the water-immersed OAM circular antenna array are presented here, and the purity of OAM modes with respect to different states is calculated from these results. The proposed antenna array generating different OAM waves can radiate into biological tissue and organ immersed in water efficiently, indicating the potential to achieve super-resolution of microwave biological imaging system.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling reduction of a printed dual element antenna system using a parasitic scatter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact printed dual element antenna system is presented here as an ideal candidate for WLAN system. The antenna comprises of two parallel oriented monopoles. A parasitic element has been introduced between the two radiators as a decoupling structure to realize a good isolation performance between them. The desirable radiator and diversity performances are ensured by simulation and / or measurement of reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, realized peak gain, envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), diversity gain(DG), and channel capacity loss (CCL).

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Isotropic 3D Dipole
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel isotropic 3D antenna on a cubic structure is presented in this paper. The antenna includes an active 0.6λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>meander line dipole and two identical orthogonal parasitic meander line dipoles that are wrapped around the cube to achieve a near isotropic radiation pattern. The cube size is 20 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm, corresponding to 0.16 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>(at 2.4 GHz). The isotropic pattern and miniaturized geometry of the antenna are attractive for wireless sensor and RFID applications.

articleTitle: Identification and Separation of Multiple Scattering from Complex Cavities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A joint sliding window statistic parameters and adaptive decomposition algorithm is presented to identify and separate multiple scattering from complex cavity. The statistic parameters of the sliding window along the line of sight of radar are used to identify the multiple scattering centers. Adaptive decomposition based on modulated sinc functions is applied to separate the cavity multiple scattering fields. An example using measured data is given to illustrate the feasibility and correctness.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Range Estimation for ATSC DTV Signal Based Positioning System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synchronization ATSC DTV signals are designed for channel modeling and multipath mitigation, and consequently can be used for accurate positioning. In this paper, we present our study of a high accuracy range estimation method for DTV signal based positioning system. The proposed method is robust, accurate, fast and easy to implement to the conventional RF receiver for indoor positioning and tracking purpose. Performance analysis was done in Matlab simulated data and verified with raw field data.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna Elements Effect on Chassis Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a 4-element printed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) loop antenna having a bandwidth of 400 MHz is proposed. The effect of the MIMO antenna on the chassis modes system is analyzed via the theory of characteristic modes (TCM), and it is shown that chassis CM are not enough for the full analysis. A defected-ground-structure (DGS) is also proposed to enhance the isolation between the antenna elements by blocking the coupling modes.

articleTitle: A proposed long wavelength infra-red metamaterial absorber for THz detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A long wavelength infrared metamaterial absorber using electric field driven LC (ELC) resonating structure is reported in this paper. The structure shows an absorption peak of 96.2% at 30 THz (10.00 μm). The structure is studied for oblique incidences under TE and TM polarizations. The structure behaves as an absorber for both TE and TM polarizations so long as the angle of incidence is within 60°. All the results are obtained using Ansys HFSS, based on Finite Element Method (FEM). The absorption characteristics is simultaneously verified using COMSOL-Multiphysics simulation software and they are found to be in good agreement. The proposed ultra-thin (~ λ30) metamaterial absorber structure is expected to find potential application in THz spectroscopy, imaging techniques and sensing.

articleTitle: Dynamic Range of an Active Radio Sensor for Bias-Switched Arrays for Microwave Tissue Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A prototype of an active radio sensor is fabricated and tested on breast-tissue phantoms in order to establish achievable sensitivity and dynamic range. The sensor is intended as an element in large arrays for microwave tissue imaging that multiplex several hundred sensors through bias switching. It consists of a printed slot antenna, a low-noise amplifier and a mixer. The sensor area that comes into contact with the tissue is largely determined by the antenna area, which is as small as 12 by 12 mm. The operating bandwidth is from 3 GHz to 7.5 GHz and the output intermediate frequency is 30 MHz. The achievable dynamic range of the sensor is measured to be 109 dB when the resolution bandwidth is 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly-Polarized 3D Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel millimeter-wave wideband circularly-polarized 3D helical array antenna that works at 30 GHz. To design an antenna with wide circular polarization (CP) bandwidth, a 2×2 axial-mode helical structure is fed by using a sequential phase feeding network. The antenna array covers a wide frequency band from 26.4 GHz to 34 GHz with an achieved maximum gain of 11 dB and an axial ratio of less than 3 dB in the whole band. Moreover, the radiation pattern of the proposed antenna has a right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) with side-lobe level below -10 dB. Subsequently, the proposed antenna array can be a good candidate for millimeterwave communication systems around 30 GHz.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Antenna with Broadband Reduced RCS and Enhanced Directivity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tri-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna with broadband RCS reduction and enhanced directivity is presented. Three hybrid cavity modes are excited, and thus the antenna resonates at 11, 13 and 14.5 GHz. A checkerboard surface composed of two artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) cells is loaded around the radiation slot and is able to realize a low-RCS design from 10.5 to 18 GHz. In addition, the antenna directivity is enhanced in all operation bands.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization Method Using Pathloss-Distance Relationship with Handset Sensor Information
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes an indoor localization method of the mobile handset using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacons. The method estimates the distance between the BLE transmitter and the handset by two different ways, i.e. the first one uses the pathloss-distance relationship, and the second one uses the Pedestrian Dead-Reckoning (PDR) relying on accelerometers built in the handset. The location is jointly estimated by using both results. Experimental results show that the localization error of the proposed method was 1.14 m on average, which is 2.16 m smaller than that of the method using only pathloss-distance relationship.

articleTitle: Application-Adaptable Chipless RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Chipless RFID has gained prominence due to its application versatility and cost and complexity advantages over traditional RFID. However, chipless RFID tags are typically designed for a specific application instead of being deployable for a multitude of applications. In this paper, a new approach to adaptable chipless RFID tag is proposed that can be optimized for a variety of applications, including materials characterization with tags as embedded sensors. Additionally, the designed approach renders tags that can be interrogated with a linearly polarized probe and achieves bit densities up to 27.57 bits/cm 2,

articleTitle: PO-based Shaped Reflector Design for Sectoral Pattern RADAR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an automatic procedure based on physical optics (PO) for the design and optimization of a sectoral pattern shaped reflector at millimeter waves is proposed. As a starting guess for the PO-based iterative procedure, a fast optimization based on geometrical optics (GO) has been developed. In order to preserve the smoothness of the reflector shape, a reduced set of control points on its surface is defined, and an interpolation is performed between them. The results show the effectiveness of the proposed technique, that can profitably find applications in the design of RADAR antennas for surveillance purpose.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging Using Focused Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel phased-array solution to two-dimensional microwave imaging is proposed in this paper. Four microstrip antennas are used as transmitters, whereas a near-field focused array antenna is used to harvest the scattered energy by the object under test (OUT), and the image of the OUT can be reconstructed by a combination of SAR algorithm and frequency scan. The proposed setting of the imaging system has two superiorities. First, the beam is focused in the near-field, with low near-field sidelobes, which reduces interruptions. Second, the use of frequency-scanned linear subarrays reduces the cost caused by complex beam-forming network or switching system.

articleTitle: Novel Low-cost Phase Shifters for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Novel low-cost phase shifter that hybridize stepwise and continuously variable phase shifting mechanisms are presented in this work. A combination of straight and curved waveguides is used to realize the step-wise phase shifts, while the variable phase shifts are achieved by inserting one or more layers of metallic vias in the waveguide to achieve a differential phase up to 90°. An alternative scheme, which achieves the phase shift in the entire 0° to 360° range by mechanically changing the length of a telescopic guide, is also described.

articleTitle: Application of the Discrete Hankel Transform to Cylindrical Waveguides Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we apply the Discrete Hankel Transform (DHT) to solve electromagnetic problems that involve cylindrical waveguide structures. We demonstrate the DHT's use by applying it to the simple problem of radiation from an open-ended waveguide. The solution is verified with the commercial solver Comsol Multiphysics.

articleTitle: Extending the Brewster Effect to Arbitrary Angle and Polarization using Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A bianisotropic metasurface design is proposed for extending the Brewster effect to arbitrary angles and polarizations. The metasurface is synthesized using the surface susceptibility tensor and Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs) synthesis method, and is demonstrated by GSTC-FDFD simulation. It is found that an extremely broad angular range (0 -30°) with near zero reflection may be obtained near the normal angle, which is of paramount interest in paraxial optics, while narrower angular range at more oblique angles may find applications in spatial filtering.

articleTitle: A Novel FSS Structure with Great Insensitivity to Incident Angles for High Performance Millimeter Wave Communication Radome
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel frequency selective surface (FSS)structure with great insensitivity to the incident angles designed for the millimeter wave communication radome is proposed in this paper. The strong coupling is introduced to realize the excellent angular stability in this design. The proposed FSS exhibits a quite stable response under a wide range of incident angles up to 80° for both TE and TM polarizations. Furthermore, a broad stopband at the second harmonic of the operating band is provided, which can suppress the spurious signals of the antenna. A corresponding equivalent circuit model (ECM)is also proposed to better analyze the principles of the proposed FSS. Finally, the results obtained by the full-wave simulations and ECM have good agreement and demonstrate that the proposed FSS structure is a good candidate for the millimeter wave communication radome.

articleTitle: Broadband Printed Log-Periodic Antenna with Coaxial Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For the application in a MIMO-OFDM radar a single antenna element has been developed. In this paper the design of a logarithmic-periodic antenna for a frequency range from 10 GHz to 40 GHz is presented. The aerial has been manufactured on PCB and for the feed a coaxial cable was soldered to the board.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Vertically Interconnected On-Package Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 17 GHz additively manufactured package integrated patch antenna is presented for vertical interconnection with a MMIC device. The antenna is fabricated using a multi-layer and multi-material 3D-printing process that combines fused deposition modeling of ABS plastic, micro-dispensing of silver paste Du-Pont CB028 and laser machining. Performance is successfully measured and characterized achieving a return loss greater than 19 dB at the desired design frequency, with a 10 dB bandwidth ranging from 16.8 GHz up to 17.4 GHz. Good agreement between simulated and measured radiation patterns is also obtained with a peak gain of 4.2 dBi.

articleTitle: A Raspberry Pi Controlled Antenna System for Switchable Tilted-twin Beams
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A complete antenna system controlled by Raspberry pi is presented for providing switchable tilted-twin beams. The antenna system is composed of a circular metal disk and sixteen T-shaped parasitic elements which are proximity-coupled to the disk. The open and short states of the T-shaped elements are obtained by using a switching circuit consisting of sixteen Single Pole Single Throw (SPST) switches. The SPST switches are controlled by a Python-based Graphical User Interface (GUI) running on a Raspberry Pi. The antenna provides sixteen switchable tilted-beams by changing the location of the open and short states of the T-shaped elements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Strip-Grated Conducting Rod Using Asymptotic Strip Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an analytical method that deals with the solutions for surface wave modes that propagate along a dielectric coated conducting cylinder loaded with a periodic array of metallic transverse strips is presented. The approach hinges on the asymptotic strip boundary conditions (ASBC) along with classical electromagnetic theory of vector potentials that dramatically simplify the formulation as compared to the use of traditional Floquet mode expansion. The method would be validated by presenting the consistency of the dispersion properties obtained from the ASBC method with those simulated by an independent full wave solver. The closed form field expressions have been derived successfully by this method.

articleTitle: Ka-band Radiometer System Design Incorporated with SIW Slot Antenna for Soil Moisture Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a passive radiometer system design for soil moisture sensing. A compact 1×8 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slot array antenna is designed and fabricated. The proposed antenna exhibits high gain (12.7 dB) and lower cross-polarization level. Besides, A Dicke type radiometer receiver has been designed and sensitivity of 1.1 K has been obtained. The proposed low-cost system results show acceptable alignment with the literature and can be a potential candidate for the remote sensing application.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-polarized Capped Bow-tie 2×2 Antenna Array for 28 GHz Band in 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the development of the fifth generation (5G) communications, dual-polarization base station antennas have increasingly attracted a lot of attention. In this paper, a broadband high-efficiency dual-polarized capped bow-tie antenna array is presented. Simulation results show that the bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 24-36.8 GHz, with its return loss better than 10 dB and the stable coverage. The directivities vary from 8 to 12dBi and the relative cross-polar level is below -10dB over the most of band. It has a simple and compact structure, and is ready to be extended for large array antennas with massive MIMO performance used in 5G communications.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Low Profile Linear-polarized UWB Antenna with Unidirectional Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an improved Vivaldi antenna with low profile and unidirectional pattern is presented. By etching grooves on the antenna, we get a compact Vivaldi antenna element. Two arms of which are bended and the antenna is folded to form a low profile UWB antenna. The studies of the behavior of the proposed antenna reveal that the pattern of the antenna is stable over a ultrawideband of 0.78GHz-13.7GHz. While its profile height is decreased about 50%. The lower profile makes the proposed antenna a better candidate for UWB application.

articleTitle: Dual-Matching for Single Resonance Miniaturized Antenna for IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniature antenna working in European, Asian and Australian ISM sub-GHz bands is presented for IoT application. The antenna was first designed and simulated to achieve a low quality factor, i.e. having good matching at 896MHz. A second-order matching network was then designed to make the antenna achieve broadband between dual desired band at 868 MHz and 922 MHz, which do not satisfy the bands requirements. Finally, the components' values are updated to obtain dual-band behaviour.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Spiral Nanoantenna for Intrabody Communication at Terahertz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a graphene-based spiral nanoantenna is proposed and investigated for intrabody communication at the Terahertz (THz) frequency band (0.1-10 THz). A spiral antenna configuration is adopted as it possesses various degrees of freedom and exhibits geometries that facilitate miniaturization, which is crucial for practical deployment of nanobiosensors. Graphene is used in the design of the spiral nanoantenna since it results in the excitation of plasmonic eigenmodes, which lead to strong resonances in the lower THz band. Full wave simulation of the proposed spiral nanoantenna is carried out by COMSOL Multiphysics, to obtain the nanoantenna parameters. The desirable features attained, along with its compact size and circularly polarized characteristic, make the proposed spiral antenna design suitable for intrabody nano-communication applications.

articleTitle: Domino- Tiling in Phased Arrays Through Innovative Computational/Analytic Strategies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the synthesis problem of domino-tiled phased arrays is addressed. A review of the tiling methods based on analytic and computational techniques developed at the ELEDIA Research Center is reported. Enumerative and optimization-based strategies are illustrated, as well as recent methodological advancements aimed at the optimization of very-large arrays. Finally, an illustrative numerical example showing the effectiveness of the proposed approaches is reported.

articleTitle: Integrating the discrete dipole approximation forward solver with a microwave tomography algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The discrete dipole approximation (DDA) has been suggested as a viable alternative method for computing the forward solutions during the iterative reconstruction process used in microwave tomography. While efficient algorithms such as finite difference time domain and finite elements have been successfully used by multiple groups, the forward solution time remains the time-limiting step. The DDA has been shown to be accurate and efficient as a forward solver. However, the configuration of the imaging scenario can have a significant impact on its efficiency. We examine two possible forward solution set-ups and describe the benefits with respect to implementing the DDA.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bandwidth Performance of Slotted Antenna Array Exploiting the Multiple Feeding Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slotted antenna array consisting of two rectangular cavities is introduced. The primary resonating cavity is probe fed, while the second one is fed through a 45° obverted slot placed on the segregating surface between them. This technique results in enhanced bandwidth operation without the need for designing a special feeding network. The array operates throughout a bandwidth of 257.4 MHz centered around the frequency of 2.5 GHz, and presents omnidirectional patterns in the E and H-plane, making up a good choice for multipath environments.

articleTitle: Two Element Loop-Loaded Printed Dipole Array for Dual-band Operation with Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, design of a two element loop-loaded printed dipole array having miniaturized dual-band characteristics is presented. At the lower operating frequency of 1.64 GHz, the proposed array exhibits tilted dual-beam radiation (peak gain 4.11 dBi)about the azimuth plane, due to the tightly coupled loop mode. At the higher operating frequency of 2.52 GHz, the proposed array exhibits bi-directional broadside radiation pattern (peak gain 3.89 dBi)due to the interaction between printed dipoles. A prototype for the proposed antenna is fabricated to validate the design methodology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Edge Detection for the Clusters in Radio Propagation Channel
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Channel modeling is an important research field in radio propagation, whereas clustering is one of key processes in the channel modeling. In this paper, edge detection algorithm is firstly applied for the clusters of signal in radio propagation channels, which can recognize the clusters with low computation cost. In the proposed algorithm, the clusters are detected based on the distribution of signals' amplitude. Besides, different operators for edge detection are conducted and compared to validate the performance of edge detection for the clusters.

articleTitle: Fused Helico-Spiral Coil Design Using Both Neural Network and Generic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fused helical and spiral (FHS) coils are proposed to improve the efficiency of wireless power transfer by using both neural network and generic algorithms. FHS coils take advantages of balancing the coupling coefficient and the quality factor. Moreover, neural network and generic algorithm are applied to optimize the structure and parameters of the FHS coils with variable pitches. From simulation, the proposed 3.25-mm FHS coil structure consists of three layers of 15 turns. The pitches of three layers are 0.075, 0.225, 0.3 mm, respectively. Due to more condensed magnetic field distribution, the power transmission efficiency is improved to 24% compared with traditional signal turn coil at distance of 20 mm.

articleTitle: Standing Wave Considerations in the Link Model of 60 GHz Directional Surface Wave Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes an improvement of the link model of 60 GHz directional surface wave antenna arrays. Since the transmit and receive arrays share the grounded substrate, the total coupling power is contained in both space and surface waves. The dominant TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> mode of the grounded substrate contributes to the surface wave coupling. In addition, it is shown that the finite extent of the substrate creates a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> standing wave. This wave is responsible for oscillations in the power coupling between the arrays as a function of their separation.

articleTitle: Simple Frequency Characteristic Evaluation of Shaped-Beam Design for Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The analysis of the reflectarray antenna's frequency characteristics is a time consuming task. This is owing to the design of the size of the phasing elements, and the analysis of the reflection phase of the phasing elements. We propose a method for estimating the frequency characteristics of a reflectarray antenna by introducing aberration theory. The frequency characteristics can be estimated without the design consideration to phasing element size, and by the analysis of the reflection phase of phasing elements by the conditions of aberration theory. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a simple method to estimate the frequency characteristics of the reflectarray antenna that does not require element design estimates the frequency characteristics by using the desired reflection phase of our proposed design frequency.

articleTitle: CAD Data Selection and Simplification Techniques for EM Automotive Simulations using EMPIRE XPU
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents effective algorithms for CAD data conversion. Complex vendor CAD data is converted application-specific to an EM simulation optimized reduced data set. The algorithms reduce the complexity of the CAD data without impairing the electrical behavior for the targeted EM simulation. The resulting dataset is significantly reduced in size to be handled easily by 3D EM simulation tools.

articleTitle: Source's symmetries and priors: the effect on information content of radiated field
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper it is studied how certain symmetry priors affect some metrics commonly used to evaluate the achievable performance in linear inverse problems such as the Number of Degrees of Freedom (NDF), the point-spread function (psf) and Kolmogorov entropy.

articleTitle: Synthesis of 4D Linear Antenna Arrays Using an Iterative Convex Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An iterative convex optimization algorithm is proposed for efficient pattern synthesis in 4D linear antenna arrays. Specifically, a 4D linear antenna array is separated into two dependent `conventional arrays' with identical array structure, whose far-field patterns correspond to the patterns at the center frequency and the sidebands, respectively. Convex optimization is firstly used to synthesize a pencil beam at the center frequency, and iterative convex optimization algorithm is then applied to suppress the sideband radiation. Due to that the iterative idea of computational mathematics is adopted, the solution tends to be globally optimal. Numerical examples are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparison of macro basis function sets for antenna array analysis with the MoM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Macro Basis Function (MBF) methods such as the Characteristic Basis Function Method (CBFM), are used to solve large antenna array problems efficiently with the Method of Moments (MoM). MBFs are defined over subdomains, which are usually the antenna array elements. In this paper, MBFs are generated over larger, overlapping subdomains and a distance-based criterion is used to generate higher-order MBFs. Results show that fewer degrees of freedom are required to provide similar accuracy than with the conventional CBFM.

articleTitle: A Ultra-Light High Gain Circularly-Polarized Antenna Array for Mobile Satellite Terminals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A ultra-light, compact, high gain 16 × 6 CP antenna array is presented in this paper for Ku band mobile satellite applications. The 96-element array consists of 24 2 × 2 CP sub arrays fed by a substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) network. Two essential and innovative techniques were adopted in this design. First, in order to achieve the ultra-light weight, the radiation patches were etched on the Polyimide film supported by a patterned foam. A piece of thin SIW network was designed to feed the radiators. The total weight of the fabricated array prototype is only 66.5 gram and profile is low as 0.05 λ0. Second, a sequential rotation (SQR) feeding technique was applied to the aperture fed 2 × 2 CP sub array, which realized more than three times bandwidth enhancement than the direct (non-SQR) feeding approach. In addition, the measured results show the CP-operational bandwidth is 700 MHz from 11.55 to 12.25 GHz. The peak realized gain is 26.4 dBic and gain variation is stable (less than 3 dB) cross the entire operating bandwidth. Be ultra-light and high gain, it is an excellent candidate for Ku band satellite applications.

articleTitle: Plane Wave Scattering by a PEC Wedge in Relativistic Translational Motion: Exact and Uniform Asymptotic Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study of fast-moving scatterers has received much attention due to its fundamental applications for modern radio astronomy and radar problems. This kind of problem relies on solving complicated time-dependent boundary conditions and only the wave phenomena associated with simplified scattering scenarios are today completely deep-seated. In this paper, a novel solution for the scattering of plane waves by a perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) wedge in motion is introduced on the grounds of Einstein's special theory of relativity. The exact solution for the 3D vector problem of an arbitrarily polarized time-harmonic plane wave excitation is obtained in closed form. In addition, a solution based on the uniform asymptotic theory (UAT) ansatz is obtained, rendering this approach a promising framework for modeling several relativistic effects of other complex-shaped and fast-moving objects.

articleTitle: Entire-Domain Spectral Basis Functions for the Efficient Design of Metasurface Antennas of Circular Shape
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper offers an efficient numerical approach to optimizing the design of large circular planar Metasurfaces (MTSs) antennas based on specially varying impedance profiles. Div-conforming spectral basis functions on the whole antenna are defined. The goal is to reduce the number of unknowns, to lead to a well-conditioned system, and to speed up the multiple solutions needed by an automatic optimization code. We consider the overall numerical complexity of the scheme and show its advantages in optimization applications.

articleTitle: Low cost folded chipless tag for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple made RFID chipless tag by folding its transmission line (TL)structure is presented. Dual polarized antennas are used to assure the back-scattering signal. The TL mutual coupling and meander shape are designed to fit the required number of bits into the specific frequency band. To achieve a practicality and low cost chipless RFID tag, the parametric study of folded multi-layer tag is also presented. A tag design with three elements, representing three bits, is performed. The elements operates in the frequency range of 55 GHz -59.5 GHz. Besides the design technique, it is demonstrated that a multi-frequency can be used for coding increase the chipless RFID tag capacity. Therefore, the chipless tag design has shown to be useful for frequency selective applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Generated Small Dipoles in Lossy Media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a comparative study of electrically, magnetically and mechanically generated dipoles in a heavily lossy medium in the ULF range. It is shown that in an electrically lossy environment the radiation efficiency of an electrically small antenna is proportional to (ka)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for an electric radiator and to (ka) for the magnetic radiator. Therefore the magnetic antenna is more efficient than its electric count partner over two orders of magnitude. The proposed small magnetic dipole has potential applications in undersea communication and biomedical treatment.

articleTitle: Frequency-Reconfigurable Quasi-Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this Paper, a Quasi-Yagi antenna for frequency reconfigurability is presented. The antenna is composed of a double-layer metallic structure and fed by a microstrip fed line. Two PIN diode switches are introduced in the driven element to control its length, resulting in shifting the resonance frequency into different regions electronically. The obtained results show that the antenna resonates at 2.9 GHz and 4.9 GHz. Furthermore, changing the position of the PIN diodes over the driven element makes the antenna resonate at other frequency bands, which is suitable for several wireless applications.

articleTitle: Accurate Method for Measuring the Characteristic Parameters and the Phase Center of the Circularly Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An accurate method is introduced for measuring the characteristic parameters and the phase center of the circularly polarized antennas using a linearly polarized source antenna. The mathematical model and the actual test system are established in this paper. The measurement results validate the advantages of strong practicability, high degree of automation and high measurement accuracy in this method. The measurement accuracy of the phase center is less than 1 mm, and it can satisfy the research and production requirements of the circularly polarized antennas.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Self-matched 40:1 two arm Archimedean Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The two arm Archimedean Spiral antenna is revisited in an attempt to improve the operating bandwidth and input impedance characteristics. Each arm is placed on either side of the substrate and the width of the arms has been increased to allow direct attachment of a coaxial connector at the center of the structure. Simulated results show S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> less than -10.5dB across the band from 700MHz to 20GHz. The input impedance varies from 30Ω to 82Ω in the same band. Acceptable 3D gain pattern is observed on simulation at 30GHz which successfully sanctions the idea of this paper.

articleTitle: Over-moded Bent Circular Waveguide Mode Converter for Gaussian Radiation Pattern from Relativistic BWOs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel over-moded bent circular waveguide mode converter is proposed to extract a hybrid HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode from a relativistic backward wave oscillator (BWO) to feed an antenna. It uses a smooth wall dual bent circular waveguide to convert a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode directly to HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>. It has higher power capacity than a corrugated TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode converter and is more compact than a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode converter together with a smooth wall TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode converter. The geometric parameters of the converter are analyzed by using coupled mode theory for curved waveguides and optimized by using the Taguchi method to output 85% TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and 15% TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> modes. The optimized mode converter was analyzed using CST. The conversion efficiency is greater than 98%, with a power capacity as high as 12.8 GW.

articleTitle: Stripline-Fed Patch Antenna with Long-Term Reliable Conductive Vias
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The long-term reliability of plated through holes to feed antennas or suppress unwanted parallel plate mode propagation is a key issue. The proposed structure has conductive vias formed in each substrate composing the multilayer substrate instead of through holes penetrating a multilayer substrate. This configuration improves the long-term reliability of the antenna because the aspect ratio of the conductive vias is smaller than that of the through holes. A heat cycle test of fabricated antennas demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Planar Ka-Band Satcom Tx-Antenna Composed of Vacuum Casted Plastic Sub-Array Modules
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar direct-radiating waveguide array antenna for Ka-band Satcom applications is presented. The antenna is made of identical metalized plastic sub-array modules that are fabricated through a vacuum casting process. This process allows to reproduce a master piece module (preferably aluminium) by using a silicone mold to produce accurate duplicates of the original module. Therefore, this procedure is perfectly suited for cost-effective rapid antenna prototyping and even for very small/micro-series production, where standard injection molding is hence not feasible due to extremely high initial costs. The antenna is composed of 16 sub-array modules, each of size 10 cm × 10 cm to obtain an overall form factor of 80 cm × 20 cm. The operation frequency is from 29.5 GHz to 30 GHz and the polarization can be adjusted to linear or circular. The measured gain is 40.1 dBi at 29.75 GHz. The antenna was tested in a real satellite link scenario via ASTRA 1L and a hub station at Technical University of Munich (TUM).

articleTitle: An Investigation on Propagation Characteristics of In-body Radio Channels for Wireless Implants
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a realistic high resolution human body model was presented to investigate the propagation characteristics of in-body radio channels (I-BRCs) at human body communication (HBC) frequency band for implantable devices. Specifically, the TX electrodes were implanted into the brain, heart, stomach, lung, and intestine, respectively, and the RX electrode was attached on the surface of abdomen. The parameters such as channel gain and group delay were explored through numerical simulations with finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method in the frequency range IMHz to lOOMHz. The results showed that as the frequency increased, the channel gain of all five I-BRCs decreased when the frequency was below 50MHz. The group delay was frequency-dependent. Furthermore, the group delay of all channels had the minimum value at about 52MHz. In addition, a 45kg pig was employed as an experimental subject to verify the validity of simulations for 1-BRCs. The results indicated that the simulations were in agreement with the measurements.

articleTitle: Near-Field Microwave Imaging of Embedded Objects in a Dense Slab with Normal Dipole Illumination
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A normal dipole based microwave imaging method is proposed to distinguish different sized objects buried in dense media. Unlike using a parallel dipole, where the energy is focused into the normal direction due to the lensing effect caused by refraction at the boundary between two layers with a high dielectric contrast, the normal dipole can provide wide-angle illumination in the dense media. The effectiveness of the normal-dipole approach is verified by implementing 3D simulation of different spherical voids buried in a dense slab.

articleTitle: Measurement of PCB Surface Finishes for Substrate Characterization up to 67 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, different surface finish technologies for PCB are investigated by measurement up to 67 GHz. As has been shown in previous publications, S- Parameter measurements of planar transmission lines can be used to characterize the permittivity of the underlying planar substrate. Especially nickel present in the surface finish is suspected to have an influence on the substrate characterization, since the frequency-dependent permeability of nickel is usually not accounted for during permittivity calculation. The commercially available and widely used surface finish technologies ENIG, EPIG, ISIG and coverlay are characterized in terms of substrate permittivity and overall loss and compared against each other and a copper only surface for reference. The influence of nickel is extracted and modelled into an effective permeability.

articleTitle: Off-Body Antenna Dual-Beam Linear to Circular Polarization Converter Based on Quarter-wave Cross-Slot Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual-beam wearable antenna based on AMC- FSS technology with a transmission type polarizer to convert linear to circular polarization at 5.8 GHz. The design is composed of 3 layers, an AMC substrate, a planar monopole and a tilted 45° cross-slots FSS superstrate. The structure provides a 1.69 dB of axial ratio purity polarization and a valuable gain of 7.32 dBi at the ISM band. The dual beam radiation pattern makes the antenna a good candidate for Off-Body underground communications.

articleTitle: A Novel DNA Inspired Mode and Frequency Reconfigurable Origami Helical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel origami helical antenna has been presented based on DNA structure. A DNA consists of double helical chain, whose length can be varied from a few microns up to 2 meter during unfolding. These interesting features are utilized in our proposed antenna design to make it reconfigurable, with respect to the mode as well as the frequency. The operating mode can be switched between normal and axial, whereas the resonance can be shifted from 360 MHz to 2.5 GHz, for different values of spacing between the turns of the antenna. The proposed design was also fabricated by using a copper tape on DNA shaped folded PET substrate, and the sample was measured. Flexible design procedure, efficient folding, compact packaging, easy deployment, as well as low cost have confirmed the potential use of the proposed origami helical antenna for the CubeSat and other space technologies.

articleTitle: Low Frequecy Surface Plasmon Waves on Metal Structured Surface with a Variable Effective Period Subwavelength Rectangular Groove Grating Using Periodically Photoinduced Semiconductor Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The propagation characteristics of low frequency surface plasmon waves on structured perfect electric conductor (PEC)surfaces with a variable effective period subwavelength rectangular groove grating using periodically photoinduced semiconductor plasma are theoretically investigated, using mode matching technique. The Bragg interaction and the leaky wave characteristic of the low frequency surface plasmon waves are theoretically discussed through the numerical result of the dispersion diagram.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured RF Devices and Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents progress made towards the design and fabrication of complex RF components and systems using multi material additive manufacturing (AM).

articleTitle: A Pixel-Based Optimization Method for the Design of Optically Transparent Antennas and Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Antennas and circuits based on transparent conductive materials inevitably suffer from a higher degree of attenuation as compared to copper-based circuits since these materials have higher surface resistances. In order to overcome this problem, an efficient pixel-based optimization methodology is proposed and validated for a transmission line. Two optically transparent materials, indium-tin oxide and copper-mesh, are specifically considered, although the proposed methodology is applicable to other materials, such as silver nano-wires and graphene.

articleTitle: All-Metal Dual-Frequency Circularly Polarized High Gain Antenna for Potential Europa Lander
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new all-metal dual-frequency RHCP high gain antenna is under development at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory for a potential Europa Lander. The antenna is mainly made of metal so it could survive the harsh environment conditions (i.e. very low temperature and high radiation and ESD levels). The antenna is also flat to meet drastic volume constraints and has efficiencies higher than 80% at both the uplink and downlink X-band Deep Space frequency bands. This antenna is a key component for the potential mission enabling Direct Link to Earth (DTE) from and Direct-from-Earth (DFE) to the lander without any relay.

articleTitle: Ultra-Miniature Loaded Loop Antenna for VHF Pager
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Loaded Loop Antenna is a good candidate for telecommunication systems which need high integration and omnidirectional radiation. In this work, an Ultra-Miniature Loaded Loop Antenna (UMLLA) has been designed on a very small VHF radio pager (ka ~0.14), the loop is printed along the outside of the plastic cover, and the load circuit is located on the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) placed inside. A capacity of 4.3 pF is used to model the optimum load at 170 MHz, and a narrowband of 1.2 MHz is obtained. A maximum realized gain of -12.5 dBi and a radiation efficiency of 4.17% have also been observed.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Perfect Anomalous Reflection via Single-Element Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report the design, fabrication, and experimental characterization of a printed circuit board metagrating (MG)for perfect anomalous reflection. The periodic structure, comprised of a single element per period, was synthesized following our previously developed analytical formalism to guarantee unitary coupling to the desirable Floquet-Bloch (FB)mode, while suppressing specular reflections entirely. The experimental setup allows a bistatic measurement of the MG radiation pattern, enabling evaluation of the scattering to the different FB modes, without requiring a reference measurement with a metallic plate. The results verify our theoretical predictions, indicating that highly-efficient anomalous reflection to the prescribed angle is achieved, thus demonstrating the practical applicability of MGs for future wavefront manipulating devices.

articleTitle: Non-contact Material Monitoring by Using Depolarizing Chipless RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A chipless sensor for the wireless monitoring of the electrical permittivity changes of dielectric objects is presented. The sensor is based on a simple passive depolarizing label comprising a couple of tilted dipoles.

articleTitle: Doppler Spectrum of Electromagnetic Scattering from Ocean Surface with Foam Distribution
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to study electromagnetic scattering from sea surface in low frequency and high sea conditions, the electromagnetic scattering of bubbles must be introduced into the electromagnetic scattering calculation of sea surface. In this paper, based on the small slope approximation (SSA) method, the electromagnetic scattering coefficient of wind-driven foam-containing sea surface is modified by equivalent dielectric constant model. Then the Doppler spectral characteristics of the difference is studied. Results show that the foam layer has a significant effect on the Doppler spectral characteristics of the sea surface.

articleTitle: Around the Corner Terahertz Radar Imaging Exploiting Diffusion Scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel method for imaging objects hidden around corners by exploiting the scattering properties of THz waves. Most common building materials have significant specular reflection components that enable THz imaging systems to see around occlusions. Additionally, such materials scatter incident waves to multiple directions which we can use to distinguish between the reflective surfaces and the object of interest. We modify the backpropagation SAR imaging algorithm to correct the clu t-tered raw data and acquire accurate THz images of the occluded areas. The new imaging approach is verified through imaging examples in the 220-330 GHz band using common building materials as mirrors.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Antenna with Added Bottom Rectangular Slabs for Gain Improvement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a new designed thin wide band antenna is introduced. The proposed monopole antenna which was fabricated on flexible substrate has compact geometry area of 51 × 22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> that makes it suitable for handheld applications. The antenna was featured with three rectangular slabs at the bottom layer in order to improve boresight gain performance over spectrum of operation. Moreover, the antenna produces semi omni directive radiation and has radiation efficiency more than 90 % over its bandwidth of operation. The antenna design along with simulation and experimental results are presented in this work.

articleTitle: Attenuation measurement of the dielectric rod using parallel strips with a resonable field environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to effectively evaluate the attenuation distribution of the dielectric rod coated with resistive thin-film, a new test fixture is designed using parallel strips and tapered structure. Hyperbolical tapered lines to parallel strips and angle gradient transitions near the connectors can operate in an ultrawideband frequency range from 1GHz to 40GHz. In the whole range, insertion loss of this fixture is blow 3dB, and return loss is higher than 13dB. The measured attenuation distribution of a dielectric rod coated with resistive thin-film is consistent with the actual at different frequencies.

articleTitle: High-Performance Reflector Antenna Design for the TROPICS Mission
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quad band antenna is designed for the TROPICS mission. The design is of an offset-fed parabolic reflector with dual feeds, utilizing a polarization grid to diplex RF energy onto both compact corrugated feedhorns.

articleTitle: Array Optimization for an On-The-Move 3D Imaging System Demonstrator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, array optimization for an imaging system demonstrator is presented. It is able to create 3D images of people as they walk through the scanner and it makes use of a very low number of transceivers. The array positions have been optimized to minimize grating lobes and maximize resolution for a given number of array elements.

articleTitle: Array-Fed Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna for Two-Dimensional Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a simple phased-array design based on a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna for the generation of a highly-directive pencil beam steerable along two directions in 3-D space. Each array element generates an element pattern in the far-field obtained through the excitation of a dominant cylindrical TM leaky wave inside the cavity. Hence, the resulting conical pattern is combined with the array factor of a N ×N square or circular arrangement of ideal vertical electric dipoles. By proper phasing such sources at the operating frequency, a pencil beam with continuous scanning both in azimuth and elevation is achieved. The proposed leaky-wave phased array is of interest for future wireless power transfer systems as well as for advanced radar and localization systems.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Perfect Absorbers: Systematic Design and High Tunability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Experimental realization of efficient graphene-based absorbers is a challenging task due to the low carrier mobility in processed graphene. In this paper, we circumvent this problem by placing uniform graphene sheets on metallic metasurfaces designed for improving the absorption properties of low-mobility graphene. Complete absorption can be achieved for different frequencies with the proper metasurface design.
