In the THz band, we observe strong tunability of the absorption frequencies and magnitudes when modulating graphene Fermi level.

articleTitle: Phase-only Shaped Beam Transmit-Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new analytical formulation is presented in this paper to obtain the phase correction function for planar transmit-arrays, to produce a prescribed amplitude template. This phase-only design enables using high transmission unit cells to favor maximum gain. Here, a transmit-array transforms the known power radiation pattern of the primary source into a desired output power pattern. As a proof of concept, two different output power radiation patterns are presented, namely, a sec<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a roll-off at 45° and a flat-top with 20° of roll-off, at the 30 GHz Ka-band. The transmit-array aperture is 180 mm × 180 mm, with 60 mm focal length. It is illuminated by a 10.8 dBi feed radiation pattern, with circular polarization.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing Technology for High Performances Feed Horn
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work the design and manufacturing through selective laser melting technology of single-band dual circular feed-system operating in Ka-band is reported. In the feed design an AM oriented architecture has been employed. The measured performances confirms the good manufacturing of the system that satisfies very stringent requirements in terms of polarization purity.

articleTitle: 3D Pattern Optimization Using PSO for an Irregular Dual-Layer Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Smart Antenna System (SAS) is one of the latest hot topics in both academic and industry. It is regarded as the antenna solution for the future generations of wireless communication system. Phased array is widely used in SAS. However, problems at size, cost and meeting the industrial regulations, for example, the sidelobe level, remains. Current studies in array pattern optimization is limited to linear array with one dimension in polar space. Such optimizer is not sufficient to cope with current complex array designs. In this paper, a design of 3D pattern optimizer using popular optimization algorithm, namely Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), is presented. The renovated optimizer is put to tests on a complex array setup, which is a dual-layer circular array with center element.

articleTitle: Characterizations of MIMO Antennas Using Multiplexing Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The multiplexing efficiency has been proposed for characterizations of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas. It has only been partially verified by measurements previously. In this paper, we complement the measurement-based verification. In addition, it is recognized that the multiplexing efficiency is a harmonic mean of the antenna branch powers, implying that the throughput performance of an MIMO system is dominated by the worst antenna branch.

articleTitle: Tightly-Packed Crossed-Dipole Array for L-band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the utilization of a tightly-packed crossed-dipole array antenna for L-band satellite communications. A thin-wire method-of-moments code called SPLAT (Scattering from Periodic Linear Arrays of Thin-wire Elements), which was originally developed for analyzing frequency selective surfaces, is used to perform a parametric study between the element spacing in the array and the impedance bandwidth. The results show that the mutual capacitance between the tightly-packed crossed-dipoles minimizes the variance in the array element current distributions across a one-decade frequency range of 0.3-3.0 GHz. This paper also demonstrates a wideband matching technique which takes advantage of this minimized variance in the current distribution. The wideband matching produces a better than 2: 1 impedance bandwidth, as defined by a voltage standing-wave-ratio (VSWR)below 2, at the antenna terminals. This tightly-packed crossed-dipole feed is designed as a non-scanning array for a deployable faceted reflector intended to be used onboard a geosynchronous L-band communications satellite.

articleTitle: Phase Shifters Design for Scan Range Extension of Rotman Lens Beamforming Based Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of the phase management unit needed for extending the scan range of a 24 GHz array antenna system based on Rotman lens beamforming is presented. The developed phase management unit consists of both static and switchable reflective type phase shifers, whose particular arrangement, in combination with a Rotman lens, allows increasing the maximum steering beam angle by 100%. Finally, the proposed concept is validated through simulation including the complete beamforming network and antenna array system.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Reconfigurable Huygens Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Huygens metasurfaces allow electromagnetic waves to be arbitrarily manipulated by implementing the required electric and magnetic boundary conditions along a surface. Reconfigurable Huygens metasurfaces offer an additional advantage of real-time tunable responses. This paper presents the design of a unit cell comprising a wideband reconfigurable Huygens metasurface, whose elements correspond to the geometry of the electric and magnetic dipoles. The design is aided by making use of an equivalent circuit model that allows the response of the cell to be accurately predicted as it is tuned. Simulation results show that the designed unit cell can achieve phase range of over 180° and insertion loss of less than 3 dB over a 40% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Non-Cooperative, Non-Line of Sight Geolocation of Radio Emitters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Estimating the location of radio emitters in multipath environments is known to be challenging, particularly when no Line of Sight (LOS) path is present. We propose novel non-cooperate Maximum Likelihood (ML) location estimator for use in dense urban environments which uniquely exploits the scattering environment geometry in order to mitigate the need for LOS paths. A simple scattering model is used to assess the performance of the algorithm. Simulation results are included demonstrating a mean location error of 89 m.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-inspired Electrically Small Platforms: Enhanced Directivity Properties
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A variety of near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) antennas have been developed as electrically small platforms to realize high directivity. These include compact arrays and Huygens dipole and multipole radiating systems. A brief review of these developments and their scattering equivalents will be presented.

articleTitle: A Design of Optimal Rectenna Array for Retrodirective MPT System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an optimal design of rectenna array for retrodirective microwave power transfer (MPT) system is proposed. By analyzing the power signal at each receiving antenna, the optimal number of rectenna array is presented numerically. In addition, the power combining performances of both RF and DC based method are analyzed and DC power combining scheme is proposed for optimal design.

articleTitle: Reduced Coupling for Through Wall Radars Using Orthogonal Circular Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we propose using orthogonal circularly polarized quadrifilar helical antennas for the transmitter and receiver of a through-wall radar system. The objective of this configuration is to achieve low coupling between the transmitter and receiver antennas. The quadrifilar helix antennas were chosen because of their high gain, wide bandwidth and compact size. Experimental validations have been performed in line-of-sight conditions with and without a target.

articleTitle: Compressive Processing in Inverse Problems: Current Advances and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Compressive Sensing (CS) paradigm recently emerged as an effective strategy to efficiently address inverse scattering problems. Even if the sensing problem has been already widely investigated in the literature, the sampling problem (i.e. the optimization of the observation setup) is still not well addressed. In this work a new CS paradigm, namely Compressive Processing (CP), is presented, aimed to jointly solve the sampling and sensing problems for a new generation of CS- based inverse scattering techniques.

articleTitle: Beam Steering of Series-fed Patch Array Using Frequency and Phase Variation Near 76.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The frequency scanning technique is proposed for use in the automotive radar to achieve beam steering in the elevation direction. A series-fed patch array antenna is implemented and used for validation. A two-dimensional array is formed by adding three more of the same antennas, and the beam steering capability both in the elevation and azimuth directions is demonstrated. The radiation patterns are observed nearly constant for both the frequency and phase variations as desired in the automotive radar applications.

articleTitle: Pencil Beam Constrained Synthesis of Linear Sparse Arrays in Presence of Coupling Effects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work an efficient method is presented for the pencil beam constrained synthesis of linear sparse arrays. As a first step, the positions of a number of isotropic radiators are found on an aperture of given length. Then, the isotropic radiators are replaced with real antenna elements, and the excitations are optimized in such a way that, taking the mutual coupling into account, the radiation pattern belong to a prescribed mask. Two numerical examples show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Polarization 4×4 MIMO Multi-Beam Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of compact dual polarized MIMO multi-beam base station antennas. By reducing both the azimuth/elevation spacings and row number of the antenna array, the sizes of the multi-beam antennas are reduced significantly. Through stacking two multibeam antennas vertically, two 4×4 MIMO 6-beam antennas with different specifications are designed and tested. Detailed array architecture and the corresponding measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Wide Scan, Wide band Arrays with Self-Dual Point-Like Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The unique matching properties of self-dual structures provide a rich platform to engineer and control the distribution of the power inside such structures. For instance, narrow gaps embedded inside a self-dual structure can be designed to predominantly carry the incident energy into the outbound interface of the structure. This phenomenon can be used to create quasi-matched radiating apertures made of point-like radiating elements. These elements possess patterns that are quite similar to those of an isolated element in free space, being fairly well-behaved and free of blind spots. These characteristics are envisioned to be of great interest for highly demanding applications of phased arrays.

articleTitle: Single-feed dual-excitation slot antenna for the LTE tablet device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The dual open-slot antennas for the metal-casing tablet device with tiny clearance area are presented. The antenna has a narrow width of 2 mm with a single-feed dual-excitation source (SFDS) which is located between the metal frame and metal back case of the tablet device. The antenna consists of two open-slot radiators (slot 1 and slot 2) with two filter circuit embedded individually that can generate two wideband LTE operations to cover the 698-960 and 1710-2690 MHz. By adjusting the values of the filter circuits which can make the impedance of the antenna become smooth variations to excite the desired modes. Two proposed antennas (MIMO antennas) are arranged on opposite directions and set on different long side of the device to avoid the hand touch effects.

articleTitle: RF MEMS switch for Reconfigurable RF-Front End with Improved Hot-Switching Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reviews the authors' past work on how to improve the hot-switching reliability for RF MEMS switch. Two methods have been proposed to improve the hot-switching reliability. The first method is to place a refractory sacrificial metal contact in parallel with the main low-resistance switch contact. The sacrificial contact will be actuated first to significantly lower the electric field strength across the main contact during hot-switching. Both sacrificial contact and main contact are integrated in a compact single cantilever actuator. The performance is demonstrated experimentally, by showing 100 times improvement of reliability in hot-switching cycle. The second method is to place the sacrificial contact in front of the main switch contact in shunt configuration. The sacrificial contact will be actuated first to block the incoming RF power while the main switch contact is switching. The main switch contact will be immune to hot-switching RF power damage. The proposed method is experimentally verified to yield better reliability. In addition to the improved reliability, the isolation of the switch is also improved, mainly due to the shunt sacrificial switch.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized C-shaped Monopole Antenna for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized (CP) monopole antenna for satellite applications. The antenna consists of two C-shaped monopole radiators and has an overall compact size of 32 × 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The two C-shaped monopole radiators along with L-shaped slot in the ground plane are mainly responsible to achieve circular polarization. The antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured results are in quite good agreement with simulations. The measured impedance bandwidth of 1170 MHz (5.5 - 6.67 GHz) and axial ratio bandwidth of 760 MHz (5.91 - 6.67 GHz) is achieved.

articleTitle: A 120 GHz Step-Profiled Horn Antenna in LTCC
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 120 GHz step-profiled horn antenna integrated in low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) is presented in this paper. Based on the substrate integrated waveguide technology, the cavities with several surrounding fences of vertical metallic vias are utilized to construct the hollow horn structure in multilayer LTCC substrates. To verify the effectiveness of the design, the proposed antenna prototype is further fabricated and measured. The measured results indicate that more than 8 GHz (115 GHz-123 GHz) bandwidth of 10 dB return loss and a gain of 13.6 dBi in the broadside at 120 GHz are obtained.

articleTitle: Wideband Antennas and Phased Arrays for Enhancing Cybersecurity in 5G Mobile Wireless
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fundamental issues on cyberspace and its security, in particular for 5G mobile wireless, are addressed from the concept of symmetric dual-space and dual-system. Formulated as a physical problem by narrowing “Information” to “Electronic Information,” and “Communication” to “Telecommunication,” with focus on “Observables,” the current cyberspace is akin to a “biological” or “intelligent” system, and even vulnerable to Chaos. A practical solution to enhance both capacity and security/privacy is within reach by employing wideband diversity antenna systems, in particular wideband wide-scan mm Wave phased arrays. Engineering, implementation, and business vision for this approach are discussed in the context of the ongoing pivotal and monumental global 5G mobile wireless thrust.

articleTitle: High Directive Loop Antenna for Low-Profile Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile loop antenna positioned above a hybrid circular (HC) surface is presented. The HC consists of two different metallic rings, which are combined in a single ground plane to improve the radiation performance of the radiating element. The integration of the loop antenna with the HC surface leads to a directivity of 11 dB and a fractional bandwidth of 14%.

articleTitle: Overcoming Feasibility Constraints in Reflectarray Design by Exploiting Non-Radiating Currents
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes a new design methodology aimed at overcoming the feasibility constraints in the synthesis of microstrip reflectarrays. Towards this end, the non-radiating (NR) currents theory is profitably exploited in order to suitably modify the reflectarray surface currents without changing the radiated pattern, and a global optimizer is employed to efficiently solve the arising synthesis problem. An illustrative example is presented in order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed design approach.

articleTitle: A W-band Single-Layer Metal-Only Array Antenna with Two Focal Planes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A W-band single-layer metal-only array (MOA) antenna with the capacity of focusing electromagnetic waves on both reflection plane and transmission plane is proposed in this paper which is suitable for passive millimeter wave imaging system (PMI). Double focal planes of the antenna make contribution to potentially raise the imaging frame rate of PMI and increase the spatial sampling rate. Square slot-type elements are employed to cover the 2n phase range and a discontinuities-slope horn is designed with symmetrical pattern offset to feed the MOA. To validate the proposed design, a MOA with 144 elements is designed and simulated. The size of -3dB focal spot is around 1.81mm at 94GHz with 3.6mm depth of focus, and the focusing efficiency is about 14.5%.

articleTitle: Characterization of diffuse scattering based on dielectric properties of construction materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A measurement campaign is carried out to deduce the complex permittivity over 40 GHz to 50 GHz by free-space measurement technology for five common construction material samples. Based on this, diffuse scattering is simulated at a central frequency of 45 GHz and a bandwidth of 660 MHz using the Wireless Insite software. The measurement campaign is well design for the development of diffuse scattering model and material identification of radio map.

articleTitle: Cell Morphology-Based Classification in Red Blood Cells by Angle-Resolved Electromagnetic Scattering Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes our theoretical and experimental investigation on light scattering from individual murine red blood cells (RBCs). Based on measured cell morphologies at different ionic strength and osmolarity conditions, we simulated the light scattering characteristics of the cells by using the Muller boundary integral equation (MBIE) method. The calculated cross section values showed good agreement with our experimental data obtained with conventional and imaging-based flow cytometries.

articleTitle: Permittivity and Conductivity Estimation for Hyperthermia Treatment Planning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, an original approach for invivo estimation of electrical properties of biological tissues is presented. Such an estimation represents an essential step in hyperthermia treatment planning, wherein typically magnetic resonance or computerized tomography images are exploited and turned into electric parameters, based on available ex-vivo measured properties, to predict the effects of the treatment. As parameters change from patient to patient and can be quite different from the ex-vivo ones, the proposed approach is based on the solution of an inverse scattering problem, processing backscattered data measured from the patient and conveniently exploiting the morphological information on tissues available from medical images, to overcome the well-known issues arising in the solution of inverse problems.

articleTitle: Fundamental Efficiency Limit of Passive Non-Magnetic Self-Interference Suppression in Full-Duplex Radios
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Passive non-magnetic self-interference suppression circuits are currently used as first stages of complex full-duplex radio systems that allow simultaneous reception and transmission within the same channel. This paper introduces the upper efficiency limit for such circuitry. It is demonstrated that for these devices it is not feasible to have simultaneously high efficiency, good transmitter-to-receiver isolation and same propagation channel for transmission and reception. More specifically, the maximum efficiency for most typical case cannot exceed 50% if good isolation is obtained.

articleTitle: Efficient and Accurate Modeling of Reflectarray Unit Cells Using SVMs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a technique for an efficient and accurate characterization of dual-polarized reflectarray unit cells by means of Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to accelerate the analysis and optimization of this type of antenna. The goal is to accurately obtain the matrix of complex reflection coefficients using geometrical data of the unit cell. To this end, SVMs are employed to obtain surrogate models of those coefficients in an efficient fashion by employing a novel grid search which accelerates by three orders of magnitude the training process with regard to an exhaustive grid search. In addition, the precision of the surrogate model is tested against full-wave simulations assuming local periodicity obtaining a high degree of agreement.

articleTitle: 6×6 Array of Four-arm Spiral Antennas for High-gain Satellite Receiver Applications at Low Elevation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 6×6 array of four-arm spiral antennas is presented for satellite receiver applications at 18 GHz. The array provides a wide-angle elevation scanning with a high gain right handed circularly polarized (RHCP) radiation beam. Each spiral element has four spiral arms with four feeding ports. The four arms are arranged symmetrically with respect to the center of the antenna. When one of the four ports are excited and other ports are open-circuited, the spiral element provides an RHCP tilted beam (θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>= 51°) with a gain of 8.4 dBi. By switching the excitation among the four feeding ports, the spiral element can switch the beam in four different quadrants in space. It is demonstrated that by combining these four unit-patterns, the 6×6 array of four-arm spirals provides an elevation scanning range of -70°≤ θ ≤ 70° with a maximum gain up to 20.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Multimode Positioning Using Common and Difference Mode Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient positioning approach based on multimode near-field communication is proposed. Using conventional loop antennas, common and difference modes magnetic fields are generated. The range between two antennas can be estimated accurately using only the near-field field strength since these modes depend on the propagation distance differently. Because magnetic fields can penetrate into different media, the proposed method is a good alternative to conventional methods which suffer from multipath effects. Moreover, as generated modes will see same propagation path and losses, no calibration is needed to compensate the unwanted anomalies. By using just the field strength and ignoring the phase of received signals, the proposed method can be effectively used in Very Low Frequency (VLF) applications for positioning in the lossy environments like subterranean mines without the need to have a good resolution. The mentioned advantages accompanied by the cost-effectiveness and simplicity of the proposed idea make it a good candidate to achieve acceptable performance in the related applications.

articleTitle: Planewave scattering by topologically insulating surface states on a spherical surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Planewave scattering from a topological insulating (TI) sphere was studied when the relative permittivity and relative permeability of that sphere are both equal to unity, in order to examine scattering by topologically insulating surface states (TISS) by themselves. The TISS were modeled via surface charge and current densities quantitated through a surface-admittance parameter. The results indicate that the extinction and total-scattering efficiencies approach the corresponding efficiencies of a perfect electrically conducting (PEC) sphere of the same size when the surface-admittance parameter becomes very large. The extinction, total-scattering, and forward-scattering efficiencies remain smaller than the corresponding efficiencies of the PEC sphere. The backscattering efficiency can be either smaller or greater than that of the PEC sphere, depending upon the electrical size of the scattering spherical surface. By themselves, the TISS do not contribute to absorption.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Level Improvement in a Frequency Scanning Antenna at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a method for sidelobe level improvement based on line-width modulation of a microstrip frequency scanning antenna is proposed. Simulation results show that 4 dB reduction in sidelobe level is achieved by this method at its center frequency. In addition, 2.2 to 4.4 dB improvement will be shown over the bandwidth of the antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband Antenna-Isolation Improvement using Photonics for STAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) technology can be used to enhance the capacity of 5G wireless networks only if a sufficient amount of isolation exists between the sys-tem's transmitter and receiver. RF cancellers utilizing photonic components can be incorporated into a node's architecture to provide additional isolation that is greater than the inherent antenna coupling response. This concept can be applied over wide bandwidths, and has been demonstrated using an over-the-air measurement that resulted in more than 14 dB of isolation improvement over a 1 GHz bandwidth centered at 2.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Beam-Forming Network for Switched-Beam Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Butler-matrix-inspired beam-forming network has been developed to provide phasing for a switched-beam 2×2 element antenna array. The network uses an arrangement of double-box quadrature hybrids to achieve wide instantaneous bandwidth in a small, planar form factor. The planar feed structure has been designed to integrate with an array aperture to form a low-profile array stackup.

articleTitle: A Compact Single Layer Orthogonal Polarized Yagi-Like Directional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact Yagi-like directional antenna is presented based on a slot loop excitation. Two orthogonally polarized beams are generated by orthogonally feeding the slot using two microstrip lines. Both the horizontally polarized (HP) and the vertically polarized (VP) beams constitute an omnidirectional radiation patterns that are made directional by using two complementary slot reflector elements. The proposed antenna has a measured bandwidth of 330 MHz (3.56-3.89) targeting the WiMAX band. The antenna is compact with a total board size of 35 × 40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Both end-fire directional beams have a minimum gain of 3.8 dBi and front-to-back ratio (FBR) of 6 dB. The efficiency of the antenna is 94% for both ports.

articleTitle: Antenna Composed of Meta- and Natural-material Loops
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an antenna system composed of an activated metamaterial loop (MTM-loop) antenna and a parasitic natural loop element. The MTM-Loop antenna acts as a counter circularly polarized (CP) radiation element, where the radiation is left-handed CP within one frequency band below a specific frequency, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> (f <; f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>), and right-handed CP within another frequency band above f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> (f> f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>). The maximum gain below f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> is smaller than that above f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>. It is found that placing the parasitic natural loop element above the activated MTM-Loop can minimize the difference between these two gain values. The antenna characteristics of the antenna system are analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Development of aperture-coupled patch array antennas at 60 GHz for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Wireless Gigabit Alliance (WiGig) is a standard pushing development of wireless communications over the 60 GHz band. The WiGig specification enables data rates up to 7 Gbps, which is 10 times the speed of the fastest Wi-Fi networks. As the demand for higher data rates is continuously increasing, WiGig proposal used for wireless data, voice, and video applications at multigigabit speeds has been attracting much interest. New 60 GHz devices with tri-band radios will be able to seamlessly integrate into existing 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi networks. However, the technology in the millimeter-wave bands is not yet so mature as in microwave bands. This paper presents a comparison of two 4×4 array antenna designs based on using different materials: low-temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) and Rogers at 60 GHz in LTCC design. The obtained directivity, at 60 GHz, is 16.3 dBi using LTCC and 14.5 dBi using the Rogers substrate.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of High Power Microwave in Rectangular Waveguide Filled with Time-Varying Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the propagation characteristics of high power microwave (HPM) in rectangular waveguide filled with time-varying plasma is studied using a 3-D fluid model. The propagation properties are influenced by parameters of the plasma and microwave, such as the electron density, distribution of plasma and the frequency of microwave. The breakdown process of the air in waveguide and the generation of the plasma are presented, and the reflection and absorption of microwave by the plasma are analyzed. These results are useful in analysis of HPM propagation in microwave devices when air breakdown occurs, and helpful to improve the performance of HPM devices.

articleTitle: A Broadband Cirularly Polarized Directional Antenna Applied on Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized antenna with directional radiation is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of four orthogonal dipoles which are backed by four near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) reflector to broaden the 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth (ARBW) and generate a directional radiation pattern. The antenna has a simple series feed structure, which can realize 90° phase shift and four equal power divisions. The total size of the antenna is 130×130×20mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (0.7λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>X 0.7λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>X 0.11λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, at 1.6GHz).

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Waveguide Structures by Coupled Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a new method to significantly reduce the size and thickness of waveguides using a new class of coupled transmission lines (CTLs). By increasing CTLs into the waveguide, new modes are generated that lower the cutoff frequency, and therefore reducing size for the same operational frequency. We considered circular as well rectangular waveguides. Due to their cutoff frequency CTL-loaded waveguides can be used at much lower frequencies and realized as extremely thin or sheet like transmission lines.

articleTitle: An improved quadrature error estimate for nearly-singular MoM integrals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A well-known numerical integration scheme for weakly near-singular integrands on triangle domains, is the Radial-Angular-RI-Sqrt near-singularity cancellation transformation quadrature scheme. Such integrals feature routinely in the method of moments (MoM), for integral equation based numerical electromagnetic field calculations. Recently, a closed-form quadrature error estimate has been proposed for this scheme. In this paper, the estimate is further improved, such that its range of applicability is extended.

articleTitle: A Ultra-Wideband Monocone Antenna with Ceramic Loading
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile top-hat shorted monocone antenna with ceramic loading is proposed. SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, a kind of ceramic, is first employed as matching layer to improve antenna's matching property and support the antenna's structure. Besides, for further increasing the bandwidth of monocone antenna, top hat and shorting pins are applied to reduce the lowest operating frequency and thus decrease the thickness of the monocone antenna to O.068λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Low</sub>. Simulated results show that a 6:1 bandwidth can be obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Scattering from a Thin Sheet
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fields scattered by an infinitesimally thin dielectric sheet are presented. An integral equation formulation is derived using the surface equivalence theorem. This technique is suitable for simulating two-dimensional materials that are only a few atoms thick.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Tunable Wave Absorbing Structure Based on Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-frequency absorbing structure is designed based on frequency selective surface in this paper. The unit is made up of two resonant rings nested together. The proposed structure can absorb more than 98% of electromagnetic waves at 5.86GHz and 9.30GHz. The two absorbing frequency has an independent adjustability by tuning the geometry. Furthermore, the structure is insensitive to the polarization characteristics, and it can keep an absorption even the incident angle increases to 60°.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Phase Controlled Focusing Metalens at 1550 nm Wavelength
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional focusing lenses are bulky and thick. The use of metalenses with sub-wavelength resolution allows us to reduce the size and amount of material needed for lenses. This work presents a metalens utilizing 3D printed dielectric unit cells with different height to focus IR light at a predetermined distance. It allows for a planar like structure which can be used for many applications such as medical imaging.

articleTitle: Method for Generating a Minimal-Rank $\mathcal{H}^{2}$ -Matrix from FMM for Electrically Large Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we develop an efficient method to generate a rank-minimized H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -matrix to represent electrically large integral operators for a prescribed accuracy. We first generate an H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -matrix using the Fast Multipole Method (FMM), and hence the complexity for H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -construction is as low as O (NlogN) for solving electrically large surface integral equations. We then convert the FMM-based H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -matrix whose rank is full asymptotically to a new H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> -representation, whose rank is minimized based on accuracy. Numerical experiments demonstrate a significantly reduced rank with prescribed accuracy satisfied.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Design of Antennas Using Variable-Fidelity EM Models and Constrained Surrogates
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fast multi-objective design optimization of antenna structures is discussed using variable-fidelity simulation models and kriging surrogates. The cost of surrogate model construction is significantly reduced by constraining the model domain to a simplex spanned by the extreme Pareto-optimal designs, further extended in orthogonal directions so as to enclose the entire Pareto front. For demonstration purposes, a UWB monopole is designed for size minimization, matching improvement and reduction of realized gain variations. A uniform representation of the Pareto set is obtained at the cost of only 195 high-fidelity EM simulations of the antenna, which is 64-percent speedup as compared to the benchmark surrogate-assisted technique.

articleTitle: An Equivalent Distorted Born Iterative Method to Solve Inverse Scattering Problem Without Updating the Green's Function
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an equivalent distorted Born iteration method (DBIM) is proposed to solve inverse scattering problem based on volume integral equation (VIE) method. For its forward problem, the object region is regarded as the scatterer and free space is considered to be the background, which relates to a free space Green's function. The equivalent DBIM inversion model is constructed base on the forward model which has the same convergent rate with the conventional DBIM. Differently, the integration kernel, the free space Green's function, remains unchanged in the equivalent DBIM while that of the conventional DBIM need to be computed and updated in every iterations. In this way, the computational complexity of the DBIM has been reduced remarkably, and it is easy to be employed in solving three-dimensional (3-D) inverse problem.

articleTitle: Sparse Direction-of-Arrival Estimation with Directive Coprime Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a sparse direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method for directive coprime arrays. The complex radiation patterns are extracted using an electromagnetic simulator and then incorporated in the DOA estimation. Three DOA algorithms are compared including Capon, MUSIC, and Lasso based on compressive sensing (CS). It is shown that when the DOA increases in the elevation plane, the performance degrades faster when using real antenna patterns.

articleTitle: A metamaterial electromagnetic wave absorber based on resistive films for micro-satellite spatial applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a thin and efficient absorber operating in the band [8-8.4 GHz] for the reduction of electromagnetic interactions between a payload telemetry isoflux antenna and the neighboring elements of the payload of a micro-satellite. The proposed design uses a 1000 Ω/sq TICER resistive film as part of a multi-layer PCB to absorb the electromagnetic energy. The multi-layer insulation (MLI) material coating the satellite acts as a ground plane for the absorber.

articleTitle: Gaussian Beam Diffraction by the Inverse Prism
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We study the diffraction of a Gaussian beam from the recently introduced inverse prism, which is a medium that is instantaneously switched between an isotropic state and a uniaxial state. The study is done by expanding all the fields in terms of their angular spectra, using previously derived temporal Fresnel coefficients for the s- and p-polarizations. It is found that the envelope of the beam strongly varies over time, as a result of the different velocities of the angular spectrum components induced by the production of new frequencies at the time discontinuity. This spatiotemporal diffraction effect, requiring both temporal discontinuity and spatial dispersion, is very unusual, and is reported here for the first time to authors' knowledge.

articleTitle: Sparsity and Coherence in Inverse Problems - from 1 D to 2D Processing through Matrix Completion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Sparseness-promoting inversion strategies based on Bayesian formulations have recently emerged as powerful, robust, flexible, and accurate techniques to address a wide variety of problems arising in microwave imaging. The success of such paradigm is motivated by the capability of the resulting formulations to (i) handle sparse linear/linearized problems even when incoherence or restricted isometry properties (RIPs) are not guaranteed, and to (ii) provide self-computed “confidence level” estimations. Unfortunately, no methodology has been proposed in the state-of-the-art to actually exploit such confidence-level indexes and enhance the reconstructed profiles once the imaging reliability is self-detected to be poor (e.g., in harsh signal-to-noise-ratio scenarios, or when the RIP does not hold true). Moreover, the most popular BCS formulations handle the unknowns as 1D vectors, therefore neglecting the “matrix” nature of the associated physical problem (e.g., contrast retrieval). In this framework, this paper is aimed at illustrating the possibility to exploit a new class of methodologies based on rank-minimization formulations to overcome the above limitations and recover reliable reconstructions of the scattering scenario by fully exploiting the 2D matrix nature of the problem. Selected preliminary numerical results will be also discussed to validate the proposed paradigm.

articleTitle: Comparison of Clustering Effect in Space-Delay Domain at 5.8 GHz Depending on the Indoor Scenarios Sizes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution provides a comparison between empty and furnished conditions within an indoor scenario in terms of delay clustering along strait paths in the band of 5.8 GHz. Indoor measurement data represent the input to analyze them form the optics of delay domain, observing the number and the shape of the different clusters configured by the different environments in broadband propagation. Results show that multipath contributions tend to group in clusters with similar delay at adjacent measurement locations. The amplitude and distribution of these clusters would be related to the performance of the radio links deployed within the considered environments. The size of the room has an influence in terms of the amplitude (lower when the room is larger) and the delay (larger as the room size grows) of these delay-domain contributions.

articleTitle: SAR imaging of hypersonic platform based on phase screen method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The plasma sheath turbulent structure which affect the performance on the point target imaging can't be ignored when the platform is moving at a high speed. In this paper a fractal phase screen model is established based on plasma sheath refractive index fluctuation. The influence of plasma sheath on SAR imaging system is analyzed. The results show that either on range or azimuth direction echo of point target on field is dispersive. Analysis for echo of point target shows that turbulent structure in plasma sheath has great effect on the SAR imaging system and it affected the azimuth direction more than range direction. This is due to a combination of hypersonic flow field and higher speed compared with common platform. Therefore, the azimuth ambiguity is one of the most important characters to scale the image quality of SAR imaging system.

articleTitle: Design of a Double-Layer Dielectric-Only Transmitarray Antenna for THz Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A double-layer dielectric-only transmitarray antenna working at 250 G Hz is presented in this paper. Different from common transmitarray using three or four substrate layers with metal patch etched on the surface, no metal is used in the proposed element and only high-resistivity silicon is adopted to form the structure. The proposed sub-wavelength element is composed of cuboid and cylinder structure. The diameter of the cylinder is used to control the transmission phase and a phase range of over 360° with low transmission loss is achieved. The transmitarray consisting 225 elements is designed based on the proposed elements. The simulation result show good performance with the gain of 21.2 dB and aperture efficiency of 42 % at center frequency.

articleTitle: Exceptional Points of Degeneracy in a Linear Array Oscillator with Gain and Loss Balance
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate a new paradigm for dispersion engineering in coupled transmission lines (CTLs)based on the occurrence of an exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD), which represent coalescence of eigenmodes. We experimentally verify the existence of the EPD through dispersion measurements in microstrip-based CTLs at microwave frequencies. We propose the “gain and loss balance” regime as a route for recovering the EPD in the presence of radiation losses hence enabling a new class of coherent EPD-based single-frequency radiating oscillators. This versatile EPD concept is promising in applications requiring high power efficiency oscillators and high radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Microstrip Antennas on Metamaterial Substrate Using Discrete Mode Matching Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The objective of this paper is to present the extension of the discrete mode matching method (DMM) for the analysis of microstrip patch antennas on metamaterial substrate. The procedure to deal with multiple metallizations in the interfaces of the multilayered structure is explained. To demonstrate the technique, a metamaterial structure is placed in the substrate which changes the dispersion properties of the antenna. A very good agreement has been achieved between the results from proposed method and commercial software.

articleTitle: A Chiral Meta-Mirror Enabled Linear and Nonlinear Chiroptical Responses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, chiral-selective absorption and circular polarization preservation of a chiral metamaterial mirror are presented. Beyond the linear regime, it is shown that the resonance also enables handedness-dependent nonlinear generation from such meta-mirrors. Moreover, we have demonstrated that the proposed chiral-mirror can be used to achieve resonance-enhanced and chiral-selective high-contrast second-harmonic optical imaging.

articleTitle: Wideband Dielectric-Loaded Venetian-Blind Polarizer for a Short f/D Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact, shaped polarizer fitting into the feed of a lens antenna with f/D = 0.7 is described. By physically combining a dielectric polarizer with a “Venetian-blind” type polarizer a polarization isolation of greater than 15 dB from 9.0 GHz to 11.5 GHz was demonstrated. The polarization isolation was increased to a maximum of 22 dB by shaping the polarizer to better match the curved phase-front of the electric field from the feed horn.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Low Cost Folded Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper shows the practicability of entirely manufacturing complex antennas, as a folded reflectarray operating in Ku band, by using a low cost plastic 3D printer. All the antenna parts have been printed, not only the antenna supports, but also the feeder, the polarizer, and the reflectarray substrate. Then, the plastic parts have been opportunely metalized or by using conductive silver based spray, or by sticking on it an adhesive copper sheet appositely cut with a vinyl cutter plotter. Some strategies to reduce the influence of the not accurate knowledge of the material characteristics, and a few manufacturing tricks are also reported.

articleTitle: Parametric Investigations and Demonstration of A Metasurface-Coated Ultra-wideband Monopole
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and experiment of an ultra-wideband monopole antenna coated by a conformal metasurface. Based on a specifically developed modal-expansion method, the dispersive property of the metasurface was tailored to achieve an ultra-wideband impedance bandwidth for an otherwise narrowband monopole. Parametric studies were conducted to reveal the impact of the metasurface properties on the performance of the monopole. Finally, the ultra-wideband metasurface-coated monopole was fabricated and characterized, showing a strong agreement between the measured and simulated results, thus confirming the proposed design.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Compact Circularly Polarized Antenna Using Coupled Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Novel ultra-wideband compact circularly polarized (CP)antenna with 5:1 CP < 1 dB bandwidth and 3:1 VSWR < 3:1 bandwidth is designed by coupling four standard half-wave dipoles capacitively in a square loop fashion. The performance of the antenna is demonstrated in free space, with metallic and electromagnetic band gap (EBG)metamaterial ground planes. In the case of metallic ground plane the total height of the antenna is 3 cm, which is 0.15 of the wavelength at the lowest frequency of operation of 1.5 GHz. Significant reduction in the height, 0.015 of wavelength, is achieved with EBG ground plane which is almost 10 times less as compared to metallic case. The CP antenna with a feed structure including a balun and 100 Ω to 160 Ω impedance transformer has been simulated and is being fabricated currently. The measured results of the coupled dipole antenna will be presented in the IEEE- APS meeting.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized Horn Antenna with Tunable Handedness Using Chiral Metamaterial Loading
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a rectangular WR-187 waveguide horn antenna that utilizes chiral metamaterial loading in the mouth of the horn to achieve circular polarization. The handedness of the polarization is shown to be tunable within the operative frequency band through simple reorientation of the unit cells.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Response from a Two- Dimensional Array of Conducting Strips Inter-Connected with Columns of Silver-Coated Micron-Sized Particles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Controlling the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) waves through a dielectric medium has applications in antenna miniaturization and beam-forming. One method of controlling EM propagation is to use a two-dimensional array of conducting strips printed on one side of a dielectric layer. The work presented in this paper demonstrates a new way to implement these conducting strips. More specifically, conducting micron-sized particles are embedded into the design of the conducting strips and are used to control the EM response of the overall host dielectric. This control occurs through the response of the particles to a magneto-static field. When a field is applied, the particles within a dielectric cavity form columns in the direction of the field lines. Since the particles are conducting, this results in conducting columns that connect various conducting strips. The advantage of using these particles is that a directly connected biasing circuit is not required and allows for the placement of these particles in very complex geometries. Finally, theory and simulations are shown to agree and validate the overall results.

articleTitle: A Planar Ultra- Wideband Phased Array Antenna with Low Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar ultra-wideband phased array antenna with wide-scanning angle and low electromagnetic scattering characteristics is proposed. The infinite array delivers a 4: 1 bandwidth from 4 to 16GHz for VSWR<;2.6 when scanning up to ± 60°. Meanwhile, a tapered slot array (TSA) as well as a PEC plate with the same aperture size is used as a reference antenna to quantitatively evaluate the low scattering performance of the proposed array. Simulated results show that the proposed array has a lower scattering in 4-18GHz as compared to the reference ones. Two prototypes for a 6×6 proposed array and a 4×8 reference array were fabricated and measured, respectively. Reasonable agreements between the measurement and simulation results are obtained.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm for Broadband Electromagnetic Scattering form Conducting Objects Using Reduced Basis Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fast algorithm based on electric integral equation (EFIE) is developed for broadband electromagnetic scattering from metallic objects. This algorithm is integrated with reduced basis method (RBM), and accelerated by the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) and the multilevel accelerated Cartesian expansion (MLACE). Benefitting from MLFMA and MLACE, the computational cost, i.e., memory requirements and computational time can be reduced significantly. With the help of RBM, a fast RCS computation over a wide frequency band can be achieved. In comparison with the traditional fast algorithm, our approach produces much less computational cost for the same solution accuracy. Moreover, its validity and efficiency are demonstrated by the numerical results provided in this paper.

articleTitle: A High- Resolution Approach to Extract the the Emissions from a Circuit Board Using the Magnitude-Only Near-Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Method of moment (MoM)source reconstruction technique is used to calculate the equivalent currents on a closed surface that encompasses a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)transmission line (TL)using magnitude-only near-field measured data. In amplitude-only measurement techniques firstly an initial value for the equivalent sources is assumed and then an iterative solver is used to enhance the accuracy of the phase. Thus, a valid initial value can result a quick convergence of the iteration to the accurate electromagnetic fields. In this paper an approach for choosing an appropriate initial guess for MoM based methods is introduced and the effect of different parameters such as the measurement height on this choice is explained.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circular Polarized Microstrip Antenna Based on Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new octagonal artificial magnetic conductor unit is proposed. The bandwidth of in-phase reflection characteristics is from 8.36GHz to 9.55GHz. Then a circularly polarized microstrip antenna loading a C-shaped slot in the circular microstrip patch with 7×7 artificial magnetic conductor is designed. Simulation results show that the antenna operates in 7.42 GHz~10.74 GHz with return loss less than -10dB. And relative bandwidth of the antenna is 36.6%. The frequency range is from 8.30 GHz to 9.37 GHz which axial ratio is less than 3 dB. Gain of the antenna is more than 6dB in the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Printed Dipole Integrated with Minimal Balun
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cunning idea for realizing antenna baluns with very simple architecture and straightforward design procedure is investigated. The key innovation is the ingenious way to connect the unbalanced terminal to the balanced output. The unique connection makes the remaining part of the balun function no more than a routine matching network, in which all kind of matching techniques can be applied to transform an arbitrary load impedance to a given source one. The concept is verified by integrating the balun to a common printed dipole antenna having three arbitrary complex loads. The matching network is simply an L-section to achieve minimal complexity. Experimental results support the unique idea and show high degrees of design flexibility.

articleTitle: Fast Solutions of Dyadic Green's Function for Multilayered Isotropic Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The discrete complex image method, the window function method and the modified fast Hankel transform method are three popular fast techniques for calculating the dyadic Green's functions in a multilayered medium. In order to provide detailed knowledge of the accuracy, efficiency and application range of the three fast methods, the efficiency of the three methods are carefully examined. The results indicate that discrete complex image method is effective for general multilayered cases and modified fast Hankel transform method is also a powerful tool, while the accuracy and efficiency of window function method is strongly dependent on the multilayered geometry.

articleTitle: Small Size Antennas Mountable on Mettalic Gas Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a solution to integrate a metallic gas cylinder in an Internet of Things (IoT) network. The work briefly explains the different attempts made, then focusing on describing the final solution. The discussion has in account the simulated and measured results. The final result is a small antenna (dimensions lower than 90mm × 3Smm) capable of taking advantage of the metallic surface of the gas cylinder without compromising its input impedance.

articleTitle: Maximum-Bandwidth Synthesis of Monopulse Array Antennas with Fixed Geometry Through Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach for the synthesis of optimal wideband sum and difference patterns with upper mask constraints on the side-lobes of the far field radiation patterns considering a fixed number of shared elements in the feeding network between both sum and difference channels. A convex optimization is iteratively applied in order to find the optimal weighting coefficients and the maximum bandwidth to obtain a radiation pattern compliant with some user-defined requirements. A numerical result is provided to preliminarily assess the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Scattering Control Using Advanced Characteristic Mode Theories
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In addition to the numerous applications of characteristic modes (CM) in radiation problems, scattering control for the antenna systems using CM is discussed in this work. It is implemented based on the CM analysis for fully dielectric coated conducting bodies and multilayered planar structures, respectively. The characteristic mode analysis provides clear information on how each mode contributes to the total scattering. Following such information, the systematical scattering control procedure can be thus realized by manipulating the modes that dominate the total scattering. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed scattering control procedure.

articleTitle: Terahertz Imaging of Transgenic Murine Breast Cancer Tumors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work applies terahertz imaging technology to examine the contrast between malignant and healthy tissue in excised breast cancer tumors from transgenic mice. Multifocal breast adenocarcinoma tumors are spontaneously generated in the mice and cut out for THz reflection imaging. Following imaging of the freshly excised tumors, samples are sent for pathology assessment at the Oklahoma Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory. The formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue prepared in histopathology lab is then imaged for additional correlation with pathology. The results show close correlation of THz imaging of fixed tissue to pathology and reasonable results with some challenges for the fresh tissue.

articleTitle: Considering a Compact SIW Filter for the Lighter Cube-Satellite Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper suggests a possible solution to make a relatively light cube satellite that has a reflectarray. The key to the lower weight is changing the bulky waveguide to a compact SIW bandpass filter as an important part of antenna feed assembly. The design shows the unwanted band of the feed horn is suppressed by the filter and it is connected to the reflectarray that contributes a useful increase to antenna gain nearly 22 dBi for 28 GHz as a 1 GHz-bandwidth Ka-band signal. Also, the suppression of the unwanted signals is shown to be larger than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Eletrically-Small Rectenna with Huygens Radiation Pattern for Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically-small Huygens rectenna is reported that operates at 915 MHz in the ISM band for wireless power transfer (WPT) applications. The rectenna consists of an electrically-small Huygens linearly-polarized (HLP) antenna and a rectifier circuit. The HLP antenna is developed by systematically combining two near-field parasitic resonant (NFPR) elements: an Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) and a capacitively loaded loop (CLL), together, with a small dipole antenna. The designed HLP antenna is electrically-small (ka <; 0.89), low profile (~0.0420), and produces cardioid-shaped directivity patterns with a very satisfactory peak realized gain value (4.4 dBi), wide half power beamwidth (~136°), and high front-to-back ratio (~26 dB). A rectifier circuit is designed and integrated with the HLP antenna to realize the rectenna. The rectifier consists of one HSMS286 Schottky diode and three lumped elements. The rectenna achieves a maximum RF to DC conversion efficiency: 86%, and a 2.4 V output DC voltage for a -5.0 dBm input power. Owing to its compact footprint and excellent radiation performance, this electrically-small rectenna is suitable for wirelessly powering sensors and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

articleTitle: Realization of Low-Cost Wide Scanning Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A growing need for phased arrays in commercial markets has pushed for lower cost and much smaller arrays. Of particular interest is the delivery of high-data/high-throughput systems, including 5G connectivity. In this paper, we illustrate a design method to enable 75% lower cost aperture for a phased array, while maintaining electrical performance requirements. We are proposing a unique approach with a monolithic dielectric substrate for the aperture. Two feeding techniques are discussed for manufacturing ease and for direct integration with beamforming circuitry. Measurements for a proof-of-concept aperture are provided.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz Integrated Slot Loop Antenna in 0.13-µm BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a rectangular slot loop antenna integrated in a standard 0.13-μm BiCMOS technology. By using the slot loop antenna, it can easily satisfy the metal density rules without dummy metal fill and can be integrated with other circuitry. The total area of the antenna including the ground plane is 0.883 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the loop antenna only occupies 0.24 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna resonates at 59.93 GHz and the bandwidth is 5.44 GHz from 57.82 GHz to 63.26 GHz. The simulated total gain is 2.69 dBi while the efficiency at 60GHz is 86%. The radiation efficiency is better than 74% over the band.

articleTitle: Design of High-Gain Antennas for 5G Systems Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes the use of the Theory of Characteristic Modes to aid the design of high-gain antennas for 5G applications. The single-layer lens consists of two shorted metallic rings illuminated by a square aperture which behaves as a novel Fabry-Perot resonator antenna. The proposed antenna has been optimized, obtaining a large S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>bandwidth, and a maximum directivity of 14.60 dBi in the range of 19.5 to 22 GHz.

articleTitle: Low-Loss Reflectarray Antenna Composed of Single-Layer Slots Backed by Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-loss reflectarray antenna is presented that has good polarization purity and is formed by a single layer of slots backed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities. The 30 dB reflectarray antenna has been designed and fabricated on a standard FR4 substrate. The FR4 substrate's high loss tangent demonstrates the low-loss nature of the design and the ability to implement the reflectarray in a low cost substrate.

articleTitle: Towards the Implementation of a Dual-Frequency Dual-Polarization Stacked Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-frequency, dual-polarization microstrip antenna array that operates at 1.25 GHz (L-band) and 9.65 GHz (X-band) is proposed for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications. The antenna uses a perforated L-band patch topology with X-band patches integrated into the same planar geometry. Stacked patches are used to meet bandwidth requirements. We present design aspects, simulation, and measurement results for the prototype design that was successfully fabricated.

articleTitle: Offset-fed Reflector Antenna with Lateral Feed Displacement for the MiRaTA Satellite
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An offset parabolic reflector antenna is fed by two compact corrugated feeds, laterally displaced from the reflector's focal point. Results show high gain, high beam efficiency, and low crosspolar pattern characteristics.

articleTitle: Directional Enhancement Analysis of All-Dielectric Optical Nanoantennas Based on Modified SIE
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent developments in optical nanoantennas made of high-permittivity low-loss dielectric particles have attracted much attention due to their promising characteristics. In this paper, based on our proposed modified surface integral equation, a full study of the dependence of the radiation pattern on the relative permittivity has been conducted for a single dielectric nanoparticle. Then the directional enhancement of radiation is explored from Yagi-Uda geometry systems made of nanoparticles with optimal permittivities for reflector and directors.

articleTitle: Non-contact RF Characterization of Reinforced Carbon Fiber Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An RF method for the characterization of carbon fibers reinforced with fiberglass is investigated. A novel measurement approach is proposed, where the unknown sample is accommodated on the bottom wall of a waveguide system. The proposed setup has the advantage that the contact between the sample and the waveguide system is not strictly required.

articleTitle: Coplanar Waveguide (CPW)-Fed Compact Dual Band Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed compact dual band antenna for wireless applications with dual polarization is presented. The above characteristics are achieved by modifying the ground planes with slots in ground plane and short between the signal strip and one of the lateral ground plane. The proposed antenna has been designed on a substrate with dielectric constant 4.4, thickness 1.6 mm and occupies an area of 18.2×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, The experimental analysis shows 2:1 VSWR bandwidth of up to 140 MHz and 130 MHz for 2.5 GHz and 5.2 GHz respectively. Antenna radiation characteristics, including reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, radiation efficiency and gain are also validated with numerical simulation and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Active frequency selective surface with two independent electromagnetic functions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper., we present a novel active frequency selective surface (AFSS) with two independent functions. The function of frequency tuning for TM polarization and the function of electromagnetic switching for TE polarization can be achieved by controlling the varactor diodes and PIN diodes loaded on the top- and bottom-layer., respectively. A parallel feeding pattern is employed to reduce the negative impact of the bias network., which also guarantees the working reliability of the structure under damages of active devices and decreases the bias voltage for the components., especially for varactor diodes. In addition., equivalent circuit models for the AFSS have been constructed to analyze the working principle of the structure and verify the simulation results from the HFSS software.

articleTitle: Breaking the Scaling Limit: A Parallel-in-Space-and-Time Method for Transient Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new time-domain method to harvest parallelism in both spatial and temporal dimensions for transient electromagnetic problems. The objective is obtained through the investigation of space-time domain decomposition formulation and rational approximation of time-domain Green's function. Comparing to traditional space-only parallel algorithms, the method provides high parallelism and significant speedup on high performance computers with a large number of processors. Moreover, it opens up new means of addressing the temporal multi-scale challenge in time-dependent multiphysics problems. Experiments validate the hypothesis and illustrate the great potential of the method.

articleTitle: Array Element Number Effects on System G/T for Single Plane Scanning Phased Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work investigates the effects of the number of array feed elements on the overall system G/Tsys for phased array feed systems, in the context of scanning along a single angular plane. It is shown that the negative impact of receiver noise caused by larger feeds on overall system sensitivity can outweigh the contribution to system gain in noisy systems. A numerical study is conducted which shows how a linear array can achieve superior performance to planar arrays with realistic receiver noise parameters.

articleTitle: Exploiting Polarization Wobble in Sinuous Antennas for the Detection of Linear Scatterers in Ground Penetrating Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
