Isolation greater than 18 dB between the antenna elements and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) less than 0.02 are obtained in the 5.21-5.5 GHz operating frequency band, whereas the edge-to-edge separation between the elements is 0.069λ0. The peak realized gain is 2.25 dBi at 5.35 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband 28 GHz ground reflected dipole antenna and array for 5G mobile handset
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 28 GHz printed dipole antenna suitable for 5G mobile handset is proposed by using multilayer PCB technology. L-shaped reflecting ground was constructed by plated through holes to realize directional radiation pattern. No clearance is needed for the integration of this element inside the 5G mobile phone. For validation, a 1×8 linear antenna array with feeding network composed of microstrip T -junction splitters was designed. Simulated impedance bandwidth of the single element for VSWR <; 2 is 12% across 27.26 GHz and 30.74 GHz. The simulated impedance bandwidth of the array is 17.87% across 26.2 GHz and 31.34 GHz, which is substantially wider than the FCC requirement and the realized gain achieved is 12 dBi.

articleTitle: Ducting Conditions During CASPER-West Field Campaign
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Coupled Air-Sea Processes and Electromagnetic ducting Research (CASPER) project involved two field campaigns. The most recent field study, CASPER-West, occurred during 27 September-26 October 2017 offshore of Pt. Mugu, California. The most significant ducting conditions observed during this field campaign included evaporation ducts and surface-based ducts. However, most of the evaporation ducts are also topped by elevated duct layers at several hundred meters above the surface. This paper provides an overview of the CASPER-West measurements and the observed ducting conditions from multiple platforms in CASPER-West.

articleTitle: SIW based Dirac Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dirac leaky-wave antennas (DLW As) provide interesting features such as radiating through broadside, beam scanning, and ease in fabrication, suggesting them as a favorable solution for radar and communication systems at upper microwave frequencies. In this paper, it is shown that a Dirac photonic crystal can be realized in Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology composed of air columns inside a host SIW waveguide, exhibiting a closed and linear dispersion around broadside. The structure is made to radiate acting as a SIW based DLWA. The directive beam scans a wide range of angles, with high efficiency, and is well matched around 28GHz, using a RO4003 substrate. The proposed SIW DLWA is well suited for emerging 5G and IoT applications that require reliable directive beaming and scanning.

articleTitle: Hybrid Physical Optics-MoM-Ray Tracing Method for the RCS Calculation of Electrically Large Objects Covered with Radar Absorbing Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: ART-PO algorithm for the estimation of the Radar Cross Section of electrically large targets coated with radar absorbing materials is presented. The proposed method relies on the calculation of the reflection coefficient of the multilayer structure (metallic surface covered with the absorbing material) with a Periodic Method of Moments. The reflection coefficient of the multilayer structure is also evaluated by using a simplified transmission line model for comparison. The proposed method is applied to a metallic corner reflector partially coated with a resistive Frequency Selective Surface.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Antenna-on-Package with Near-isotropic Radiation Pattern for IoT (WiFi Based) Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Futuristic IoT applications demand antenna designs to fulfill a number of challenging performance metrics. The antennas for such applications must be small to be easily integrate-able with miniaturized devices, have near-isotropic radiation pattern to be able to communicate in an orientation insensitive way, provide sufficient bandwidth (4% for 2.4 GHz WiFi)requisite of concerned communication protocol and be low cost enough to be implemented in billions of devices. Also, as these antennas integrate with the devices in very small spaces, so the effect of components (such as battery, chips etc.)also require consideration in design. This paper presents for the first time, a WiFi 2.4GHz near-isotropic T -shaped monopole antenna additively manufactured on the package. The antenna is designed whilst taking battery and WiFi chip effect into consideration. The maximum gain is 1.78 dBi with a gain deviation of 6.84 dB. The VSRW=2 bandwidth is achieved from 2.4 to 2.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of 28GHz band Massive MIMO Antenna RF Frontend Module for 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the 5th generation mobile communication system, large system capacity, low latency and massive connection will be provided for novel and various applications. In order to realize these features, we are developing high SHF band massive-MIMO system which can secure wide system bandwidth and high spectral efficiency. Especially, the combination of analog beamforming (APAA: Active Phased Array Antenna) and digital MIMO signal processing for the multi-beam multiplexing is one of the promising approaches for reducing the complexity and power consumption. In this paper, hybrid beamforming configuration for 28GHz band Massive-MIMO system and antenna RF frontend module are shown.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual Band Antenna Design for WiFi Applications Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimized design of a dual band antenna using the genetic algorithm (GA). The approach is based on dividing the surface of the patch antenna into pixels. For every iteration of the GA, a random number of pixels was cut, and the influence on the return loss was checked. The proposed antenna operates at 5.2 GHz and 5.8 GHz frequency bands (Wi-Fi bands) which makes it a good candidate for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Antenna for IoT Applications Operable even in Close Proximity to a Metal
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact antenna for IoT applications is presented, which can operate 2.4 GHz band. The proposed antenna is comprised of a Double Folded Loop (DFL) antenna. A DFL antenna has connection points at the quarter wavelength from the feed point. These connection points connect between the inner and outer loop antenna. To realize the compact antenna, we use a dielectric substrate and via holes to bend the DFL antenna. It has a total size of 37 × 20 × 1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, The radiation efficiency of a DFL antenna is higher than 6 dB as compared with the half wavelength dipole antenna in close proximity to a metal. The simulated and measured results of the proposed antenna prove that the realized gain is more than -1 dBi independent of the metal distance. Moreover, the proposed antenna can operate even if the metal is close to the front side or the back side.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of the Huygens' Box: Arbitrary Waveform Generation in a Metallic Cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Applying the electromagnetic equivalence principle, we synthesize the necessary electric and magnetic currents along a boundary enclosed by an active Huygens' metasurface, and thereby generate an arbitrary waveform within the area enclosed. We call our contraption the Huygens' box. In this paper, we report the generation of travelling waves inside the Huygens' box: we show calculations, full-wave simulation results and experimental measurements which demonstrate the successful generation of plane waves which travel at an arbitrary direction inside a metallic cavity. These plane waves form unconventional modes in that (i) their existence is forbidden in a typical cavity, and (ii) their linear combination can be used to construct an arbitrary waveform inside the cavity. The ability to construct an arbitrary waveform within an enclosed area by controlling its boundary is a novel concept, with dramatic applications in RF imaging, subwavelength focusing, scattering measurement and waveform control in general.

articleTitle: Improving Stability of Negative Capacitors for use in Active Metamaterials and Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The most challenging issue in implementation of negative capacitors and negative inductors (non-Foster elements) in active metamaterials and antennas is their proneness to instability. Recently, it was suggested that the `band-pass' design of a negative element may remove inherent unstable DC pole and, therefore, significantly improve stability properties. This paper reports analytical, numerical and experimental verification of aforementioned idea.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Capabilities of a Fully Dielectric Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the beam steering capabilities of a fully dielectric antenna array made out of Rexolite are investigated. The antenna array, which is designed for W-band frequencies, consists of four dielectric rod antennas fed by a special power divider, which is based on a multimode interference phenomenon. In order to achieve different beam steering angles, different lengths of the dielectric waveguides, feeding the rod antennas are used. Two different beam steering configurations are designed, providing a beam direction of 15° and 8° at 95 GHz. The measured antenna patterns are in good agreement to the simulations with side lobe levels between -6.2 to -10.5 dB.

articleTitle: Dual Band Circular MIMO Antenna System for 5G Wireless Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circular, dual band, connected printed inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is presented for 5G wireless devices. It consists of four antenna elements forming multiple input multiple-output (MIMO) configurations. The proposed configuration is designed to operate at 28 and 37 GHz frequency bands with 10 dB impedance matching bandwidths of 4.2 GHz and 3.2 GHz, respectively. The proposed design is modeled on RO-4350B with the height of 0.76 mm and dielectric constant of 3.48. It has a low profile with compact size, where the total diameter of the substrate is 22 mm.

articleTitle: Compact Tri-Band Microstrip Stub Filter Using Embedded MTM-EBGs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work introduces a methodology for designing multi-band devices using the recently introduced metamaterial-based EBG (MTM-EBG). Cascaded MTM-EBG sections are used to realize a tri-band quarter-wavelength microstrip stub with arbitrarily chosen operating frequencies, which is then employed as a compact tri-band-stop filter. Simulated and measured results are in very good agreement, and demonstrate rejection of over 20 dB at all band-stop frequencies. Enhanced functionality could be achieved in many other microstrip devices with this approach.

articleTitle: The Concept of an Airborne VLF Transmitter with Vertical Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the idea of a Very Low Frequency facility based on an airborne, mobile transmitter equipped with a symmetric-dipole antenna. The antenna, to be flown under an aerostat to high altitudes (between 12 and 60 km), is to present, in comparison to ground facilities, less financial issues and modified field intensity. The antenna concept was proven during three experiments flown in 2014 and 2015, with the longest aerial having the length of 200 m. The prototype transmitter is planned to be launched in 2019.

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna with a Meanderline Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a dual band circular polarized array antenna is presented. The proposed terminal consist of an array antenna in which the radiating elements operating around 20GHz and 30GHz are nested one into the other in order to form a dual band antenna. A meander-line polarizer is used to realize circular polarization. Using this system, a low level of Axial Ratio is obtained on both bands of interest.

articleTitle: Investigation of active load pulling effect on radiated power of the antenna elements in a finite phased array transmitter for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effect of variable scan impedance on the power amplifiers performance in a 7×7 phased array transmitter is investigated. It has been found that the output power of the amplifier degrade by up to 2.5dB due to active load pulling phenomena at large scan angles in phased array transmitters.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction between Two Circular Patches Using H -Shape DGS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Isolation enhancement between two closely spaced microstrip circular patches is presented in this paper. Two patches are placed on the top of RO3003 substrate with thickness of 1.52 mm and relative permittivity of 3. Defective Ground Structure (DGS)of H -shape slot was inserted on the ground plan underneath the two patches to achieve mutual coupling reduction of 18 dB with an isolation of 0.05 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> edge-to-edge at 4.8 GHz. The total gain of single antenna fed in the array is 5.5 dBi after the present of the DGS. The array is suitable for MIMO applications where high isolation is required.

articleTitle: A PSO Based on SA for the Sparse Linear Array Synthesis with Multiple Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a kind of particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm which is based on simulated annealing (SA) for the synthesis of sparse linear arrays. This algorithm is used to optimize the element positions to suppress the peak side lobe level (PSLL) of the array with many constraints. With this method the freedom increase amounts are used as optimization variables, which plus the minimum element spacing constraint is deemed as element spacing of the array. And the method has downsized the searching region by indirect expression of element spacing. The simulated optimization results demonstrate the better suppression effect of PSLL of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: 60-GHz Array Antenna for mm-Wave 5G Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 60-GHz array antenna for mm-wave 5G wearable applications is proposed. The antenna is composed of a patch antenna array with feed lines, parasitic elements, and a ground. The antenna has a fan-beam radiation pattern and simulated 3-dB and 10-dB beamwidths are 38.9° and 142.9°, respectively. To demonstrate the antenna performance in the practical wearable environment, the antenna characteristics were simulated on the 60 GHz head phantom.

articleTitle: Realization of Low-RCS Parabolic Reflector Antenna Using Curved 3-D Frequency-Selective Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high gain and low radar cross section (ReS) antenna based on a parabolic curved 3-dimensional bandstop frequency-selective structure (FSS) backed with an absorber. For the in-band frequencies, the proposed structure can achieve both reflecting and focusing for incident waves, resulting in a highly directive beam in the far field. For the out-of-band frequencies, the incident waves can be almost absorbed, leading to a low ReS. Simulated results show that the proposed low ReS parabolic reflector antenna has a gain of 24.4dB and aperture efficiency of 61.8%.

articleTitle: Folding, Tessellation, and Deployment of an Origami-Inspired Active-Material-Enabled Self-Folding Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effects of tessellation facet size and focal length to diameter ratio on the radiation pattern of an origami-inspired parabolic reflector antenna are presented. Tessellations are determined from the discretization of a parabolic dish into an approximate faceted structure. Varying levels of discretization are analyzed for their impact on antenna behavior. Structural and electromagnetic modeling and simulation tools are presented for their applications in origami-based designs. A structural prototype is presented to demonstrate manufacturing and folding abilities.

articleTitle: Multi-Parameter Modeling with ANN for Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel artificial neural network (ANN) model with three parallel and independent branches is proposed. A data-classification technique is introduced to classify antenna geometrical variables into the proper categories. Once the geometrical variables are input, the ANN model can simultaneously obtain the antenna VSWR, gain and radiation pattern from each independent branch. The validity and efficiency of this proposed model are confirmed with an optimization design of an ultrawide band (UWB) antenna examnle.

articleTitle: Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Modified Aperture Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we will introduce a novel leaky-wave antenna based on the half-mode substrate integrated waveguide. By modifying the aperture of the proposed antenna, the side-lobe level of the radiation pattern in the E-plane is reduced up to -19 dB. The operating band of the antenna is from 27 to 29 GHz that is one of the allocated 5G bands. The radiation efficiency is increased to 53 % by partial removal of the dielectric layer that leads to the reduction of the scanning speed. Hence, the frequency sensitivity of the radiation pattern decreases. The length, width, and height of the antenna are 70mm, 11.5mm, and 0.127mm, respectively. The small size of the antenna makes it a suitable candidate for circuit integration.

articleTitle: A High-gain Large-scanning 60 GHz Via-fed Patch Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a 7 × 7 via-fed patch phased array antenna for next-generation communication systems. The low-profile antenna array is fabricated on a printed circuited board (PCB) resulting in a low-cost approach. While the via-fed design enables testing of the antenna component in a laboratory environment, it also provides a path for direct integration on a transceiver chip. The designed finite array is well matched at 60 GHz with the bandwidth covering 57 GHz to 64 GHz. The maximum realized gain for the 7 × 7 array is 22.15 dBi with the gain reduction of ≤ 4 dB under the condition of the maximum scanning angle. Moreover, the scanning volume of the designed antenna is ±55° in H plane and ±53° in E plane without using any superstrate. As a single-layer patch array, the designed array satisfies high gain and large scanning volume in both E and H planes.

articleTitle: Design of a Reconfigurable Metasurface Antenna for Dynamic Near-Field Focusing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We show the design of a dynamically reconfigurable holographic metasurface antenna for near-field beam-focusing applications. A metasurface layer is used to modulate the guided-mode reference to an aperture field of interest producing the desired radiated wavefront. Exciting the dynamically reconfigurable metasurface layer with the guided-mode reference produces a reconfigurable focus in the near-field of the antenna aperture. The reconfigurable operation is achieved in an-all electronic manner, without the need for any mechanical moving apparatus or phase shifting circuits.

articleTitle: Magnetic Pendulum Arrays for ULF Transmission
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ultra Low Frequencies (ULF) have many applications including underwater and underground communications. However, it is a challenge to build portable and efficient antennas at these frequencies since the wavelengths are of the order of kilometers. In this paper we present an electromechanical system called magnetic pendulum array for efficient ULF transmission. We take advantage of the high quality factor and low dissipation in this mechanical system for efficient radiation at these frequencies. We present a proof of concept demonstration of the magnetic pendulum array at 154 Hz by measuring the generated time varying field.

articleTitle: Design of Thermoacoustic Monitoring System for Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes the design of a monitoring system based on thermoacoustic imaging for breast cancer hyperthermia. The monitoring technique is improved compared to previously reported works. Detailed design procedure of three parts of the system is introduced. Practical experimental system based on this work can be built to validate the thermo acoustic monitoring technique.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Toroidal Lens-Array Antennas Experimental Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High gain steerable antennas are the key element of the modern millimeter-wave communication systems: high gain required for overcoming large pathloss in this band, while steering is required for mobile access and reconfigurable backhauling links. In this paper we propose and evaluate the toroidal lens-array antenna (LAA) design, which provide high gain by focusing the beam in elevation plane, while beamsteering can be done in the azimuthal plane. Three LAA systems of different size demonstrated reliable multi-gigabit link at distances 100-300m. The further gain (and aperture) increase of LAAs limited mainly by the lens size and weight.

articleTitle: A Log-Scale Interpolation Method for Layered Medium Green's Functions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel spatial interpolation method using logarithmic scale is presented for rapidly computing layered medium Green's functions from their samples. Numerical examples demonstrate that the method is effective at subwavelength distances between source and observer points.

articleTitle: A Compressive Millimeter-Wave Interferometric Imager for Security Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a Passive Millimeter-Wave Imager based on a physical layer compressive sensing approach. Previous works demonstrated the effectiveness of an original interferometric imager architecture operating in the S-Band. The system associates a passive microwave coder to an interferometric array leading to a drastically reduced number of the receiver chains compared to conventional architectures. Considering the preliminary results, this concept is an attractive prospect for a simplified architecture of passive screeners dedicated to security applications.

articleTitle: Rough Surface Analysis for Short-Range Ultra-Broadband THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present an ultra-broadband terahertz (THz) channel model in typical office environment across a wide spectrum from 300 GHz (0.3 THz) to 310 GHz (0.31 THz). This ray-tracing model is used to study the indoor multipath propagation and its impact on terahertz channel by considering smooth and rough surfaces. These multipaths between Transmitter (TX) and Receiver (RX) are computed according to Kirchhoff Approximation, which accounts for specular losses by introducing Rayleigh roughness factor calculated from the surface height distribution. We employ the tangent plane approximation to scattering properties of common building materials in our propagation models which take Gaussian hypothesis on the height distributions into consideration.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Multi-Beam Antenna Array Based On A Compact Wideband 8×8 Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a multi-beam antenna array fed by a wideband 8×8 Butler matrix, based on low loss PCB based aperture hybrid couplers, is presented. The compact Butler matrix with the size of only 42 mm×61 mm is usable from 25 ... 30GHz. As a radiation element a 1 × 8 Vivaldi antenna array was implemented. Beam pattern measurements results are highly coincidental with the simulations showing 8 beams with different spatial angles in the range of ±61°, more than 8dB side lobe suppression and an average 13dBi radiation gain.

Author Keywords: beam steering. beam switching. passive beamforming network

articleTitle: A Flexible High Gain Wide-Band Antenna for Wireless and Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband, flexible printed antenna, fed via the Co-Planar Waveguide (CPW) geometry, with high gain is presented in this paper. The high gain was realized by using a reflector on the same level with the radiator and around it. The high gain performance of the antenna was observed throughout the whole wide spectrum of 1.53 GHz to 2.74 GHz, with a percentage bandwidth of approximately 57%. For flexibility, the antenna was printed on the flexible Rogers Ultralam 3850 substrate. With such characteristics, the antenna can be recognized in a number of wireless applications; such as, WLAN, WI-Max and RFID, as well as, wearable applications.

articleTitle: Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm Enhanced Characteristic Mode Solver for Large-Scale Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Typically, the characteristic mode (CM) analysis is based on the electric field integral equation (EFIE) and the characteristic modes are calculated numerically using the method of moments (MoM). The high computational complexity of conventional MoM approach hinders large-scale CM analysis in the practical engineering application. In this paper, the conventional multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is embedded into the implicitly restarted Arnoldi method (IRAM), an iterative eigenvalue solver to solve standard complex eigenvalue problem, which provides an appealing possibility for the CM analysis of electrically large complex objects.

articleTitle: Paired Metasurfaces for Amplitude and Phase Control of Wavefronts
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Gradient metasurfaces that are passive, low-loss, and reflectionless, are generally limited to tailoring the phase of an incident wavefront. Here, we show that by using two phase-discontinuous bianisotropic metasurfaces, the amplitude and phase distributions of an aperture field can be independently controlled. The paired metasurfaces are separated by a distance on the order of a wavelength. Due to the flexibility of the design procedure, an arbitrary incident field can be used as a source to produce a desired complex field pattern. This property makes the method relevant to a variety of applications, including producing custom (shaped and steered)far-field radiation patterns and 3-dimensional holograms.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Information- Theoretic Partitioning of Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Phased array technology has progressed towards fully digital architectures over recent years. This has significantly increased the agility of phased arrays, which in turn has created a need to determine how to optimally configure these arrays for dynamic missions. Previous work on assigning signals to antennas in phased arrays has focused on minimizing measures of the sidelobes in the beam patterns produced by thinning or interleaving the array using genetic algorithms (GAs). This work explores a novel application of the GA to optimize the resolution of a narrowband imaging array with respect to the transmit/receive antenna partition when considering self-interference in a simultaneous-transmit-and-receive operation. The results demonstrate the GA's effectiveness at finding optimal or near-optimal array partitions without exhaustively exploring the impractically large search space.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction in a T/R Array with T-Resonate Cavity EBG (TRC-EBG)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Mutual coupling between transmitter antenna and receiver antenna is an issue in radar and communication systems. A method to reduce the mutual coupling in a transmit-receive (T/R) array is proposed by using E-shaped EBG with T-resonant cavity (TRC-EBG). The T/R array includes a 2 × 2 patch transmitter array and a 2 × 2 patch receiver array. A designed periodic TRC-EBG structure was placed between the T/R antennas to reduce the mutual coupling at 6.04 GHz. The simulated results show that the mutual coupling between the T/R antennas was reduced from -35 dB to -66 dB, which is 31 dB isolation improvement compared with the case without the TRC-EBG structure. Moreover, adding the TRC-EBG structure does not affect the radiation patterns of the T/R array.

articleTitle: Geodesic Ray Tracing on Faceted Convex Surfaces for Co-Site Interference Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An algorithm is proposed to identify geodesic rays between two antennas on a faceted electrically large convex conducting platform. The algorithm is based on launching numerous geodesic ray strips from a transmitting antenna in all directions and tracing them until a receiving antenna is reached or a predefined number of facets are traced. It was used to identify two geodesic rays between antennas on a faceted circular cylinder and a faceted ogive. The algorithm is required to predict co-site interference between antennas on an electrically large platform.

articleTitle: FSS based Hexo-Fractal Dual Passband Filter for 28 and 380Hz 5G Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual passband frequency selective surface for future 5G communications. The FSS has two ring slots with hexagonal shape, one of which has been applied with a fractal generator. The FSS unit cell is 3.7×3.7mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The pass band ranges are 27.639 - 28.997 GHz and 37.442 - 41.452 GHz, covering both 28 and 38 GHz 5G bands. The FSS has been modelled using very thin 0.127 mm flexible Rogers substrate. The dual band response, low cost and unique design makes this FSS suitable for EMI shielding as well as radome applications for future 5G and millimeter-wave communication systems.

articleTitle: Compact Meander Magnetic Dipole Antenna for Wide-Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the meander structure magnetic dipole antenna for wide-angle scanning application has been proposed. The proposed antenna has wide half power beam width (HPBW) at the large ground. Moreover, the size of the antenna becomes compact by adjusting structure of the antenna, feeding point and distance between antennas. As a result at 5.8GHz, the proposed antenna has a compact size of 0.25λ × 0.21λ × 0.03 λ, and has wide HPBW about 159° in the E-plane with 6.31dB peak gain, 90° in the H-plane with 4.67 peak-gain.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Antenna Based on SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper., a compact dual-band antenna based on substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed. The antenna is comprised by three layers. The top layer is a SIW cavity-backed slot antenna while the middle layer is a quarter-mode SIW (QMSIW) antenna. A microstrip feeding line is configured on the bottom layer connecting to a vertically-oriented probe penetrating through the three layers to feed the antenna. Full-wave simulations show that two operational bands with unidirectional radiation along broadside direction are successfully achieved at 2.6 and 5.9 GHz. The fractional bandwidths are equal to 1.54% and 2.71 %., respectively. The overall size of the antenna is 33mm×43mm×5. 23mm, which is extremely compact. Moreover., parametric studies revealed that the two bands can be tuned separately by adjusting the appropriate design parameters.

articleTitle: DCGAN-based Scheme for Radar Spectrogram Augmentation in Human Activity classification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In recent years, data augmentation has drawn great attention due to its wide application on deep learning based natural image detection and recognition. To classify human activities in radar image with enhanced performance, a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DeGAN) based scheme is proposed to augment micro-Doppler radar spectrograms. The experiment results show that the proposed scheme achieves an average accuracy of 96.1%, better than 92.3% obtained by the conventional method without data augmentation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna over A Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed over a metasurface for achieving wideband circularly polarized radiation. The antenna consists of a rectangular DR, a metasurface, and a coaxial probe. The metasurface-based ground plane has improved the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth and gain of the rectangular DRA. This DRA over the metasurface, which consists of an array of “+” shaped unit cells, exhibits a wideband 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 19% (4.45 GHz-5.39 GHz) with less than 2-VSWR and a realized gain of more than 6.0 dBic across a frequency range from 4 GHz to 5. 25 GHz.

articleTitle: RF Energy Harvesting System Integrating a Passive UHF RFID Tag as a Charge Storage Indicator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting unit integrating a passive UHF RFID tag as a charge storage indicator. In this system, an energy harvesting unit converts the RF signal to DC and charges a storage capacitor. The RF switch, consists of a pin diode and UHF RFID tag, monitors the capacitor voltage and transmits signal to RFID reader if voltage at the capacitor terminals approaches 0.633 V. The proposed RF energy harvesting system operates at European UHF RFID spectrum from 865.7 MHz to 867.7 MHz. The experimental results indicate that 0.633 V at the capacitor terminals can be achieved with -5.5 dBm RF input power to the energy harvesting unit.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern of a Monopole Antenna on an Electrically Large Conducting Convex Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Asymptotic solutions based on the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) are well developed and efficient for radiation, mutual coupling and scattering problems associated with electrically large conducting convex surfaces. However, these solutions are available for infinitesimal sources. In this paper, it is proposed to predict the radiation pattern of a monopole antenna on a conducting convex surface using the extended UTD solution for radiation by sources on or close to the surface. The product of a sinusoidal current distribution and the UTD based electric field is integrated along a monopole antenna to compute its radiation pattern. The UTD result for the radiation pattern of a monopole antenna on a circular cylinder is validated compared to the result based on the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM).

articleTitle: Impact on Reflection Phase by Different Geometrical Structures of AMCs for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The reflection phase of various finite AMC structures is presented. The finite geometrical structure of an AMC has a direct impact on the reflection phase compared to that of an infinite unit cell. The reflection phase of a unit cell is used as a benchmark when compared to finite AMC structures using the same unit cell. A correlation is established between the geometry and different reflection phases compared to the original unit cell. Frequency and phase shift between each finite structure and the original infinite unit cell are described.

articleTitle: PolyStrata® X/Ku/K/Ka-band, Dual-Polarized, Tightly Coupled Dipole Scannable Focal Plane Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband, dual-polarized array that supports both electronic scanning and fixed-beam applications in a modular, scalable architecture is presented. A tightly-coupled dipole array is designed to cover 9.5-37 GHz. Six different instrument bands, both radiometry and synthetic aperture radar (SAR), share the common aperture with co-located phase centers. Element-level diplexing is demonstrated to enable precise aperture control across all bands. Amplitude tapering is implemented with unequal power combiners to control sidelobe levels and help equalize beamwidth across frequency for feeding a reflector. Measured realized gain patterns are provided vs array code predictions and ideal directivity calculations. Better than 10 dB return loss is measured for all six instrument bands. Digital scanning of measured sub-array patterns to 30 degrees is demonstrated in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Integrating the Small Wind Turbine with its Power Generator and the Cylindrical Antenna Array Generating Multibeam Sectorial Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the paper we present results of our work aiming at assembling the cylindrical antenna array with the wind turbine. The wind turbine drives integrated electrical power generator and supply several radio modems. The assembled system mitigates snow and ice adverse effect on antenna.

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna with Small Frequency Ratio
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the development and the experimental characterization of a circular polarized printed antenna for dual operation at 2.32 GHz and 2.58 GHz. The design is based on the gap-coupling mechanism applied to a disc patch antenna. The degeneration principle is the driver of the CP for the first mode, while the gap coupling strategy is used to create a pair of modes, which operate in the opposite direction with respect to first one.

articleTitle: On-Chip Antenna Test Structure Design with Reduced Sensitivity to Probe Pad Effects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper has shown that, by simply inserting a matching line, the probe pad effects on antenna impedance matching and frequency shift can be reduced. Simulation and measurement results confirm the method.

articleTitle: UWB Antenna for Medical Image
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Medical imaging based on different technologies is an essential tool in clinical practice, either to provide an accurate initial diagnosis or to monitoring diseases evolution. Microwave imaging technique has recently emerged as complementary method for breast imaging with high potential to become quite important for biomedical applications. This paper contributes to the technological development of this new technique, with the development of a broadband antenna (3 to 10 GHz) that operate in the range of the microwaves, which can be used for the detection of possible tumors, in particular, breast cancer. Also, some preliminary experience in a test bed is considered in order to detect possible differences between three samples which represent different situations: healthy breast, benign and malignant tumor breast.

articleTitle: Wideband Transceiver Front-end Integrated with Vivaldi Array Antenna for 5G Millimeter-wave Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a Q-band transceiver (T/R) front-end for 5G millimeter-wave (MMW) communication is presented in this paper. The transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) are designed using highly integrated chips and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The wideband SIW vivaldi array antenna is integrated with the millimeter-wave circuits directly by utilizing the metal block as a transition. A 64QAM signal with the date rate of 400 Ms/s are applied to evaluate the system performance. The signal-to-noise (SNR) and the error vector magnitude (EVM) of the demodulated signal is measured at 28.4 dB and 2.4 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Element Placement on Chassis Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the effect of an actual antenna element location on the chassis modes is investigated. The chassis modes are significantly affected by the presence of the antenna and the amount of effect depends on the structure as well as the location of the antenna on the chassis. The presence of the antenna also creates a new mode that only depends on the geometry of the antenna and is not affected by the location of the antenna on the chassis. In the presence of the antenna, the current maxima of all the modes shift towards the antenna element, that is why pure excitation of single characteristic mode is not possible.

articleTitle: Error Control of MLFMA within a Multiple- Precision Arithmetic Framework
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a new error control scheme that provides the truncation numbers as well as the required digits of machine precision for the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). The proposed method is valid for all frequencies, whereas the previous studies on error control are valid only for high-frequency problems. When combined with a multiple-precision arithmetic framework, the proposed method can be used to solve low-frequency problems that would otherwise experience overflow issues. Numerical results in the form of optimal truncation numbers and machine precisions for a variety of box sizes and desired relative error thresholds are presented and compared with the results available in the literature.

articleTitle: A Flexible Frequency Selective Surface for Beam-switching applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new Passive Frequency Selective Surface (PFSS) based on periodic unit cell structure is proposed. The low-profile FSS periodic structure with dimension of the unit cell of 0.2λ *0.2λ offers a good transmission coefficient in the frequency range of 3 and 6 GHz. The FSS presents a nearly linear phase variation with the operation frequencies that can be used as a planar form in a cylindrical reconfigurable antenna. The proposed structure could be used for enhancing its gain, beam-switching radiation pattern and shielding nearby conductive surfaces. The FSS design and simulated results of the unit cell are discussed and presented.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Magneto-dielectric Substrate for RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A magneto-dielectric substrate [MDS] technique is introduced in this paper for miniaturizing microstrip patch antenna. The microstrip patch antenna is placed on MDS layer, the MDS layer is used to increase the magnetic permeability so the size of the patch is decreased. The proposed antenna is designed to operate at UHF RFID band. An RFID chip is a matched with the antenna using matched loop. By using MDS, the size of the antenna is reduced the size about 77 % compared to conventional antenna. The proposed antenna is suitable for passive RFID tag.

articleTitle: Non-Uniformly Fed Broadband CTS Array for Side Lobe Level Reduction is E-plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose here a new architecture of parallel-fed Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) antenna array based on nonuniform power dividers. The antenna comprises 16 slots fed in parallel by a parallel plate waveguide (PPW) corporate feeding network and a pillbox PPW coupler. For the first time, this network divides non-uniformly the power among the slots to achieve reduced side lobe levels (SLL) in E-plane. This is made possible by the development of a novel asymmetrical power divider in PPW technology. A CTS array has been designed in E-band (71-86 GHz) and validated by full-wave simulations over the entire bandwidth, with SLL below -28.5dB both in E- and H-planes. The gain remains stable between 71 and 86 GHz and in the range of 25 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of Wearable Dual-antenna System Based on Theory of Characteristic Mode
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a flexible MIMO antenna system with polarization and pattern diversities has been proposed for wearable applications. The antenna has only one conducting layer and is easy to integrate in the clothing. Characteristic mode theory was utilized to design and analyze the performance of the antennas before full wave simulations. The compact MIMO antenna with the size of 38.1 mm × 38.1 mm was fabricated on the felt with the thickness of 2 mm. It operates over a wide band and has been verified to be robust when in close proximity to the human body and not sensitive to the bending and body movement. Fairly good antenna gains of 1.6 dB and 1.2 dB and diversity capability ensure reliable wearable communication links between the proposed antenna system and other devices. The proposed antenna is competitive for wearable applications, due to its compact size, single layer structure, easy integration, robustness, and reasonable on-body antenna gain.

articleTitle: Thinned Array Design via Autocorrelation Matching Strategy
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel methodology for designing thinned arrays with controlled pattern features is presented. The optimization of the binary weighting coefficients of the array elements is carried out through a multi-step procedure. In a first stage, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to determine the binary sequence whose autocorrelation function is closest to a target one. Then, the thinned array is constructed from one of its cyclic sequences which optimizes a given figure of merit. A preliminary numerical example is illustrated in order to show the potentialities of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Near-shore Electromagnetic Propagation to the Spatial Variability of Evaporative Duct Properties
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The vertical thermodynamic structure of the marine boundary layer exhibits significant spatial variability in the near-shore/littoral regions or in the vicinity of ocean sea surface temperature fronts due to a variety of coupled mesoscale atmospheric and oceanographic processes. As a result, the ubiquitous and tactically-relevant evaporative duct (ED) also exhibits significant spatial variability correspondingly [1]. This paper explores this variability in near-shore ED properties through aircraft and buoy data collected as part of the Coupled Air-Sea Processes and EM ducting Research (CASPER) project's East and West field campaigns. We further explore impact of such spatial variability on electromagnetic wave (EM) propagation. The results should provide some guidance to retrieval of evaporation duct properties using propagation loss measurements. The sensitivity of propagation loss to the spatial resolutions of ED characteristics such as evaporative duct height (EDH) and evaporative duct strength (EDS) will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Luneburg Lens from Hyperuniform Disordered Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Luneburg lens made of hyperuniform disordered composite materials is presented in this paper, it is proven to be able to reduce back scattering in comparison with its counterpart design based on metamaterials due to the Bragg diffraction from periodic structures. The Maxwell-Garnett effective medium theory is used to achieve material parameters required by the lens design. Numerical results show that the Luneburg lens made of dielectric scatters in a triangular lattice demonstrates distinctive reflection at one specific angle. We however observe that a lens structure made of dielectric scatters with a hyperuniform disordered distribution presents diffused reflection, which in practice can be applied to dielectric lens antenna designs with reduced Radar Cross Section (RCS). Both designs are performed with measurement data to be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Physical Optics Simulation of a THz Standoff Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a Physical Optics-based simulation code for radar imaging systems at THz frequencies is presented. The simulator predicts the electromagnetic behavior of the antenna system used to scan a model of a target placed on the imaging area and also the electric field scattered by the target and collected at the system receiver. The code allows to generate synthetic data useful to help in the design and optimization of novel radar architectures for imaging at security and other applications. Representative simulation results showing the simulator behavior are presented.

articleTitle: Recent Studies on 4D Antenna Arrays and Their Applications to Wireless Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a serious of novel studies on four-dimension (4D) antenna arrays are reviewed and their relevant applications to wireless electronic systems are proposed. Theoretical analysis of 4D retro-directive arrays, generation of orbital angular momentum modes, large-scale 4D heterogeneous arrays and wideband power pattern based on 4D antenna arrays are presented. Then their applications to physical layer secure communication, efficient optimization algorithm for radiation patterns and wideband transmit beamforming are discussed. These studies demonstrate that 4D antenna array is a preferred choice for the next generation wireless electronic systems.

articleTitle: Integrated GPS Antenna with Circular Polarization for Metal-Rimmed Smartwatch Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An integrated GPS antenna with circular polarization (CP)is proposed for smartwatches with an unbroken metal rim. By utilizing a small feeding structure in the ground plane, two dominant characteristic modes of the metal rim along the x-axis and y-axis are simultaneously excited for radiation. For CP operation, the time-phase difference between the two modes can be provided by adjusting their resonant frequencies to be inductive and capacitive, which can be further tuned by changing the values of loaded capacitors between the metal rim and ground plane. The proposed technique can generate a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 10 MHz with left-hand circular polarization (RHCP)and right-hand circular polarization (LHCP)at the front side and back side, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Passive RFID Temperature Sensor Using Liquid Crystal Elastomers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A passive RFID temperature sensor is presented. This sensor design utilizes a patch antenna integrated with a customized slot. Using a novel Liquid Crystal Elastomer (LCE) switch, the slot is shorted when the temperature reaches a specified threshold. When the temperature decreases below this threshold, the switch retracts to the original position. As a result, the antenna operates at one of two states corresponding to a controlled shift in frequency within the RFID band. Additionally, a single impedance matching network is designed to accommodate a favorable match between the two antenna states and the RFID IC.

articleTitle: Full-Diversity OAM Multiplexing by Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a method to use a single planar antenna array with a conserved number of elements to generate multiple LG modes simultaneously, so that OAM-based spatial multiplexing can be realized. The method considers generating modes of various l and p values to fully take advantage of the spatial diversity offered by both the azimuthal domain and the radial domain. At the same time of ensuring the multiplexed signal can be resolved over a finite receive aperture, the sidelobe radiation beyond the aperture is controlled to reduce the possible interference to other users in the surrounding environment.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Broadband Multi-Beam End-Fire Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm Wave) broadband multibeam end-fire dual circularly polarized (CP) antenna array using dielectric loaded stepped slot elements is proposed. The proposed antenna element exhibits excellent performance, including broad bandwidth, wide beamwidth, and compact element size. The feeding network using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is designed for multi-beam array applications. A broadband 4×4 SIW Butler matrix, interconnections, and transitions are designed and applied in the array prototype. The fabricated array prototype achieves the impedance bandwidth of 29.3% and the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 22.5%. The proposed multi-beam end-fire dual-CP antenna array would be an attractive candidate for 5G mm Wave applications.

articleTitle: Improved Measured Source Antenna Representation in Satellite Antenna Placement Analysis with Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Combination of measurements and simulations is becoming a popular and effective solution for antenna placement analysis. This is in fact an efficient and reliable implementation of a domain decomposition techniques where the main source is first measured and described in terms of the so-called Huygens box and then is imported in the Computational ElectroMagnetic (CEM) software performing the simulation of the complex environment. A crucial point for the reliability of the analysis is the correct measurement of the source antenna, which should satisfy proper conditions. For example, in case of flush mounted antenna, the correct local boundary conditions should be enforced by measuring the antenna with a minimum representative ground plane. A validation activity for space antenna testing has been previously presented [1] showing good results, but not as good as expected. This was due to the lack of measurement of the source antenna performed not in optimal conditions. In this paper, the same test case scenario will be taken into account considering another antenna this time measured under proper conditions, namely using a metallic ground plane. The new analysis will allow obtaining insights on the achievable accuracy for the considered scenario.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna with Sector Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, we have shown that by properly arranging two concentric patch antennas excited with different radiating modes, it is possible to generate an electromagnetic field with an anomalous polarization state, resembling the structure of a Mobius strip. In this contribution, we expand this finding by considering a single radiating structure consisting of an inner circular patch excited at its fundamental mode and an outer circular ring excited with a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub> mode, both operating in circular polarization. Through an analysis based on the phase singularities of composite vortices, we show the possibilities for pattern shaping offered by this configuration. In particular, we demonstrate that the radiation pattern can be properly tailored to emulate that of a bulkier structure, i.e. a dipole placed at a quarter of wavelength from a reflector, thus, obtaining, a sector radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Iterative PO to the Characterization of EMI/EMC Ground Test Facility for Electric Propulsion Thrusters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper an electromagnetic characterization of an EMI/EMC test facility for electric propulsion thrusters is presented. To this end, an analysis of the electromagnetic field radiated outside a hollow dielectric cylinder by an internal elementary source has been conducted, by means of a high-frequency technique, stemming from an iterative implementation of Physical Optics. The numerical implementation shows very good agreement between the simplified high frequency solution and the results obtained by CST simulation.

articleTitle: Well-Conditioned FEM-BEM-DDM for Electromagnetic Scattering by Composite Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The domain decomposition method(DDM) based on the hybrid finite element-boundary element (BEM) is presented for simulating electromagnetic scattering problems in this paper. In this method, the first order Robin-type transmission condition (RTC) is used to connect the interfaces of FEM and BEM regions and the second order transmission condition (SOTC) is used to joint the interfaces in interior FEM regions. The ingredients of this paper are as follows. First, the combined field integral equation (CFIE) is applied into FEM-BEM-DDM. Second, the conditioning of the discretized matrix equation can be essentially improved and rapidly converging iterative solutions can be obtained by properly choosing the coupling coefficients of the equations.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Output-Phase Error Ridge-Gap Coupler for Antenna Arrays Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave)quadrature low output-phase error coupler using ridge-gap waveguide (RGW)is designed and developed. The proposed coupler is designed using large coupling-aperture. The phase variation over the apertures can compensate for the progressive phase of the coupler and yield a very low output-phase difference. The proposed coupler is suitable for using in mm-wave beamforming networks such as Butler matrix beamformer. In this paper, a multi-coupling aperture technique is discussed for designing the coupler. The coupler is simulated using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: BEM Based Adaptive Cross Approximation Algorithm for Solving Low Frequency Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper shows an accelerated solution for low frequency eddy current nondestructive evaluation (NDE) problems with the boundary element method (BEM) by using adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm. ACA algorithm is used to deal with the far-block interactions. Numerical results show the robust and efficiency of our method for low frequency NDE problems.

articleTitle: A Parasitic Decoupling Technique for Two Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient parasitic decoupling structure (PDS) for two closely coupled antennas is presented in this paper. The required parameters of the PDS can be accurately determined for perfect decoupling according to the derived parasitic decoupling theory. A prototype of two monopole antennas is realized on a Rogers PCB for demonstration purpose. The simulated and measured results show that good impedance matching and high port isolation are achieved simultaneously.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of K-band E-Shaped Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Elements for SATCOM Receive Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that a single and a rotated dual E-shaped microstrip patch antenna elements with asymmetric slots can produce a circularly polarized (CP) radiation pattern at two desired frequencies at K-band. The rotated dual E-shaped patch element is ideally suited for constructing a K-band CP receive array antenna for communications satellite that operates at dual frequencies.

articleTitle: Multi-Port Dual Polarized Integrated Patch Antenna for RF Detection at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-port dual-polarized patch antenna is designed and fabricated to detect signals at 5.8GHz. Two inset feeds are used in conjunction with a power combiner to ensure receiving both vertical and horizontal polarizations. The two other sides of the patch are utilized for direct connection to integrated circuit devices with complex input impedance by incorporating inductively coupled feeds. The test chips placed at these ports are RF energy harvesting diodes to showcase an efficient multiport integrated antenna design with minimal impact on the return loss of power combining feed. Good agreement between simulated and measured results is achieved.

articleTitle: The Lossless, Resonant, Minimum Scattering Approximation for Fast Phased Array Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The classical framework for phased array beamforming, analysis, and design is based on the array factor approximation. As research in antenna arrays has progressed, attention has turned to sophisticated, high sensitivity applications that require more accurate models. Mutual coupling, edge effects, surface waves, and other non-ideal effects can be accounted for full wave numerical methods, but the run time for the model becomes large, and design optimization can be unduly time consuming. A middle ground between the array factor and full wave numerical models is provided by the lossless, resonant, minimum scattering (LRMSA)approximation. Embedded element radiation patterns with open circuit loads on the element ports are approximated using an analytically known or modeled isolated element pattern, and mutual coupling is included to first order using the element pattern overlap matrix and relationships from the network theory of antenna arrays. We give an overview of the LRMSA method for fast phased array modeling and design in this paper, and the presentation will include numerical comparisons and design examples for a variety of phased array application areas.

articleTitle: Reflection Analysis of Spherical FDTD Absorbing Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A system of equations is derived for the purpose of predicting numerical performance of absorbing boundary conditions for the finite-difference time-domain method in spherical coordinates. Multi-layer reflection analysis, coupled with spherical wave functions, are used to construct this system of equations. Subsequent analysis detail the strong performance dependence on ABC's radial distance and rotational mode orders. Obtained results can serve to design and/or develop efficient spherical FDTD absorbing boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Singular Integration in BEM by Interpolation: The EFIE Case
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An approach of populating all weakly singular and near weakly singular integrals enchanted in Electrical Field Integral Equation (EFIE) Boundary Element Methods (BEM) using universal look-up-tables and multi-dimensional interpolation is outlined. The method is compared to a state-of-the-art singularity subtraction method for the lowest order Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions in various PEC triangular meshes. For common triangle, weakly singular, interactions the proposed approach out-performs singularity subtraction integration by 3 - 4 decimal digits, while offering up to 100 × speed-ups. Early implementations for common edge, near weakly singular, interactions show 40 × speed-ups but at a somewhat lower, yet acceptable, accuracy.

articleTitle: Evaluating Effect of Calibration Factor for Lead Computational Model to Assess MRI RF-Induced Heating
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this case study the calibration factor of the lead electromagnetic model (LEM) was evaluated for different helix and straight lead geometries and insulator electrical properties at 128 MHz. Our results indicate that the LEM is suitable to predict the RF-induced power deposition at the lead tip if the calibration factor is measured, or simulated, for exactly the given lead, without making any simplification.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Printed Gap Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the idea of designing a 1D periodic leaky wave antenna (LWA) using printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology. A new H-polarized substrate integrated gap waveguide leaky wave antenna (SIGW-LWA) is designed that has good scanning from backward to near broadside. The presented antenna has wide impedance bandwidth and narrow fan beam that scans with frequency. The beam scanning range of the antenna is from -43° to -13°. The realized peak gain of the antenna is 17.67 dBi with less than 1.3 dBi variation throughout the frequency range from 55-65 GHz. Experimental measurements show good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Parallel Non-Uniform MLFMA for Multiscale Electromagnetic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a parallel, non-uniform wideband MLFMA which enables simulation of electrically-large objects with sub-wavelength features or regions of dense discretization. We demonstrate both excellent control over accuracy and parallel performance.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Small-Footprint Hybrid Ring-Patch Stacked Antenna for Pico-Satellites
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a small-footprint wideband, wide beamwidth circularly polarized (CP) hybrid stacked patch-ring microstrip antenna for cubesat applications. The antenna ground plane size is chosen such that it can be accommodated on the top plate of a cubesat for communicating with high-orbital satellite networks. Hybrid perturbations are applied on patch and ring for obtaining wide axial ratio beamwidth. The axial ratio bandwidth achieved is significantly larger compared to typical CP patch antennas. This design uses only one probe-feed which significantly reduces the system complexity in cubesat applications. A simulated impedance bandwidth (for VSWR ~ 2) of 8%, AR ~ 3 dB bandwidth of 6% and beamwidths in the order of 96 degrees are achieved from this antenna.

articleTitle: A Deeply Implantable Conformal Antenna for Leadless Pacing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Finite battery life and complications caused by leads of conventional pacemakers are key issues in pacemaker technology. In this paper, we propose a deeply implantable antenna which can be conformed on a commercially available leadless pacemaker and has the potential capability of receiving and harvesting radio frequency (RF) energy to achieve cardiac pacing. More specifically, a deeply implantable conformal antenna at 2.45 GHz has been designed in ANSYS HFSS and then manufactured and integrated with a 3D printed mock pacemaker. The antenna performance was measured in tissue simulating liquid (TSL) and good agreement was achieved with the simulation results. Moreover, it was concluded that the proposed conformal antenna design on a commercially available pacemaker has the potential to be integrated with a rectifier for leadless pacing.

articleTitle: Triple-layer Complementary FSS for the Mutual Coupling Reduction of Relay Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel triple-layer complementary frequency selective surface (FSS) for the mutual coupling reduction of relay antenna arrays is proposed in this paper. The relay antenna arrays include a 2 × 4 antenna array (the backhaul antenna) and a 1 × 2 antenna array (the access antenna). Four sets of triple-layer complementary frequency selective surface and the metal reflector form a cavity for the backhaul antenna. Simulated results show that the port isolation with the same polarization and the cross polarization can be improved at most 2.7 dB and 7.2dB over the frequency band of 2.5—2.7 GHz, respectively. More importantly, the backhaul antenna still keeps good performance with VSWR<1.5 and stable radiation pattern, while the FSS-based cavity is loaded.

articleTitle: Inverted-F Antenna Radiation Efficiency Enhancement based on a Slotted Ground
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact and highly-efficient inverted-F antenna (IFA) suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. A slotted ground is applied to significantly improve the antenna radiation efficiency. Compared to a conventional IFA on a solid ground plane, the proposed structure enhances radiation efficiency approximately 100%, from 14% to 27%, at 750 MHz. Simulated and measured results are in an excellent agreement, fully validating the IFA response.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable UWB Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a reconfigurable ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna. The presented antenna covers 440 MHz to 5 GHz (11: 1) frequency range while keeping its size compact for MIMO applications. The ultrawideband functionality is obtained by integrating a UWB monopole antenna together with a tunable matching network via two different signal paths from a single feed point. The tunable section covers 440 MHz to 700 MHz frequency range while the UWB antenna operates over the rest of the band. Two identical UWB antennas are orthogonally placed on the same substrate to achieve polarization diversity and construct MIMO configuration. Reflection coefficient for entire operation region and MIMO diversity parameters are presented.

articleTitle: A Reflective Metasurface for Generating Orbital Angular Momentum Vortex Wave Across Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reflective metasurface is designed to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM)vortex wave across wide bandwidth at X band. The double square rings element which offers a slow slope of the reflected wave phase as approximately a linear function of the rings' length to achieve a wider operational bandwidth is utilized as reflective units to generate OAM vortex wave across a broad bandwidth of 9-12GHz. The prototype of this metasurface is simulated, manufactured and measured. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of this design methodology.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel translator calculation method for the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is proposed based on a machine learning approach. The generalized regression neural networks are introduced to fit the translation function of MLFMA during the procedure of eletromagnetic scattering analysis. Compared to the traditional method, the new method inherits advantages of the generalized regression neural networks (GRNN) and can approximate the translator with high accuracy simultaneously. As an example, a two-level 2D MLFMA for a perfect electrically conductor (PEC) is finally implemented and the translators are reconstructed by using the proposed model. The numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Holographic Artificial Impedance Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses the design of polarization reconfigurable holographic artificial impedance surfaces (HAISs). the proposed metasurface is fed by two monopoles and it radiates a pencil beam with horizontal, vertical or circular polarization depending on the monopole or the combination of monopoles that feeds the metasurface. The HAIS is operated at a non-phase crossover frequency.

articleTitle: Calculation of Mutual Coupling between Two Antennas of Diverse Displacements and Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically large antenna system is vulnerable to the interference with other communication links. An accurate and fast prediction of antenna coupling can reduce an adverse effect of the interference in preliminary stage of antenna system design.
