In this paper, the integral form of coupling formula is employed in examining the mutual coupling between two antennas placed in the near-field and far-field region. It demonstrates the feasibility of applying the coupling program to diverse cases of mutual coupling.

articleTitle: UWB Off-Body Channel Characterization in a Mine Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents Off-Body channel characterization measurement results for Ultra- Wide-Band Communications in an underground gold mine. Frequency measurements from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz are described in terms of the channel parameters, impulse response and channel capacity. Results show that channel parameters degrade at non-line of-sight compared to line-of-sight configurations. The time dispersion, path loss and capacity results demonstrate that the UWB channel is better suited for the in-mine communications than the 2.4 GHz band at line of sight and non-line-of-sight scenarios.

articleTitle: Sandwiched PRS Fabry-Perot Structure for Achieving Compactness and Improved Aperture Efficieny
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a unique approach to achieve compactness and improved aperture efficiency through sandwiched partially reflecting surface (SPRS) in the Fabry-Perot antenna. The proposed antenna features both low profile and high aperture efficiency. A prototype antenna has been designed and validated numerically, which can achieve an aperture efficiency of 74.94% and a gain of 12.35 dBi at 25.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Beam Scanning Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurface (MTS)antennas have been shown to be a versatile class of planar antenna. In particular, they allow for beam shaping and pattern control through the modulation of the boundary conditions, while keeping unchanged the overall antenna structure. This feature makes them suitable for dynamic reconfiguration. In this contribution, we show how an electronic beam scanning can be achieved by controlling either the average equivalent impedance or the modulation period of the modulated MTS.

articleTitle: Improved Probes for Fully-Passive Wireless Recording of Neural Activation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To address the need for continuous and localized brain electrical activity recordings, implantable neurosensing systems are often used. However, current systems involve highly-invasive procedures that can interrupt day-to-day activities. This paper presents an approach for developing a device that can be used to obtain neural data during normal activity and without hindering the quality of life. In this paper, for the first time, we present the design and application of improved neural probes for a fully-passive wireless brain implant. The integration of these neural probes to the neurosensing system results in enhanced impedance matching capable of sensing neural signals as low as 15 μVpp and improve the RF sensitivity to ~ -135 dBm. As such, all neural activity can be recorded.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Patch Antenna with Liquid Metal Tuning Slots and 3D Printed Microfiuidics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the development of a novel class of reconfigurable microstrip antennas: patch antenna with liquid metal tuning slots. By manipulating liquid metal in 3D printed microfluidics bounded on top of a slotted patch antenna, various attractive reconfigurable characteristics can be achieved with simple patch topologies. Two representative designs are presented to demonstrate the capabilities of patch antenna with liquid metal tuning slots: a frequency reconfigurable patch antenna with frequency tuning bandwidth of 70% and instantaneous bandwidth of 2 %; and a polarization reconfigurable patch antenna with right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), left-hand circular polarization (LHCP), and linear polarization (LP) with arbitrary orientation in x-y plane. The process for prototyping patch antenna with liquid metal tuning slots is also presented, which successfully minimized the skin residues. Measurement has been performed with good agreement to the simulations. We believe that this design and prototype strategy can be applied to other potential topologies with various reconfigurable functionalities.

articleTitle: Effect of introduction of hypotheses in Antenna Optimization: Thinned array test case
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the effect of the introduction of some hypotheses in the optimization of a thinned array will be analysed. The results are analysed using three different evolutionary optimization algorithms: the Stud-Genetic Algorithm, a very effective implementation of Genetic Algorithm, the binary Particle Swarm Optimization and the binary Social Network Optimization.

articleTitle: Low-Observable Reflectors Using Perfect Pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new technique for suppressing specular reflection using binary reflective surfaces (such as those easily fabricated on a printed circuit board)that maximally suppress mean currents on the reflector using the theory of perfect pulses. We simulate multiple versions (or orders)of these structures to characterize the nulling depth and manufacturing tolerance of the designs. In addition, we run another set of simulations to characterize the specular reflection as a function of the direction of incidence. The simulation reveals that the specular reflection from the proposed structures is at least 9.3 dB less than that from a flat metal plate of the same dimensions.

articleTitle: Antenna-based carpet device for extremely large obstacles: experimental verification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we report our recent experimental results on a fully passive antennas-based carpet device inspired by Van Atta array configuration for retroreflectors. We have realized an electrically large triangular bump over a ground plane, whose sides are covered by two arrays of conventional patch antennas. The antennas are connected to each other following a VanAtta-inspired connection, which ensures the restoration of the reflection angle as if the bump were not present, mimicking the ground reflection. The performances have been experimentally evaluated, showing the ability of the proposed setup to mimic the reflection from a ground plane for different illumination angles.

articleTitle: Application of Social Network Optimization to shaped beam Transmitarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In recent years, Transmitarray Antennas (TA) have became interesting alternatives to other type of high-gain antennas, especially for their flexibility, that make possible to obtain radiation patterns with different features just changing the TA unit cell distribution. In this view, Evolutionary Optimization Algorithms can be applied successfully to the design of configurations able to radiate a shaped beam. Because of the high computational cost required by such a process, the use of an efficient optimization algorithm is really important. In this paper, a population-based evolutionary algorithm named Social Network Optimization, whose efficiency has already been proved in several cases, has been applied to the optimized design of a shaped-beam Transmitarray.

articleTitle: Impact of Tropospheric Scintillation on Earth-Space Link in West Africa
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Tropospheric scintillation occur as a result of signal fluctuations in satellite communication systems. Great attention has been giving to scintillation today because of increase in demand of bandwidth at frequency above 10 GHz. However, in West Africa countries few work have been reported in this area. Data from ITU-RP study group 3 data bank was used as input data for the analysis of tropospheric scintillation for seventeen (17) West Africa locations. Monthly and yearly mean of temperature, pressure and relative humidity were used as input parameters. The results revealed that lowest scintillation values were observed for Carpe Verde at 0.118 dB, followed closely by Niger, Mauritania, Senegal and Mali with 0.139 dB, 0.140 dB, 0.151 dB, and 0.152 dB respectively at C-band. While, countries like Ghana, Togo, Benin republic, Ivory Coast and Nigeria has the highest scintillation fade with values 1.575 dB, 1.560 dB, 1.472 dB, 1.453 dB and 1.236 dB respectively. The results also suggest that 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> fadeout link might occur if a satellite communication system is planned with a low margin of about 1 dB for tropospheric scintillation fade depth at V band in these locations.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Stepped Open Slot Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design of a miniaturized stepped open slot antenna (SOSA) for UWB applications is presented. The proposed SOSA consists of a stepped open slot antenna, L-shaped slots, and a strip director. L-shaped slots are inserted on the ground plane of the SOSA to create a resonance in the low frequency, which reduce the size of the SOSA. A strip director is appended to the SOSA in order to increase the gain in the middle and high frequency regions. The fabricated SOSA has a frequency band of 3.02-11.04 GHz for a VSWR <; 2, which assures the operation in the UWB band, and the measured gain ranges 3.0-6.5 dBi in the band.

articleTitle: Comparative study of three Deterministic Radio Propagation Models in a Complex media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effect of a periodical saw-teeth profile made from juxtaposition of 12 metallic lockers on radio wave propagation is investigated through deterministic modeling. The received signal, from three respective transmitter-receiver antennas systems, is discussed. Furthermore, the modeling techniques are validated through comparison of measurement' results with three different models, namely, GTD, UTD and heuristic slope UTD diffraction models.

articleTitle: Optimization of LPDA Antennas with Axial Twist
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional log-periodic dipole antennas (LPDAs) can be generalized to have a constant angle twist `ljJ about the array axis in each period. In previous work it has been shown that such antennas can produce high-quality circular polarization over a substantial bandwidth, while maintaining gain typical of that observed in conventional LPDAs. In this paper we apply a direct search method to optimize a weighted combination of gain and axial ratio. The variables varied were the connecting line characteristic impedance Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, the scaling factor T, the smallest element position R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sub>, and the twist angle Ψ. Simulations of an example 26-element design for 500 MHz -3 GHz show improved gain and VSWR and improved axial ratio bandwidth.

articleTitle: Series Feed Network for Power Distribution Control in the Millimeter-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A series feed network using two slits is proposed for power distribution control for antenna arrays operating in millimeter wave bands. The effects of slits are investigated using a 3D full-vector simulator. It was shown that the proposed feed network can control the ratio of the power coupled to each radiator to the power available from the feed line and reflection coefficient by adjusting the positions of the slits.

articleTitle: Design of a split-ring resonator based microstrip sensor for near- field inspection of composites
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterials have been increasingly used in the past few decades in the design of novel microwave circuits and sensor systems. This paper deals with the design of a SRR sensor for microwave non-destructive evaluation (NDE) applications. Building on the previous works in this field, a modified design of the sensor is used for interrogating composites through edge coupling. A built-in calibration system, integration of multiple sensors (high and low frequencies) and high-Q factor are some of the benefits of the sensor. Specifically, the sensor's super resolution capability for detection of sub-wavelength defects inside the composite materials will be investigated. The sensor design, experimental results and demonstration of the whole system will be presented to demonstrate its feasibility for practical NDE applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of UWB Modified Maltese Shaped Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, design of a modified Maltese shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed. Conformal strip feeding of trapezoidal shape is used to feed the DRA. The Maltese shape introduces air gap in the DRA design which helps in reducing the Q-factor and in turn helps in achieving wide bandwidth (BW). Further, circular slots and two orthogonal slits are introduced in a Maltese shaped DRA to achieve ultra-wide bandwidth (UWB). The proposed DRA is fabricated, tested and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulation. Measured return-loss bandwidth of about 111 % covering frequency band from 3.6 to 12.6 GHz is achieved. Various design parameters along with measured and simulated results are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Improved Reduced-Order Model with Equivalent Surface for Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An improved model-order reduction scheme for scattering problems is introduced. An equivalent surface is introduced into the scattering problems to enclose the background scatterers. By performing random singular-value decomposition (RSVD) to the matrix expression of the interaction between equivalent surface and scatterers, a set of orthonormal vectors are obtained. The matrix representation of the interaction between radiator and scatterer is approximated by a number of the orthonormal vectors with certain truncation error. In addition, the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM) is used to select the most important vectors which minimizes the truncation error. The scheme is suitable for simplifying the scattering problems, especially when the location of radiator changes frequently.

articleTitle: Planar Bi-Blade Antenna integrated with Balun for GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of co-planar Bi-Blade Antenna (BBA) with a double-Y balun having a transition between the microstrip to co-planar stripline has been presented for ultra-wideband applications, such as ground penetrating radar and microwave wideband imaging. A portion of the dielectric is removed from the region between the two blades to increase the path length of the fields in that region, thereby reducing the minimum operating frequency within a specified dimension. The designed prototype provides an impedance bandwidth of 22:1 corresponding to the 0.48 GHz to 10.80 GHz frequency range, along with a maximum realized gain of around 10 dBi.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Cylindrical DRA with Identical Radiations Using HEM11δ/HEM12δ /HEM111Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-frequency cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) excited with three different modes of similar broadside radiation patterns has been explored. Dominant HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> and higher order HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub> and HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12δ</sub> modes are excited simultaneously in a conventional CDRA structure with radius to height ratio<;1.0. A prototype realized from a block of dielectric constant 10 promises of 6 dBi, 7.3dBi and 9.5dBi peak gains at three operating frequency bands showing symmetrical radiation patterns over the principal planes. This should find suitable applications in modern multi-frequency/multi-band wireless communications.

articleTitle: Measured and Field- Based Theoretical Q of Gravitationally-Small Gravitational Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in detection of gravitational waves not only demonstrate the transmission and reception of such waves, but also prompt comparisons to electromagnetic antennas. Although the transmitting gravitational antenna and signal generator may be the inspiral of a binary neutron star orbit, such new gravitational antenna observations raise interesting questions from an antenna engineering perspective. In particular, measured data are used to determine the Q (quality factor) of the gravitationally-small gravitational antenna comprised of the neutron star quadrupole, along the lines of Wheeler-Chu limits for electromagnetic antennas. The recent gravitational wave event GW170817 had signal frequencies below 75 Hz and implied orbital separation near 250 km, which suggest a gravitationally-small radiator below 0.07 wavelengths. In addition, qualitative arguments based on quadrupole gravitational field components suggest a theoretical Q inversely proportional to the seventh power of gravitational quadrupole antenna size. Measured data are presented that somewhat better support quadrupole gravitational antenna Q inversely proportional to the fifth power of gravitational antenna size, more so than seventh power. Lastly, an antenna engineering perspective should provide insight for metamaterial and non-Foster enhancement of gravitational antenna designs.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Frequency Rectangular Loop Antenna Placed on a Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design of a dual-frequency antenna composed of a rectangular loop element “Hentenna” placed on a ground plane. By adopting unbalanced feed through a parallel wire transmission line, dual-frequency operation is realized in the designed antenna. Characteristics of the designed antenna are evaluated by the finite-difference time domain (FDTD) analysis. From the simulated results, it is found that the designed antenna has actual gain of 8-9dBi at two operation frequencies of 2.86 GHz and 4.39 GHz, which is 3-4 dB higher than that of the conventional Hentenna without a ground plane.

articleTitle: Rectenna Array on Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design methodology, demonstration hardware, and test results are presented for a novel design of the rectenna grid array on flexible substrate.

articleTitle: Radome Enhancement Technique for High-Power Wideband Millimeter Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A technique to enhance the mechanical and thermal properties of a radome configuration for a wideband, high power millimeter wave horn antenna is presented. Using reinforcing metallic strips across the aperture of the antenna enclosed by a radome, the ability of that radome to withstand certain pressure and heat loading is enhanced. The design is presented and validated in the electrical, thermal and mechanical domains.

articleTitle: First-Principle versus NRW Retrieval of Metamaterial-Insert Constitutive Parameters Using Measured Scattering Matrix
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we compare the first principle homogenization theory (FPHT) with the Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) approach for determining the complex permittivity and permeability of periodic metamaterials from the measurement of S-parameters. We show that the FPHT overcomes the anti-resonant behavior associated with the wrong sign for the imaginary part and negative slope for the real part versus frequency, for permittivity or permeability in the NRW method. A homogenous slab and a slab embedded with metamaterial inserts formed by U-spiral-pair resonators are then used as examples to prove the accuracy and robustness of the FPHT.

articleTitle: A W-Band Curved Aperture Horn Antenna with Consistent Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The analysis and design of a wideband `Dewey' curved-aperture horn antenna, designed to cover 75-110 GHz is presented. The development process features a fitness metric used to minimize radiation pattern variance. The main objective is to achieve H - plane radiation pattern invariance over the active bandwidth. Design data is favorably compared with measurements to fully validate the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: New Perspectives for the Longitudinal Spectral Solution of Sommerfeld Half-Space problem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using Fourier longitudinal spectral expansion an alternative expression for the fields produced by a Hertzian dipole on a two-layered half space is deduced. It is found that the nominal reflected and transmitted fields are not source free, therefore the solution is incomplete. In order to make the solution source free one needs to introduce auxiliary fields that neutralize the spurious source. Numerical results for nominal and auxiliary sources and associated fields are shown.

articleTitle: Quad-IFA MIMO Antennas Using Self-curing Decoupling Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates that quad-IFA MIMO antennas for a compact wireless terminal can be effectively decoupled using the self-curing decoupling technique by only adding a lumped capacitor at an acupoint near the shorting arm of each IFA antenna. A typical MIMO antenna scenario is studied with two IFAs on the top edge while the other two on the bottom edge of the grounded PCB board. The PCB size imitates a typical mobile phone and the four IFAs work at band of 2.4-2.5 GHz. The measured results show that the six possible mutual coupling among the four IFAs can all be effectively reduced simultaneously by using the self-curing decoupling technique.

articleTitle: Multi-Plane Frequency Scanning using a Leaky-Wave Antenna Array with Double-End Series Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-plane frequency scanning antenna structure is introduced as a low-cost and frequency-functional antenna system for applications such as radar, spectrum sniffing and realtime spectroscopy. The structure consists in a leaky-wave antenna array with double-end series feeding network, excited at its four corners according to a suitable switching sequence. The design of the frequency-scanning antenna structure is validated via fullwave simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a 3-Facet Linearly-Polarized Transmitarray Antenna at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution presents the design of a 3-facet transmitarray operating at Ka-band. The proposed design methodology and initial numerical analysis are presented. The study is validated by electromagnetic (EM) simulation of a 400-element linearly-polarized 3-facet transmitarray antenna.

articleTitle: Log-Periodic Dipole Antennas Using Wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The log-periodic dipole antennas was proposed in order to solve the problem which existing ridge horn antenna holds, and it showed over self-complementary antennas structure, constant impedance, wide-band characteristics, and frequency band 5-12GHz, gain 8dBi more than, and VSWR=2.0 or less than.

articleTitle: Innovative Method for Designing Multibeam-on-Receive Scanning Arrays with Optimized Sub-array Configuration and Analytic Phase Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design methodology for multibeam-on-receive scanning arrays is here presented. A hybrid analog/digital beam-forming network and a clustered architecture are considered. The proposed methodology aims at optimize the clustering configuration in order to guarantee the lowest possible side lobe level when steering the beams within a given scanning range, and operating within a given bandwidth. A novel analytic phase synthesis method allows the efficient computation of optimal sub-array phases for pointing the beams towards desired directions. Moreover, a global optimizer is used for the clustering configuration optimization. Finally, a numerical example has been reported to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Near-Field Antenna Design for UHF RFID System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents two near field reader antennas for applications in the UHF radio frequency identification (RFID) system. Strong vertical and horizontal magnetic fields in near zones are respectively excited by those two reader antennas, so that the readable distance of the nearfield tags attached on objects can be enhanced significantly. Thus, the reader antennas are capable of near-field identification and positioning applications, such as a casino gaming table. For the gaming management system, many stacked chips with tags embedded can be recognized by using near-field reader antennas so that manpower may be saved to significantly improve counting efficiency.

articleTitle: A Simple Direction Finding Compensation Method of Surface-Mounted Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple direction finding (DF) compensation method of surface-mounted patch antennas is proposed. Radiation patterns of an array with complex structure are different with ideal beam patterns, because of mutual coupling with adjacent elements and surrounding structures as well as the characteristics of the element itself. These errors make large direction finding error when amplitude comparison and phase comparison monopulse (interferometer) are used. To solve the problem, the amplitude and phase differences are approximated, and simple DF equations are derived considering search angle, frequency, and polarization of the receiving antennas and incident wave. A surface-mounted five patch antennas are simulated to verify the proposed method. The central element could be used to find the incident wave polarization, or to increase detection range by combining sum pattern.

articleTitle: Compact Flat Dipole Rectenna for Energy Harvesting or Wireless Power Transmission Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses the design and the characterization of a compact (2.3 cm x 3.4 cm) flat dipole antenna surrounded by a rectangular ring. Due to its wide frequency bandwidth, this antenna covers the UMTS, LTE 4G, WiFi and WiMAX (IEEE 802.16e) bands and can be advantageously used for RF Energy Harvesting or Wireless Power Transmission applications. A compact rectenna using the proposed antenna was manufactured and characterized. It allows reaching a RF -DC conversion efficiency of 38.6% for an E-field of 7V/m with a 1.5 kΩ load.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Interference in Electric Vehicle Cables
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The development of electric cars that use large electrical voltages, release harmonics that cause interference in nearby systems. This study carried out simulations with the CST software, which simulated the induction of a pulse in cables of electric vehicles that can cause interference in other equipment or systems that operate in frequency bands of 200 MHz to 800 MHz.

articleTitle: Broadband Modified Elliptical Ring Quasi-Isotropic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadband modified elliptical ring quasi-isotropic monopole antenna. The antenna is designed and fabricated to cover CDMA, GSM900, GSM1800, 3G, 4G and Wi-Fi bands. It has a measured bandwidth from 820MHz to 3.5GHz for| S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤-10dB. The antenna is both horizontally and vertically polarized, with a gain greater than 2dBi over the entire bandwidth. It has a uniform radiation pattern over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: The Multiobjective Delaunay Tessellation Optimization Algorithm and its Applications in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm (MOEA) called Multiobjective Delaunay Tessellation Optimization (MODTO), and applies it to several canonical test problems alongside other classical MOEAs and some popular new ones. The advantages and limitations as well as the future intended development of the algorithm in the context of electromagnetics optimization are discussed.

articleTitle: Causality Verification using a First-Order Chebyshev Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a novel method for causality verification and enforcement of scattering parameters (S-parameters) which may result from computational electromagnetic tools and are often required in performing transient simulations of electromagnetic systems, including antennas. We propose a method which uses a first order Chebyshev filter, derive the exact expression of truncation error, and perform a thorough error analysis of the numerical implementation of the Hilbert transform based on frequency-normalized and magnitude-normalized plots of absolute error due to a) truncation error and b) discretization error. The proposed technique, summarized as an algorithm, operates on the sampled frequency responses, without the need for extrapolation.

articleTitle: A Refinement - Free Calderón Preconditioner for the Electric Field Integral Equation on Geometries with Junctions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a refinement-free Calderón multiplicative preconditioner (RF-CMP) for the electric field integral equation (EFIE) working on arbitrary geometries, that is, the case that the geometry has junctions is included. This is in stark contrast to existing Calderón preconditioners requiring the use of dual basis functions (e.g., Buffa-Christiansen (BC) or Chen-Wilton (CW) basis functions), which have not been generalized to arbitrary geometries. We obtain this result by a generalization of loop-star functions on junctions and using the fact that the loop and star transformation matrices can, if combined elaborately, be used to cure the dense-discretization breakdown of the EFIE. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Microstrip Ridge Gap Waveguide Hybrid Coupler at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3dB hybrid coupler is designed to cover the 60 GHz band (57-64GHz) using the Microstrip Ridge-Gap-Waveguide (MRGW) technology. The hybrid coupler has magnitude variation less than 0.6 dB and a 90 ±2.5° phase variation between the output ports.

articleTitle: An Experimental Pilot Study of Cranberry Crop Yield Estimation Using Near-Field Microwave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a pilot investigation of near-field microwave sensing for cranberry crop yield estimation using an open-ended rectangular waveguide suspended above the cranberry canopy surface. We compare the performance of two estimation techniques applied to 1.0-1.3 GHz reflection coefficient data measured at 20 unique test sites in a bed in central Wisconsin. The maximum cranberry yield at these test sites was 900 cubic centimeters (cc) per square-foot surface area. A linear discriminant analysis (LDA) with principal component analysis (PCA) and error-correcting-output codes applied to the measured microwave data was able to correctly estimate the volume within 125 cc (roughly 50-60 berries) of the true canopy berry volumes in 71% of the test cases.

articleTitle: Design of a Capacitively Loaded Implantable Loop Antenna in the Cerebral Spinal Fluid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A capacitively loaded implantable loop antenna operating at 400 MHz is proposed for the implantation in the cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) above the brain. The specific absorption rate and temperature analysis were carried out to investigate the maximum input power for the implantable antenna without violating the safety considerations inside an anatomical realistic human head model. The implantable antenna achieves a maximum input power of 15.7 mW with 1 °C increase in the temperature of the human head tissue. Thus, the implantable antenna can be integrated with a low-power RF neural module.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin metalens generating coverging vortex beam in microwave region
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a planar ultra-thin metalens is proposed to generate converging vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) in microwave region. Phase changes are introduced to manipulate the transmitted wave front by designing rotation angles of Pancharatnam-Berry phase unit cell. Based on the superposition of phase profile of converging lens and spiral phase plate, the converging vortex beam with OAM mode can be generated by proposed metalens in microwave region. The measurement results are in good accordance with simulation results, which verify the theoretical design procedures.

articleTitle: Measurement Validation of Hybrid Electromagnetic Field Analysis Method for Airport Surface in VHF Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Authors proposed a method of electromagnetic field analysis suitable for the airport surface so far. In this paper, the proposed method is validated by the measurement using the scaled airport model. The tendency and the null position of the both results agreed and the validity of the proposed method is indicated.

articleTitle: Co-design of Antenna and Illumination Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, integration of a wireless communication system with an illumination system is proposed. A transparent radiator is designed on an illumination cover surface which allows visible light to pass through and to transmit and receive radio frequency (RF) signals simultaneously. A transparent single patch antenna and antenna array have both been considered. Possible applications include smart lampposts, headlights of automobiles (vehicle-to-vehicle communications) or helmets for providing data services and illumination at the same time.

articleTitle: A New Dihedral Reflector for Simultaneous Polarimetric Calibration and Background Clutter Extraction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new diamond-shaped dihedral reflector is proposed for simultaneous polarimetric calibration and background clutter extraction in target polarimetric scattering matrix (PSM) measurement. Traditional rectangular and triangular-shaped dihedral reflectors rotating with an integer multiple of 180° rotation around the radar line of sight (LOS) have relatively high biased components due to the long line connecting the two right-angled plates. Dihedral reflector with two diamond-shaped right-angled plates and a short connecting line demonstrates much better characteristic. Simulations are presented to show the essential improvement of performance using the proposed dihedral design.

articleTitle: Fast Estimation of Wireless Charging System in a Large Tissue
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless charging technology enables designers to miniaturize medical implants and eliminates the redundant surgical procedure to replace batteries. In this paper, we propose a precise and fast method of predicting mutual coupling inside a human body. A magnetic field at 6.78 MHz is generated with two different types of resonant coils - circumferential and Helmholtz coils. The circumferential coil generates a vertical magnetic field while the Helmholtz coil produces a horizontal field. They can operate individually or simultaneously. The combined field mitigates orientation mismatch and increases ability to charge the implant wirelessly within the volume of interest. To predict M precisely and rapidly, a theoretical derivation is presented and compared to a commercial full-wave solver. The results show that the theoretical value is well aligned with the simulated one. The time required to produce an estimation of the coupling within the entire constellation can be substantially reduced with this approach.

articleTitle: Dealing with Complexity in Electromagnetics through the System-by-Design Paradigm - New Strategies and Applications to the Design of Airborne Radomes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The efficient solution of complex electromagnetic (EM) design problems is addressed through the System-by-Design (SbD) paradigm. The synthesis is dealt with several interconnected functional blocks, while the overall system functionality is considered as the design target. A significant time-saving with respect to standard approaches is achieved thanks to the exploitation of a fast surrogate model instead of fullwave simulations to explore the solution space. Moreover, an innovative adaptive sampling strategy is proposed to enhance the accuracy of such a predictor to better guide the optimization algorithm. A numerical example is shown to assess the effectiveness of the proposed SbD strategy when dealing with the design of large-scale airborne radomes.

articleTitle: Additive Manufactured 60 GHz Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) enables fabrication of complex geometries, rapid prototyping, and the ability to inexpensively manufacture low quantities. Antenna design and manufacturing has many opportunities to benefit from these advantages. This study demonstrates a custom slot array antenna operating at 60 GHz. Manufacturing tolerances, particularly surface roughness, may influence performance especially at millimeter wave frequencies.

articleTitle: On RFID Tag Detection Inside Metal Pipes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the detection of a passive UHF RFID tag is analyzed when the tag is located inside a metallic cylindrical pipe. By modeling the pipe with a cylindrical waveguide, it is possible to relate the tag detection with the propagation of a TE or TM mode inside the guided structure. Simulated and measured results are here described.

articleTitle: Path-Loss Compensation and Target Design for Dielectric Waveguide based Radar Target Generators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution the path-loss behavior of dielectric waveguide (DWG) based radar target generators (RTG) is modeled and discussed. By comparing it to the path-loss of realworld radar scenarios, so-called compensation targets are defined which enable the proper radar emulation. Moreover, several RTG targets are presented. Measurements which proof the path-loss theory and the target modeling are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation on Balanced Double-Sided Gap Waveguide for W-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a double-sided gap waveguide (DSGWG) working at W-band has been proposed. For the conventional double-sided parallel strip line (DSPSL), its performance is deteriorated by the losses at W -band. Based on the newly proposed half-height pins structure, the DSGWG has been investigated. For this new DSGWG, there is no dielectric loss compared to DSPSL since waves propagate in the air-filled gap. In addition, the spurious radiation has been suppressed by the half height pins. This DSGWG has achieved the good transmission performance at W -band. The characteristics impedance of offset DSGWG has been investigated. It shows that the offset DSGWG can realize a relatively high impedance without change the line width. Furthermore, the DSGWG with an inserted conductor plane is researched as well. The inserted conductor can function as a virtual ground (GND) to isolate different circuits on the top and bottom layers. Based on those characteristics, some results based on offset structure and dual band structure have been given to verify the DSGWG's performance.

articleTitle: Effect of electrode geometry on the lead electromagnetic model and RF-induced heating
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this case study we investigate the dependence of the RF-induced power deposition (P) and the temperature rise (ΔT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) in gel at lead electrode on the electrode geometry for helix and straight leads at 128 MHz. The results indicate that shortening the electrode length from 10 mm to 3 mm resulted in up to fourfold increase of Δ T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>.

articleTitle: 60-GHz Polarization-Diversity Compact Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact polarization-adjustable 2×2 phased array antenna is presented at 60 GHz frequency band. The array elements are dual-feed patch antennas fabricated using substrate technology. By adjusting the excitations of the antenna ports through the phased-array chipset, a quadri-polarization diversity antenna is achieved. The array beam can be steered for any selected polarization in both E- and H-planes. The impedance bandwidth covers all 4 WiGig frequency channels and the achieved gain at 60 GHz is 11 dBi.

articleTitle: Thin Substrate Narrow Slot with Less Back Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An investigation is performed on a narrow slot antenna where two additional strips act as reflectors are added beside the microstrip feeding line to reduce the back radiation. In the design process, the original slot is kept the same, but the width and length of the microstrip line, the positions, and dimensions of strip reflectors are adjusted to get proper antenna performance. The simulated results show that the front-to-back ratio is improved from 1.88dB to be 7.06dB after using the additional strip reflectors.

articleTitle: Ongoing Developments Towards the Realization of a Microwave Device for Brain Stroke Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The present paper describes our on-going work towards the realization of a novel device to perform continuous monitoring of a patient after a stroke onset. The realization of the antenna array and of the control electronics will be discussed, together with a first experimental test of the system.

articleTitle: Generation of mm-Wave Higher Order OAM Modes using Flat Phase Plates
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to demonstrate high data rate secure transmission using orbital angular momentum (OAM) modulated beams, we have designed flat OAM phase plates. We report generation of orthogonal OAM beams having OAM L = 1-4. These flat phase plates (FPP) are made of high permittivity material of ε ≈ 10.8. An iterative circle packing technique, with circles representing the holes in a dielectric, has been used to design the FPP for each specific OAM mode. Numerical simulations are carried out using a horn excitation on the FPPs to produce the required OAM modulations. Experimental results of OAM beam generation and demodulation to demonstrate high data rate transmission will be presented in the meeting.

articleTitle: High-Order PT-Symmetric Telemetric Sensors with Singularity-Enhanced Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a new parity-time (PT)-symmetric telemetric sensing system to greatly enhance the sensitivity of passive inductor-capacitor (LC) wireless sensors, widely used in RFID sensors and internet-of-things (loTs). We demonstrate that by tailoring the equivalent circuit of inductively-coupled sensor and reader to satisfy the PT-symmetry (space-time reflection symmetry), the sensitivity can be the significantly improved when compared to that of conventional loop-antenna readers. This finding may have an impact on various wireless sensing and imaging systems, which employ micro/nano-machined RFID tags, wearables, and bioimplants.

articleTitle: Multiband Antenna Design for Ambient Energy Harvesting based on RF Field Investigation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the results of RF field measurement carried out in a semi-urban region in Islamabad, Pakistan. The objective of the paper is to explore the potential of energy harvesting from ambient sources. To author's knowledge it is the first time that this study has been carried out. The ambient RF power level from 10 MHz to 3 GHz has been measured covering FM band, all cellular frequency bands (2G, 3G, 4G) and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi band. The measurements done for both indoor and outdoor settings provide valuable insights into the available ambient power for harvesting purposes. GSM 900 and 1800 MHz show the highest available power whereas Wi-Fi band has the lowest power among the measured bands. Based on this analysis, a multiband planar bow-tie energy harvesting antenna covering GSM900, GSM1800 and WiFi bands is also presented.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave Microstrip Fed Slot Array Antenna with PMC Packaging for Future 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper deals with slot array antenna fed by PMC packaged microstrip lines at 30GHz frequency range. The slots are etched in the ground plane of the microstrip substrate. The microstrip feeding line is placed on the other side of the substrate. Also, a PMC layer is placed on top of the feeding microstrip line to stop surface waves or any unwanted field leakage or radiation from the feeding line. In this work, the PMC surface is realized by periodic metal pin structure. The antenna works at 30GHz band with reasonable S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and radiation performance.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Integral Equation Approach to Solve the Anisotropic Forward Problem in Electroencephalography
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The boundary element method provides a computationally efficient solution to the Electroencephalography (EEG) forward problem on piece-wise homogeneous head models by using surface integral equations. However, realistic modeling of the head medium requires a proper account of the anisotropic electric nature of the human skull, which cannot be handled by standard surface integral equations. This work addresses this issue by presenting a new formulation which perturbs the standard Lippmann-Schwinger approach with volume elements within the skull. The resulting surface/volume integral equation can handle computations of fully realistic modeling for both skull and white matter. Numerical results will confirm the validity of the approach as well as its applicability to real case scenarios.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Strokes Using Microwave Tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Brain stroke is a major cause of disability and death worldwide. There are two types of stroke, ischemic or cerebral infarction (85% of cases) and hemorrhagic (15%). The diagnosis must be made quickly (within 3 to 4 hours after the onset of symptoms) to determine the nature of the stroke and proceed to treatment. Recent works have shown the modification of the complex permittivity according to the nature of stroke [1] in the microwave domain. We are interested here in the detection of brain strokes using microwave tomography. We present results obtained by electromagnetic simulations coupled to a realistic noise model of measurements. The forward problem is based on a massively parallel computing using domain decomposition method, and an inverse problem based on L-BFGS algorithm with a regularization based on total variation (TV).

articleTitle: Multilayered Axially Modulated Cylindrical Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An axially modulated metasurface leaky-wave antenna (AMLWA), with multiple dielectric layers, is proposed for conformal and wideband applications. The bandwidth performance of a single-layered AMLWA is compared to that of a three-layered and a five-layered AMLWA. It is shown that the bandwidth of the gain and the scan-angle range increase with the increase in the number of dielectric layers.

articleTitle: Hardware Efficient Adaptive Beamformer Based on Cyclic Variable Step Size
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an improved adaptive beamforming solution based on Global Sidelobe Canceler (GSC) and Least Mean Square (LMS). By analyzing the impact of step size on LMS performance, a simple yet effective new Cyclic Variable Step Size (CVSS) algorithm is proposed to enhance the convergence speed and excess MSE performance of LMS. By adding just a few shift operations to adapt the step size cyclically, the CVSS LMS is efficient for hardware implementation. Initial study shows that it's possible to double the convergence speed with minimum overhead. The numerical simulation confirmed the effectiveness and performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Review of Adaptive Microwave and RF Phased Arrays for Thermotherapy Treatment of Cancer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Adaptive microwave and radiofrequency (RF) phased arrays for thermotherapy treatment of cancer are described. Results from four clinical trials for wide-field focused microwave treatment of patients with invasive cancer in the intact breast are reviewed. A pre-clinical system that employs an adaptive nulling ring array for deep heating at VHF is described.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band Frequency Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Antenna Array Using a Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new frequency reconfigurable filter used to frequency tune an antenna array at Ka-band. The frequency reconfiguration is achieved without affecting the radiation pattern of the array. A reconfigurable filter provides the desired resonant frequencies by activating an integrated PIN diode that modifies the length of a stub. The overall design also includes a sequential rotating feeding approach that provides an improved right hand circular polarization (RHCP) for an array antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of Airborne Antennas Using Hybrid Computational Techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With growing communications, nowadays there are increasingly sophisticated antenna systems with associated electronics aboard aircrafts. Advances in electromagnetic (EM) simulations have significantly improved the design process for such systems, resulting in reduced testing time and costs. In this paper, we will review hybrid computational techniques that are becoming popular to analyze and optimize antenna designs as well as antenna placement on air borne platforms. Accuracy of simulations using hybrid full wave and asymptotic techniques will be presented.

Author Keywords: full wave and asymptotic hybrid methods

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Wideband Dual-Polarized Base-Station Antenna with Stable Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact wideband dual-polarized antenna with stable radiation patterns for 2G/3G/4G (LTE)base station application is presented. The proposed antenna consists of two dipoles printed on a square-shaped PCB boards. The dipoles are carefully designed by introducing additional stubs at both ends of the arms of each dipole. It could be adjusted by tuning the coupling structures to achieve compact size and enhance the bandwidth. It is shown that the dual-polarized base-station antenna has a bandwidth of 50% (1.69-2.81 GHz)for return loss greater than 15 dB. A high isolation of 40 dB is obtained between the dual-polarization ports. Stable radiation patterns in both the vertical and horizontal plane are obtained over the entire frequency band.

articleTitle: LTCC- Based Phased Array Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application in Mobile Device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact size couple-fed loop antenna element and its phased array is proposed in this paper. The antenna element is fabricated on LTCC and mounted on the Rogers RT5880 substrate. It is demonstrated that the proposed mmwave antenna system has good performance in terms of antenna gain and scanning property for 5G application in mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Clutter-Suppressed, Subsurface Interferometric SAR Imaging of Target Under Slightly Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A subsurface interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) imaging technique is proposed for the detection and localization of underground facilities in the presence of a rough ground surface. The new approach consists of a two-step procedure: first, surface clutter suppression is performed with a polarimetric difference operation that does not alter the propagation phase of the target scattered signal; then a subsurface interferometric algorithm is applied to infer target depth by correlating the clutter-suppressed images obtained at two observation angles. The performance of the overall sensing algorithm for scene depth profile mapping from an airborne system is demonstrated with full-wave simulation data.

articleTitle: Power-Dependent Bandstop Filters for Wide-Bandwidth, High-Speed Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Power-dependent switchable bandstop filters are discussed in this paper. The co-design of a switchable bandstop filter, a sensing bandpass filter, a sensing analog circuit, and a switch driving circuit enable all-pass-to-bandstop switchable filters that automatically activate when power above a designable threshold is present within the bandwidth of the filter. A third-order suspended-stripline power-activated switchable all-pass-to-bandstop filter with a second-order resonant power sensor was fabricated and measured to test the technique at 2.15 GHz. The measured all-pass state has less than 1.7 dB insertion loss while the automatically-switched bandstop state provides more than 18 dB attenuation.

articleTitle: PSO-Driven Synthesis of Realistic Time Modulated Arrays with Optimal Instantaneous Directivity through a System-By-Design Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synthesis of time-modulated arrays (TMAs) showing optimal instantaneous directivity is addressed through the System-by-Design (SbD) framework. The developed methodology enables a significant reduction of the overall time cost of the design procedure even if a realistic modeling of the radiating elements and of the beamforming network is fully taken into account during the optimization process. A preliminary numerical benchmark is presented in order to verify the potentialities of the SbD in achieving a comparable solution “quality” with respect to standard approaches together with a significant reduction of the overall computational times.

articleTitle: Optimization of Reactively Loaded Reflectarrays via Semidefinite Relaxation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The versatile semidefinite relaxation-based optimization framework developed for near-field wireless power transfer (WPT) systems is adopted for optimization of scanned reflectarrays in the far-field. As confirmed via simulation results, the framework can be used to maximize gain by finding the optimum loading element for each antenna element. The procedure is straightforward and can also be useful for design and optimization of reconfigurable reflect- and lens arrays.

articleTitle: A Compact Slotted-Cavity Antenna for HPM Reflector Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: a compact resonant slotted-cavity antenna that using TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">506</sub>high-order mode is studied in this paper. Resonant cavity has high power capacity that is well applied in HPM (high power microwave). High-order mode excited in the resonant cavity has no requirements to use mode converters and power divider. TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">506</sub>mode has the merit of improving equalization performance of pattern and cross-polarization rejection. Electric magnetic simulation software CST demonstrates the high performance of this novel antenna based on TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">506</sub>mode.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Specific Absorption Rates with High Resolution Human Head Models at 890 MHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We evaluated the spatially averaged 1- and 10-gram specific absorption rate (SAR)for PIFA (Planar Inverted- F Antenna)-type mobile phone antennas using three high-resolution surface-based human models. Use of these human models instead of the SAM (Specific Anthropomorphic Mannequin)phantom for SAR estimation significantly affected the SAR estimates. The obtained 1g and 10g peak SAR levels for the human models exceeded those for the SAM phantom by factors of three to four.

articleTitle: Beamwidth Evaluation of Finite-Length 1- D Bidirectional Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work we analyze the beamwidth properties of one-dimensional (1-D) bidirectional leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) when the antenna is pointing close to broadside. Existing formulas neglect the effect of the aperture truncation, which affects the exact value of the beamwidth for practical realizations of 1-D LWAs. Using a rigorous theoretical framework, we find a transcendental beamwidth equation, whose numerical solution furnishes the exact value of the beamwidth for finite-length 1-D bidirectional LWAs. Numerical results confirm that the aperture truncation considerably affects the beamwidth properties, especially for limited efficiencies.

articleTitle: Symmetric Positive Semi-Definite FDTD Subgridding Algorithm in Both Space and Time
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A symmetric positive semi-definite FDTD subgrid-ding algorithm in both space and time is developed for fast FDTD simulations. The resultant explicit time marching is not only accurate, but also guaranteed to be stable. Moreover, it permits the use of a time step local to the base grid and subgrids. Numerical experiments have demonstrated its performance.

articleTitle: Real beam, volumetric radar imaging at 340 GHz for security applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work we present a 340 GHz volumetric radar imager with 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> voxel resolution and multi-hertz frame rate. The radar uses a sparse focal plane array of 16 transceivers and mechanical scanning to achieve real beam imaging of people for future aviation security applications.

articleTitle: 1-bit, 2-bit Polarization Insensitive Reflection Programable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a 1-bit and 2-bit polarization insensitive reflection programmable metasurface based on pin diode. The metasurface consists of single substrate layer and symmetric structure. The pin diodes are positioned between the split gaps and biasd through the metal vias. For the 1-bit type, the reflection phase responses are 45° and -135° corresponding to “0” and “1”, respectively. For the 2-bit type, the reflection phase responses are 90°, 0°, -90°, and 180°, corresponding to four digital elements “00”, “01”, “10”, and “11” respectively.

articleTitle: Single Layer Dual-Band ‘Phoenix’ Reflectarray Unit Cell with Dual-Linear Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new single layer `Phoenix' reflectarray phase-shifting cell with dual-linear polarization. The unit cell uses two independent sets of concentric slots in order to control the reflected phase independently at 9GHz and 14.5GHz. Simulations show that the unit cell offers a complete phase cycle of 360° at both frequencies, with linear and parallel variation of the phase. A 13 × 13 reflectarray was designed and simulated in order to demonstrate the dual-band behavior of the proposed cell.

articleTitle: A Wideband Double Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna with Unidirectional Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband double circularly polarized (CP) square slot antenna is proposed in this paper. This antenna has a simple structure and compact size. The structure of the antenna is an inverted planar structure paralleling with the ground. It has two ports to generate different CP waves. The designed antenna works around 1.5GHz, which covers the BDS, GPS and GLNOSS band. The results show good performance of impendence bandwidth (IBW) (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10dB) is approximately 57.2%, the 3-dB AR bandwidth (ARBW) is approximately 43.8%, and the peak gain is about 7.1dBic at 1.4GHz.

articleTitle: Heat Dissipation Antenna Array for Compact Massive MIMO Radio Unit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new passive air cooling system with a heat dissipation antenna array to dissipate large amounts of heat from massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radio units is proposed. The antenna array has a radome with apertures and compact antenna elements as heat sink fins arranged for effective air flow. In thermal simulations, the proposed system achieved about a 1.8-times higher heat dissipation performance per volume than that of conventional passive air cooling system and a 1/1.8 miniaturization of radio unit volume, which is dependent on heat sink size.

articleTitle: Fast 3D Synthesis of Aperiodic Rectangular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a fast and simple method to generate a 3D pencil beam with a sparse array of elements having uniform excitations and located on a rectangular grid. The presented algorithm extends a recently proposed Gaussian approach, introducing a desired pattern as the product of two suitable Gaussian functions. This reduces the problem to a couple of independent one-dimensional problems, and the optimal positions of the array elements are found in closed form. Numerical examples show the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Design of Small GPS Anti-Jam Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a small GPS anti-jam antenna. The method is based on adaptive null-steering processing with miniature antenna elements. Our antenna system can maintain GPS tacking and adaptively steering null(s) for optimal performance. The adaptive antenna technology provides the performance advantages of a null-steering array in a small footprint antenna, allowing an increase in performance without a significant increase in size or cost.

articleTitle: Metal-Only Transmitarray Based on C-Shaped Slot
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of metal-only transmitarray using unit-cells based on C-shaped slots. The unit-cell consists of four identical layers separated by a quarter-wavelength spacer at 20 GHz (3.75 mm). The phase variation reaches 360° by varying the inner radius of the slot. An example of linearly-polarized transmitarray is provided to validate this concept at K-band for satellite communications in the down-link band.

articleTitle: Terahertz Time-Domain Pulsed Spectroscopy of Human Breast Cancer Tissues
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work utilizes time-domain pulsed terahertz spectroscopy to obtain the refractive index and absorption coefficient of normal and malignant human breast cancer tissues. The excised tissues are purchased from the National Disease Research Interchange and shipped within 24 hours of surgery. The tissue is immersed in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium plus antibiotic during the shipment. The solution is characterized in the terahertz frequency band (0.1-4 THz)showing insignificant differences compared with distilled water and other common solutions. Healthy fibrous and fatty breast tissue are obtained from breast reduction surgery, while malignant tumors are obtained from breast cancer mastectomy or lumpectomy surgeries. The results will help understand the interaction of terahertz waves with human breast tumors and also to develop phantom tissue that can be manipulated to advance terahertz imaging.

articleTitle: Simple Phase-Mode Coefficients for Equiripple Sidelobe Reduction from a Uniform Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reducing the sidelobe levels in the array pattern from a uniform circular array is challenging due to the inherent complications imposed by the geometry. In this paper, we present a technique that uses the phase-mode transformation to enable application of an equiripple stopband formulation adapted from digital FIR filter design.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 3D Printed Hexagonal High Gain Short Backfire Antenna with Hard EM Walls
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A short backfire antenna with hard EM walls (hard SBFA) to provide high aperture efficiency is under development for dual-band (Ll and L2) GPS and other satellite applications. The antenna is excited by a slotted subreflector fed and supported by a two wire transmission line via a low loss air-filled coax matching network on the back. The antenna was optimized for maximum aperture efficiency at Ll and L2, which also resulted in greatly improved cross-polarization due to a more uniform amplitude taper over the aperture. The SBFA hexagonal aluminum cavity with 7.5 “apothem was built by 3D printing (additive manufacturing). The hard boundaries on the cavity walls were implemented with anisotropic impedance metasurfaces (AIM) on a foam liner. Aperture efficiency of 85% (Ll) and 96% (L2) were demonstrated. A 19” diameter circular A-SBFA was also designed, providing 92%/17.7 dBi (Ll) and 99%/15.8 dBi (L2) aperture efficiency/directivity.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Reconfigurable UHF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel planar reconfigurable meandered loop antenna that is suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. This antenna reconfigures its frequency of operation between two ISM bands, 760 MHz and 575 MHz. The antenna structure also has three folded edges, six layers and with total dimensions of 40×40mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The top layer (layer 1) is a meandered loop patch placed on top of a dielectric substrate and an air gap. The patch is fed through a shorting sheet from the feeding network. The feeding network constitutes the fourth layer of the antenna structure, which is placed on top of a dielectric layer and a full ground plane. The antenna has a compact size with miniaturization percentage of 70% at 760 MHz and 80% at 575 MHz.

articleTitle: Explicit and Unconditionally Stable FDTD with Analytical Method for Identifying Unstable Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In existing explicit and unconditionally stable time-domain methods, the root cause of instability has been identified to be the eigenmodes of the governing system matrix whose eigenvalues are too high to be accurately simulated by a given time step. The unstable modes have been found numerically, and subsequently deducted from the system matrix to permit an unconditionally stable time marching. In this work, we show that such unstable modes as well as stable modes can be found for the FDTD method in an analytical way. Numerical results have validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Global Optimization Technique for Microwave Imaging Based on the Simulated Annealing and Multi -Directional Search
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a novel global optimization technique for solving the inverse-scattering problem in electromagnetic imaging of dielectric objects. The presented optimizer combines the simulated annealing method with a multi-directional search algorithm to obtain candidate solutions that make the search towards the desired solution significantly more effective. We have demonstrated the strength of the method in solving the inverse-scatting problems by some numerical results, and showed the convergence of the presented method to the desired solution in the experiments that the standard simulated annealing may fail to provide an appropriate solution.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Dielectric Resonator Antenna Using Superstrate for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is proposed for future fifth-generation (5G) wireless technology. The proposed antenna structure operates at 28 GHz bands and achieves high gain thanks to the use of superstrate. The design utilizes a modified transition, microstrip to slot, to feed the antenna and enhance adaptation. Simulated results showed a large bandwidth covering about 3 GHz and a very high gain reaching 18.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Dual-band Microstrip antenna Array using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an array of multiband Wi-Fi antenna using genetic algorithm (GA)is proposed and optimized. The two-element antenna array is designed and simulated using CST Microwave Studio. Details of the design, simulation results on return loss and gain of the antenna array is also presented. The proposed array increased the gain in both 5.2 GHz band and 5.8 GHz bands used for Wi-Fi communications.

articleTitle: A Quad-Band Compact Inverted-F MIMO Antenna for USB Dongle Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper shows multi-band (quad) inverted-F MIMO antenna with the high isolation that covers WIFI and WiMAX bands (2.4, 3.7, 4 and 5.3 GHz). The design consists of two symmetric inverted-F antennas separated by 0.12 λ0. The high isolation is achieved by adding a meander line immersed in inverted T-slot shaped in the ground plane which is a vital element for the least three bands. Moreover, two V-shaped slits were etched on the two 50 Ω transmission lines to modify the impedance matching. The S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11 <;</sub> -15db to ensure the high isolation of the proposed design that covers multi-range bandwidth. The proposed design was modified by shifting the vias locations, chamfering the edges of the feeding lines and extending the length of the inverted-F antennas to cover the lower band of WIFI. The proposed design dimension is 52×77.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Reconfigurable Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Excited by Double-Ring Slot
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency-reconfigurable cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fed by double-ring slots is presented. The DRA is capable of bandwidth tuning at three different frequency bands between 2.58 and 3.04 GHz.
