Four p-i-n diode switches, implemented bias voltage using metalized vias, are located on the diameter line along with x -axis at the bottom. Through the combination of different switching actions, the effective current path of the feed for dielectric resonator has changed, which varies the bandwidth of the proposed antenna. The overall dimension of the antenna is 50 × 50 × 16.537 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Interference Mitigation for 5G Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) low-cost transmit/receive architecture with reduced power and hardware requirements that includes interference mitigation capabilities and accommodates multiple users. Specifically, a novel encoding approach is introduced to multiplex signals across large bandwidths and achieve secure communication and interference mitigation through spread signals. In this paper, a detailed description of the proposed high data rate system architecture is presented. Simulations are also provided in presence of high power interferers with 8 concurrent users. To further assess the systems performance and impact of the encoding/decoding process, a noise analysis was conducted for the transmitter and receiver chains. Specifically, Bit Error Rate (BER) curves are generated at different stages of the system showing interference-to-signal ratios improvement by at least 10 dB.

articleTitle: Novel Metal Only, Low Profile, High Gain Stepped Reflector Antennas for Future 5G mmWave and CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Several emerging technologies such as next generation CubeSats and 5G mm Wave networks require antennas capable of providing high data rates while maintaining a small form factor. This paper describes a systematic approach for synthesizing high gain stepped reflector antennas with profile heights of the order of a wavelength, resulting in a very small form factor for mmWave bands. The reflector aperture is comprised of confocal parabolic sections which scatter in phase, resulting in a focused far field beam. Both symmetric and offset configurations are discussed. In particular, two distinct methods of synthesizing low profile offset reflectors are presented in this work, which makes it possible to meet application specific design constraints.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Scattering Analysis of Arbitrary Objects in a Stratified Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An inhomogeneous absorbing boundary condition (IABC) is proposed to efficiently perform scattering analysis with the presence of a stratified medium using the finite element method. The analytical expressions for the incident fields in the right-hand side of the IABC are derived. The parallel dual-primal finite-element tearing and interconnecting (FETI-DP) algorithm is adopted to enable large-scale electromagnetic simulations. A multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA)-based far-field calculation is developed to reduce the computational complexity. Examples are presented to demonstrate the solution accuracy and large-scale modeling capability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: On the Study of the Effect of Frequency Deviation on Electric Field Characteristics Inside Jet Engines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel analysis of effect of frequency shift on the characteristics of the electromagnetic field distribution inside a simplified jet engine model is provided. The simplified jet engine structure is modeled as a metallic cylinder and is simulated using a stepwise stationary blade rotations. The rotation of the blades provides necessary randomness for the medium. The frequency shift introduced by the blade rotation is emulated inside the engine environment by varying the excitation frequency. The characteristics of the electric field values are analyzed at different operating frequencies to analyze the effect of frequency deviation on the field magnitude and phase.

articleTitle: Multiview Imaging with Real-Time Microwave Camera from Known Positions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution shows the application of multiview processing technique to a recently-developed real-time 3D microwave camera. The camera, which operates based on efficient synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging techniques, provides a good trade-off between fast image production and image quality. These cameras, as it happens with standard optical cameras, provide a good image of a volume in front of their apertures, but they cannot provide information about the complete object under test. Furthermore, it is usually convenient to consider multiple view angles as the best quality image is achieved when the area to be image is parallel to the aperture (as the specular reflection is captured). In this paper, we illustrate how recently-developed techniques, inspired from computer vision approaches, can be used to merge multiple views to obtain a more complete image of an object.

articleTitle: Phasor Representation Method for Synthesizing RCS-Reduction Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A phasor representation method, for synthesizing the additional RCS-reduction metasurfaces to reduce the RCS of almost any original metasurface without replacing it, is presented. The method is validated with simulated results. The introduction of RCS-reduction metasurface, synthesized using the proposed method, reduces the RCS of original metasurface in the targeted frequency range.

articleTitle: A Fast and Broadband Surface Method for Skin Effect Modeling in Multiscale Lossy Conductors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A surface integral equation-based solver for large-scale electromagnetic problems is proposed, with particular attention to accuracy and robustness over a wide range of frequencies and structure sizes. A differential surface admittance operator is employed to accurately model skin effect, and is combined with the augmented electric field integral equation, accelerated with the adaptive integral method (AIM). Two structures of vastly different electrical sizes are successfully analyzed over a wide frequency range of 1 kHz-40 GHz. Results are validated via direct LU factorization as well as the finite element method.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Flexible Antenna for WLAN/Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact flexible monopole antenna (18 mm×16 mm) with coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed structure for dual-band applications is presented in this paper. The antenna is fabricated on a 50 urti flexible Dupont material with dielectric constant 3.2 and loss tangent 0.003. The antenna has a bandwidth (-10 dB) of 80 MHz in the 2.4 GHz band and 125 MHz in the 5.8 GHz band, which is suitable for WLAN and Wi-Fi applications. The measured gain is 1.44 dB and 2.65 dB in lower and higher bands.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Bailey Power Divider Using SRRs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a technique to miniaturize the Bailey power divider by etching split ring resonators (SRRs) in the ground plane under the transmission lines forming this device. A miniaturized Bailey power divider operating at 600 MHz is designed and simulated with 5:1 split ratio. Size reduction of more than 60% is achieved as compared to the conventional layout. Full-wave simulation shows an input port matching better than -15 dB, and transmission parameters, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub>, of -1.6 dB and -8.55 dB at the design frequency, respectively.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface for Dual band filter applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for dual band applications has been proposed. A novel FSS unit cell is composed of closed metal patch in the shape of a “Clover” and FR-4 media substrate. By placing a high frequency switching PIN diode at an improved intersection in a closed metal sheet, a controlled frequency response can be obtained. Simulated results show that the proposed RFSS structure can achieve a dual-band response centered 2.5GHz and 6.2GHz when the PIN diodes at ON state. Therefore, the design can be used in C-band shielding applications.

articleTitle: Analyzing Practical Issues in SAR Measurements of Multiple-Antenna Transmitting Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple-antenna devices are expected to playa key role in 5G wireless communications. To ensure such devices complied with safety regulations and standards, determining the maximum SAR is essential and unavoidable. In our previous works, we introduced a fast estimation technique to evaluate the maximum SAR of such devices. This paper will analyze some practical issues, which might influence on the evaluation of maximum SAR of multiple-antenna devices. Important issues include incorrect phase setting, imprecise probe re-positioning, choosing “area scans”, and simplified estimation assumptions.

articleTitle: Internal Dual-Resonance High-Gain 1.5 Wavelength Loop Antenna for FDD Satellite Phone Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents a novel internal dual-resonance 1.5 wavelength high-gain loop antenna design for FDD satellite phone applications. It demonstrates that dual resonant modes with similar good performances can be generated successfully for covering both uplink and downlink bands operation by simply integrating a 1.5 wavelength folded loop radiator and a shorted capacitively-coupled feeding portion. The proposed antenna can be closely integrated at the top side-edge of a corner of a handset ground plane with a low-profile and compact antenna size. Fan-shape and directional radiation patterns toward the sky with good radiation characteristics can also be formed in the both desired uplink and downlink bands. The constructed prototype has been studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Smooth Walled and Corrugated Horns for Different Profile Options
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a systematic performance comparison of a smooth walled conical and a corrugated horn antennas for different profiling options. The parameters like, return-loss, peak gain and cross-polar isolation are considered for comparison. By changing the profile of a horn, significant variations are observed in the horn performance. The specifications of a D-band horn, used for the plasma diagnostics in reflectometry system are considered for simulation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Horizontal Polarized Omnidirectional Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband horizontal polarized omnidirectional loop antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of a loop loaded with periodical slots and a one-to-four power feeding network. With proper slots loaded in the loop, the ring behaves as the mu-negative transmission line (MNG-TL), and the current in the loop can remain in phase and uniform. A one-to-four power feeding network is used to further keep current in the loop uniform. Simulated results show O.2dB of gain difference in the omnidirectional plane. The measured results prove that a horizontal omnidirectional pattern with a wide bandwidth of about 560MHz (2.01GHz, 2.57GHz) is achieved.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Quadrifilar Helical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quadrifilar helical antenna with polarization and pattern reconfigurabilities is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a reconfigurable radiator and a switchable feeding network. The radiator combines two individual QHAs which can be alternatively activated. The feeding network provides switchable quadrature excitations to the radiator. By controlling the PIN diodes, the antenna can provide RHCP/LHCP waves with broadside/backfire radiation patterns. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna obtained wide impedance and axial-ratio bandwidths (18.6% and 44.2%, respectively) with a compact size (0.26 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.26 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.23 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>).

articleTitle: On Rapid Estimation of Impedance-Matrix Ranks via Grid-Based Techniques
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The performance of three sampling-grid-based techniques for estimating the rank of impedance matrix blocks are evaluated: Method I constructs a volumetric grid-to-grid propagation matrix between regular but coarsely sampled grids enclosing the source/observer domains and evaluates this matrix's rank using the truncated-SVD. While effective in the quasi-static regime, the method rapidly becomes impractical for electrically large domains. Method II evaluates the rank of the same grid-to-grid propagation matrix using the ACA. Method III uses a set of reduced/belt proxy grids designed for multilevel compression and interpolation of phase- and amplitude-compensated fields. For quasi-planar configurations of electrically large domains, Method III is found to be asymptotically superior while Method II is found to be effective until ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Combination of GO/PO and PTD Method for EM Scattering and SAR Image Simulation from Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a combination of the geometrical optics and physical optics (GO/PO) hybrid method and the physical theory of diffraction (PTD) is presented for the analyses of electromagnetic (EM) scattering and SAR imaging simulation from a complicated electrically large target. For this method, the scattering field from surfaces on a target is calculated with the GO/PO hybrid method, the diffraction field is calculated with PTD. Then the contribution of diffraction field and the scattering field from targets with different shapes are analyzed. It is shown that for the targets with wedges that are composed of two nearly mutually perpendicular flat surface, the scattering field from the surfaces is much strong than the diffraction field from edges. Otherwise, the diffraction field must be taken into consideration, especially for the directions away from the mirror region. The simulated SAR images also show the method can be applied to the simulation of SAR images.

articleTitle: A 6: 1 Bandwidth Dual-polarized Linear Phased Array of Tapered Slot Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Previous studies on tapered slot antenna (TSA) arrays are mainly focused on single-polarized linear array or dual-polarized 2-D arrays, where their ultra-wideband (UWB) behaviors are achieved by using contiguous electrical connection or creating necessary mutual coupling between adjacent elements of the array. However, for the application with narrow and long space constraints, due to the lack of mutual coupling for the polarization ports perpendicularly to the linear array direction, they behave in a narrower bandwidth compared to another polarization ports. This paper presents a prototype UWB dual-polarized linear array of TSAs with L-shaped lattice. A 14-element linear array has been built and validated. Active element patterns and scanning performance of the array are evaluated and performed with periodic boundary conditions. The antenna exhibits an operational bandwidth of 6:1 (1-6GHz range) for H-plane ±45° scan in vertical-polarization and 5.5:1 bandwidth (1.1-6GHz range) for E-plane ±45° scan in horizontal-polarization, respectively, maintaining active VSWR less than 4.4.

articleTitle: Bilinear Transform Approach for Wideband Digital Non-Foster Matching of Electrically-Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A digital non-Foster design approach is presented for wideband matching of an electrically-small monopole antenna using the bilinear transform. A digital negative capacitance in a series/parallel-RLC digital non-Foster matching network is used to increase bandwidth by cancelling a large portion of the capacitive reactance of an electrically-short monopole. A digitally-implemented positive inductance tunes the center frequency, eliminating residual reactance. A second digital resistor in parallel enhances stability. Simulation results show wideband impedance match of a 0.75 m monopole, with better than 6 dB return loss from 19.0 to 23.8 MHz, compared to a conventional passively-matched bandwidth of 20.2 to 20.7 MHz and a Wheeler-Chu limit of 3.3 percent for ka=0.314.

articleTitle: A High-efficiency Dual-band Wireless Energy Harvesting Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-low threshold power, large dynamic range and high-efficiency dual-band wireless energy harvesting circuit is designed and demonstrated to operate in all released global system for mobile communications (GSM) bands in China (0.87-0.96 GHz and 1.71-1.86 GHz) for passive wireless sensor network node and cellular IoT tag applications. The measured features of the proposed circuit show that the RF-to-DC conversion efficiency is with the range of 20-63.2% for an available input power range of -22 to 1 dBm in GSM900 band, and with the range of 13.8-55.5% for an available input power of -22 to 3dBm in GSM1800 band. In addition, the harvested energy is stored in the super capacitor through the energy management circuit.

articleTitle: Unwanted RF Energy Coupling During Electrocautery: An In-Vitro Tonsillectomy Study
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an in-vitro tonsillectomy study demonstrating that unwanted Radio-Frequency (RF) energy gets coupled into adjacent metal-based objects (e.g., mouth retractor) during electrocautery. In turn, this unwanted energy might cause adverse effects, such as dysgeusia. Our in-vitro set-up employed: 1) a ground-beef phantom that emulated the average properties of the human body, 2) a metal-based mouth retractor placed around an artificially-formed mouth cavity, 3) a 31kHz monopolar bovie firing at 30 W of power, and 4) a highly sensitive RF current monitor placed around the mouth retractor. Notably, currents as high as 181.48mA were shown to be unintentionally coupled to the retractor, which were ~ 40 times higher than the associated noise floor. As a first study of its kind, our results highlight the need for further explorations in future.

articleTitle: On the Design of Graphene Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensors for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR)sensors utilizing fiber optic technology have gained allot of attention due to their various medical applications. In this paper, we present the theoretical background, recent medical applications, principle of operation, analysis model and performance parameters of Graphene enhanced fiber optic SPR sensors. It is indicated that the geometrical and physical properties of the SPR sensor like the length and composition of sensing region and the fiber core diameter affect the performance of the SPR sensors and should be chosen carefully.

articleTitle: Modified Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi antennas with Substrate-Integrated Lenses for 2–18 GHz Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional balanced antipodal Vivaldi antennas (BAVAs) normally have deep ripple levels in mainlobe region and significant beamwidth variation over upper frequency band, which are drawbacks for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. This letter describes two types of lenses in front of BAVA to overcome these defects. A gradient-index semi-cylindrical lens and a cylindrical lens are utilized to improve ripples depth of E-plane mainlobe and broaden H-plane beamwidth, respectively. Both these lenses and BAVA are integrated on the same substrate and the desired refractive indexes of lenses are realized by a combination of a set of air-filled holes in the substrate. The detailed analysis, design and discussion for the modified BAVA with lenses (BAVA-L) and conventional BAVA are performed. The results show that BAVA-Ls offer attractive features such as smaller ripple levels in E-plane mainlobe, wider H-plane beamwidth and higher aperture efficiency, while maintaining good bandwidth characteristics over 2-18GHz.

articleTitle: Channel Analysis and Performance Evaluation of Wireless Backhaul at 5G Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless backhaul (WB) based on the Heterogeneous Network (HetNet) architecture has been attracting increasing interests in the fifth generation (5G) cellular mobile communications and beyond for providing convenient and agile networking. Meanwhile, 5G is extending cellular mobile communication from sub-6 GHz bands to millimeter wave (mmWave) bands for larger under-utilized bandwidth. To efficiently and accurately estimate the performance of wireless backhauling technologies, correct understanding of the backhaul channel is important. However, there still lacks a comprehensive study on the impact of back-hauling channel on the key performance metrics for applications in different deployment scenarios and 5G frequency bands. In this paper, applicable channel models are recommended for the backhaul link and access link in urban environment. Moreover, an in-band WB scheme adopting unified bandwidth allocation is evaluated by the recommended 3GPP channel models for both Random and Hotspot user equipment distributions. It is observed from the numerical results that the frequency and distribution have significant impacts on the performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Quad-Polarization Reconfigurable Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quad-polarization reconfigurable omnidirectional antenna is presented. The quad-polarization antenna consists of a circular loop for horizontal polarization (HP) and a top-loaded monopole for vertical polarization (VP). The left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) and the right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) are obtained by exciting the loop and the monopole simultaneously with different phases. It is shown that the bandwidth overlapped for HP, VP, LHCP, and RHCP is about 30% (1.65-2.25 GHz) with good omnidirectional patterns.

articleTitle: A Multi-bit Reconfigurable Transmitarray Design Approach Using Cascaded Spatial Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design approach for multi-bit reconfigurable transmitarrays is proposed. A 90° spatial phase shifter is designed using a double-layer slotted H-shaped patch element with two PIN diodes. By spatially cascading it with a T-bit reconfigurable transmitarray element, a 2-bit phase resolution is obtained. The simulated results of a Ku-band 2-bit element show that four well distributed phase states are achieved, and the average element insertion loss is 1.4 dB at 12.5 GHz. The proposed design approach is considerably easier to implement compared to conventional 2-bit transmitarray designs, and can be extended to 3-bit and multi-bit designs by further cascading a 45° phase shifter and so on.

articleTitle: Improving the Radiation Efficiency of Liquid Metal Antenna with Polarization Agility
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to realize a polarization agility antenna using liquid metal (eutectic gallium indium) and additive manufacturing. The antenna is a combination of both liquid metal alloy and copper tape which is adhered to a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film. The polarization is controlled by the position of the pressure-driven liquid metal encased in four cavities constructed by both the elastic dielectric material (i.e. Ecoflex) and PET film. The proposed fabrication technique not only enhances the radiation efficiency compared to conventional ones because of using minimum amount of lossy materials, but also manages to maintain its bendability. For the proof of concept, a reconfigurable aperture coupled patch antenna operating at 2.45 GHz with multi-polarization function is designed, fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: An Alternate Approach to Use Sommerfeld Integrals Codes for Electric Current to Derive Voltage Vector for Magnetic Frill Current in the Context of MoM
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method is proposed to use existing Sommerfeld integrals codes written for electric current sources to derive the voltage vector for the magnetic frill current source problem in the context of the Method of Moments (MoM). The proposed method is validated for the case of a short dipole used as a testing function for the field radiated by the magnetic frill current.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Modified Sierpinski Antenna for WiFi Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual band modified Sierpinski antenna for WiFi applications. The design is based on Sierpinski triangle fractal printed and it covers both the 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz Wifi Band. The antenna has a maximum gain of ~3.6 dBi and total size of 5.5×4 cm. An overview of the antenna design along with the full wave simulation is provided.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Multiobjective Evolutionary Optimization in Python for EM Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A highly efficient algorithm for the optimization of EM problems is proposed. The algorithm is mostly based on Python open-source libraries and was successfully used in the development of antennas and arrays using HFSS.

articleTitle: An Angled-dipole Antenna with Angled Directors for Wide-Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An angled-dipole antenna with angled directors that can be applied to wide-angle scanning phased array antennas is presented. The dipole antenna is angled for a small form factor. To realize a wide beam-width pattern, a pair of angled directors and an etched ground plane are used. For a wide frequency range of operation, an integrated balun is used to feed the proposed antenna. The proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 4.9-7.3 GHz for -10dB reflection coefficient. At 5.8GHz, the proposed antenna has a half power beam-width of 203°in E-plane and 225°in H-plane.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Reconfigurable Unit Cell for Programable Transmit-Array Lens in C-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electronically reconfigurable unit cell with 1-bit phase resolution (0°/180°) is presented for programable transmit-array lens (TAL) in C-band. The I-bit phase resolution is obtained by using two PIN diodes integrated in the transmitting layer of the unit cell. The simulated results verify that the proposed unit can achieve good 1-bit phase tuning, with minimum insertion loss of 0.2 dB and 2-dB transmission bandwidth of about 10%.

articleTitle: Modulated Metasurface Antennas Design Based on Generalized Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new and efficient design approach for modulated metasurface antennas where the meta-surface elements are characterized using generalized boundary conditions. With surface susceptibilities and equivalent model of elements, corresponding surface impedances of surface-wave mode could be analytically computed, which are then utilized to design modulated metasurface antennas. The validity of this design method is demonstrated through comparison with both full-wave simulation and measurement of an antenna prototype.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna Array for Modern Beamforming Radars
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radar systems are in a great progress, as a consequence of the evolution of technology, the needs for autonomization and the cooperation between vehicles and things. New radars, with faster and digital control, with capability to handle multiple adaptive beams, are necessary. This article presents an array of 8 slot antennas, modular and designed for 24GHz, which can be scaled to larger arrays for use in the modern radar systems.

articleTitle: Study on Directional Radiation Characteristics of Ultra- Wideband Dielectric Rod Antenna Based on Traveling Wave Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to explain the stable directional radiation characteristics of dielectric rod antenna, a traveling wave model is established based on the simulation of the electric field distribution in the dielectric rod. The dielectric rod antenna is regarded as a traveling wave continuous array with small aperture and the pattern function expression of dielectric rod antenna in broadband is obtained in the model, and the patterns drawn by the expression are in good agreement with the patterns obtained by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software simulation, which proves the correctness of the proposed method. The simulation results show that the field distribution in the dielectric rod is the traveling wave mode.

articleTitle: Metagratings for Perfect Anomalous Refraction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We formulate a design procedure for metagratings (MGs), periodic structures composed of only a handful of polarizable particles (meta-atoms) per period, for perfect anomalous refraction. The MGs are comprised of three layers of metallic strips loaded by printed capacitors, whose individual geometry and respective positions can be tied to the scattered fields in an analytical manner. Utilizing the analytical model, we derive conditions on the multilayered configuration and the capacitive loads that would yield perfect coupling of an incident wave towards a desirable refraction angle, while suppressing coupling to all other propagating spurious Floquet-Bloch modes. The simultaneous semianalytical resolution of multiple degrees of freedom, verified via full-wave simulations, demonstrates the potential of MGs as a platform for extreme wave manipulation, greatly reducing the computational effort typically required to obtain physical realizations of comparable metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Using Resonance Coupling Method for Implantable Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a physically small wireless power transfer (WPT) system that is able to provide a high power transfer efficiency using the resonance coupling method for implantable applications. The resonant circuit topologies used at the transmitter and receiver are Series and Parallel respectively (referred to as an SP topology). The circuits utilize loop antennas and are designed to operate at 403 MHz and the power transfer efficiency can reach 85.66%. The effects of varying power transfer distance and load impedance on the system performance are inspected via software simulation.

articleTitle: Beam Domain Formulation for Tomographic Inverse Scattering. Part I: The Forward Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a local UWB inverse scattering approach using pulsed-beam wave processing. The theory utilizes a phase-space set of shifted titled and delayed pulse-beams which has been shown previously to constitute a frame at any z= canst. plane, thus providing a local alternative to the plane-wave spectrum. This pulsed-beam frame (PBF) is used here to expend the scattering data and then back-propagate it for local reconstruction of the medium. In this paper we explore the beam-domain representation of the scattered fields and show, within the Born approximation, that the beam-domain data correspond to local Radon transform (LRT) of the medium. This result will be used in Part II of this paper for local reconstruction within this subdomain.

articleTitle: Multiple Directional Radiation Patterns, Integrated Antenna for ATSC-TV Indoor Reception
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact, wideband, four directional radiation patterns, antenna. The radiating element topology is inspired from the Annular Slot Antenna (ASA) and printed wideband monopole. The antenna is designed for North American ATSC-TV indoor reception. For an S11<;-6dB, it covers both High-VHF and UHF bands. It presents four relatively uncorrelated patterns. The antenna simulated performances are thoroughly analyzed and validated via measurements.

articleTitle: Beam pattern measurement on offset Gregorian reflector mounted with a wideband room temperature receiver for the Square Kilometre Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present measured on-dish beam patterns for a room temperature spline-profile quad-ridge flared horn (QRFH) feed designed for the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) Band 1 covering 350-1050 MHz. The feed and LNA package has been mounted on the offset Gregorian SKA precursor prototype telescope, Dish Verification Antenna 1 (DVA-1) located at the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) near Penticton, British Columbia, Canada. Telescope beam pattern cuts are measured by sweeping over the sun and adding corrections for the solar disk size, elevation and aperture efficiency. Sensitivity calculated with measured receiver noise show good agreement with the predicted performance.

articleTitle: Beamforming Concept for Multi-Beam Antennas Based on Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel beamforming concept for small cells in 5G cellular systems at millimeter wave frequencies is proposed. Base station antenna arrays may be mounted on street lights or similar elevated structures to form small, densely deployed cells. In such a scenario, the power received by a mobile user within a cell depends on the scan angle due to varying directivity and propagation losses which has considerable impact on the base station efficiency. In order to overcome these issues, multi-beam antennas are employed as array elements. Depending on the scan angle, a suitable beam is selected and then steered towards the user. The multi-beam antennas are designed by means of the theory of characteristic modes. The basic feasibility of the proposed concept is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Novel L-CRLH Based Compact Wide Band Filtered Power Divider for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new compact power divider based on inductor loaded composite right/left-handed transmission line (L-CRLH) is presented in this paper. The proposed power divider size is only 17.3 × 15.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, (0.53×0.47) λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> g at mid frequency. The results show 3 dB insertion losses and 14 dB return losses at each output port in the frequency band 5 GHz to 6.5 GHz. Moreover, the power divider has filtering function

articleTitle: A Design of Dual-band Circularly Polarized Millimeter-wave Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-feed dual-band circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna operating in Ka-band is proposed. The lower band and the upper band are excited by Archimedean spiral radiator. The main polarization mode of two resonant frequency (29 GHz and 38 GHz) are left-hand circular polarization(LHCP). The antenna achieves a small frequency ratio(1.31). The overlaps between -10 dB impedance bandwidth and axial ratio 3-dB bandwidth are 1.3 GHz(4.5% at 29 GHz) and 2.4 GHz (6.3% at 38 GHz).

articleTitle: A Novel Four-Port Pattern Diversity Antenna for 4G Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an angular symmetric, common radiator with separated ground plane coplanar waveguide fed four-port antenna is analyzed. The antenna is designed on a 183mm×183mm×6.35mm Polyguide substrate to cover 4G communication bands extending from 0.68-1 GHz long-term evolution (LTE) band, 2.5-2.9 GHz, 4.8 GHz-7.2 GHz (S11 = -10 dB criteria). The additional results would be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Refinement and Unification of Checkerboard and Gradient Index RCS-Reduction Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel radar cross section (RCS)-reduction technique, which unifies the concepts of checkerboard metasurfaces (CMS) and gradient index metasurfaces (GIMS), is presented. More importantly, it refines the concepts of both of these meta-surfaces as well as overcomes numerous limitations associated with them. A sample metasurface is fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: A Heart-Like Unidirectional Millimeter-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A heart-like unidirectional millimeter-wave antenna is devised to obtain wide bandwidth and unidirectional radiation patterns. The designed heart-like antenna is composed of a heart-like radiating patch with a C-like parasitic strip, CPW ground plane, a copper cavity-backed designed on the back of the substrate. The copper cavity-backed structure is to reduce the back radiation and can get a better directional characteristic. The proposed antenna has a bandwidth ranges from 30.4GHz to 43.85GHz, indicating a relative bandwidth of 36.2%. Also, the proposed antenna has a great unidirectional radiation characteristic. The results show that the proposed heart-like millimeter-wave antenna possesses a huge bandwidth and amazing unidirectional radiation patterns.

articleTitle: A V-Band Patch Array for Drone Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present our design of a v-band patch array for compact, lightweight, and power efficient drone radar. The 60 GHz radar has a bandwidth of 7GHz. Several compact V-band antennas, such as Yagi, patch, aperture coupled and dual-slits patch antenna are studied and compared. The impact of different antenna design on the compact radar board geometry and quality of performance was analyzed.

articleTitle: Some Considerations on the Physical Meaning of Orthogonality Sampling Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The orthogonality sampling method has been recently introduced in inverse scattering literature to perform the reconstruction of the morphological properties of unknown targets. With respect to other qualitative methods, orthogonality sampling shows attractive features, namely the remarkable simplicity and the possibility of being exploited also for a single incidence. However, notwithstanding its straightforwardness and effectiveness, the physical meaning of the method is not yet fully assessed. Since such an understanding would be helpful to take full advantage of its features, in this contribution we present a first attempt to formulate a physical interpretation of the method.

articleTitle: A Single-layer Series-fed Microstrip Array with Enhanced Bandwidth for Automotive Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A series-fed antenna array is designed on a single-layer substrate with enhanced bandwidth to provide a cost-effective solution for automotive radar systems. Coplanar coupled feed is used to enhance the impedance bandwidth of a conventional rectangular patch. Differential feed technique is applied to cancel the inherent directional offset of the radiating patches. And the feed network is designed based on the Taylor distribution of the current to obtain low side lobe. The simulation results show that the proposed array exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 1180 MHz ranging from 23.6 GHz to 24.78 GHz. The gain is better than 15.5 dBi in bandwidth, and the side lobe level is lower than −23 dB.

articleTitle: Mode-Based MIMO Antenna with Polarization and Pattern Diversity for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new design approach for multi-element MIMO antennas that exploit the mode-based technique. Such a technique applied to a multi-element antenna with circular symmetry allows to obtain orthogonal radiation patterns and full port decoupling by means of a mode decomposition network (MDN). Typically, the MDN input ports require matching networks to achieve proper antenna operation. The objective of the proposed design approach is to overcome the need of such matching networks therefore enabling wider operating bandwidths. This approach is then used to design a four-element MIMO antenna capable to achieve polarization and pattern diversity by means of four radiation patterns directed along a hemisphere. Simulation results of the antenna show that very low envelope correlation coefficients (ECC) and good mean effective gains (MEG) can be achieved. These features along with full port decoupling make the proposed antenna design very attractive for base station applications of next generation.

articleTitle: Compact Waveguide-to-Microstrip Transition with Embedded Power Divider for mmWave Antenna Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel waveguide-to-microstrip transition with an embedded 1:4 power divider for millimeter-wave antenna array applications. The proposed transition design consists of a machined spacer and a coupling patch printed on a single layer PCB substrate. Additionally, a 1:4 power divider is embedded in the coupling patch design, making the total transition area very compact. The power divider incorporates differential ports that eliminate the extra delay line and facilitate the symmetry of the feeding layout about the center of a 2D antenna array structure. The center-feeding scheme is desirable for a large antenna array as it enhances the mechanical robustness and reduces the feeding line loss simultaneously. The resultant transmission loss of the proposed transition is only 0.8 dB at 24GHz.

articleTitle: Small Epidermal UHF RFID Loop Antenna for Passive Oral Cavity Control Applications and Patient Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces small loop type antennas and their potential for use in UHF RFID far-field applications. They are typically known as `magnetic loops' and an established antenna for HF applications. Here we evaluate their potential for use, both by simulation and measurement in the challenging environment of the oral cavity for patient health monitoring and assistive technologies.

articleTitle: Wideband Compact Slot Antenna Based on Triple-Resonance Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slot antenna based on triple-resonance cylindrical substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity is presented in this paper, which shows a wideband property and also a stable radiation pattern over a whole working frequency band of interest. The wideband property is realized by combining high-order modes (TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub>, and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub>) of the cylindrical cavity. This antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 270/0 with S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10dB, from 15.5GHz to 20.5GHz. Compared with other wideband SIW cavity-backed slot antennas, which work with the same principle (multimode resonance), the proposed antenna has a compact size, whose diameter is about O.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> denotes to the wavelength of waveguide corresponding to the lowest operating frequency). The structure is simple, easy to fabricate by using planar circuit board technology and can be integrated with other planar circuits. It can be applied to advanced communication systems thanks to its simple structure, wideband property, and broadside radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Broadband Frequency Reconfigurable Metamaterial Absorber using Switchable Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a broadband Frequency reconfigurable metamaterial absorber using a switchable ground plane (SGP). We proposed the multi-layers and a PIN diode of middle layer for the SGP. Because between the top structure and the bottom ground plane determined the resonant frequency, the switchable ground plane is proposed. When the PIN diode of the SGP turns off, the middle layer becomes reactive and bottom ground plane is working as ground plane of the absorber. On the other hand, when the PIN diode of the SGP turns on, the middle layer becomes ground plane and the bottom ground plane does not affect the absorber. The proposed absorber is demonstrated by full-wave simulation and measurement. The fabricated sample with 27 × 27unit cells is measured for the absorption under normal incidence. When the PIN diode of the SGP turns on, the absorption with more than 90% is achieved from 3.5 to 11 GHz. On the other hand, when the PIN diode of the SGP turns off, the absorption with more than 90% is achieved from 1.7 to 5.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Effects of Complex Wall Structures on Antenna Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Future indoor wireless systems must have a high level of performance in terms of quality and capacity. High performance systems require careful deployment of access points. However, there are relatively few degrees of freedom available to the system planner during the deployment of these systems. The antenna type, location and orientation need to be carefully selected to achieve high performance, as measured path losses can be significantly affected by the antenna's radiation characteristics. Most studies of antenna deployment effects on indoor wireless system performance make use of radiation patterns measured in free-space conditions. In practice, antennas will be mounted on complex inhomogeneous dielectric structures such as cavity walls (comprised of two drywall layers with timber or steel supporting frames). This paper reports results of a research project investigating how complex cavity wall structures influence the radiation characteristics of access point antennas, and to what extent any such effects could be exploited to improve system performance.

articleTitle: A Research on Broadband DOA Technology Based on Virtual-Stagger Baseline
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For the problem of phase difference ambiguity using multi-baseline interferometers in direction finding, a mixed method is proposed for solving the phase difference variety ambiguity by stagger distance difference and short virtual baseline after the analysis of the phase difference. Computer experimental analysis gives the results of the simulation experiment in angle error and the successful probability of solving ambiguity.

articleTitle: The scattering of Vortex Electromagnetic Waves by a coated sphere
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The scattering characteristic of vortex electromagnetic wave with different orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes by a coated sphere are studied by using the generalized Lorenz-Mie theory. Results indicate that when topological charge l increases, the Radar Cross-Section (RCS) of particle alternating appear extreme values in the forward and backward scattering. With the increasing of the radius of the outer sphere, the RCS increases, while the RCS decreases as the inner radius grows.

articleTitle: An Explicit Marching-on-in-time Scheme for Solving the Kirchhoff Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An explicit marching-on-in-time scheme for solving the Kirchhoff integral equation enforced on an acoustically rigid scatterer is proposed. The unknown velocity potential introduced on the surface of scatterer is expanded using unit pulse functions in space and Lagrange polynomial interpolation functions in time. The resulting system is cast in the form of an ordinary differential equation and then integrated numerically in time using a predictor-corrector scheme to obtain the unknown expansion coefficients. Numerical results demonstrate that the time step size required by the proposed explicit scheme to ensure an accurate and stable solution is as large as that used by its implicit counterpart.

articleTitle: Multi-parameter Microwave Inverse Scattering with Group Sparsity Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a multi-parameter inverse scattering method with group sparsity constraint, which improves the image reconstruction results in case the images of different parameters have similar shape or structure. In inverse scattering imaging, the system of equations to be solved is often under-determined where the number of measurements is less than the number of image pixels. This becomes even worse for objects described by a multi-parameter material model where the total number of unknowns grows by a factor of the number of material parameters. However, in many cases, images of different material parameters, such as permittivity and conductivity, share similar structure or shape, where group sparsity regularization can be used to effectively capture this prior information. We compare the inverse scattering of 3-parameter dispersive material objects using Tikhonov, sparsity, and group-sparsity regularization. After minimizing to the same measurement objective function error, compared with Tikhonov and sparsity regularization, the group sparsity regularized inversion produces a better shape and contrast reconstruction of all 3 parameters and achieves the lowest overall image pixel value error.

articleTitle: E-Band High Gain Gap Waveguide Slot Array Antenna with ETSI Class-III Radiation Pattern Suitable for Mass Production
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As a low loss transmission line and low cost technology, gap waveguide has been shown to be an attractive solution for several millimeter-wave applications. A high gain antenna has been designed and manufactured to be used in fixed beam applications at E-band. Good agreement between simulations and measurements for radiation patterns, gain values and reflection coefficient are shown. The design is suitable to be used for mass production using injection molding process.

articleTitle: UWB Radar Sensor Development using Drone Arms for Sensing Applicaions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes the wrapped version of the bowtie antenna around a drone arm for ultra-wideband (UWB) based sensing applications. Several antenna variations were studied and a comparison highlighting expected performance metrics is presented.

articleTitle: Compact Planar Antenna System for Full- Duplex Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Orthogonal polarization and ninety-degree rotational symmetry are used to design a compact antenna system with high port isolation for full-duplex wireless applications. Two transmitter and two receiver elements are fed perfectly out of phase with wideband one-hundred-eighty-degree couplers. The system is modeled, achieving a simulated isolation of greater than 52.3 dB and gain of greater than 8.6 dB over the band from 5.24 to 6.94 GHz.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a Monopole Antenna in the Vicinity of a Grounded Cylindrical Stratified Media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a monopole antenna radiating near a grounded cylindrical stratified media is characterized. The impact of a single conducting cylinder and a dielectric coated conducting cylinder on the performance of the monopole is investigated. An impedance bandwidth of 41.53% is achieved for a monopole radiating in the presence of a coated cylindrical conductor. The optimized result obtained through simulations is compared using the full-wave Green's function approach.

articleTitle: Radially Arrayed CP Metamaterial Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An array antenna composed of eight metamaterial lines printed radially on a dielectric substrate is analyzed. The unit cell for the metamaterial lines is designed to radiate a circularly polarized (CP) wave. Analysis shows that the array is reconfigurable and has a half-power beam width of 193° in the azimuth plane, a gain of approximately 4.7 dBi, and a VSWR of 2.2 at the design frequency, when one of the eight feed points is activated (1FP activation). The gain increases to approximately 7.3 dBi when two feed points are activated (2FP activation).

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Probe Immunity to Absorber Plate Position
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dual-polarized probes with wide-bandwidth operational capabilities are highly desirable for time-efficient Planar Near-Field (PNF) measurements [1]-[2]. However, sometimes the performance tradeoffs necessary to achieve the desired operating bandwidth make such probes impractical for many applications. Traditional probes are often bandwidth limited, and their electrical size can be an undesired source of scattering in PNF measurements, especially if the probe-AUT distance is small. A novel octave-band probe has recently been presented combining wide bandwidth, near constant directivity, low cross-polarization, and minimum scattering [3]. Since the probes have a very broad pattern, an absorber collar must be placed behind the probe to prevent reflections from the metal flange, the coax adapter, and mounting structures behind the probe being received by the probe. In this paper the effect of the absorber plate on the measured antenna radiation pattern will be investigated by the use of the inverse source method [6]-[7] implemented in the software INSIGHT [8]. In particular, equivalent currents on the absorbers collar will be filtered in order to quantify their disturbing effect on the main radiation of the antenna aperture.

articleTitle: Generalized Quasi-Static Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Maxwellian equations are determined for generalized quasi-static electromagnetic fields used to define the quality factor for electrically small antennas that are allowed to contain highly dispersive lossy material. Only the original nonquasi-static source densities are required. The generalized quasi-static fields eliminate the radiation fields but involve the inductive fields as well as the conventional quasi-static fields.

articleTitle: Transfer Matrix Method Extension to Space- Time Modulated Electromagnetic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Transfer Matrix Method (TMM), commonly used in problems involving purely spatial discontinuities, is extended to the problem with space-time discontinuities, of great interest in emerging space-time metamaterials.

articleTitle: Radiation by an Aperture in a Planar Screen Illuminated by a Gaussian Beam at Optical Frequencies for Studying Baffle Scattering in Interferometric Detectors of Gravitational Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Field from apertures large in terms of wavelength, can be obtained via Kirchhoff approximation as a surface integral on physical optics currents, and corrected via fringe currents evaluation. If the aperture is very large in terms of wavelength, surface integral can be costly to compute, and formulas allowing its reduction to a line integral be more effective.

articleTitle: Empirical Technique for Meeting Balance Condition of Coupled-Line Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses the empirical investigation of a coupled-line leaky-wave antenna's matching which allows to suppress the stop-band appearing at the transition frequency corresponding to a broadside beam. The presented technique allows to estimate the required modification of the unit cell's dimensions necessary to meet the balance condition. To determine which element of the unit cell should be modified dielectric samples are being placed on top of either short-circuited or connected in cascade transmission-line sections. The achieved substantial improvement of the measured S-parameters proves the correctness of such an approach.

articleTitle: Compact Overlapping Annular Slot Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four-element annular slot array is presented for applications requiring omnidirectional gain with minimal variation in azimuthal gain and phase. Cavity-backed annular slots are overlapped to form a single compact array aperture. The slot feed structures are designed to reduce undesirable modes and inter-element coupling. The resulting array achieves a simulated 2.5:1 VSWR bandwidth of 26% with less than +/-1 dB of azimuthal gain pattern ripple at the horizon and less than +/- 20 degrees of horizon azimuthal phase ripple.

articleTitle: High Gain Left Hand Circular Polarized Millimeter-Wave Radial Line Slot Antenna with Low Side Lobe Level
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain Radial Line Slot Antenna (RLSA) with left hand circular polarization (LHCP) and low side lobe level (SLL) at millimeter-wave band is presented. The orientation of the slots reduced the SLL below -30 dB at 29.2 GHz. The gain of the antenna is 20 dB and the radiation efficiency is 84%. The antenna has symmetrical radiation pattern for both planes. The antenna is suitable for 5G wireless communication at base station.

articleTitle: New techniques for the evaluation of antenna performances in ground stations for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new powerful technique for evaluating the RF performance of satellite antenna terminals and calculating the transmit eirp density restrictions to cope with the ITV standards for reduced satellite orbital separations.

articleTitle: Curvature and Slope Correction in High-Frequency Diffraction at Thin Dielectric Layers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Finding the higher-order terms for the electromagnetic diffraction at a thin dielectric layer is reduced to a sequence of standard 1D boundary-value problems (BVPs) of a certain type. The solvability and the uniqueness of solution for such BVP are proven. The higher-order terms for the curvature and slope correction are obtained in the closed form. Numerical results are verified by a comparison with the data computed with an accurate method.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf analysis of the scattering by a two dimensional periodic semi - infinite array of dipoles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a rigorous solution of the scattering of plane waves by a truncated planar array of dipoles which is infinite and periodic in one direction and semi-infinite in the orthogonal direction, thus presenting an edge truncation. By applying the Wiener-Hopf technique to the Z-transformed system of equations derived from the electric field integral equation, the contributions to the current on the dipoles due to the scattering by the edge of the array and the excitation of surface waves are obtained rigorously.

articleTitle: The Concept of Recoverable Energy
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, the concept of recoverable energy has been revisited by working it out for real radiators. This energy is the maximum energy that can be recovered from the field distribution in space generated by a radiating device up to the time point considered. This paper discusses this concept from a physical point of view. It starts from the basics and builds a physical line of reasoning that ends with the question whether this energy can be identified with the concept of “stored energy”, a quantity studied in literature by numerous authors.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Printed Antenna with Quad-crossed Dipobles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband circularly polarized (CP) printed antenna with a quad-crossed dipoles is proposed, fabricated and measured. The antenna consists of a trapezoidal transformation balun, a three-quarter annular transmission line (TL) and four radiant dipoles. The total size of the proposed antenna is 70×70×2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. This printed planar antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 48.5% (1.59-2.61 GHz) for the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) <; 2. The 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 33.4% (1.59-2.26 GHz). A peak gain of 2.8 dBic and a half power beam width (HPBW) more than 116° are achieved.

articleTitle: Coordinate Transformation Based Field Tapering Device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Spatial coordinate transformations can be used in the design of electromagnetic devices with unconventional and exotic behavior. However, their realizations are generally limited by the complex material properties that are required. In this paper, the coordinate transformation technique is employed to successfully design two field tapering devices. 2D continuous models are presented that confirm the desired field tapering functionality for the targeted microwave frequency band. Next, a scheme that utilizes a method of parameter reduction to simplify the complicated tensors produced by the conventional coordinate transformation technique is applied to one of the taper designs. A two-step procedure is introduced to simplify the tensor properties of the material by eliminating non-diagonal components. Furthermore, the resulting permittivity and permeability distributions for the taper device are calculated and presented.

articleTitle: A Stable Low Frequency Time Domain EFIE with Weighted Continuity Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new time domain electric field integral equation is proposed to solve low frequency problems. This new formulation uses the current and charge densities as unknowns, with a form of the continuity equation that is weighted by a Green's function as a second constraining equation. This equation can be derived from a scalar potential equivalence principle integral equation, which is in contrast to the traditional strong form of the continuity equation that has been used in an ad-hoc manner in the augmented EFIE. Numerical results demonstrate the improved stability of this approach, as well as the accuracy at low frequencies.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Broadband Fast Multipole Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband fast multipole algorithm (FMA) is proposed using a hybridization of the plane wave and multipole expansions of the Green's function. By representing the low order harmonics using the plane wave expansion and representing the high order harmonics using the multipole expansion, the proposed method is accurate at all frequencies. The error analysis is performed to achieve arbitrarily high accuracies. The method can be regarded as a unification of the conventional dense and diagonal FMAs. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Subsurface Cylindrical Cavity Detection via TE and TM Mode Mismatch Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method to detect cylindrical cavities in the subsurface of a lossy-dielectric using low-frequency resonance mode scattering in the transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes is presented. The technique offers a method to detect a cylindrical cavity in the sub-surface and find the cross sectional area of the cavity. Experimental data is shown to confirm the correlation between observed and theoretical data.

articleTitle: On a Conforming Impedance Boundary Condition EFIE
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a fully conforming Impedance Boundary Condition - Electric Field Integral Equation (IBC-EFIE) that is shown to be stable both at low frequency and for dense meshes. In this work, the classical IBC is replaced by a conforming one that takes into account the skin depth of the scatterer. It is shown this equation can be stabilized in the low frequency regime using quasi-Helmholtz operators and in the dense grid regime using a traditional Calderón preconditioner.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of a New Planar Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new class of low side lobe, rectangular planar arrays with monotonically decreasing nonuniform excitations is examined. Simulation results for directivity, side lobe level, and half-power beamwidths, are presented and their variations with the new array parameters and the direction of the pattern main beam maximum are discussed.

articleTitle: Circulary Polarized Antenna for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work is focused on the design and simulation of a resonant box type antenna with crossed slots and circular polarization. This design is done in order to implement RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) systems for logistics and IST (Intelligent Transport Systems) applications operating in the 915MHz ISM (Industrial, Scientific and Medical) band.

articleTitle: Wideband Antennas for Microwave Brain Stroke Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a monopole antenna designed to operate in a matching medium is described. The dimensions of the antenna is optimized with Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) to obtain the desired reflection coefficient and gain characteristics. All simulations are performed with HFSS in an automated manner by the PSO algorithm via Matlab. The reflection coefficient of the antenna is tested by embedding it to the characterized matching medium. The dielectric properties of the medium is verified with the well known open ended coaxial probe measurement technique. The antenna will be tested with a phantom material mimicking the brain tissues and the results of the microwave imagine algorithm will be presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of the PML Performance on Spherical FDTD Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We evaluate the performance of the spherical perfectly matched layer (PML) applied to the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm implemented in spherical staggered grids. The spherical PML performance is evaluated by simulating the fields produced by electric dipoles within spherical FDTD grids terminated by a (spherical) PML, and computing the reflection error. The influence of several parameters on the PML reflection error is examined.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID Tags' Identification Algorithm by Using an Eigenmode Approach Combined with Signal-Processing Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel identification algorithm of chipless RFID tags by using an eigenmode analysis based on the SVD-decomposition, in conjunction with a signal-processing technique is presented. We start by extract a dominant eigenmode of the tag and show that we can significantly enhance the capability to carry out the scatterer recognition by exciting the tag with a transmitter antenna array with an excitation coefficient associated to the dominant mode. Later, a signal-processing algorithm is proposed to identify a tag based on the signals received by an array including fields scattered from the direct coupling between the transmitter and the receiver antennas in presence and in absence of the tag in the reader area. In addition, an identification vector is processed to detect the presence of multiple chipless tags simultaneously with range information and to identify a particular tag.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized antenna array with integrated low noise amplifier into the lightweight antenna composite structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the paper we present results of our research on integrating dual-polarized circular patch antenna and column of eight such antenna elements with low noise amplifier made in monolithic integrated circuit technology. The antenna operates in C band and is made with composite panel. Two different types of amplifiers are considered.

articleTitle: A Radial Multi-Mode Filtering Power Divider for Antenna Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A symmetric radial filtering power divider is presented herein. The power divider is implemented in a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and is designed using filter theory to obtain equal 6-way power division with a filtering function to each port. The filter/power divider operates at a center frequency of 11.53 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 37.2%, insertion loss of 8.44 dB to each port, and worst-case isolation of 9 dB between ports.

articleTitle: Antennas for Deep Space: Design and Technology Challenges
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper highlights the High Gain Antenna (HGA) RF and Thermo-Mechanical design solutions adopted by Thales Alenia Space Italia in deep space missions, supported by the European Space Agency (ESA) with different mission profiles and different environments. Present technology challenges are also highlighted.

articleTitle: Polarization independent Frequency Selective Surface Design Using Rotated Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design of frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented in this paper. Multi-resonant type structure is adopted in the element design, which consists of symmetrical microstrip units printed on two sides of the thin substrate. The basic type of FSS achieves a second-order bandpass property in the X band, and two transmission zeros exist on both sides of the passband. In addition, an improved FSS structure is developed by 90° rotating the basic unit cells. Stable bandpass transmission responses are achieved for either the TE or TM polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Ultra-Wideband Signals Using Direct RF Sampling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a direction finding (DF) system using a Direct RF sampling technique. This technique promotes a low cost and versatile approach with minimum complexity. Specifically, a high-speed Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) as a transmitter and a high speed Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) as a receiver are used. The transmitted signal was a random Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) Signal, coded with a Gold code of length 127. The total bandwidth is approximately 1.3 GHz.

articleTitle: A Correction for Free-space Method by Considering Dispersion of Gaussian Beam
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Frequency dependence of beam waist radius is discussed based on the dispersion property of Gaussian beam, and cutoff frequency of Gaussian beam is deduced by an analogy with the metallic waveguide. For the free-space test system that using focusing antennas with a Gaussian beam illumination, the effect of this dispersion property on material electromagnetic parameters test is analyzed.
