Correction factor that introducing beam waist radius is proposed to improve the test precision of free-space method.

articleTitle: On the Treatment of Strongly Singular Integrals Over Flat Triangular Domains
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional Method of Moment (MoM) employs divergence-conforming basis functions to expand unknown current densities so that the treatment of higher-order singular integrals can be facilitated. Compared with MoM, the Nyström method interpolates unknown functions with polynomials of arbitrary orders, which not only decreases the computational cost of matrix entries, but also enables the use of nonconforming grids. However, the Nyström method must treat the higher-order singular integrals related to dyadic Green's function. The dyadic Green's function gives rise to strongly singular integrals which are challenging to handle. This paper presents new closed-form formulas for calculating strongly singular integrals. A numerical example is used to demonstrate the approach and good result has been observed.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces to Control Direction of Wave Propagation at the Same Frequency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study, we demonstrate circuit-based metasurfaces, or the so-called waveform-selective metasurfaces (WSMs), to control the transmittances of various surface waves at the same frequency in response to their pulse widths. Especially, we show three types of WSMs that preferentially transmit either of a short pulse, a continuous wave, or an intermediate pulse at a constant frequency. These structures are all combined to allow the propagation of surface waves to different directions depending on their pulse widths. Thus, the concept of these structures can be potentially exploited for new solutions to electromagnetic interference issues, antenna designs, and wireless communications at the same frequency.

articleTitle: Near-Field Multi-Beam-Splitting for Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna system
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Near-field multi-beam-splitting Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC) antenna systems are proposed. A cavity-backed coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed slot antenna is combined with orientation-sensitive FSS designs. Vertically oriented unit cells in the uniform FSS design (FSS-AH) split main beam from a source into two or four beams.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Extremely Low-profile Antenna for Low-VHF Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an extremely low-profile antenna with high gain assisted by parasitic elements is presented. This work is based on a previously-designed short monopole antenna. By introducing eight parasitic elements with identical structures, the proposed antenna achieves substantial gain enhancement compared with the short monopole while maintaining the same height (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/150). The antenna is then modified for frequency tuning by adding a tunable trimmer capacitor to the feed. This simple tuning technique significantly improves the fractional bandwidth of the antenna and provides a return loss of better than 10dB within the entire tuning range.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Assisted Multi-Objective Antenna Design with Equal-Compartment-Size Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-cost procedure for multi-objective design optimization of antenna structures is proposed. Our approach exploits variable-fidelity EM simulations, kriging surrogates, and domain segmentation to reduce the volume of the design space to be sampled for the sake of surrogate model construction. Design space compartments created during segmentation are enforced to be of equal volume which reduces the number of training samples as compared to the standard segmentation. The operation and performance of the proposed technique is demonstrated using a UWB monopole antenna example.

articleTitle: Exponentially Tapered TEM Horn Antenna with Dielectric Support for Monopolar Input Pulses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an exponentially tapered TEM horn antenna with dielectric support for monopolar input pulse is proposed. FR-4 substrate is used as dielectric plates with simple feed and slots are introduced in the TEM horn antenna. The characteristics of the antenna such as return loss, realized gain, E-field, radiation pattern are simulated and return loss is compared with the measured result. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the designed antenna is from 0.6 GHz to around 4 GHz with gain around 6 dB or above for most of the frequency range.

articleTitle: Loss Contributions in V-band Substrate Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The loss contributions are estimated at V-band (60GHz) for the components of Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) as a function of copper plane and via roughness, substrate thickness, and frequency. This can be done only by simulation and very careful and precise application of CST is used. Knowing these loss contributions paves the way for better informed SIW design, including configuration and materials usage.

articleTitle: Development of a Textile Antenna Using a Continuous Substrate Integrating the Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The exponential growth in the wearable market is boosting the industrialization process of manufacturing textile antennas. The patch of the printed antennas can be easily cut, embroidered or screen printed by machines. The conception of an optimal industrial substrate that meets all the mechanical and electromagnetic requirements is still a challenge. This paper presents a printed textile antenna for ISM band using a continuous Substrate Integrating the Ground Plane (SIGP). The SIGP is a novel textile material, which is a double fabric that integrates the dielectric substrate and the conductive ground plane in a single textile.

articleTitle: Packaging Considerations for Integration of mm-Wave Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Although mm-wave phased array antennas can be well integrated with other parts of the circuit (e.g., chip package) due to compact size, they are more sensitive to device-level implementations. This paper reviews different possible integrations, and investigates some of the far-field effects due to device-level implementations. Experimental studies and comparisons are presented for an end-fire phased array antenna at 60 GHz unlicensed frequency band.

articleTitle: Time Dispersion Indoor Channel Characterization in the 8–12 GHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present measured and simulated time dispersion results for two indoor scenarios in the 8-12 G Hz frequency band. The simulated results have been obtained with a full 3D ray-tracing model. The comparison between measured and simulated data shows the potential of these models to describe the time dispersion behavior of the propagation channel at high frequencies. The results reported can be useful for the design and deployment of future wireless systems.

articleTitle: Two-Step Optimization of Linear Distributed Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Coherent distributed arrays are composed of widely separated elements which are coherently coordinated for distributed phase-coherent operations. Such arrays are inherently sparse, and thus their radiation patterns are characterized by significant sidelobe energy. In this work, we explore the use of a two-step optimization routine to mitigate sidelobe energy within a window around the mainbeam in extremely sparse arrays. We consider a linear sparse linear array consisting of 9 distributed elements within a span of 1000A, each with a minimum distance of 10λ separation. The two-step optimization consists of an initial genetic algorithm (GA) optimization routine as a coarse layout design after which a particle swarm optimization (PSO) routine is used to refine the solution. We show that the GA achieves > 10 dB sidelobe suppression within a 10° region, and the PSO step improves this by > 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: Samsung Smart Antenna Technology(SSAT) using the closed-loop auto frequency tuning algorithm for portable handset
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we proposed and implemented a new antenna closed-loop algorithm which was the useful method for improving the radiation performance of a portable handset. The proposed method was solved narrow tuning ranges and complexity of realization in the conventional antenna closed-loop algorithm with impedance loading. As the results of applying the proposed antenna closed-loop algorithm with aperture loading to commercial handset, the radiation performance was improved up to 7 dB at LTE and WCDMA low band on a flat handy phantom. This result was dramatically improvement of a radiation performance on degradation conditions due to external factors of a portable handset.

articleTitle: SIW Structure Explored as a Low-Profile Wideband Antenna bearing User-Friendly Characteristics for Wireless Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact low profile wideband antenna is developed and discussed. Its basic structure is derived from the circular cavity following the repetitive segmentation along the quasi-magnetic wall to obtain the 16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> mode geometry. Periodic slots have been etched out alternatively from the top metallic surface, the thickness of which has been engineered to obtain wideband operation from the antenna. The ground plane has been modified for achieving an user-friendly radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: An I-slab System for Tilted Beam Formation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses an antenna system designated as the I-slab system (where the number of slabs is I = 1, 2). All slabs have square loops made of conducting strips. For the analysis, the loops have a fixed outer side length and different inner side lengths, i.e., the loops have different strip widths. The analysis reveals how the scattering parameters for the unit cell constituting the I-slab system change with the loop strip width. The tilt angle of the beam radiated from the I-slab system is estimated based on the scattering parameters and compared to results obtained using full wave analysis.

articleTitle: Generation of Dual-Polarized Dual-Mode OAM Radio Beams Through Transmit-Array Lens
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-polarized transmit-array lens (TAL) is presented for the generation of dual-mode convergent orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams in C-band. The proposed TAL consists of dual-polarized metamaterial unit cells, which are composed of four stacked patches coupled by cross aperture, to complete the phase correction for both polarizations and stimulate the dual-mode convergent OAM beams. The simulated results verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Implementation of a novel two port four element rectangular patch array antenna with tunable circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design of a circularly polarized four element patch array antenna is discussed. The proposed design consists of two ports each of them placed on either sides of the radiating elements. Due to the presence of two ports, the idea of using the antenna also as a filter element is explained. The concept of encrypted polarization is introduced where circularly polarized radiated waves can be left-handed or right-handed at a particular instant in time. This shift in polarization state is controllable and switchable dynamically. Simulated results successfully validate this idea.

articleTitle: Wideband Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna with Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband reconfigurable antenna with righthanded circular polarization (RHCP), left-handed circular polarization (LHCP), and linear polarization (LP) is proposed. The antenna consists of a cross slot antenna and a metasurface. Four pin diodes are connected between the slots to achieve the polarization reconfiguration. By loading the metasurface above the slot antenna, the axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) can be enhanced, and the boresight gain is also increased. The simulated results show that this antenna in RHCP/LHCP has a very wide impedance bandwidth (IMBW) of 4.25~6.52 GHz (42.2 %) and ARBW of 4.79~6.26 GHz (26.6%). The antenna in LP has an IMBW of 5.33~5.84 GHz (9.1%).

articleTitle: Accurate Solution of Müller Equations for Electromagnetic Analysis of Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) equations are widely used to describe electromagnetic problems with penetrable media and the Müller equations with a similar form is less addressed. However, the Müller equations have certain merits in numerical solutions and it is necessary to investigate the robust approach of solving them. In the traditional method of methods (MoM), expensive conforming meshes are required in the geometric discretization and the electric and magnetic current densities on the material interfaces should be represented by appropriate basis functions. In this paper, we propose a Nyström method to solve the Müller equations and its advantages are demonstrated by a typical numerical example.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Synthetic Aperture Focusing for Packaging Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Synthetic aperture focusing technique is proposed for developing a packaging inspection system. The SAF algorithm is reformulated. The SAF reformulation is tested for a package inspection application with finite element simulation data.

articleTitle: Realization of Fourth Order Exceptional Points of Degeneracy in Uniform Coupled-Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present the general conditions to realize fourth order exceptional points of degeneracy (EPD) in two uniform (i.e., invariant along z) coupled transmission lines (CTLs). The CTLs are modeled as distributed generic components where each line (when uncoupled) may support forward propagation, backward propagation or evanescent modes. We show the novel and important fact that a fourth order EPD may be supported in uniform CTLs when there is coupling between a forward propagating mode and an evancent mode. We also provide a microstrip possible implementation of a uniform CTL exhibiting fourth order EPD using a very subwavelength unit cell length.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Computation in Time Domain for Cylindrical Optical Cavities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate the computation of resonance frequencies and quality factors in an optical cylindrical cavity with a curved upper distributed Bragg reflector (DBR). Both values of interest shall be extracted from FDTD-like time domain simulations with an absorbing boundary condition (ABC). The quality factor solely originates from the light emission through the mirror (neglecting material losses) and hence strongly depends on the performance of the discretization and the ABC. Additionally, the fields in the cavity are slowly decaying and the structure of the DBR may lead to long setting times. Finally, we show, that both values converge w.r.t. the mesh resolution.

articleTitle: Cost Effective Smooth Walled Conical Horn Using Polynomial Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, design and results of a smooth walled conical horn using a novel polynomial interpolation approach is discussed. The simulated results for various parameters like return-loss, radiation patterns, peak gain, etc. are presented. It emerges that this type of a horn can be a suitable choice for many practical applications. This can also be used in place of a corrugated horn, which is quite challenging from manufacturing point of view especially at millimeter-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: A Graphical Method for the Preliminary Design of Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A graphical method for the preliminary design of phased array antennas is proposed. Despite its simplicity the proposed technique results computationally efficient and allows to estimate both the number of elements and their mutual distance, taking into account constraints on the side lobe level, the bandwidth and the beamwidth requirements.

articleTitle: Toward the Solution of the Two Wedge Problem by using the Generalized Wiener Hopf Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents our recent efforts in developing an effective technique based on Generalized Wiener-Hopf Technique (GWHT) to deal with the canonical diffraction problem constituted of two separate perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) wedges. The model considers the near field interaction between the two wedges.

articleTitle: A fully-3D-printed complementary right/left-handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this effort, a full-3D design of a complementary right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line structure with a transition frequency of 7.5GHz, which takes advantage of the unique capabilities of additive manufacturing technologies (AMT) is presented. A fully-additive fabrication process, combining SLA dielectric and aerosol conductor printing, is utilized. The fabricated CRLH structure is shown and measured. The approaches reported in this effort may set the foundation for the emergence of novel exotic metamaterial structures, enabled by the unique manufacturing capabilities of AMTs.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Broadband Planar Cavity-Backed Antenna with Approximately Symmetrical Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mmWave) broadband cavity-backed antenna with approximately symmetrical radiation pattern is proposed, which is fed by the substrate integrated waveguide. The proposed antenna exhibits excellent performance, including broad impedance bandwidth, stable radiation pattern, and compact structure. The antenna has approximately equal E-plane and H-plane radiation patterns. And its impedance bandwidth is 37.6% for| S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤ -10 dB. The 3dB-gain bandwidth is 31.9%. The proposed broadband antenna would be an attractive candidate for 5G mm Wave applications.

articleTitle: Subject-Specific, Helmet-Restraint, RF Coils for Awake, Non-Human Primate MR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In non-human primate [NHP] neuroimaging, the head needs to be immobilized. This is currently achieved via surgical implants; however, this method is invasive with risks of medical complications and limits the number of subjects that can enroll in a study due to the long waiting time after surgery for the implant area to heal and high cost. The purpose of this study is to demonstrate a non-invasive, subject-specific, restraint helmet with an integrated MRI RF coil. This system removes the need for invasive head post implantation and can be designed and implemented quickly at a low cost. Low dose computed tomography (CT) images were processed to create a subject-specific restraint helmet and structure of an RF coil. The helmet coil was 3D-printed from polylactic acid (PLA) plastic. The measured S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of the fabricated coil is -32 dB indicating a good match at 127.8 MHz (the frequency corresponding to 3T MRI). Imaging was performed on a MR spherical phantom, and a high signal- to- noise ratio of 924 in the region of interest was measured.

articleTitle: When Deployable Spacecraft Antennas Don't
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The objective of this paper is to explore possibilities for continued use of certain deployable spacecraft antennas when full deployment fails. Four (4) deployables are used as examples, including 1) a reflectarray, 2) a parabolic reflector, 3) a loop, and 4) a set of 4 monopoles. The measure of “continued usability” in each case is relative antenna gain as a function of partial deployment. Note, types (and levels) of partial deployment presented here are strictly hypothetical. Also, discussions of actual deployment mechanisms are considered outside the scope of this paper.

articleTitle: Dual-band Cavity-Backed Dipole Antenna for Millimeter- Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cavity-backed dipole antenna with dual-band characteristics is presented in this paper. The dipole radiator and the balun with a microstrip line to slotline transition structure is built on both sides of a RT/Duroid 5880 substrate. Two linear arrays with 8 elements is simulated to observe the operating bandwidth and radiation performance of the antenna. The proposed antenna can cover both 28 GHz and 39 GHz.

articleTitle: A Single Source Volume Integral Equation for the Inhomogeneous Maxwell Scattering Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we introduce a new volume integral equation method to compute the electromagnetic scattering of inhomogeneous medium. The medium can be inhomogeneous both in ε and μ. The integral equation is of the second kind. The electric and magnetic fields are obtained solving two decoupled volume integral equations (each one single source). The drawback of the method is that it requires E(x) and μ(x) to be smooth functions. Numerical examples are shown by using the windowed Green's function method [1].

articleTitle: Elliptical Monopole Antenna on InP Substrate for Sub-THz RTD-based Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The high permittivity of InP substrates has been a limiting factor for the bandwidth and efficiency of antennas fabricated in this material. In this manuscript we propose an elliptical monopole, monolithically fabricated in InP, fed by a CPW line. The suggested topology was simulated using HFSS finite element method. Input reflection coefficient measurements were performed on the monopole to validate the proposed antenna. Simulated and measured -10 dB bandwidths of 27 and 24 GHz were obtained, respectively. The peak simulated efficiency and realized gain were 95.37 % and 4.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Analysis of Nested Double Split Ring Resonator for Linearly Polarized Dual Band Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an extensive parameter analysis of nested double split ring resonators for a linearly polarized dual band reflectarray. The unit cell has been investigated not only for two rotational parameters but also six independent parameters which are the rotation angle, the outer radius and ring gap of inner and outer ring. With the help of these six degree of freedom approach we designed dual band reflectarray unit cell with dimensions 17.19 mm × 17.19 mm (0.47λ × 0.47λ) that operates at 8.23 and 12.4 GHz and the designed unit cell has a phase range of 360° The designed unit cells provide 360° phase range at both 8.23 and 12.4 GHz simultaneously.

articleTitle: Study of the Angular Spectrum of a Bianisotropic Refractive Metasurface at a Dielectric Interface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an initial study of the angular spectrum of a bianisotropic refractive metasurface at an interface between two dielectric media. In this study, we report on the existence of three distinct angular regions: a) a rotated transmission cone, b) a modified total internal reflection region, and c) a new total retro-reflection region.

articleTitle: On the Spectral Behavior and Normalization of a Resonance-Free and High-Frequency Stable Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The combined field integral equation (CFIE) used for solving scattering and radiation problems, although a resonance-free formulation, suffers from an ill-conditioning that strongly depends on the frequency and discretization density, both in the low- and high-frequency regime, resulting in slow convergence rates for iterative solvers. This work presents a new preconditioning scheme for the CFIE that cures the low-and the high-frequency as well as the dense discretization breakdown. The new preconditioner for the CFIE is based on a spherical harmonics analysis and the proper regularization with Helmholtz-type operators. Numerical results have been obtained to prove the effectiveness of this new formulation in real scenarios.

articleTitle: Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging on Lunar Surface with Observatory on Earth
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Antenna of the Arecibo observatory is chosen to simulate synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging on lunar surface. A lunar-centered lunar-fixed (LCLF) coordinate system is defined to describe the ephemeris of the antenna, considering the orbital motions of the Earth and the Moon in the ecliptic plane. A frequency-domain algorithm (FDA) is used to reconstruct the image, resulting in a spatial resolution of 3 m.

articleTitle: Flat beam optimization of 1-bit Reflectarray by means of Social Network Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reconfigurable reflectarray is an important topic in antenna research. Different kind of objectives can be identified for these systems, from beam scanning to adaptive beam shaping. In this paper 1-bit reflectarray has been optimized in order to obtain a flat beam. The reconfiguration capability of the array has been exploited in order to change properly the desired beam width. The optimization process has been done by means of a novel Evolutionary Optimization Algorithms, Social Network Optimization, suited for binary optimization problems.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Microstrip Array of Two Types of Antenna Units for Scattering Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hybrid microstrip array antenna is proposed for scattering cancellation. The array is composed of two types of antenna units. The two types of units are designed to have similar radiation properties and different scattering properties. Type I is a common antenna unit, and type II is with two slots on the microstrip patch. The two slots are used to control the phase difference of scattering field compared with the one without slots. The two types of units are then utilized to design an array to achieve scattering cancellation. Simulated results show that 15 dB radar cross section (RCS) reduction can be achieved by this method.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Study of a New RF-coil for 7 Tesla Small-Animal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work we demonstrate a comparative study of the a new proposed coil based on periodic capacitively-loaded thin wires and a conventional loop coil both optimized for small-animal imaging applications at 7 Tesla. The proposed coil uses hybridized eigenmodes of the flat periodic array comprising a number of thin metal wires, excited by a small non-resonant loop. Tunability of the proposed coil within the desired frequency range is ensured by the structural distributed capacity implemented as a PCB attached to the ends of all the wires. The proposed coil was compared to the conventional loop coil with lumped capacitors by numerical simulations. Quantitative comparison has been done in terms of B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> per square root of accepted power efficiency as well as the loaded Q-factor. Up to 42 % improvement of the transmit efficiency has been demonstrated over the conventional loop coil in a homogeneous phantom.

articleTitle: Available Universe of Input Impedances for the Probe-Fed Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, through the cavity model, the universe of achievable input impedances generated by the probe-fed circularly polarized rectangular microstrip antenna is investigated. Results of the analysis at the frequency of operation are displayed on an easy to use graphic. To prove the concept, an antenna was designed with an input impedance located in the predicted universe.

articleTitle: A Novel CPW-fed Patch Antenna for Ultra Wide Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a new coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna for ultrawideband (UWB)radar is presented. The antenna of the radar has a small size of 60 × 60 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and the impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is as large as 68 % relative to the centre frequency of 2.02 GHz. The antenna has many advantages, including small size, wide-bandwidth (1.33-2.70 GHz), and good omni-directivity.

articleTitle: Validating Models of Bistatic Scattering from Dielectric Surfaces with Small Roughness
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prediction of radar clutter produced by rough ground surfaces is an important part of detection performance analysis for ground penetrating radar (GPR). In this paper., we consider surfaces with small roughness., such as a dirt road., which are suitable for treatment by the small perturbation method (SPM). We compute the bistatic scattering coefficient from such surfaces using first-and-second-order SPM., as well as an FDTD-based approach. The results obtained over the entire range of bistatic scattering angles and different polarizations show a very good agreement between the two techniques. Additionally., the V-V case exhibits some interesting phenomenology which could be exploited in a bistatic radar system for buried target detection.

articleTitle: UWB imaging Using Computational FDTD TR and TRO Methods
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Time reversal (TR) imaging technique is a good candidate to detect and locate multiple targets in complex environment. The traditional TR imaging technique is to find the spatiotemporal focal point through retransmission of the time-reversed signals by TRM (time reversal mirror) to the interest region. Other methods are based on the so called TR operator (TRO), which include the Decomposition Operator of TR (DORT) and the TR MUltiple SIgnal Classification (TR-MUSIC) techniques. The performance of traditional TR imaging and TRO imaging methods was studied and compared through FDTD method in this letter. The results shows that the conventional TR imaging and DORT method have limited capability to separate closed located targets, while TR-MUSIC has super resolution capability.

articleTitle: Negative Refraction Based on Guided-Mode Assisted Meta-Gratings
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Highly efficient wave refraction at arbitrary angles has been a long-standing practical challenge and of great importance in scientific and engineering applications. In this paper, we reveal the possibility of exciting persistent radiating modes propagating at arbitrarily chosen negative angles with respect to the designed structure's surface normal. The interplay between the excited backward propagating guided modes of dielectric waveguides and the scattered field from the periodic dielectric meta-surfaces plays the crucial role in achieving such characteristics. Here, we study this in more details.

articleTitle: A Robust and Systematic Approach to Multiband Antenna Design for Operation on Complex Platforms under Geometry Modification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents a robust and systematic strategy for handling the problem of platform modification, which requires a retuning of the antenna designed to cover multiple frequency bands. We show that the key is to design the antenna with multiple arms such that varying the parameters of the arms can systematically retune the antenna in different bands, when such retuning is needed as the geometry of the platform itself is modified by the designer.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Solution of Volume-Surface Integral Equations for Dielectric-Conducting Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transient analysis for the structures including both dielectric and conducting media requires the accurate solution of time-domain volume-surface integral equations (TDVSIE) in integral equation approach. The problem is traditionally solved by combing the method of moments (MoM) in spatial domain and a march-on-in-time (MOT) scheme in temporal domain. In this paper, we propose a different scheme to solve the problem and it uses a Nyström method to discretize the spatial domain and a Galerkin's method with Laguerre basis and testing functions to discretize the temporal domain. The merits include the simplicity of Nyström method in space domain and unconditional stability of Galerkin's method in time domain. A typical numerical example is presented to demonstrate the approach and good results have been obtained.

articleTitle: The Impedance Characteristics Of An Electrically Long Dipole Immersed In a Magnetized Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically short dipole antenna (l-2m) mounted on the payload of a sounding rocket is commonly used as a probe to measure plasma properties in the earth's ionosphere. The complete measurement system consisting of the dipole and associated circuitry is called a Plasma Impedance Probe (PIP). Here we report on the behavior and impedance characteristics of an electrically long dipole antenna, obtained through a finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation. The motivation for this study is to design a combined impedance probe - plasma wave receiver system. In order for plasma waves to be efficiently received, the dipole antenna must be optimized to receive signals usually in the electron cyclotron resonance range. However, it is found that the overall antenna behavior changes when the cyclotron and antenna resonances are moved closer to each other. In the case of our simulations, the plasma cyclotron resonance frequency is shifted lower by 20%.

articleTitle: FSS based Radiation Pattern Decorrelator for MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a novel technique to reduce the correlation coefficient between adjacent antenna elements in a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) configuration. The proposed technique utilizes a phase-gradient frequency selective surface (FSS) as a superstrate in a Fabry-Perot cavity configuration, which tilts the beam of individual elements in such a way that it lowers the correlation coefficient. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated by designing a two-element MIMO antenna system at 9.7 GHz along with the proposed superstrate. The correlation coefficient is calculated based on simulated far-fields for without and with the proposed superstrate. The proposed technique results in a 96.4 % reduction in the correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Inductance Matrix Calculation for Shielded Multiconductor Systems Using an Eigenmode Projection Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The inductance matrix of a shielded multiconductor system is determined using a quasi-analytical approach based on an eigenmode projection technique. The proposed formulation expands the static magnetic field in the structure under study in terms of a complete set of solenoidal eigenmodes of a fictitious canonical conducting cavity enclosing the actual structure. The expansion is then used in the Maxwell's curl equation to obtain the eigenmode coefficients upon enforcing the boundary conditions and material profile of the actual problem. The inductance matrix is shown to be directly obtained from the proposed approach matrices, without further post-processing. Results are verified by comparison with full-wave solvers and show excellent agreement.

articleTitle: A Fast Method to Estimate the Total Delivered Power of a 2-Channel MRI Radio Frequency Coil
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The total delivered power of an MRI radio frequency (RF) coil is an important parameter for MRI safety control. For a 2-channel MRI coil, this parameter is not only dependent on the excitation strength on each channel, but also dependent on the object loading inside the coil. The purpose of this investigation is to propose a fast method to assess the total delivered power of a 2-channel MRI RF coil. Four hundred and ninety simulations for a high-resolution anatomical model were performed to validate this method. Among these simulations, ten random excitation-pairs of the 2-channel coil and forty-nine patient landmarks ranging between -200 to 1000 mm were considered. It is proved that this fast estimation method can calculate the total delivered power of a 2-channel RF coil with any excitation pairs by only two simulations and its relative error is less than 1.5%.

articleTitle: Offset-fed Metal-only Reflectarray Antenna Design Using 3D-Cross Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present an offset-fed metal-only reflectarray design utilizing a 3D phasing element, namely a 3D-cross, to achieve the phase shift coverage of up to 360°. This design is suitable for space applications for which the use of dielectrics is not desirable. The design presented herein points the beam in the direction normal to the reflectarray, with the illumination from a feed horn incident at a skew angle of 30°. The simulated gain for the normal-directed beam is found to be 28.9 dBi at 35.6GHz. The aperture efficiency is 47%, while the sidelobe level is -19.7dB, relative to the main lobe.

articleTitle: Polarizability and Light Scattering by Subwavelength Graded-Index Plasmonic Spheres
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Light scattering by a subwavelength sphere exhibiting radially inhomogeneous permittivity is here presented. The theoretical foundations describing the scattering response are given in a simple manner and the concept of polarizability is generalized incorporating the inhomogeneity effects. Two illustrative examples are briefly discussed, i.e., a power-law and a Drude-like inhomogeneous profile, exposing the physical mechanisms of their scattering response. The presented results can open the path towards the implementation of graded-index subwavelength particles in modern nanoantenna applications.

articleTitle: On the Randomized Cross Approximation of EFIE Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fully algebraic approach is presented for the evaluation of the non-neighboring group interactions of electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems in the case of the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) method. The proposed method exploits the numerical rank deficiency of the non-neighboring groups interactions in a similar way as the Adaptive Cross Approximation (ACA) method, but following a procedure that leads into considerably lower ranks than ACA. Instead of factorizing the interaction impedance matrix, the proposed method operates on the core of the impedance matrix by factorizing the integral equation kernel (Green`s function). The factorization specifically is implemented by following a randomized scheme of selecting rows and columns instead of the time consuming adaptive partial pivoting that ACA does. By these ingredients the proposed Randomized Cross Approximation (RCA) method presents considerably lower ranks than ACA while having a low frequency O(N) and high frequency O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.75</sup>) complexity for a single non-near interaction.

articleTitle: Cassegrain Reflectarray Antennas using Higher Order Orbital Angular Momentum Modes Combined and Cancelled in Near Field
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Cassegrain reflectarray with higher order orbital angular momentum combined and cancelled in near field. The simulated results show the antenna with the first orbital angular momentum combined and cancelled in near field has gain of 28.6dBi and good reflection coefficient under 10dB.

articleTitle: Model-based Inversion of 3D Anisotropic Objects and Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A model-based inversion method for inverse scattering problems of anisotropic objects is discussed. The forward algorithm is based on the curl-conforming volume integral equation method. The inverse scattering problem uses the multiplicatively regularized Gauss-Newton method. Numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the numerical algorithms to reconstruct the anisotropic objects.

articleTitle: Effective Constitutive Parameters Evaluation for Meta-Materials with Highly Interaction Fields
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study is concerned with meta-materials made of thin wire inclusions arranged in an infinite periodic structure. The polarizability coefficients and the constitutive parameters are extracted by using Lorentz or Maxwell-Garnett homogenization techniques. The validation is performed by calculating the transmission and reflection coefficients for incident fields illuminating the structure from three directions. The results are compared to simulation results from the EM commercial software HFSS. This study demonstrates the necessity of extracting the polarizability coefficients taking in consideration the interaction fields in the periodic structure.

articleTitle: Oblique Plane-wave Scattering and Shielding Analyses of Cylindrical Shell Made of Carbon Fiber Composites
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The oblique plane-wave scattering and shielding analyses of multilayer carbon fiber composite material (CFCM) cylindrical shells is formulated and developed. A multifilament doublet currents method (MFDCM) is presented and studied, which is combined with tensorial boundary condition (TBC), to analyze the scattering and shielding performances. The bistatic echo widths are investigated under different layer numbers and fiber patterns. These different scenarios are also taken into consideration in the prediction of shielding effectiveness (SE). Both TE and TM modes are excited within the cylindrical shell under arbitrary incidence plane wave over high frequency range. Our numerical results are in good agreement with published ones. The proposed method is simple and concise, and it can also be applied to handle shells with arbitrary smooth cross section shapes.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflective Metasurface for Linear to Circular Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar reconfigurable reflective metasurface is used as a polarizer. The metasurface allows the conversion of a linear incident wave to a circular one. The proposed structure is composed of meta-atoms incorporating voltage-controlled varactor diodes. By varying the dispersion responses of each meta-atom., the operating frequency can be tailored. Simulations and measurements on a fabricated prototype are presented to validate the concept at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Further Observations on the Shape Synthesis of Closely-Spaced Antennas Using Sub-Structure Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Earlier work devised a shape synthesis approach for closely-spaced electrically-small antennas operating at different frequencies. The method uses the substructure characteristic mode concept. Definition of the objective function of this shape optimization process in terms of such modes allows the feedpoint to only be specified after shaping is complete. Certain problem issues identified in this work are resolved in the present paper, and an illustrative example of such shape optimized antennas is provided.

articleTitle: A Passive Multi-Channel Brain Implant for Wireless Neuropotential Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A passive, wireless and batteryless multi-channel (8 channels) brain implant is proposed with the following unique features: a) 28 times better sensitivity, b) 2 times smaller footprint, and c) scalability to 100s or even 1000s of channels. To verify the operation within biological tissues, in-vitro measurements are presented using fresh pig skin. Experimental results show that the proposed neuro-sensing system exhibits 20 μV<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</sub> sensivity at all channels. That is, it can record any signal generated by the human brain. Overall, this technology brings forward transformational opportunities for patients with epilepsy, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Algorithm for Collision Detection in Ray- Tracing Propagation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nowadays, deterministic channel modeling methods play an increasingly important role in the research of wireless communication. With the growing precision requirements in the modeling process, the exploration of increase in computational speed and reduce in complexity is motivated. The improved vector algorithm in ray-tracing simulation presented in this paper realizes the research of the improvement and acceleration of collision detection in three-dimensional (3D) scenarios. Moreover, these methods will guide the construction of fast collision detection algorithm in ray-tracing propagation simulation.

articleTitle: Bit Error Rate Performance of FD-Relay in OLOS Mine Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates the bit error rate (BER) performance when the communication channel is obstructed by a vehicle in an underground mine tunnel. In this case, the radio signal is obstructed by the vehicle and communication between a source and a destination cannot occur. To overcome this issue, we proposed an investigative relay, installed around the vehicle, with Zero-Forcing Beam-Forming sche me (ZFBF). For the simulation scenario, we consider an application of this particular of the relay in underground mine environment with a vehicle which is obstruct line of sight (OLOS) between two communicating nodes. The relay is equipped with two antennas while both source and destination are equipped with a single antenna. The simulation results show that proposed method can expeditiously minimize the BER and enable the communication between source and destination where vehicles can be obstructed LOS or increase propagation complexity conditions.

articleTitle: GA-Produced Refiectarray Elements Having Arbitrary Phase-Difference Between Two Orthogonal Linear-Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes novel reflectarray resonant elements designed by genetic algorithm(GA), which have arbitrarily phase difference from -180° to 180° between the TE (V-pol.) and the TM (H-pol.) polarizations from 13 GHz to 17 GHz. Moreover, these elements have two axially symmetric structure in the unit cell so that the cross polarization level is suppressed less than about -60 dB for the wide frequency range. A reflectarray antenna with two-separated offset feeds is designed by using proposed elements in the Ku-band, and its effectiveness is verified by evaluating radiation patterns numerically.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Semi-Circular Monopole Antenna for Broadband 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically small antenna for future 5G millimeter-wave applications is presented. The proposed antenna has a size of 4×4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, The antenna is semi-circular in shape with an arc slot, resulting in a broadband characteristic. The proposed antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth that ranges from 23 to 37 GHz. The antenna has a maximum absolute gain of 3.44 dBi and is more than 89% efficient. The length of any side is less than 0.49λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>at 23 GHz, making it extremely useful for array configuration deployment. Modelled on thin Rogers substrate with attractive characteristics and low-cost fabrication requirements, this antenna becomes an excellent candidate for future 5G communications.

articleTitle: Dual-band Tapered Slot Antenna for Integrated Biomedical System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single Tapered Slot Antenna (TSA) for biomedical array system is proposed in order to apply for integrated microwave imaging and hyperthermia system. The proposed TSA operates in dual frequency band as a resonance type at 2.45 GHz for hyperthermia and a traveling wave type in 4.5 ~ 10 GHz for microwave imaging system. Additional impedance matching technique is applied to overcome the wide-band impedance mismatch. The antenna operating characteristics and time-domain analysis are shown to demonstrate the potential of using in the integrated biomedical system.

articleTitle: Ultra Compact Truncated Ground Monopole Antenna for DCS 1800/ PCS 1900 Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A printed microstrip fed single band monopole antenna having a dimension of 0.240 λg × 0.095 λg suitable for 1.8 GHz (DCS 1800) application is depicted. The structure comprises of a truncated ground microstrip fed simple monopole to achieve the compactness. The simulation and experimental results are in good agreement and shows that the proposed antenna exhibits good impedance match, gain and stable radiation patterns in both principal planes. To give a deep understanding about the performance of the antenna, equivalent circuit model of the antenna is also developed.

articleTitle: Comparison of Topology Modification for Size-Reduction-Oriented Wideband Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates various types of geometry modifications aimed at reducing the physical dimensions of the wideband antenna structures. Three types of modifications, pertinent to the ground plane, feed line, and radiator, are considered and compared. The results obtained for a set of benchmark UWB antennas indicate that feed line modifications permit highest miniaturization rates, whereas radiator modifications are of minor importance. For the sake of fair comparison size-reduction-oriented design optimization is performed for each considered antenna structure.

articleTitle: Variabilities of Evaporation Ducts in a Near-Shore Coastal Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study characterizes the evaporation ducts observed offshore of Duck, North Carolina using measurements from the east coast field campaign, the Coupled Air Sea Processes and Electromagnetic ducting Research (CASPER-East), conducted from 10 October 2015 to 6 November 2015. Pressure, temperature, humidity, and wind speed and direction were collected by sensors on the bow mast of the CASPER research vessels R/V Hugh R. Sharp and R/V Atlantic Explorer. An Infrared SST Autonomous Radiometer was used to measure the sea surface skin temperature. The surface layer mean profiles of temperature and specific humidity were derived using the flux-profile relationships employed in the COARE bulk flux algorithm version 3.0 with inputs from bow mast measurements using 20-minute averaging. Significant cooling was observed between 17 October 2015 and 20 October 2015 caused by the strong northerly flow that brought cold and dry air to the experiment domain. Duct height and strength were generally higher during the cold and dry air advection events observed on 17, 24 and 25 October. In addition, a sharp increase in the duct height was identified associated with stable surface layer conditions on 14, 22, 26, and 30 Oct. Duct height varied from 0 m to 49.8 m and mean duct height was 10.4 m during the experiment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Reflection from Shocked Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an analytical model is proposed for computing the time-harmonic electromagnetic wave reflected by shocked dielectric materials. This model finds application in the remote sensing of shock waves in dielectric materials. First results obtained from shocked PolyMethyl MethAcrilate are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: Design and Human Trials of Microwave Noninvasive Blood Glucose Detection Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microwave noninvasive blood glucose detection sensor and its human trials are presented in this paper. Changes in blood glucose concentration will affect its relative dielectric constant. The blood glucose detection sensor, which uses resonant cavity structure, can monitor the relative dielectric constant's float in testing environment. By means of loading detction sensor with split-ring as well as choke, excellent testing precision and anti-environment disturbance ability are achieved in human trials.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Resistively Loaded Vee Dipole Fed by an Even-Mode Matched Marchand Balun
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design of a resistively loaded vee dipole (RLVD)fed by an integrated even-mode matched Marchand balun is proposed. The RLVD is designed for use in a pulsed radar application with a bandpass characteristic from 0.5-1.5 GHz. The Marchand balun creates the bandpass response when cascaded with the typical high-pass response of the RLVD. To achieve good matching between the balun and the RLVD, an even-mode matching circuit is developed and incorporated at the balanced ports of the balun. Experimental results show prototype return loss better than -10 dB from 400 MHz to 1.9 GHz and a significant decrease in low-frequency monostatic coupling.

articleTitle: Broadband CPW-fed Slot Antenna Using Superformula
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband printed CPW fed slot antenna using superformula is proposed. The supershaped slot and the supershaped patch are used to provide additional surface current paths along the edges which also influences impedance matching. The characteristics of the antenna such as return loss, realized gain and radiation pattern are simulated and return loss is compared with the measured result. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the designed antenna is from 2.5 GHz to around 9 GHz with gain around 5 dB or above for most of the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Modelling the Interaction of THz Waves with Breast Cancer Tissues
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate the application of Double Debye theory combined with Finite-Difference Time-Domain technique to model terahertz wave interaction with breast tumor tissues. It has been shown that terahertz signals are strongly absorbed by water. Biological tissue has high water content, which is a possible reason for contrast when utilizing terahertz technology in breast cancer imaging. While results demonstrated the contrast between fatty and cancerous breast tissues, the challenge lies in the low contrast between cancerous and fibroglandular tissues (normal tissue). Therefore, computer simulations are needed to investigate a method to manipulate and enhance the contrast between these tissues for the sake of using terahertz technology in tumor margin assessment.

articleTitle: Efficient 60 GHz Antenna Based on Open-End Microstrip Line Fringing Fields
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain antenna at 60 GHz is presented. The antenna utilizes the radiation from open-end microstrip lines fringing fields as an efficient radiator. The proposed antenna structure is very compact in size. The simulated antenna has realized boresight gain of 11.5-dBi, and matching bandwidth of 2.2 GHz (i.e., 3.66% relative bandwidth). The proposed antenna simplicity allows easy fabrication and low cost.

articleTitle: A Compact, Broadband, Two-Port Slot Antenna System for Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband common-aperture, and dual-polarized sub-array of Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna (CBSA) with two ports having a very high level of isolation is presented in this paper. The antenna is designed for wideband full-duplex wireless communication and FMCW radar systems. The antenna is composed of a thin rectangular cavity on which four cross-slots are cut out for radiation. The radiating cross-slots are fed by two concentric orthogonal slots on the back wall of the cavity. One polarization is excited by an end-launch coaxial to waveguide transition which is used to excite the cavity through a feeding slot. A two-pronged microstrip line symmetrically crossing over another feeding slot, oriented orthogonal to the feeding slot, is used to excite the other polarization. The microstrip line is designed such that each prong would couple to the waveguide feed out-of-phase and as a result, a very high isolation level is achieved between channels over a very wide bandwidth. Designed to be compatible with metal 3D printing, the devised antenna is fabricated out of aluminum using Direct Metal Laser Sintering (DMLS) technology. This sub-array slot antenna with dimensions smaller than 1. 28 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>×1.28 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>×0. 27 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> (where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> is the wavelength at the lowest frequency), provides a minimum gain of 10 dB for both channels and exhibits a polarization isolation better than 20 dB within the main beam and a channel isolation above 54 dB over 40% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: Compact and Low-Cost Microwave Helmet Brain Scanner for Monitoring Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In view of the recent advances in the field of neurology, molecular biology and microwave imaging techniques relating to Parkinson's disease (PD), the clinical management of the world population of patients afflicted with Parkinson's disease is poised to undergo major changes. All of these usher in the significant improvement in patients' quality of life. A light-weight low-cost helmet microwave brain scanner for monitoring Parkinson's Disease is a timely instrument for the benefits of PD patients.

articleTitle: Active Surface Cloaking with Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Active interior electromagnetic cloaking cancels an object's scattering through the use of an array of active sources placed along its boundary. Unlike previous passive methods, conventional antennas can be used and cloaking achieved regardless of the object's geometry and material composition. The work in this paper continues upon expanding the potential of active methods in the development of a practically realizable cloak. Here, a thin conformal cloak is constructed out of 20 planar folded patch antennas to hide a metallic circular cylindrical target at 2.5 GHz. The performance of this cloak is then demonstrated through full-wave electromagnetic simulations. By weighting the input voltages on each patch, the cylinder's radar cross-section is reduced by -15 dBsm in all directions.

articleTitle: A Simple Tri-Band Proximity Coupling Fed Compact Antenna for 2.7GHz, WLAN and Sub-6GHz Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple multi-band antenna is proposed for 2700MHz, upper WLAN and sub-6GHz fifth generation wireless communication applications. The proposed antenna is fed by using a proximity coupling fed structure to excite two spiral strips. The feeding line is a 50-Ohm microstrip line, and the two spiral strips are set at both sides of the feeding line. There is a partial ground plane at the bottom of the FR4 substrate. The designed antenna is created by using the HFSS, and the simulated results from the HFSS show that the antenna has a good triple-band characteristic and an omnidirectional radiation pattern at these three operating bands.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Plasma-based Tunable Absorber
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile tunable absorber based on the interaction between electromagnetic (EM) waves and plasma medium in the microwave regime. The design is implemented by integrating discrete plasma-shells and practical biasing network layers in a resistively loaded frequency selective surface (FSS). Two approaches., comprised of lossy inductive and lossy capacitive FSS layer, are investigated. A transmission line model is used to provide the working principle of the absorption and its frequency tuning capability. The total thickness is about 3.5 mm corresponding to 0.11λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> where λ0 is the free space wavelength of the absorption center frequency (fo =9.5 GHz). Through proper activation of the plasma, which induces a dielectric loading on the FSS layer, a linear tuning response is obtained.

articleTitle: A New Decoupling Method for Massive MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel method for reducing mutual coupling in massive MIMO antennas is proposed. The decoupling is achieved by embedding two couples of metal meander line strips vertically and horizontally between two antenna elements, providing additional coupling paths to reduce the coupling between two input ports. The decoupling method is validated by simulating a 3 × 3 and a 4 × 4 dual-polarized antenna arrays. It is shown that the isolation is improved by 10 dB between the input ports of two adjacent antenna elements with the same polarization while there is little change for radiation patterns and the isolation between the input ports for two orthogonal polarizations.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Frequency Selective Surface Design based on Cascaded Patch Resonators with a Slotted Ground
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a novel wideband bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS), which is comprised of sandwiched arrays of cascaded back-to-back patch resonators with a C-type slotted ground in-between. Three transmission poles are generated to realize the desired wideband frequency responses, with a 3-dB fractional bandwidth of 85% and an insertion loss of 0.27 dB at the center frequency of the passband when the incidence is normal. The out-of-band rejection bandwidth is shown to range from 14.5 GHz to 22.8GHz for the presented design, though it is scalable.

articleTitle: 4D Antenna Array of UWB Vivaldi Elements with Low Side Lobes and Harmonic Suppresion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents a design of a time modulated antenna array with UWB Vivaldi elements. The array is composed by 7 elements worked in the range of frequency from 2.65 GHz to 17.26Ghz. The design consists in the optimization of the switching times of the Vivaldi elements for side lobe and side band levels reduction. The optimization is carried out by the particle swarm optimization. Simulation results show a good performance of the proposed array.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Conformal Load Bearing Antenna using 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and characterization of conformal antennas on conformal load bearing structures using additive manufacturing. Specifically, we will show two methods that employ printing, via micro-dispensing, of conductive inks within a structural composite. We experimentally validated our methods by designing and fabricating a low-profile antenna operating at 6GHz.

articleTitle: Adaptive Antenna Array Beamforming Based on Norm Penalized NLMS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm constrained normalized LMS algorithm (L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS) is proposed to find out the solution of the thinned array adaptive beamforming. The proposed L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS integrates an additional l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm penalty on the filter coefficients compared with the constrained NLMS (CNLMS) algorithm, which aims to seek the solution towards sparsity and finally thinned array. To reduce the computation burden, an approximating l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm method is presented and integrated into the CNLMS algorithm. The simulation experiments are created to show that the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS algorithm is effective in sparse adaptive beamforming.

articleTitle: Dual-loop antenna with band-stop circuit for GPS/Bluetooth metal-rimmed smartwatch Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-loop antenna design for full metal-rimmed smartwatch application is presented. The proposed design exploits smartwatch's metal rim structure as the radiation antenna, which tightly surrounds the smartwatch's system circuit board. The unbroken metal rim was divided to two loop antennas via a feeding point and a grounded point, and the longer one was used to cover the 2.4GHz band (2400-2485 MHz) for Bluetooth/Wi-Fi operation. Moreover, an additional band-stop circuit composed of a parallel two lumped elements (a capacitance and an inductance) was placed between the GND and the loop. Due to the effect of the band-stop circuit, the GPS Ll band (1575.42MHz ± 1.023MHz) was covered with very little effects on the Bluetooth band. The detailed design process and the results are discussed in the article.

articleTitle: High Resolution Subsurface Imaging of Buried Targets Using Distributed Robotic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new subsurface imaging technique using distributed sensors is introduced. Instead of monostatic transceivers employed in conventional ground penetrating radars, the proposed technique utilizes bi-static transceivers to sample the reflected signals from the ground at different positions and create a large two-dimensional aperture for high resolution subsurface imaging. The coherent processing of the samples in the proposed imaging method eliminates the need for large antenna arrays for obtaining high lateral resolution images. In addition, it eliminates the need for sampling on a grid which is a time-consuming task in imaging using ground penetration radar. Imaging results show that the method can provide high-resolution images of the buried targets using only samples of the reflected signals on a circle with the center at the transmitter location.

articleTitle: Printed Coil Antenna for Wireless Capsule Endoscopic Communication System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, two printed coil antennas for wireless capsule endoscopic (WCE) communication system are proposed. Diagnostic images taken by WCE cameras are sent to an external device and displayed simultaneously. Two resonant frequencies of the proposed antenna are 38.5 and 57.6 MHz. Due to low resonant frequency, signal attenuation inside human body can be decreased, compared to a WCE antenna operating at Medical Implant Communication Systems (MICS) band (402-405 MHz). The receiving antenna size is 64 × 64 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and the transmitting antenna is 10 mm in diameter and 2 mm thick. A human equivalent phantom is used to evaluate the influence of human body. In addition, the communication link sensitivity with different locations, orientations and misalignments are discussed.

articleTitle: Through the Wall Human Signature Detection using Principle Component Analysis (PCA)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Life sign signal detection through the wall suffers from strong clutter due to the boundary of a dielectric wall and other environmental noises. Principle component analysis (PCA) method is applied to enhance the information of a life target beyond the boundary by suppressing the undesired clutter. The effect of this clutter reduction makes the low-frequency variation of heartbeat detectable in further moving target indicator (MTI) processing step. The detection result of a human subject is represented in a Range-Doppler plane, from which the location and the characteristics of the subject have been determined.

articleTitle: Estimation of Evaporation Duct and Surface-Based Duct Parameters from a Combined Refractivity Model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study of atmospheric refractive conditions is essential in the shipboard radars and radio communication conditions in the maritime environment. Especially at low altitudes, as radio refractivity can vary considerably with both height and range, characterizing marine atmospheric boundary layer properties, ducting in particular, is thus crucial for air-sea interaction research. This paper proposes a novel refractivity profile model and describes a way to estimate parameters defining both evaporation duct and surface-based duct using the measured one-way propagation loss from a receiving X-band array at multiple range. The data was measured during the CASPER-West at-sea experimental campaign, which was conducted off the coast of Point Mugu, CA, during October-November of 2017.

articleTitle: Aperture Coupled Beamforming Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An aperture coupled micro strip patch antenna for V-band is designed in this paper. It consists of two substrates with slot cut ground in the between two substrates with patch at the top and feed line at the bottom of other substrate. Power is coupled from feed line through slotted ground to the patch. This antenna gives good matched results for 59 GHz to 63 GHz below -10dB and gain of maximum 14-15 dBi in for single antenna and more than 24 dBi for 16 array elements beamforming array. The beam forming of ±45° is shown for channel 2 and channel 3 of IEEE 802.11ad.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Wideband Remote Electrical Tilt Multi-Beam Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of the dual-polarized wideband remote electrical tilt (RET) three-beam arrays for wireless communications (0.69-0.96 GHz). Based on the required specifications such as gain, the range of the electrical down-tilt, the azimuth beam coverage, the cross-over point between beams, the side lobe level, and the grating lobe, two wideband dual-polarized three-beam RET antennas have been designed, implemented, and tested.

articleTitle: The Effect of Phase Continuity on Synchronous Antenna Tuning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
