abstract: Synchronously tuning a narrowband antenna at the symbol rate of a frequency shift keyed (FSK) modulation has been shown to increase the efficiency of the transmitter. When tuning by switching between a set of matching networks, it is important to not only have phase continuity between the symbols but to also switch at a precise phase in the transmitted signal, which restricts the usable FSK frequencies. When tuning by changing the reactance of a single tuning circuit, it is not obvious that strict phase control between symbols is necessary. This paper investigates the importance of the phase of a FSK signal at symbol transitions when synchronously tuning by changing the capacitance of a varactor diode on the antenna.

articleTitle: A Graphene Based Bandwidth Enhanced Metamaterial Absorber using Circular Ring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A thin (~ λ/8) bandwidth-enhanced metamaterial absorber has been presented in this paper where the unit cell contains single circular ring. The geometric parameters of the graphene-embedded structure are controlled in such a way that the absorber should exhibit bandwidth-enhanced absorption between 42.5 THz and 65 THz. Three distinct absorption peaks are obtained at 46.872 THz, 53.374 THz, and 61.035 THz with respective absorptivity of 99.9%, 98.4% and 80%. The proposed structure has been investigated under oblique incidences for both TE and TM polarizations where bandwidth enhanced absorption has been observed up to 50° incident angles for both cases. Furthermore, the graphene embedded structure exhibits polarization insensitive bandwidth-enhanced absorption.

articleTitle: 2.45 GHz Wearable RF-Harvester for Large Area Textile Harvester (LATH) Integration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a textile based RF-power harvester. This power harvester was designed to operate at 2.45 GHz to harvest Wi-Fi power for wearable electronic applications. The harvester comprises of: 1) 2.45 GHz patch antenna and 2) single-diode based rectifier circuits. The antenna and the circuit was implemented on organza and denim fabrics, respectively. The textile patch antenna demonstrated -10 dB Su-bandwidth from 2.38 GHz to 2.53 GHz with maximum realized gain of 4.7 dBi at broadside. Further, the textile-rectifier prototype demonstrated a 43% rectifying efficiency at 2.45 GHz with 0 dBm input power. Thus, a rectifier surface that occupies an area of only 2.2 cm×1.8 cm can operate small body-worn sensors.

articleTitle: Comparison of Measured Ground Penetrating Radar Response of Soil Surface to FDTD Model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When using non-ground coupled Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) to detect buried objects, one major source of clutter is the surface of the ground. This is especially true if the surface of the ground is not very flat. Responses from the surface will show up below the main response from the ground and mix with the responses of buried objects. To better understand this response and potentially remove it I investigated measuring the soil surface profile with a LIDAR and then modeling the GPR response using the FDTD code gprMax. The modeled response was then subtracted from the measured GPR data.

articleTitle: A wideband millimeter-wave bidirectional circularly polarized antenna array using sequential rotation feeding
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-layer wideband antenna array with bidirectional dual-orthogonally circularly polarized (CP) property at millimeter-wave band is proposed. The CP waves are generated by a perturbation using a shorting via in the SIW cavity. The operating bandwidths are improved by adopting the sequential rotation feeding technique. To validate the design, a prototype operating at 42 GHz was fabricated and measured. The measured 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths in +z and -z directions can cover a frequency band of 39.5-44 GHz, and the measured peak gains can reach 10.6 dBic at 43 GHz.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Digital Beamforming and Power Minimization Adaptive Nulling Algorithms Using a Software Defined Radio Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We compare adaptive nulling algorithms for digital beamforming (DBF) and non-DBF arrays. These algorithms will be implemented on a DBF array made from software defined radios. Results show that these techniques can achieve desirable signal to interference ratios that are comparable, and as such, implementing techniques applicable to non-DBF array are more cost effective.

articleTitle: Waveguide Slot Filtering Antenna Using Mushroom-Type Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a waveguide slot filtering antenna using a mushroom-type surface is presented. First, a filtering waveguide is described. It is comprised of a common rectangular waveguide and a mushroom-type surface embedded at the bottom of the waveguide cavity. Under proper design, a bandgap can be arrived by the surface at specified frequency range, in which the propagation of electromagnetic wave is stopped. As a result, a bandstop filter function is obtained by the waveguide. Then, a filtering antenna is achieved by cutting radiating slots at the top of the filtering waveguide. The simulated results show that the proposed filtering antenna exhibits an operating bandwidth of 7.5%, covering a frequency range of 5.15’, 5.55GHz, with VSWR less than 1.5 and gain higher than IldBi. At the same time, a suppression level more than 40dB is obtained within the stop band of 7.90’, 8.75GHz.

articleTitle: TX-RX K/Ka Band Polarizer Based on a SIW Polarization Twister
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A K/Ka band polarizer obtained stacking a SIW polarization rotator and a meander-lines polarizer is presented. The rotator is realized with SIW cavities that selectively twist the polarization of the incident wave. In this way, incident 30GHz horizontally polarized waves are converted in RHCP signals, while incident 20GHz waves with the same polarization are converted in LHCP signals. The proposed polarizer may be used with linearly polarized aperture antennas and, for this reason, it can be considered as an after-market add-on that does not affect the performance parameters of the antenna itself.

articleTitle: Kernel DOA estimation in nonuniform arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An algorithm to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) in non uniform linear antenna arrays based on the use of Mercer's kernel nonlinear interpolation is introduced. Interpolation is followed by the synthesis of a virtual uniform array. The methodology uses kernel functions, Support Vector Regression (SVR) for the interpolation, and standard MUSIC and root- MUSIC for the DOA estimation from the interpolated data. Multiple experiments are conducted using this algorithm. The results compare the interpolated DOA detection with a standard detection algorithm using non uniform array and shows a significant improvement in performance of the proposed detector.

articleTitle: Compact Third-Order Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface with Wide Spurious-Suppression Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact third-order bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) with high selectivity and wide spurious-suppression bandwidth characteristics is presented. The proposed multi-layer FSS filter operating in the C-band, is composed of three Jerusalem Cross (JC) periodic array layers coupled together through periodic square aperture layers. The wide rejection band is obtained by incorporating bandstop JC layers that are designed to suppress spurious responses. The analysis of the design based on its equivalent circuit model (ECM) shows that the proposed FSS design can be synthesized with inductively coupled bandpass resonators from filter theory. To demonstrate its superior response, the proposed third-order FSS is compared through full wave simulation with its counterpart [5], which uses complementary JC layers that behave as parallel LC bandpass resonators.

articleTitle: A New Class of Reconfigurable Origami Antennas Based on E-Textile Embroidery
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a new class of Origami-based tessellated antennas whose RF characteristics can be self-tuned by reconfiguration of the antenna shape. To enable mechanical flexibility and robustness, the antennas are fabricated using automated embroidery of silver-coated polymer E-threads. As a proof-of-concept, an E-textile accordion-dipole is fabricated, and shown to vary its resonance frequency in the 627 MHz to 991 MHz range. The proposed tessellated, E-textile antennas can be easily integrated into clothing and mechanical structures, providing a non-invasive way of quantifying deformation for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: A CPW Fed Trapezoidal Fractal Patch Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A CPW fed UWB Trapezoid fractal patch Antenna (TFPA) is presented in this paper. The antenna has been simulated using Ansoft HFSS (version 14), fabricated and measured. The measured results show a 3.41 GHz - 10.3 GHz 10 dB return loss bandwidth with maximum matching at 7.1 GHz, and gain 6.75 dB. The measured co-polarization and cross-polarization radiation pattern also have been plotted, which show that the cross polarization component is 19 dB down than the co-polarization component.

articleTitle: Development of Tunable Breast Tissue Phantoms for Terahertz Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work improves on breast cancer phantom materials for use in a terahertz imaging setup. Previously-developed solid-emulsion phantom formulations based on oil, water, and TX151 solidifying powder are updated to include agar and margarine in order to improve the consistency of the optical properties. Additionally, updated methodology using a heating process is introduced to remove excess air bubbles from the phantom and improve terahertz imaging. Spectroscopy of fibrous and cancer tissue phantoms shows good correlation of the optical properties in the terahertz range compared to published values, and a reduction in air gaps is also seen using terahertz imaging.

articleTitle: Vivaldi-Inspired Logarithmic Spiral Antenna for 28 GHz 5G Communication Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a logarithmic spiral antenna for 5G 28 GHz band. The antenna has 3.982 GHz of impedance bandwidth ranging from 26.396 - 30.378 GHz. The antenna has directional characteristics with gain of 5.36 dBi and radiation efficiency greater than 94 %The antenna is modelled upon Rogers substrate suitable for low-cost PCB fabrication. The proposed antenna has physical size of 6×4.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and an electrical size of 0.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.41λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna has wide bandwidth, high gain and small size making it a natural choice for future 5G mobile applications.

articleTitle: Comparison between NU-CNLMS and GA for Antenna Array Failure Correction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the comparison between two algorithms for the array failure correction or the re-optimization of radiation pattern is presented which are the non-uniform norm constrained least mean square (NU-CNLMS) and genetic algorithm (GA) respectively. By using those algorithms, array elements' excitation are redistributed to optimize the side-lobe level and null depth of the array pattern which belongs to an equidistance linear array antenna and it has the function of adaptive beam-forming by using the algorithm of minimum variance distortion less response. The performance differences between those failure correction algorithms are compared under feature selective verification algorithm by simulation and the conclusion is drawn that NU-CNLMS algorithm is little better than GA in the situation under investigation.

articleTitle: Reversibly Reconfigurable Liquid Metal Patch Antenna Using A Superhydrophobic Spray-Coating
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Liquid metal-based reconfigurable antennas typically must be flushed with an electrolyte to remove the nanometer-thick oxide skin of EGaln that adheres the walls of the microchannels. The EGaln residue prevents repeatable actuation, but the presence of electrolyte introduces other challenges owing to its often corrosive and electrically conductive nature. To overcome this issue, we present a technique for enabling reversible infusion and withdrawal of EGaln into acrylic micro-channels and wide planar cavities by coating the surfaces with a silica-particle based superhydrophobic coating. The coating prevents adhesion of the liquid metal to the acrylic media and allows it to be reconfigured multiple times without the typical flushing process.

articleTitle: Simulating Engineered Electromagnetic Surfaces in Ray-Tracing Software
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Engineered electromagnetic surfaces (EES) are surfaces which can be fabricated on a thin layer of plastic using a low-cost printed electronics technology. These surfaces can be installed at strategic locations in indoor and outdoor propagation environments to improve the coverage or mitigate interference at millimeter-wave bands for 5G applications. Two methods used to embed uniform and non-uniform EESs into ray-tracing software tools are introduced along with a propagation prediction example for an outdoor scenario that incorporates EESs.

articleTitle: A Dual-Circularly Polarized Compact Feed Horn at 5G Millimeter-Frequency for Reflector Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high-performance feed horn with dual circular polarization is proposed at 5G millimeter-Wave (mm Wave) band for reflector antenna applications. The feed consists of two rectangular ports, a cylindrical waveguide, a TEd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>polarizer and a conical horn. This feed horn is designed to operate within a frequency band of 50GHz to 53GHz. Simulations shows that the feed has inter-port isolation below -20dB, port reflection coefficients below -15dB, axial ratios below 0.2dB at the center of the beam and polarization isolations over 24dB. Furthermore, the feed is easy to fabricate. This feed is being manufactured currently and experimental results will be presented during the symposium.

articleTitle: A Posteriori Element-wise Error Quantification for FEM Solvers Using Higher Order Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present methods for quantification of numerical error for computational electromagnetic solvers using adjoint operators and duality. We outline the concept of adjoint operators and further introduce applications of the adjoint problem toward analyzing numerical error of forward solutions. We give an illustrative example of contribution to the total error on an element-wise basis for a 1-D slab scattering problem solved by a higher-order finite element method.

articleTitle: Field Focusing with Novel Implantable Lens Designs using 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present two novel 3D implantable lens designs to provide power focusing of electromagnetic fields, based on the 3D printing concept, and applicable for wireless power transmission into the human body. The first design consists of concentric conductive rings inside the tissue. The second design is made of two wires, making it possible to focus any arbitrary polarization by choosing appropriate orientations. Also, we propose a fundamentally different approach to 3D printing for medical applications -3D printing inside the body - which reduces the risk of infection and surgical complication, thus improving patient recovery.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Unit-cell for Perforated Dielectric Transmitarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new unit-cell is introduced with the aim of improving the efficiency and bandwidth of dielectric perforated transmitarray antennas. The behavior of the proposed unit-cell is compared with that of a conventional one, consisting of a single dielectric layer with a central square hole. In the structure here proposed, two additional tapered layers have been added, acting as matching circuits. Two transmitarray antennas of 40×40 elements, each using one of the two unit-cells, have been designed and numerically characterized. The results show significant performance improvements when the new unit-cell is used: the 1-dB Gain bandwidth increases from 13.4% to 27.6% and the aperture efficiency from 33.4 % to 44 %.

articleTitle: Dual-band Antenna Decoupling Design with Stepped Impedance Loaded Dual-band Dummy Element
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band WLAN MIMO antenna with improved isolation. The antenna covers 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz band, and high isolation at 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz between the antennas is obtained by using one dummy element with a second-order impedance transmission line. The measured results proved that proposed antenna has good impedance matching performance and high isolation.

articleTitle: Harmonics-Based RFID Sensor Based on Graphene Frequency Multiplier and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present here a compact graphene-based radiofrequency identification (RFID) sensor that can simultaneously detect two (bio-)chemical agents with the molecular-level sensitivity. We demonstrate that a simple circuit comprising the functionalized graphene transistors can realize a chemically-sensitive frequency modulator, whose output high harmonics are sensitively influenced by two (bio-)chemical agents. Moreover, the machine learning method is used to analyze multiple output harmonics for retrieving chemical properties of (bio-)chemical agents under detection. The proposed RFID sensor may find various wireless sensing applications and internet-of-things (IoTs).

articleTitle: HF Channel Model at Sunrise with Dominant Galactic Noise
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on recent results from solar physics and past measurements, we provide a new model for the noise encountered in the High Frequency (HF) channel when the main contribution comes from galactic noise. Our goal is to improve past modeling of the heavy tail part of the measured distribution. Our model is an additive mixture of a Gaussian interior with a Kappa exterior. At high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the model can be approximated as a Kappa distribution. This model benefits HF communication, planetary exploration, and possibly major earthquake prediction.

articleTitle: A Metal-Only Reflectarray Antenna Element with Wide Angular Response based on Spiral Slots
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a low cost and reliable metal-only reflectarray antenna element, for operation in the Ku frequency band. The proposed unit-cell consists of two metal sheets placed atop each other, with an air gap spacing in-between. Four square-shaped spiral slots, that are etched on the top metallic sheet, are used to control the reflection phase. Fullwave simulations of the proposed element show that the proposed element produces greater than 360° reflection phase over the Ku frequency band. Furthermore, the element exhibits a low reflection loss of 0.55 dB at normal incidence, which is desirable.

articleTitle: Robust BCS-based Direction-of-Arrival and Bandwidth Estimation of Unknown Signals for Cognitive Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The problem of the estimation of the directions-of-arrival (DoA) and the bandwidth (BW) of wideband signals impinging on an array of electromagnetic sensors is addressed in this work. A novel strategy based on a customized implementation of the Multi- Tasks Bayesian Compressive Sensing (MT -BCS) is proposed to increase the robustness of the joint DoA-and-BW estimation, thanks to the statistical correlation of multiple frequency data samples acquired at consecutive time instants. A preliminary numerical result is reported to show the behavior and the validity of the proposed approach in case of severe noisy condition.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for MIMO Systems with Antenna Tuning Switches
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna for MIMO applications in mobile communication systems is proposed. The proposed design is a monopole antenna with two reflective strips and two antenna tuning switches. By controlling the antenna tuning switches between the strips and the ground plane, two switchable radiation patterns with correlation coefficient as low as 0.15 are achieved.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Leaky Wave Antenna with Broadside Radiation Based on SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized magnetoelectric (ME) dipole leaky wave antenna (L W A). The proposed antenna characterizes its broadside radiation and contains circular polarization when beam scans from backward to forward as frequency increases. Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) is employed as the basic transmission line to guide electromagnetic waves. Impedance matching technique is adopted to eliminate the open-stopband (OSB) effect, which produces a discontinuity for a seamless L W A. A ME dipole layer is added to realize circular polarization (CP). Simulations demonstrate that the scanning range of the proposed antenna is from -12° to +12° and the axial ratio (AR) is below 3dB between 21GHz and 26GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly-Polarized SIW Edge-Radiating Antenna for Beamsteering in 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact circularly-polarized substrate integrated waveguide antenna for the use in a be-amsteering array in 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>generation mobile devices. The circular polarization is achieved through a compact notched-septum polarizer which is optimized for SIW s. Radiation is achieved through a dielectric lens with the addition of via extensions on either side for smaller beamwidth in azimuth and higher gain. A bandwidth of 700 MHz from 27.4 GHz to 28.1 GHz is achieved with worst case HPBW s of 70° in elevation and 60° in azimuth and a gain of 6.2 dB to 6.6 dB. Axial ratios of better than 3 dB are achieved in both planes.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optimization Approaches for Designing Nonuniform Helical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Comparison of various optimization approaches for the design of nonuniform helical antennas is presented. The considered helices have linearly varying radius and pitch. Results show that this design has many similar (or suboptimal) solutions with significant differences in geometry. Combination of particle swarm optimization and Nelder-Mead simplex algorithm proved to be a robust and an efficient optimization approach.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Agile Stub-Loaded Square Patch Antenna with Proximity Coupled Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design of a polarization-agile microstrip-line-coupled-fed patch antenna is proposed. The simple structure of the proposed antenna consists of a square patch symmetrically loaded with two PIN -diode connected short-circuited stubs, and the use of proximity-coupled feed allows inherent impedance matching and RF and DC signal isolation without the need of DC blocking components. The fabricated 1.6-GHz prototype of our proposed antenna, when biased with different DC voltages, can achieve linear and right- and left-handed circular polarizations, respectively.

articleTitle: Triple-Band Loop Antenna for 5G/WLAN Unbroken-Metal-Rimmed Smartwatch
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design concept of integrating the loop antenna into the inner metal frame of a smartwatch for 5G/WLAN application is introduced. The antenna is constructed from a rectangular metal frame which encircled the system circuit board of the watch. A separation distance between the loop and the system ground plane is set to alleviate the strong coupling between the antenna and the ground. The antenna can easily cover the 2.4-GHz band (2400-2485 MHz) for WLAN operation, 3.4-GHz band (3300-3600 MHz) and 4.9-GHz band (4800-5000 MHz) for 5G application in China. Simulated results show that the antenna has an efficiency of 67%-91 % in these operation bands.

articleTitle: Loop Antenna for Deep Implant Powering in an Intracranial Pressure Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a loop antenna for deep implant powering in an intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring application. This work is continuation of our on-going development of a wirelessly powered implantable system for ICP monitoring. Experimental results indicate that the implant can be activated until the depth of 19 mm from the skin. This is 8 mm more than our previous work where we were able to activate the implant until 11 mm depth from the skin. Moreover, we have also presented pressure readout experimental results with the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Towards Integrated Active Antennas for 5G mm-wave Applications at Gapwaves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, in preparation for the upcoming 5G systems, the telecom industry has been showing a great interest in high frequency active antennas. We present a brief overview of the innovative design solution developed at Gapwaves for mmwave digital beamforming applications, capable of addressing all the associated technical issues. We review the general antenna architecture and components and explain how gapwaves technology enables us to achieve high performance, highly integrated active antennas in a cost effective way.

articleTitle: Optimal choice of measurement points in near field: numerical results
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the problem on how to sample the radiated field in order to maximize the performance in inverse source problem is addressed.

articleTitle: Rigorous Statistical Modeling of Propagation in Tunnels with Rough Surface Walls
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The roughness of surface walls, a source of additional and often significant path loss, can play an important role in the accurate modeling of wave propagation in tunnel environments. Despite the long history of tunnel propagation studies, the relevant literature on accounting for surface roughness is rather limited. This paper presents a rigorous approach to incorporate surface roughness into vector parabolic equation based models. The validity of the approach is demonstrated through comparisons to experimental data.

articleTitle: A Substrate-Integrated Fan-Beam Dipole Antenna with Varied Fence Shape for mm-Wave 5G Wireless
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A mm-Wave 5G dipole antenna is presented featuring high gain, fan-beam with wide HPBW in the elevation plane (HPBWEI), and high front-to-back radiation ratio (F/B). The dipole is implemented using vias at the edge of Rogers RO5880 substrate. For boosting the gain and HPBW, flared parasitic vias are added in front of the dipole. To suppress the back radiation, the dipole is surrounded by a via-fence. Two fence shapes were investigated; namely, the rectangular fence and the U-fence where a single dipole, 2×1, and 4×1 arrays were fabricated for each of them. The single elements achieve a measured bandwidth of more than 6.5 GHz around 28 GHz. All fabricated prototypes have F/B greater than 36 dB, with the rectangular fence and U-fence 4×1 dipole arrays achieving HPBWE1/gain of 133.1°/12.61-dBi and 118°/13.5-dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Forward Scattering Based Approach for Remote Impedance Measurement of Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A forward-scattering technique for probeless antenna measurement is presented and demonstrated for a slot element in a large ground plane. The 3-port impedance model representing the probing antennas and antenna under test, and the formulation for the probe-less characterization, are included. Simulations are used to validate the approach. We compare the simulated input impedance of isolated slot antenna (in the absence of probing antennas) with the impedance using remote dipole probing antennas. The agreement is good.

articleTitle: High-Directivty Broadband Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband, circularly polarized (CP), and high-directivity STAR reflector antenna system is proposed. The high system isolation is achieved by mounting well-designed CP receiving (RX) and transmitting (TX) antennas with high front-to-back ratio (F/B) back-to-back. The TX antenna is the feed of a parabolic reflector which flips its sense of circular polarization leading to co-polarized TX/RX radiation and high TX directivity. The designed TX and RX antennas have directivity > 20 dBic and 9 dBic, respectively, and VSWR <; 2 over full C-band (4-8GHz). The system has measured isolation > 46 dB over the band.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Helical Antenna Based on Origami Neoprene with High Radiation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an endurable reconfigurable helical antenna fabricated with 0.1-mm thick conductive polyester sewed on 3-mm thick origami neoprene for more practical applications compared with previous origami antennas based on sketching paper. Measured results show that the proposed antenna achieves max. realized gain of 9.4 dB and 9.2 dB respectively at the unfolded and folded state with a measured 3-dB realized gain bandwidth (BW) of 64.3% and 76% at the two states. Further, the measured radiation efficiency at the two states during their operational BW is no less than 80%.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Use of Different Flux-Gradient Functions in NAVSLaM During Two Experiments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Experimental data from two field campaigns (RED 2001 and CASPER-East 2016) are used to compare and validate variants of the Navy Atmospheric Vertical Surface layer Model (NAVSLaM) using different Monin-Obukhov similarity theory dimensionless scalar profile functions. These comparisons show that using the “Kansas”-type scalar gradient functions of the form Φ = (1-23ξ)-1/2 within NAVSLaM results in the best agreement between modeled and measured propagation loss for both experiments.

articleTitle: Mobile Testbed for Video-Rate Multistatic Microwave Imaging Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A mobile testbed capable of real-time (10 Hz) standoff microwave imaging for concealed threat detection is presented. The system samples a scene with a 1m x 1m multistatic switched antenna array operating at 24–29 GHz. It constructs images on a cost-effective processor at video rate, through the use of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) imaging. Design and operation of the testbed are discussed, and representative experimental images are presented.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Quasi Yagi Antenna Using Lens Technique for 5G Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a lens technique is proposed to enhance gain and bandwidth of a planar Quasi- Yagi antenna. The proposed structure works at 28 GHz which makes it suitable for the challenging 5G wireless communications. In the proposed antenna structure, a loaded dielectric hemisphere lens is used to focalize electromagnetic energy and enhance the gain. The design utilizes a planar quasi- Yagi antenna, which uses a dipole driver and five directors. Simulated results showed a large bandwidth covering about 2 GHz and a high gain up to 15.5 dBi.

articleTitle: SIW-based Reflectarray Antennas with Sharp Gain Selectivity and Large Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution proposes to couple resonant patches with substrate integrated waveguides (SIW)through various slots to design reflective unit-cells with large bandwidth and very sharp frequency response. Such performance is achieved by appropriately combining the patch and slots resonances, while the required phase delay is obtained by adjusting the SIW length. The proposed cell is planar, easy to manufacture, low-loss, and can operate from micro to millimeter waves. A reflect array based on this unit-cell has been designed and analyzed at 9 GHz, exhibiting a 3 dB bandwidth of 18% and a sharp gain selectivity over 16 dB.

articleTitle: Coherence Time and Doppler Spread Analysis of the V2V Channel in Highway and Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we have performed an analysis of the coherence time and Doppler spread of the vehicular-to-vehicular (V2V) propagation channel based on channel measurements at 5.9 GHz. The measurements were collected in a highway and urban environment, where the study of the time variability of the received signal is important due to the motion of both terminals, the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx), together with the objects that are around. The results reported here permit us a better understanding of the V2V propagation channel and can be useful to the deployment of the future vehicular networks.

articleTitle: Compact 2-D FDFD Analysis of Waveguide Structures with ARPACK
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The compact 2-D FDFD method for waveguide is concluded as an sparse eigenvalue problem (EVP). ARPACK is an open software to compute a few eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors of large scale sparse EVPs. As we are just interested in the first few modes, ARPACK is very suitable for solving the EVP. In this paper, a method with ARPACK is proposed to solve the EVP, by which the first few eigenvalues of the waveguide EVP can be solved without the generation of spurious modes, and great efficiency is achieved.

articleTitle: Optimization of Stepped Patch Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna has been optimized by using the covariance matrix adaptation evolutionary strategy optimization method to achieve the impedance bandwidth requirement of the ultra-wideband systems. The antenna has a compact size of 40 × 40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. 3D electromagnetic simulation software, CST STUDIO SUITE is used to simulate the proposed antenna. The measured results show that the antenna provides a wide bandwidth of 118.5% (3.07 -12 GHz).

articleTitle: Embroidered UHF RFID Moisture Sensor Tag on Dishcloth Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present an embroidered passive UHF RFID moisture sensor tag made of dishcloth and conductive yarn. This extremely cost-effective and environmentally friendly wireless sensor can be easily embedded into versatile structures. The initial read range of the sensor tag was 4.7 meters at 915 MHz. In this preliminary study, 10 drops of water were applied on the sensor part of the structure and the performance of the sensor tag was measured in office conditions after 5, 10, and 15 minutes. After 5 minutes and 10 minutes, the read range increased to 5.0 and 5.2 meters, respectively, due to the conductivity improvement of the antenna pattern and increased backscattered power from the tag. After that, the sensor tag started to dry and the read range started to decrease. After 15 minutes, the read range was back to 4.7 meters at 915 MHz. Based on these initial results, these tags show potential for low-cost identification and sensing solutions.

articleTitle: A New Butterfly Radiating Element for Circular Polarized Series Fed Phased Array with Wide Axial Ratio Beamwidth at Millimeter Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new wide beamwidth circular polarized radiating element known as the Butterfly antenna is proposed for series fed phased array antenna applications. The unit Butterfly radiating element investigated at millimeter wave band (86 GHz) demonstrates superior performance with axial ratio (AR) beamwidth of 140° and symmetric pattern performance compared to a conventional Herringbone antenna element. A series-fed 8 × 24 planar array has symmetric beam steering capability of ±34° along φ = 0° plane of the array. While a full phased array antenna with its beamforming network is being developed and fabricated, a passive fixed beam aperture prototype of size 32 × 24 is fabricated and experimentally verified for high purity right-hand circular polarized (RHCP) radiation pattern in the broadside direction.

articleTitle: Coaxial fed Substrate Integrated Waveguide H-Plane Horn Antenna with Air-Filled Concave Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a coaxial fed substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna with phase correction using air-filled concave structure is proposed. This antenna provides high gain along with less variation over the bandwidth as compared to conventional SIW H-plane horn antenna. An impedance bandwidth of 4.7% for| <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup>11| <; -10 dB with a peak gain of 8.4 dBi at 25.8 GHz has been achieved.

articleTitle: 4–40 GHz Transmission Measurement of Indoor Building Materials at Normal Incidence
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transmission of common building materials, such as drywall, cinder block, gypsum board, and glass are characterized over the 4-40 GHz range for normal incidence in a compact anechoic chamber. Results indicate that many interior materials only exhibit modest increase in loss compared to UHF (1 to 4 dB), whereas cinder block can increase loss by as much as 20 to 30 dB.

articleTitle: A Quad-Band Eight-Antenna Array for 5G/WLAN MIMO in Micro Wireless Access Points
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An eight-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array for 5G/WLAN micro wireless access points is proposed in this paper. The proposed MIMO antenna is formed by integrating eight identical antenna elements. For each array element, four operation bands, namely, LTE bands 42/43 (3400-3800 MHz), 4.9-GHz band (4800-5000 MHz) and 5.2-GHz WLAN (5150-5350 MHz) are fully covered for 8 × 8 MIMO use. Through pattern diversity, high isolation and low envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) are achieved. Details of the antenna structure are described. Simulated S-parameter, total efficiency, gain and ECC are also presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Agile Antenna for Smart IoT Gateways
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A pattern agile antenna for smart IoT gateways operating at 2.44 GHz is presented. Several radiation patterns pointing in different directions and characterized by different beamwidths can be obtained.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of a Compressive Reflector Antenna Producing Spatial Coding
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and fabrication of a Compressive Reflector Antenna (CRA)for high-sensing-capacity millimeter-wave imaging applications. The CRA is fabricated using additive manufacturing or 3D printing and metalized by applying silver conductive coating spray on its surface. The near-fields of the CRA are measured when it is fed by a conical horn antenna, a compressive horn antenna, and a perturbed cavity. The singular value distribution and sensing capacity of the CRA fed by the aforementioned antennas are calculated and compared.

articleTitle: Multipath Mitigation Using Weight Suppression for Equalization in Indoor Positioning Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multipath is the dominant source of error in indoor positioning systems, since the reception of multipath can significantly distort the shape of the correlation function used for time-delay estimation. When a band-limited signal is used, the range resolution is often insufficient to decompose the overlapped received signals. This paper presents a multipath mitigation algorithm for ATSC DTV signal-based positioning systems. The algorithm combines sample interpolation with a multipath signal delay estimator based on an equalizer which periodically suppresses a specified number of the lowest-magnitude equalizer weights. The goal of the new equalizer is to more accurately predict the channel response. MATLAB simulations were carried out to demonstrate the proposed method and was confirmed with field-test data. The proposed approach can reduce the range estimation resolution by 60% compared to the Fourier limit.

articleTitle: Design of A Compact Tri-band Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact tri-band omnidirectional circularly polarized (CP) antenna using the zeroth- and the first-order resonance modes of epsilon-negative transmission lines is proposed and designed. The antenna structure is based on a circular mushroom patch with two-group unequal length curved branches with low profile and small size. A left-hand CP (LHCP) at the zeroth-order resonance (ZOR) and two right-hand CP (RHCP) at the first-order resonance (FOR) are obtained, and the omnidirectional axial ratios at the resonance modes in the azimuthal plane are less than 1.44 dB, 1.45 dB and 2.41dB., respectively.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Transmit and Receive System with 1 GHz RF Cancellation Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To address the challenges of the ever increasing spectrum demands, one approach is to implement in-band full duplex wireless systems. A popular approach for implementing full duplex communication without increasing resource utilization is the simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) scheme. However, coupling of the high power transmit signals onto the colocated receiver leads to high signal interference in the operating frequency. Suppressing the high power self-interference is necessary for a successful STAR transceiver implementation, but is very challenging. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of RF self-interference cancellation filters, by suppressing the coupled signal 25dB across 1GHz bandwidth. This wideband cancellation should be contrasted to past cancellation that were narrowband and did not exceed ~100MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Empty Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An Empty Substrate Integrated Waveguide (ESIW)antenna array concept is presented. The ESIW provides an array feed network which offers low loss, low cost, and low profile, in addition to being able to integrate the antenna with other electronics into a single printed circuit board. The antenna is a V-band (60 GHz)4×4 broadside slot-fed Grid Antenna Array. The design of the integrated antenna and feed network is presented, and performance is estimated by simulation.

articleTitle: Phased Antenna Array Calibration Based on Compressed Sensing Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a calibration technique for phased array radars. The real embedded patterns of the array elements are measured independently in operating mode, taking antenna coupling and other parasitic effects into account. A set of angular dependent error coefficients used for the calibration process are extracted from the received signals by making use of a suitable compressed sensing based approach.

articleTitle: A Method for Reducing the Influence of the Limited Ground and Coaxial Feeder on Monopole Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To eliminate the influence of the limited ground and coaxial line on the radiation pattern of the monopole and increase the gain of monopole along the ground direction, a printed circular monopole antenna with a printed choke which is fed by Coplanar Waveguide (CPW)is proposed and analyzed. The antenna is fed by coaxial line and a finite large circular ground is also loaded on the antenna. It is simulated in CST Microwave Studio software®. Simulation results show that the operating frequency band of the antenna is 3.83 GHz-4.06 GHz with its reflection coefficient less than -10 dB. By comparing the simulation results of antenna with and without the choke, it can be concluded that antenna with the choke improved the gain along the direction of the ground at about 13 dB compared with the antenna without choke. This method can be used to decrease the influence of the ground and ceiling on the direction pattern of monopole antenna.

articleTitle: A Compact Multiband Planar MIMO Antenna with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact MIMO antenna with high isolation and a small size of 25×89 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is presented. The proposed antenna consists of two planar-monopole antennas which is capable of covering 890-960 MHz and 1.88-2.69 GHz. To increase the isolation for the two operation bands, slot on the ground and parasitic elements are used. Both of simulation and measurement results show the isolation between two antenna elements is over 10 dB, and all the measured results show the proposed MIMO antenna is a good candidate for portable MIMO applications.

articleTitle: A Biological Testbed for Implanted Antennas Using Layered Porcine Tissue
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A biological testbed developed from layers of pork flesh and products for testing implanted antennas operating at 433 MHz is designed and verified with real-world measurement and CST simulation. The model gave consistent S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> results for a copper dipole across measurement and simulation.

articleTitle: Triband Metamaterial Embedded Implantable Antenna for Biotelemetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Compact metamaterial embedded antenna is presented with tri-band radiation characteristics suitable for biomedical implant applications. The antenna exhibits simultaneous radiations for the Medical Implant Communications Services band for the frequency band of 402-405 MHz as well as Industrial Scientific and Medical bands of 902-928 MHz and 2.4-2.48 GHz. Differential feeding is used for achieving high bandwidth and better radiation characteristics. The overall size of the antenna element is 15.8×13.2×2 mm, with top layer of the proposed antenna consisting of various open ended stubs along with split ring resonator metamaterial for radiation in the upper frequency range. Whereas the bottom layer of the antenna comprises of line segments with slots embedded for the radiation in lower frequency range. The proposed antenna is analyzed and optimized in CST for various dimensions of the lines and stubs. The frequency response along with radiation plots are presented for validation of concept.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Cavity Backed 2⨯4 Slotted Waveguide Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A slotted waveguide antenna array that is fabricated using electroplated 3D printed plastic is demonstrated. The waveguide antenna array is fabricated in three separate pieces and snapped together using a Lego-like process. The waveguide center feed is directly printed with the back cavity which simplifies the process and makes it robust. Measurement results show a 2x4 slot array in good agreement with simulation results. Measured return loss and gain at 7.7 GHz are -15 dB and 15.86 dBi, respectively. In this design, the waveguide is directly printed with the back cavity which simplifies the process and makes it robust.

articleTitle: Effects of Glob Top on mmWave Bond Wire Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We quantify the effects of glob top on the impedance, bandwidth, gain and radiation pattern of quasi-half loop bond wire antennas at 60 GHz using numerical modeling and RF measurements.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Triple-Feed Multi-Beam Array Antenna Using Planar Magic- Ts
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly polarized triple-feed multi-beam array antenna employing two types of planar magic- Ts is proposed. The proposed array antenna, where each of the antenna elements are circularly polarized antennas provides three different radiation patterns in the x-z and y-z planes. The performance of the proposed antenna is experimentally evaluated. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is better than 3.1 % and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is 0.81%. All these features make the proposed antenna very suitable for direction-of-arrival estimation antennas, beam steering antennas and wide-angle rectennas.

Author Keywords: beam steering antenna and wide-angle rectenna

articleTitle: A Novel Meander Line RFID Reader Antenna for UHF Near-Field Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel RFID (radio frequency identification) near-field reader antenna based on electromagnetic coupling in the UHF (ultrahigh-frequency) band. The proposed antenna is composed of a meander open-ended micro-strip line and a loaded 50-ohm resistance to generate a fairly strong and uniform electric field distribution in the near-field region. The measurement results show that the antenna is able to detect multi tags simultaneously within a reading volume: 170 × 150 × 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Fast Node Communication ADMM-based Imaging Algorithm with a Compressive Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a norm-I regularized algorithm, based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), in which the sensing matrix is divided by columns. This technique is based on sectioning the imaging domain into different regions and optimizing them in distributed computational nodes. The information shared among nodes is highly reduced compared to the consensus-based ADMM, when dividing the matrix by rows. The combination of the sectioning-based ADMM with the imaging capabilities of the recently proposed Compressive Reflector Antenna allows a distributed, real-time imaging with fast node communication.

articleTitle: Single-Frequency Material Characterization Using a Microwave Adaptive Reflect-Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Personnel screening systems having reconfigurable reflect-arrays at microwave frequencies have been widely used in airports, government buildings, and other facilities to detect potential threats concealed under clothing. In order to reduce the false-alarm of such systems, a dielectric characterization algorithm using a single-frequency is needed. This paper presents a new algorithm, based on Physical Optics, which is capable of characterizing the complex dielectric constant of a security threat. The proposed method derive the geometric and constitutive properties of the threat by minimizing the variance of the modeled and measured fields at 24.16 GHz. Preliminary results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High Gain Disc Resonator Antenna Array with CPW Coupled for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a disc resonator antenna array with compact size and wide band for THz applications. The disc antenna is designed based on modified SOG technology platform from high resistivity Si. A Dielectric Waveguide (DWG) is matched with the disc dielectric antenna using CPW feed. The CPW feed is designed on the Pyrex side of the Si wafer bonded to the Pyrex. The proposed antenna is designed to operate from 325 GHz to 500 GHz with good return loss. The endfire and broadside antennas are introduced with high gain about 17 dB. The antenna has high efficiency and low cost.

articleTitle: Ray-tracing Simulation and Analysis for Air-to-ground Channel in Railway Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wave propagation in the air-to-ground (A2G) channel is a new trend in wireless communication research. In this paper, we focus on the wireless channel characteristics in an A2G channel at 1.4 GHz, with a transmitter operating at an altitude of 20 km or 100 km to provide wireless connectivity to the users on the train. We reconstruct the three-dimensional (3D) model of an A2G scenario and realize extensive ray-tracing simulations. Based on the simulation results, we model the path loss and shadow fading, which forms the fundamental of effective link budget for the A2G channel in a realistic railway environment.

articleTitle: Effects of Localized Defects / Sources in a Periodic Lattice Using Green's Function of Periodic Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel method is developed to efficiently analyze the effects of localized defects and excitation sources in a periodic array of scatterers such as photonic crystals and metamaterials. The Green's function of the periodic scatterers and the free space Green's function are used to formulate a set of coupled surface integral equations (SIEs) over one or multiple enclosed surfaces surrounding the localized defects and / or excitation sources. The defects can be the removal, deformation, displacement, or distortion in material properties of a scatterer in localized cells. The Green's function of the periodic scatterers represent the field response due to a point source inside the array of the periodic scatterers. The periodic scatterer Green's function is only required to be calculated once to solve any form of defects and/or sources in the localized region of interest. The Green's function of the periodic scatterers can be also represented using few band solutions of the periodic lattice by using the newly developed BroadBand Green's Function with Low wavenumber extraction (BBGFL) technique. This renders the approach applicable to efficient broadband simulations of localized defects / sources analysis and designs.

articleTitle: Study of Misalignment Effects on Hybrid Power Transfer and Wireless Antenna System for Implanted Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the study of the effects of lateral and angular misalignment on a hybrid compact system consisting of a high-frequency coil (13.56 MHz) to transfer power, and an ultra-high frequency antenna (905 MHz) for data communication for implanted medical devices. We numerically simulated the system under misalignment conditions and studied the system performance of power transfer and communication to an implanted receiver inside a layered body tissue model. Insertion loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>) and transmission efficiency (η) for different misalignment conditions were evaluated. It is shown that the proposed hybrid system performance is stable in the range of lateral misalignment of -10 mm to 10 mm, and angular misalignment of 0° to 60°.

articleTitle: Path Loss Measurements and Models at 28 GHz for 90% Outdoor Suburban Coverage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Achieving adequate coverage with high gain antennas is key to realizing the full promise of the wide bandwidth available at mm/cm bands. We report an extensive outdoor suburban measurement campaign at 28 GHz, with over 1300 links measured for 6 NJ houses for ranges of 20 m-200 m, using a specialized narrowband channel sounder. The measurements for the fixed wireless access application, with a 50° (10 dBi) transmit antenna on an exterior of a house and a 10° (24 dBi) receive horn antenna at 3 m height, emulating a lamp post-mounted base station. The 10° base horn antenna was spun at speeds up to 300 rpm to capture azimuthal angular power distribution. It is found that in this suburban environment the Line of Sight condition even on the same street is extremely unlikely beyond 30 m. Measured path gain-distance dependence is well represented by power-law models with a slope of 4, with log-normal deviation of 6.1 dB. Azimuth gains at the base are degraded by scattering by more than 4.5 dB for 10% of links.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Dual-Pol Monopulse Shaped Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: MIT LL is developing a small dual-polarized Ka-band monopulse antenna, which has very challenging specifications imposed on the radiator that require a sophisticated and efficient reflector antenna design. Reflector shaping is a technique that can be used to create a specific non-standard reflector profile to generate a desired aperture illumination that classical parabolic reflector surfaces cannot provide. A comparison with the classical Cassegrain parabolic reflector antenna will be reviewed and results discussed for the antenna design approach utilized at MIT LL. Measured data will be presented for the prototype antenna that was constructed.

articleTitle: Wideband Echo Simulation and Its Application to SAR Image of Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Compared to the narrow band signal, the wideband echo signal includes much more frequency components which have different scattering property with the center frequency. To simulate the scattering echo for the wideband synthetic aperture radar (SAR) more precise, the frequency domain based echo simulation method is proposed which considers the scattering properties of all frequency components. And the hybrid method that combines the geometrical optics (GO) and physical optics (PO), which considers the scattering of reflected rays and has a high calculation accuracy, is used to calculate the scattering property of each frequency component. With the wideband echo signal, the SAR image is generated to analyze to the impact of multiple scattering on complex target.

articleTitle: Self-Oscillating Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer with Robust Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We show that a capacitive wireless power transfer device can be designed as a self-oscillating circuit using operational amplifiers. As the load and the capacitive wireless channels are part of the feedback circuit of the oscillator, the wireless power transfer can self-adjust to the optimal condition under the change of the load resistance and the transfer distance. We have theoretically analyzed and experimentally demonstrated the proposed design. The results show that the operation is robust against changes of various parameters, including the load resistance.

articleTitle: On the Design of Conformal Radomes for Beam-shaping of Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we describe a systematic approach to synthesizing conformal radome., comprised of phase shift structures (PSSs), which is designed to reshape the primary beam in a desirable way. The reshaping technique proposed herein is based on the application of Generalized Law of Refraction (GLR). The design procedure for the beam-shaping conformal radome is discussed and a design example is presented to demonstrate that the reshaping technique can be used to successfully modify the primary beam of a feed horn, placed behind the radome, to a flat-top radiation pattern, which was our desired goal.

articleTitle: Wideband Multi-Loop FSS Absorber Design Based on Q- factor Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Absorbing materials are important to many structures and systems in the defense industry. Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) can be designed to provide a conformal absorptive solution. In this work, a wideband and absorptive FSS is presented that operates over the entire X-band (8.2 to 12.4 GHz). Nickel is utilized for the three-loop conductive elements in order to achieve wideband operation. The design approach utilized here considers the equivalent resonator model, which requires that the radiation quality factor (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rad</sub>) and parallel combination of the conductive and dielectric loss quality factors (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) be comparable for absorptive FSS properties. Using this approach, a single loop FSS is first designed that, when used as a basis for the wideband three-element design, provides the necessary condition of Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rad</sub> = Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The wideband operation is ultimately achieved through proper selection of the individual loop dimensions and relative spacing.

articleTitle: Three Color Correction with Metasurface-backed Gradient-Index Lenses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In practical multi-lens systems, improved optical performance is typically achieved through the use of many individual lenses. However, the introduction of too many elements negatively affects SWaP (size, weight, and power) considerations of the optical system. At the same time, broadband performance typically requires three or more lenses to reduce frequency-dependent (i.e., chromatic) aberrations. Nevertheless, we demonstrate here that by intelligently pairing inhomogeneous lenses with phase-gradient metasurfaces one can achieve broadband chromatic performance while greatly reducing system SWaP.

articleTitle: Field Optimization for Scalar Metasurface Designs for Anomalous Plane- Wave Reflection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For impenetrable metasurfaces described by a scalar surface impedance, a field optimization technique is presented for anomalous plane-wave reflector applications. To the incident and reflected plane waves, a set of evanescent waves co-polarized with the propagating waves are introduced. The discrete evanescent waves are numerically optimized toward obtaining a passive and lossless surface characterization everywhere. Full-wave simulation of an example design characterized by an optimized reactive surface impedance predicts near-perfect anomalous reflection.

articleTitle: Low Cost Broadband Phased Array System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design reviews of 8 to 36 GHz phased array system using piezoelectric transducer (PET). The PET controlled phased array provides benefits such as a low cost, extremely wide bandwidth, and easy fabrication. The proposed phased array system employs a l×4 power divider, PET controlled phase shifter, and four antipodal tapered slot antennas (ATSAs). The multi-thru PET controlled phase shifter showed a total perturbation loss of less than 4 dB up to 40 GHz, with a maximum phase shift of more than 650°. The measured radiation pattern validates the beam scanning performance of the fabricated broadband array system.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analyze of Conformal SCMR System for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple scenarios of using a Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) system for wireless power transfer (WPT) will be studied. The effects of the CSCMR will be studied on different parts of the body as well as embedded in pork to represent the human flesh. The test points on the human body are shown in the figure below. We will analyze the SCMR systems response on different part of human body operating environments and the impact they have on the efficiency of operation. Our analysis is conducted through accurate simulations and validated through physical implementation.

articleTitle: On the Modeling of the Bistatic Coherent Scattering from a Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we investigate on the coherent bistatic scattering generated by a radar system when illuminating a rough surface. Moving from the well-known scattering theory based on the Kirchhoff approximation, we propose an extended formulation of the Fung-Eom model, by introducing a higherorder expansion on the phase term of the impinging spherical wave. We demonstrate and discuss the importance of such correction for the accurate characterization of the coherent scattering generated in bistatic radar system. We give insight, for the first time, on the role played by both the antenna pattern and the wavefront sphericity in bistatic scattering in the whole incidence plane, not limiting the analysis to the backscattering and specular directions. This is particularly important for practical applications, such as the modeling of the scattering generated by sources of opportunity.

articleTitle: Demonstration of TM01 Circular Waveguide Mode in Matched Feeds for Single Offset Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Matched-feed horns can be employed to reduce the inherent cross polarization of offset reflector antennas. For circular horns, the traditional method is to excite TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> modes in the aperture. We recently proposed that TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> or TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> modes can be used instead, for horizontal and vertical polarization, respectively. To validate this, a matched feed using TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o1</sub> is designed and demonstrated for the first time. The presented horn reduces cross polarization by 17 dB at the design frequency and by 10 dB over a 2.2 % bandwidth.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Compact Range Feed with 30 dB Polarization Isolation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We have developed a dual polarized compact range feed with a cross-polarization level of -30 dB from 10.7 GHz GHz to 13 GHz.

articleTitle: The Design and Analysis of a Compact Directional Antenna Composed of the Discrete Monopoles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To increase the gain of the directional antenna and reduce the size on the polarized direction, a directional antenna with twelve uniform discrete monopoles was proposed. Each monopole has an isolated ground plane, and the driven element is fed by a coaxial line. The Simulated results by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\bigcirc R</sup> and the experimental results of the manufactured antennas prototype show that the operating band is 2.349-2.543 GHz with the VSWR less than 2. And the gains in the band are better than 10 dBi in ISM band. The current phases are simulated and analyzed to explain the radiation mechanism. This antenna can be used in ISM band communication systems.

articleTitle: An Effect of Via-Holes Barriers on Circularly Polarized Patch Antennas for Getting Currents' Phase-Lags
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple way to get 90 degrees currents' phase-lags on patch antennas is presented in this paper. Structures to get 90 degrees currents' phase-lags are necessary for constituting circularly polarized (CP) antennas. In this study, via-holes barriers are made for making the currents' phase-lag on patch antennas. The effect of the via-holes barriers on a square path antenna is explained first. Then, the via-holes barriers have been applied to constitute a CP patch antenna. The CP antenna is constituted to the size of 0.17μ×0.15μ (μ is the free space wave length) due to the via-holes barriers.

articleTitle: Perturbative Reciprocal Formulation for Maxwell's Equations: a First Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate theoretically the electromagnetic field scattered by a manufactured object having inhomogeneous perturbations of electromagnetic material properties. A well-known objet having the same geometry and homogeneous material properties is exploited as a reference. Hence only small variations from reference configuration are of interest. Starting from the Volumetric-Perturbative Reciprocal Theory (VPRT), we derive an expression of the relationship between the reference configuration (which is supposed perfectly known) and the perturbed one: in addition to the permittivity, we extend the VPRT to permeability perturbations and we derive the first order expression for axisymmetric objects having axisymmetric perturbations. The resulting formulation can be used in a direct way, for example to propagate uncertainties, as well as to solve an inverse problem for example in non-destructive testing applications.

articleTitle: Virtual Drive Test for Vehicle Antenna Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Drive test has been the method to evaluate the performance of the automotive antennas in urban and suburban/ rural environments. Virtual drive test (VDT) using high-frequency electromagnetic and wave-propagation simulation software can be used instead to evaluate vehicular antennas performance. This paper presents a simulation-based method for evaluating LTE automotive antenna installed on a roof of a vehicle in an urban environment with and without surrounding traffic. A full-wave method; namely, the Multi-Level Fast Multipole Method (MLFMM) is used to perform the analysis of the antenna placed on a vehicle. Whereas Ray-optical Intelligent ray tracing model (IRT) is used to evaluate the installed antenna performance, in here received power, in a non-stationary environment. The received power of the vehicle antenna with and without traffic was found to minorly disagree in a complex urban environment.

articleTitle: Analytical Solution to the Incident Power of the Tapered Wave in 3-D Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The tapered incident has been applied in rough surface 3-D scattering to meet the surface truncation requirement of the method of moments (MoM). The properties of such a wave provide concentration near the scattering center and attenuation to negligible in intensity for most of the incident angles. The resulting scattered intensities need to be normalized by the tapered incident power, to quantitatively predict the radar cross-section (RCS). The exact expression is analytically elaborated instead of the conventionally numerical method, to avoid losing information on the surface edges and improve the computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Sub-array Design of a Cavity-Loaded E-Band Partially-Corporate Fed Waveguide Slot Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 16×16-element partially-corporate fed waveguide slot array with 4×4 sub-arrays has been developed in the E-band with a bandwidth of about 9%. Wideband design of the 4×4-element sub-array is under development for covering the frequency band of 71-86 GHz.
