To further enhance the bandwidth, we introduced the air-cavities on the top of radiating waveguides, and applied over-loading technique to redesign the standing-wave fed sub-arrays. Finally, the bandwidth for reflection less than -15 dB is enhanced to 18%.

articleTitle: Dispersion Analysis of Electron Bernstein Waves in Magnetized Warm Plasmas by Finite Element Particle- in -Cell Modeling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report on a study of the dispersion characteristics of electron Bernstein waves in magnetized warm plasmas using a conservative finite element time domain (FETD) particle-in-cell (PIC) algorithm. Conventional FETD-PIC algorithms on irregular grids violate charge-conservation because the ensuing charge continuity equation leaves residuals at the discrete level. It is shown that the use of a charge-conserving FETD-PIC algorithm suppresses spurious static (self-)fields due to charge deposition on the grid and consequently produces less noisy spectral bands.

articleTitle: Backward to Forward Beam Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna Base on Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide (CSIW) with rectangle ring slot is proposed and designed for leaky wave antennas (LWA) capable of beam scanning from backward to forward directions. The rectangular ring slot does not only enable the energy leaking, but also provides serial capacitance. In addition, the grounded vias and quarter-wave open-circuit stubs provide shunt inductance. Thus, the proposed CSIW exhibits lefthanded characteristics which enable beam scanning through the broadside. To suppress the stop-band, an equivalent circuit model is developed. Finally, a balanced leaky wave antenna is designed with a radiation angle from −53° to 23° with the frequency ranging from 9.8 GHz to 12 GHz, and the gain is better than 8.5 dB and the maximum gain achieves 10.7 dB.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Tunable Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tunable phase shifter is presented in this paper. The phase shifter is built using a multi-material 3D printer and is presented as a proof of concept for a 3D printed Liquid Crystal Device (LCD).

Author Keywords: Buried Corrugated Substrate Integrated Folded Waveguide (BCSIFW)

articleTitle: A Silicon-Based Beam-Steering Tapered Antenna Array for W-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a Silicon Image Guide (SIG) tapered antenna array for operating at 77 GHz. A novel and simple technique is used for steering the main beam. The antenna provides a beam-steering capability up to ±12°. the optimized antenna array demonstrates radiation efficiency better than 95% and the max gain of 15 dBi, which drops only 0.1 dB all over the beam scanning range.

articleTitle: Gain Improvement of Phased Array using Sub-Arrayed Microstrip Patch Antennas for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a sub-array structure of a microstrip patch antennas is proposed as a phased array element to improve gain at low elevation angle for satellite communication. This subarray antenna has a radiation pattern with the conformation of two main lobes. Each 3dB beam-width coverage of beam pattern is ±17.7° to ±65.0°. The gain of the proposed phased array antenna was increased 2.67dB at theta 55°, compared to the conventional phased array antenna. The proposed antenna operates left-hand circularly polarization (LHCP) at 11.85GHz for satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Planar Wide-Angle Scanning Periodic Sparse Phased Array Using Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a planar periodic sparse phased array using two-dimensional pattern reconfigurable antenna elements is proposed to realize wide-angle scanning performance. The pattern reconfigurable element consists of a circularly polarized microstrip antenna and four parasitic elements with diode switches. The antenna element can radiate towards the normal direction or steer its main beam in four different space quadrants by changing the states of the diode switches. For each dimension of the array, the distance between neighboring elements is 0.7 λ. Simulation results indicate that the array can scan its main beam from -60° to 60° with a gain fluctuation less than 2 dB. The coverage of 3-dB beamwidth of the array is from about -71° to 71°. Meanwhile, the side lobe level (SLL)maintain bellows -8.2 dB. Then, comparisons to a conventional phased array are performed to highlight its advantages.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Intra-chip Transmission between Wireless Interconnects using Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we have shown enhancement of intra-chip transmission between wireless interconnects, which are implemented as antenna-on-chip (AoC), using Jerusalem-Cross Artificial Magnetic Conductor (JC-AMC). AoCs are located at the center of four-quadrants of a multicore chip. For each quadrant, a zigzag monopole AoC above a JC-AMC surface is simulated to resonate at 30GHz with a return loss of -13dB. The enhancement is almost 3dB for two out of three antenna pairs. This enhancement has almost doubled the received power at the antenna with JC-AMC which is beneficial when designing on-chip integrated transceivers. For experimental validation, fabrication of the zigzag antennas with JC-AMC surfaces on silicon wafer are under progress.

articleTitle: High Performance Dual Polarized Near-Field Probe at V-Band for Spherical Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: V-band (50-75GHz) applications such as 5G and myriad others are the catalyst for high performance near-field antenna measurement systems. For Spherical Near-Field (SNF), the traditional approaches at millimeter wave frequencies collect two full spheres of data in the near-field where each sphere samples one of two linear and orthogonal fields of the antenna under test (AUT). These two orthogonal polarizations are traditionally achieved through mechanical rotation of a single polarized probe. To improve measurement time and accuracy, MVG has developed a dual polarized V -band probe. This probe has been integrated in a millimeter wave SNF system (u-Lab) and is connected to two simultaneously sampled parallel receiver channels. This approach only requires one sphere to be measured and it ensures the two polarization components are sampled at the same point in space and time. The SNF probe design proposed in this paper is based on an axially corrugated aperture. The probe includes a compact integrated ortho-modal transducer (OMT) and the ports are WR-15 waveguide. This paper will present the design requirement, design details, and measured performances of the proposed dual polarized SNF probe.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Polarized Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized antenna with a novel planar configuration is presented for base station applications. Two groups of simple dipoles are fed by two microstrip feed networks to achieve ±45° polarizations. A novel feeding technique that leads to a planar configuration is described. Measured results show that excellent matching and stable radiation performances are achieved over a wide band.

articleTitle: A Forward Approach to Establish Parametric Scattering Center Models for Complex Dielectric Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a forward approach to establish parametric scattering center models for complex dielectric targets. It proposes a space ray diversity method for complex medium targets based on ray splitting tracing method. Based on the high frequency electromagnetic mechanism of complex targets, a method of calculating the equivalent action point of internal coupling action ray is proposed. This solves the problem of the forward calculation of the three-dimensional position parameters of the scattering center. Finally, the decomposition and its quantitative characterization technique of strong scattering source for complex dielectric targets are obtained, and the target scattering center model with complex dielectric has been established with clear and accurate scattering mechanism. This method greatly expands the scope of target application in the forward modeling method of attribute scattering center. Finally, a simplified wing calculation example shows the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stochastic Finite Difference Frequency Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel stochastic numerical method called stochastic finite difference frequency domain (S-FDFD). S-FDFD introduced in this paper directly inserts the statistical variations of electrical properties into the FDFD. Comparison between full-fledged multi run Monte Carlo results and those of single run S-FDFD shows that the S-FDFD method can predict the mean and variance of EM fields with a fair degree of accuracy in a computationally efficient way.

articleTitle: Spreading and wander of partially coherent beams propagating in the turbulent atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The influence of turbulence on the beam spreading and wander of partially coherent beams (PCBs)in the atmosphere is analyzed. PCBs show advantage over fully coherent ones in mitigating the turbulence-induced beam wander, and it can be further enhanced by modulating the spectral degree of coherence. Beam spreading will be increased and beam wander will be decreased by increasing the beam parameters n and β of Laguerre-Gaussian Schell-model (LGSM)and Bessel-Gaussian Schell-model (BGSM)beams.

articleTitle: Numerical Implementation of Equivalence Principle Algorithm for Potentials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel implementation of the equivalence principle algorithm (EPA) applied to the recently developed potential integral equations (PIEs) for low-frequency problems involving perfect electric conductors. The equivalence integral equations are generalized and updated by including potentials, making it possible to use PIEs to formulate inner problems. The stability of the implementation is demonstrated on canonical objects.

articleTitle: An Inkjet-printed Origami-based Frequency Selective Surface with Wide Frequency and Bandwidth Tunability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A state-of-the-art inkjet-printed tunable origami frequency selective surface (FSS) on cellulose paper is presented that can change its resonant frequency as well as its bandwidth by mechanically folding the structure. Special “bridge-like” structures are introduced alongside the conductive traces to increase their flexibility, thereby avoiding breakage during the folding or bending process. The structure also features a wide angle of incidence rejection capability that facilitates it usage to a wide range of applications ranging from smart skins, tunable radome design and reduction in radar cross section of antennas.

articleTitle: Cutting The Cord: A Button-Sized Rectenna for Wireless Patient Monitoring Using Radiated Near-Field Signals at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2.4 GHz RF power transfer device is presented for wireless patient monitoring in the radiated near-field zone. Instead of near-field coils that are highly sensitive to misalignments and distance, an external button-sized rectifying antenna (rectenna) is proposed. This rectenna can be easily attached to the patient's skin or clothing. It consists of a small (15 × 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) antenna connected to a voltage doubling rectifier with a minimum conversion loss of 4.2 dB. A position sensitivity analysis is demonstrated across a 20 cm diameter, and concludes with a demonstration of a temperature sensor being activated wirelessly on a human phantom.

articleTitle: Rigorous Modal Analysis of Electromagnetic Coupling Between Circular Horns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a rigorous modal analysis of electromagnetic coupling between circular horns. The Generalized Scattering Matrix (GSM) of each horn is obtained by the hybrid boundary contour mode-matching (BCMM) technique, and then connected by free-space spherical wave transmission lines, leading to a global GSM description. Two numerical examples, with respect to horns of the same shape and different gains, respectively, are proposed to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the hybrid method.

articleTitle: Design of a Multiband Feed Antenna for Orthogonal Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multiband feed antenna can achieve the goal of function integration and structure miniaturization. As the main part of the feed antenna, a coaxial orthomode transducer (OMT) is proposed to separate the incoming signal into two linear polarizations and transfer them to the orthogonal ports. Using a turnstile junction in OMT, good input match, high isolation and cross polarization isolation can be achieved over a wide bandwidth. This paper reports on a multiband feed antenna which applies to remote sensing area has low loss and good isolation covering three remote sensing detection working frequencies (89 GHz, 22.3 GHz and 18.6 GHz).

articleTitle: Hourly Variation of Gaseous Attenuation in Tropical Station
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Attenuation by water vapor and oxygen is one of the major reasons electromagnetic waves in some frequency bands get degraded. It is of key importance to study, understand and mitigate these effects as much as possible. In this work, hourly attenuation due to water vapor also known as wet attenuation as well as attenuation due to oxygen, known as dry attenuation in decibel per kilometer was calculated for the Ka, Ku and V frequency bands. The International Telecommunications Union-676 model was used to calculate these values using 60 seconds integration time measured values of Pressure, Temperature and Relative humidity. These parameters were obtained from the Covenant University Davis-Pro Automatic weather station installed in Ota, Nigeria. The computed results between April and December 2012 are hereby presented.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Shaped Beams using Active Element Patterns and Spectral Factorization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We solve the problem of synthesizing mask constrained power patterns by means of linear arrays by extending the Spectral Factorization approach to the case wherein mutual coupling or platform effects are present.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Metasurface Based Absorber for Sub Millimetric / THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metasurface absorber is designed in the THz band in order to investigate the field polarization. the conventional SRR and the proposed structure are investigated, firstly by applying X-polarized electric field on both cells and secondly applying Y -polarized electric field on both cells. as a result the conventional SRR reflects the incident electric field when the electric field is X-polarized and absorb when the electric field is Y -polarized. in case of the proposed structure is checked, it absorbs the incident wave in both directions of electric field polarization and the absorption is enhanced greater than the conventional one.

articleTitle: Acceleration of reduced matrix filling in near field region for M-CBFM using 2-level CBFs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As the importance of the direct solver-based MoM algorithm increases, we proposed 2-level MCBFM which reduces degree of freedom by using 2-level CBF and increase efficiency of near field region calculation.

articleTitle: A Broadband RHCP/LHCP SIW-Integrated Patch Array Antenna for MM-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Right-hand (RH)/left-hand (LH) circularly polarized (CP) antenna, made of two integrated linear polarized (LP) microstrip patch antennas (MPA) fed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW), is presented. The antenna uses a 3dB SIW quadrature hybrid coupler to generate right/left hand CP radiated field from two LP antennas with two excitation ports. The structure was designed and simulated. Simulation results reveal that the antennas show 3dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth over the frequency band ~51.15-68.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Imaging of Two Dimensional Scatterers using Descent Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we study the application of the supervised descent method to two-dimensional electromagnetic inverse problems. The inversion process contains two stages: offline training and online prediction. In the offline stage, the average descent directions of cost functions are learned from a set of training data; and in the online stage, model reconstruction is achieved through iterative minimization based on learned descent directions. This scheme offers a new perspective to incorporate prior information into inversion, and reduce the computational complexity in the online inversion. Numerical examples validate the accuracy and efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Components Based on Gap Waveguide Using Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper shows additive manufacturing as an advantageous option for manufacturing and designing components based on gap waveguide. 3D printing increases the degree of freedom in structural design because its complexity has no impact on the cost of production. This makes 3D printing an ideal manufacturing method for small devices with intricate details, such as the designs proposed in groove gap waveguide for W -band. In addition, the plating process of the printed plastic structure results in a very thin and smooth copper layer which produces very low losses.

articleTitle: Study of the Resonant Frequencies of an Electrically Small Broadside-coupled Split-ring Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The resonant frequencies of a broadside-coupled split-ring resonator (BC-SRR) printed on an FR-4 substrate are studied by eigenmode analysis to realize an electrically small multi-band BC-SRR antenna. It is shown that not only the resonant frequency of the first (lowest) mode but also those of higher-order modes can be controlled by connecting conductive patterns to the ends of a BC-SRR. A BC-SRR resonating in the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands for wireless LAN was designed. At the first resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz, the outer dimension of the designed BC-SRR is as small as 0.029λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.025 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> is the wavelength.

articleTitle: A Loop-Line Antenna with Wideband Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using the moment method, we analyze a loop antenna with parallel wires for circularly polarized (CP) radiation. Special attention is paid to a CP wave bandwidth versus the loop height above the ground plane. It is found that a maximum bandwidth of 8% for a 3-dB axial-ratio criterion is obtained for a loop height of 0.2 wavelengths. This leads to a further analysis of a microstrip-line antenna consisting of the loop elements (loop-line antenna). It is revealed that the CP wave bandwidth is wider than that of a conventional loop-line antenna by a factor of two.

articleTitle: Broadband, Wide-Beam Antenna for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadband, wide-beam antenna composed of a sleeve monopole, a grounded reflector, and a parasitic director. The antenna configuration achieves a wide azimuth half-power beamwidth of approximately 145°-180°, and the director and feed cable are shown to provide elevation pattern control. The antenna exhibits return loss better than -13 dB from 1.7-2.7 GHz corresponding to 2G/3G/4G frequencies. The antenna is ideal for base station applications requiring a wide azimuth beamwidth.

articleTitle: Determining Characteristic Mode Metrics of Interest for Electrically Large Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) is often applied to electrically small designs. However, when studying the modal decompositions of electrically large structures with noncontiguous geometries, namely finite antenna arrays, one must adopt a new means of presenting and making use of CM data. In this work we explore some prominent differences for which one must account when studying CM data for larger designs.

articleTitle: Stepped Impedance Resonator Based Uniplanar Dipole Antenna with Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact uniplanar stepped impedance dipole antenna for 2.4 GHz WLAN application is presented. This antenna resonates at its fundamental frequency with excellent suppression of higher harmonics. The proposed antenna has an overall dimension of 45 × 12 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>when fabricated on a substrate of relative dielectric constant 4.4 with a loss tangent of 0.02. The antenna offers good radiation characteristics with reasonable gain. The simulated and measured radiation characteristics of the antenna are presented in detail.

articleTitle: On the use of MmCn-BBO for Antenna Problems Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This communication deals with a new family of global optimization algorithms, named M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> -BBO. The different schemes are modifications of the Biogeography Based Optimization (BBO) algorithm, developed with the aim to improve its performances, and in particular to reduce its risk of stagnation and slow convergence. The capabilities of the MrnCn-BBO schemes are here analyzed and compared with other algorithms when they are applied to the optimization of a planar reflectarray.

articleTitle: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioning in Voxel-based Finite Element Analysis of Scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The nonconforming voxel finite element method (NVFEM) simplifies the meshing of complex structures by using cubical elements of different sizes. It has been proposed as an alternative to traditional, unstructured finite element methods for electromagnetic scattering problems. Recently a multigrid preconditioner was introduced for solving the matrix problem. It is shown that this preconditioner allows the matrix equation to be solved in O(n) time as the mesh is refined, where n is the number of degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Higher-Order Bessel Beams Launchers Comparison
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discuss the characteristics of the field radiated by higher-order Bessel beams launchers when generated through a cylindrical standing wave or a cylindrical inward traveling wave aperture distribution. In both the cases the launchers are obtained by using a properly designed Radial Line Slot Array antenna. The actual case where the radiating elements are arranged on the upper plate of the parallel plate waveguide, starting from a circumference of not infinitesimal radius, is analyzed.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of a Broadband Dual-Polarized Minkowski Fractal Microstrip Antenna for S-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband dual polarization Minkowski fractal microstrip antenna for S band is proposed. This antenna design can realize dual polarization by using orthogonal slots coupling feeding technique, broaden the bandwidth and increase the gains by double-layers radiation patches. In addition, Minkowski fractal boundary is employed to reduce the sizes of the radiation patches achieving the antenna's miniaturization. The Simulated results by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> indicate that the impedance bandwidth of |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB is 2.93-3.82 GHz (26.4 %) and the gains varies smoothly from 8.6 to 9.6 dBi. The radiation patterns of the antenna are stable in the whole operating band with the main lobe width of 77° + 8.75° and the front-to-back ratio (FBR) over 16.5 dB. This antenna is easily to form an array for the gains' improvement.

articleTitle: An Optical Leaky Waveguide Excitation by Offset Prabolic Reflector using Photonic Bandgap
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a excitation method of optical leaky waveguide antenna (OLWA) by parabolic reflector using photonic bandgap. We evaluate the performance of OLWA by proposed and conventional excitation method in the simulation. Our proposed method enables to excite OLWA with small feeding circuit.

articleTitle: Decoupled Dual-band Slot Antenna with Bidirectional Patterns for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-port dual-band slot antenna with bidirectional radiation pattern is presented in this paper. A fork-shaped monopole is designed as the element, generating three resonant points to cover the desired two bands for WLAN systems. In order to obtain bidirectional patterns in both operation bands, the monopole is printed above a slotted square ground, forming the slot antenna. Besides, a decoupling structure is proposed, which consists of three protruded strips connected with a rectangle patch for isolation enhancement, simultaneously maintaining the operation band for each element. A prototype is fabricated and measured for validation. The measured results show that the proposed antenna exhibits two operation bands of 2.36-2.65 GHz and 5-5.5 GHz, with the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> lower than -10 dB. An isolation of higher than 15 dB is also achieved in the operation bands.

articleTitle: Unbalanced-Fed Rectangular Loop Antennas for Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Analysis is newly performed for a one-wavelength rectangular loop antenna having an unbalanced feed. This antenna radiates an axial beam in a direction normal to the antenna plane. Subsequently, the axial beam is transformed into a conical beam by taking the loop perimeter to be two wavelengths. It is found that as the aspect ratio is varied, the antenna shows two minima in the axial ratio characteristic, where the rotational senses of the circular polarization are different from each other. Finally, a tilted beam is formed by superimposing the axial and conical beams for a double-loop antenna.

articleTitle: Functional All-dielectric Metasurfaces for Efficient Manipulation of Electromagnetic Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: All-dielectric metasurfaces based on high-index particles with large aspect ratio for efficient manipulation of electromagnetic waves in visible and microwave frequency domains are discussed. Microwave metasurface exhibiting the multiband unidirectional response insensitive to the polarization of the incident wave is demonstrated. A novel type of all-dielectric metasurfaces which support dominant toroidal dipole response over a wide frequency range in the visible is proposed.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Microwave Biosensor for Single Biological Cell Characterization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A highly sensitive label-free biosensor for detection and characterization of human cells is presented. The biosensor is based on a split-ring resonator with a split-cut of 35μm wide that operates at 2 GHz. The biosensor is designed and simulated using a full-wave simulation tool (Ansys HFSS). Two types of human cells ware modeled as solid spheres with their corresponding experimentally measured electrical properties found in the literature. The resonator successfully differentiated between the two human cells by the means of frequency shifts and changes in its insertion loss.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of Plasmonic Thin-Film Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents the fabrication and experimental characterization of a plasmonic thin-film terahertz photoconductive antenna. The fabricated plasmonic thin-film devices were characterized in a time-domain spectrometer setup. The devices demonstrated a 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> times increase in the average power when compared to a conventional device, as well as over 4 THz usable bandwidth. This increase in performance was due to the combination of plasmonic nanostructures and a thin-film optically resonant photoconductive layer. These features effectively trap the optical laser beam used to drive the antenna in a region of the photoconductor nearest to the antenna electrodes, increasing collection efficiency of the photocarriers and output THz power of the antenna.

articleTitle: A Unit Cell for Bianisotropic Huygens' Metasurface Designs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Bianisotropy in metasurface designs offers a solution to produce arbitrary wave transformations even when the incident and transmitted waves differ largely in their transverse wave impedances. By using asymmetry in unit cell designs, bianisotropy can be generated. Such asymmetric bianisotropic unit cells have been discussed and investigated utilizing the stacked-layer topology. However, an asymmetric version of the more natural dipole-loop unit cell has yet to be proposed. In this paper, we present an asymmetric dipole-loop unit cell which demonstrates matching capabilities that may be used for bianisotropic reflectionless wide-angle refraction. This concept is verified using fullwave results for a normally incident plane wave intended for refraction at 71.8° at 20GHz.

articleTitle: Slot-loaded SIW-fed Wide-band Yagi Antenna having End-fire / Broadside Scanning Features
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, design of a wide-band SIW-fed printed Yagi antenna with frequency dependent radiation properties is reported. The proposed antenna utilizes an offset longitudinal slot on the SIW-feed structure, which excites a higher frequency antenna resonance having broadside radiation characteristics. Merging of this slot-mode with the end-fire Yagi dipole-mode in lower frequency range results in wide impedance bandwidth as well as radiation features showing gradual transition from end-fire to broadside direction with increase in frequency.

articleTitle: The Impact of Integration Order and Accuracy on the Stability of Time Domain Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The integration rules and orders for the computation of kernel elements directly effect the stability of the discretization of time domain integral equations for electromagnetic analysis. Our previous works examined this effect for closed objects using an analysis based on the combined field integral equation. In this work, we use adaptive quadrature to show the impact of integration accuracy in kernel computation on stability for open structures analyzed with the electric field integral equation. Numerical results show a high integral order does not necessarily bring a high accuracy, and that a higher accuracy in the near field integration can be helpful to achieve stability.

articleTitle: Thin Metallic Coatings on Carbon Fiber for Enhanced mm-Wave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the effect of metal plating on the reflection, transmission and absorption of resonant fibers in epoxy. We demonstrate that addition of either a nickel or copper coating leads to reduced reflection, reduced transmission and enhanced loss for low concentrations of these carbon fibers. At mm-wave frequencies, we demonstrate that more than lOdB of absorption can be achieved in transmission through a 1.65mm sample of epoxy containing copper/nickel-coated carbon fibers.

articleTitle: Effects of Antenna Pattern Asymmetry on Radar Angle Rate Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for the direct measurement of the angular velocity of moving objects using a distributed radar has recently been demonstrated by the authors. The theoretical accuracy of the angular velocity estimation depends on the angular distribution of the electric field intensity, and asymmetry in the distribution will cause the estimate to degrade. In this work, we analyze the effect of asymmetries in the electric field for linear arrays generating a near-optimal dual-beam electric field pattern. We show that for errors of up to 3 dB between the two beam intensities, the estimation accuracy degrades by less than a factor of two.

articleTitle: Integrated vs Separated Radomes for Slotted-Waveguide Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The usage of radomes improves the resistance of slotted-waveguide antennas against complex environmental conditions and extends possible applications of the antennas. In the presentation, two approaches to the development of radomes for such antennas are considered. The first approach is based on the application of standard separated radomes of the sandwich type. The second, alternative, approach is relied on the usage of a dielectric layer integrated directly in the slotted waveguide. The corresponding designs and fabrication technologies of antennas with such radomes are discussed. The development of X-band panel antenna arrays with different radome realizations is presented to illustrate and compare the solutions.

articleTitle: Influence of Different Antenna Locations on Channel Characterization for V2V Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The V2V communications have been widely investigated. This paper studies the influence of different antenna locations on channel characterization for V2V communications. First of all, we carried out the channel measurement in urban with different antenna locations. Then, some typical channel parameters are extracted, such as power delay profile and path loss. Using these channel parameters, we analyze the effect of different antenna locations on channel characteristics in V2V communications. These results contribute to the design of the V2V communication system.

articleTitle: Spurious-Free Surface Integral Equation Characteristic Mode Formulation for Dielectric Bodies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new surface integral equation based formulation for computing characteristic modes of lossless and lossy dielectric and magneto-dielectric bodies is presented. For lossy objects, the imaginary part of an eigenvalue gives the ratio of the dissipated and radiated power, while the real part is connected to the ratio of the reactive and radiated power.

articleTitle: Space-time focusing using a dispersive axicon
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dispersive axicon is proposed as a means of generating pulses that are localized in both space and time. The axicon's frequency-dependent dielectric constant allows the generation of Bessel beams with varying group velocities, which is exploited to compress pulses propagating in free space. The spatial localization inherent to Bessel beams combined with this temporal localization results in simultaneous space-time focusing.

articleTitle: Designing New Generation Antennas for 5G MiMo Systems - A New Perspective in Array Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current design methodologies of new generation antenna arrays for mobile wireless communication systems are aimed at maximizing radar-based performance metrics that are of secondary importance for the desired application. Indeed, these approaches expect the capacity of the system, which is the main quality metric of a communication system, to be maximized as a secondary effect of the design process. In this work, it is proved that the channel performance of “classical” design methodologies can be overcome, by means of innovative “unconventional” design methodologies, if the propagation scenario, and therefore the capacity of the system, is taken into consideration in the design process. Towards this end, an illustrative numerical example is shown in order to provide a preliminary proof-of-concept.

articleTitle: Wave-Matter Interaction Analysis of Metamaterial Unit Immerged in Liquid Media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper analyzes the interaction between the incident electromagnetic wave and the metamaterial unit (the regular split ring pair) immerged in a low-loss liquid media, and interesting dynamic phenomena are observed. The resonance frequency shifts of the meta material unit exposed in air and immerged in polyalphaolefin (PAO) are experimentally investigated and compared, and such shift ranges in different acting times are also provided. The observed resonance shift is mainly resulting from the distance reduction between the two split rings because of the induced Ampere's force acting on the structure. Such findings can open a new research area in the metamaterial community and have many potential applications for the characterizations of the liquid media with metamaterials.

articleTitle: Characteristic Basis Function Method for the Analysis of Composite Objects Embedded in Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai Equations associated with the Mixed Potential Integral Equations (PMCHWT-MPIE) are used to analyze objects comprising of lossy composite materials embedded in layered media, and the Discrete Complex Image Method (DCIM) is used to generate the Dyadic Green's Functions. Compared to the MOM analysis based on the Impedance Boundary Condition (IBC), the PMCHWT-based analysis is more robust when dealing with highly lossy objects embedded in layered media. We choose the Characteristic Basis Functions Method (CBFM) for this problem because it is iteration-free and, hence, is suitable for dealing with multiple RHS efficiently. Yet another reason for this choice is that the GPU can be used to accelerate the filling process of the submatrices of the impedance matrix when generating the Characteristic Basis Functions (CBFs).

articleTitle: Direct Optimization of Quasi-Periodic Surfaces in Multi-Reflector Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In recent years, there has been an increasing interest in replacing traditional periodic surfaces, e.g., frequency selective surfaces, with quasi-periodic surfaces (non-identical elements) in multi-reflector systems for satellite applications. Quasi-periodic surfaces can be used to improve existing antenna solutions or to provide innovative concepts not possible with periodic surfaces. In many scenarios, the periodic/quasi-periodic surface is used in a multi-reflector configuration, e.g., as a subreflector, where the design specifications are on the radiation pattern from the main reflector. For these applications, the design of the surface is usually carried out using an in-direct optimization approach which may provide sub-optimal designs. In this paper, we demonstrate the direct optimization of quasi-periodic surfaces for the final pattern performance. This means that all array elements in the quasi-periodic surface are optimized simultaneously to directly fulfill the goal specifications on the final pattern from the main aperture.

articleTitle: Accurate Identity Operator Discretization for the Combined Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The accuracy problem of the classically Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretized magnetic field and combined field integral equations originates from the strong singularity of the identity operator. With a novel basis transformation scheme, i.e. two subsequent weak-form rotations of the RWG basis functions, the accuracy of the identity operator discretization is improved. The presented discretization scheme is immediately compatible with fast algorithms and is combined with the multilevel fast multipole algorithm. The good accuracy and the good conditioning behavior of the formulation are verified in several numerical simulations, also including electrically large problems.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing of a Conductive Polymer Cavity-Backed Metasurface Antenna for Computational Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate a new 3D printing technique, making use of a copper-polyester conductive composite filament (Electrifi) to achieve additive manufacturing of a frequency-diverse metasurface antenna. Using the 3D printed antenna, we synthesize a computational microwave camera performing 3D imaging at K-band frequencies.

articleTitle: Efficient High Power Microwave Absorber Boxes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents recent advancements in the development of efficient high-power microwave absorber boxes used during high power thermal vacuum (HPTVAC) test of spacecraft payloads. The pickup horn (PUH) and generic pick up horn (GPUH) presented earlier [1], [2], [3], were designed to absorb up to 2 kW of power from a single radiating horn. Recent development increased power absorption to 4 kW while maintaining the same or better functionalities as the earlier units. CMI successfully designed, built, and tested several Advanced Generic Pickup Horn (AGPUH) that can absorb 4kW of power. Also presented is how the AGPUH advancements have been applied to array applications.

articleTitle: High Aperture Efficiency 2D Center-fed Transmission Line-Grid Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a 2D single-point-fed transmission-line grid design that operates as a standing-wave antenna (SWA) featuring both extremely high aperture and radiation efficiencies. The generated pencil beam is directed at broadside. This broadside beam is maintained over a reasonable bandwidth and does not squint or split with frequency. The proposed structure is simply center-fed from the back using a coaxial cable where a printed λ/4-transformer matching network is also integrated.

articleTitle: Manipulating the Radiation Pattern of Patch Antennas by Exploiting Phase Singularities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In most applications the shape and the pointing direction of the antenna radiation pattern have a direct impact on the performance of the overall system. Therefore, the possibility to shape and rotate the radiation pattern of the radiating element is of interest for a multitude of different scenarios. In this contribution, we show how the radiation properties of patch antennas can be manipulated in a robust way through the phase singularities of vortex fields. In particular, we show that this can be accomplished by properly superimposing to the fundamental mode of a standard patch antenna, circularly polarized higher order modes exhibiting topological singularities.

articleTitle: General Boundary Conditions in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The most general form of linear and local boundary conditions (General Boundary Conditions, GBC) is considered in this paper. The conditions are defined in terms of four vectors tangential to the boundary surface and two scalars. The number of parameters needed to define the conditions is at most 8. Well-known examples of boundary conditions are found to emerge for various choices of the vectors and scalars. The reflection dyadic yielding the reflected wave for a given incident plane wave is found and its eigenproblem is solved with examples considered in the paper.

articleTitle: Wideband Autocorrelation Radiometer Receiver for Rapid Thickness Measurement of Dry Snowpack and Lake Icepack
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wideband autocorrelation radiometry (WiBAR) is a new technique wherein the microwave propagation time across a layered media, such as snowpack or lake icepack, can be remotely sensed. This microwave propagation time yields the vertical extent of the pack. In this paper, we developed a radiometer back-end that observes the entire spectrum of interest simultaneously, which will greatly reduce the observation time, possibly down to microseconds, which would make observations from a moving platform possible.

articleTitle: Microwave-Induced Thermoacoustic Imaging Using Compressive Sensing and a Holey Cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper explores the use of compressive sensing (CS) methods to microwave-induced thermoacoustics (TA) imaging. Moreover, it proposes the use of a holey cavity as a mechanism to enhance the reconstruction properties of the sensing matrix. The CS imaging and the holey cavity reduce the number of measurements needed to perform the imaging, thus reducing the overall complexity of the imaging system.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering from Multi-Layer Dielectric Media with 3D Random Rough Interfaces Using Translation Matrix Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Translation Matrix (T-Matrix) solution to the 3D problem of scattering of the electromagnetic waves from a dielectric layered media with random rough interfaces is presented. The solution is based on the coupled vector integral equation using the periodic Green's function. It is shown that the T-Matrix solution conserves energy, the bistatic scattering pattern has no pole singularity for the layered media waveguide mode case, and also in the small height regime will coincide with the SPM2 solution which is an analytical approach.

articleTitle: High Gain and Dual Circularly Polarized SIW Slotted Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual circularly polarized (CP) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slotted antenna is proposed. The antenna is composed of a CP SIW slotted antenna and a big reflected ground (Gnd.). The CP is realized by bending a straight SIW to a circular shape. The Gnd. is set at the bottom of the antenna with a quarter wavelength distance, which will improve the antenna gain with about 2 dB. Left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) and righthanded circular polarization (RHCP) can be achieved by feeding 2 different ports. The proposed antenna has good performance. The -10 dB impendence band is 9.6~10.5 GHz. The 3 dB axial ratio band is 9.6~10.1 GHz where the average realized gains are around 10 dB.

articleTitle: Continuous Long Term Patient Motion Monitoring Using Ultra Wide Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Use of electromagnetic modeling tools has significantly helped in analyzing human vital signs and gait. The paper will briefly discuss modeling efforts; radars used, and some recent simulated and measured results. This is a very important step in developing a practical 24/7 activity tracking system.

articleTitle: Smart Antennas Mounted on Complex Platforms by Using Phase-Shifted Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A preliminary investigation of the modal excitation purity effect on a three dimensional platform is presented. A novel Balanced Inductive Exciter (BIE)is proposed for improving the modal excitation in the considered scenario. The Modal Weighing Coefficient (MWC)and radiated power (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) have been accurately investigated in order to assess the performance of the new exciters when compared to previously adopted solutions.

articleTitle: Asterisk Metasurface at 193 THz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a simple metasurface unit-cell based on epsilon-negative and near-zero (ENNZ) metamaterial-lined apertures operating at 193 THz. The unit cell can be used as a metascreen or metafilm achieving -1 dB transmission or reflection, respectively, at resonance for a size of λ/5. The metasurface is fully scalable, shows strong field enhancement, and is polarization independent, making it ideal for many applications in sensing and imaging.

articleTitle: Target Recognition Using Sparse Representation: A Performance Comparison
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper compares two sparse representation techniques for classifying high range resolution profiles (HRRP) of four commercial aircraft models with real backscatter data as recorded in a compact range. Adverse scenarios such as azimuth ambiguity, additive noise, occlusion, extraneous scatterers, and azimuth mismatch are all considered.

articleTitle: Design of a Triple-Mode Wideband Antenna Using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The theory of characteristic modes (TCM)is utilized to design a triple-mode wideband antenna in this paper. The antenna consists of two dipole resonators and one loop resonator. First of all, a full characteristic mode analysis of the antenna structure was carried out. It was observed that the first three characteristic modes (CMs)of the antenna can be used to design a wideband antenna. Then, a proper feeding network was designed to excite those selected CMs. After optimizing the antenna's geometric parameters, a wide impedance bandwidth of 56.9% with | S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10 dB can be obtained.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Directional Channel Measurements at 67 GHz and Advanced Analysis of Interactions U sing Geometric Information
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents results from a high-resolution channel measurement campaign at 67 GHz in a street canyon in Tokyo, with focus on an extended evaluation method which incorporates map-based side information. Besides being beneficial for validating the results of the path estimation, the analysis allows the identification of main sources of interaction and the differentiation between first and higher order interactions.

articleTitle: A Design of the Parachute Conformal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Parachute conformal antenna is mainly used for temporary communication interference in the battlefield. This paper proposes a parachute conformal antenna design. When the parachute's ropes open, its structure is similar to that of a biconical antenna, so the scheme is based on the biconical antenna. Then in this paper, an antenna with a novel structure that works in the frequency range of 40 MHz to 90 MHz is designed. It has a large radiation angle and a downward radiation direction. Finally, an experimental model with feasibility is created and the standing wave ratio of the antenna is measured and analyzed. It is found that the standing wave ratio of the real object agrees well with the simulation result. And when the jammer is connected to the bottom of the parachute, the interference range is found about 1 km.

articleTitle: A K-means clustering based frequency shift correction method for OTHR
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: According to the operation mode of sky wave over-the-horizon radar(OTHR), the detection of targets is greatly affected by the ionosphere. The instability of the ionosphere causes a variety of distortions and contaminations of the echo signal. Here we propose a method based K-means Clustering to correct doppler frequency shift in the range-doppler domain. Extensive experiments using measured data show the efficiency of the proposed approach. Besides, we also compare the algorithm with other method.

articleTitle: Improving a monostatic radar system for 3D Standoff Human Body Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents an evolution of the design of an imaging system capable of generating high resolution images in real time at a standoff distance of 8 m and a field of view (Fo V)of 80 × 50 cm. The initial prototype, which has been constructed and validated, presents an important limitation that deteriorates the quality of the obtained reconstruction. The system uses a monostatic configuration that can misrepresent certain areas of the target. Depending on the deviation between the back and forth paths, the system may not be able to receive the real response produced by the Object Under Test (OUT). Due to this situation, the use of secondary transmitters that maximize the amount of information received by the system is proposed. This article presents the description of the new bistatic configuration and the results obtained through the simulation of different scenarios.

articleTitle: Mm-Wave and THz Active Electromagnetic Systems on Chip: Circuits-EM-Systems Codesign Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The ability to integrate antennas in silicon at mm-Wave and THz frequencies creates an interesting opportunity for a fundamentally new class of active and reconfigurable electromagnetic systems at these frequencies. Being able to realize radiating surfaces on-chip in close proximity with millions of active devices that can synthesize and detect signals at these frequencies with high precision allows us to move away from the classical partitioned block-by-block design approach in favor of a more holistic one. Active sub-wavelength synthesis and sensing on-chip at mm-Wave and THz frequencies can enable new forms of multi-functional electromagnetic (EM) structures for signal generation and reception for fully integrated, high-performance THz systems-on-chip. In this paper, we highlight a few examples from phased arrays on chip to imaging and source-free spectroscopes that exploit this concept of sub-wavelength synthesis and sensing to enable ultra-miniaturization and integration.

articleTitle: Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain Electric Field Integral Equation Method for Solving Non-conformal Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The discontinuous Galerkin time-domain electric field integral equation method based on marching-on-in-degree scheme (DG-TDEFIE-MOD) is proposed for simulating transient electromagnetic responses of some multiscale and non-conformal PEC structures. With the implementation of both DG method and MOD scheme, the developed algorithm is used to simulate transient scattering and radiation responses of either conformal or non-conformal meshed geometries, where late-time instability is successfully eliminated. Some numerical examples are given to validate its stability and accuracy.

Author Keywords: time-domain electric field integral equation method (TDEFIE)

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement in WiFi dual-band two PIF As for compact size antenna module applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with high isolation is proposed for WiFi dual-band antenna module applications. The antenna module with a compact size of 30 mm × 30 mm, and the no ground portion is 30 mm × 10 mm consists of two printed inverted F antenna (PIF A) elements. Based on suppressing surface wave and near-field coupling, an efficient technique of protruded spiral ground-line is introduced to increase isolation. It is found that isolation of more than 15 dB can be achieved between two polarization diversity dual-band PIF A elements. There is good agreement between simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: Discovery of Blocking Terrain in a Millimeter- Wave Network by On-the-Fly Incoherent Tomography
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Future mm-wave mobile communications networks will likely employ beamforming arrays. A principal difficulty in such networks is initiating and maintaining beam alignment. This problem is exacerbated by intermittent blockage along the line of sight (LOS), and is particularly acute in peer-to-peer links between mobiles operating among buildings and vehicles. In this paper we demonstrate a simple technique for unaided discovery of blocking objects in such networks. This technique uses histories of path loss accumulated “on the fly” between pairs of mobiles to construct a map indicating the likely locations and geometry of blocking objects. Information obtained using this technique can be used to improve beam pointing initialization and tracking, as well as to anticipate outages and proactively set up multi-hop links.

articleTitle: A Printed Wideband MIMO Antenna System for Wireless Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The proposed work reports a four element wide band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for WLAN (5.15-5.85GHz) and upper UWB (6-10GHz) application. Reduction of mutual coupling between the firmly packed wide band antennas has been possible by shorting one edge of the patch with the ground, using extended ground stub and ground slots. The desirable antenna and diversity performances are ensured in terms of reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, peak gain, efficiency, envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG).

articleTitle: Highly-Efficient Backward Scanning Leaky Wave Antenna Using Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel highly-efficient, backward-scanning leaky wave antenna (LWA) using ridge gap waveguide (RGW) is introduced. The antenna has impedance and scanning bandwidth extending from 22 GHz to 30 GHz and scanning range from -11° to + 11°. The antenna total efficiency is above 90 % over its scanning bandwidth and its average gain is 14 dBi.

articleTitle: Two Elements Self-Complementary MIMO Antennas for Wideband Mutual Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact, two elements MIMO antenna systems with a size of 57.2 × 57.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antennas have mutual coupling reduction over a wide band of 2.35 GHz to 2.65 GHz. It consists of two monopole triangle self-complementary antenna elements (TSCA). The simulation results show that the proposed MIMO antenna configuration has below enhanced mutual coupling which goes lower than -20 dB (an enhancement by more than 10 dB compared to conventional configuration). The obtained results are simulated using fullwave simulations.

articleTitle: Short Range SAR Imaging for 2D Micro-Deformation Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the development of modern remote sensing techniques, high stability and super-resolution detection abilities are required to obtain an excellent performance in micro-deformation monitoring regions, such as civil architectures monitoring, disaster alarming and environment monitoring. A portable synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system based on interference technique and phase inversing technique is proposed and utilized for 2-D micro-deformation monitoring in this paper. Experiments are constructed to verify that the system can preciously and accurately get the micro-deformation in range direction and azimuth directions.

articleTitle: Looking for the Optimal Trade-Off between Computational Costs and Reliability in Synthesizing High-Complexity Electromagnetic Systems - the Case of Satellite Communications Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of high-complexity electromagnetic (EM) systems is addressed through the System-by-Design (SbD) methodology. The proposed SbD approach relies on the integration and interconnection of suitable functional blocks for solving the design problem at hand in an effective and computationally-efficient way. Towards this end, a fast surrogate model is exploited to remarkably reduce the overall time cost of the synthesis procedure, guaranteeing an optimal trade-off between accuracy and time saving. An illustrative example is shown to assess the suitability of the SbD for the fast synthesis of a hat-fed parabolic reflector for satellite communications.

articleTitle: Accuracy Controlled $\mathcal{H}^{2_{-}}$ Matrix-Matrix Product in Linear Complexity and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Existing linear-complexity H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>- matrix- matrix product lacks an explicit accuracy control. A new linear complexity algorithm is developed in this work to compute the product of two H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> matrices with controllable accuracy. The complexity of the algorithm for variable-rank H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is also derived. Applications to both large-scale capacitance extraction and electromagnetic scattering problems involving millions of unknowns on a single core have demonstrated the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Upper Bound Study of 5G RF EMF Exposure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Power density emitted by 5G user equipment should not exceed the power density limits set by compliance guidelines. When the amplitude of each port of millimeter-wave array antennas is uniform, the power density maximization problem can be relaxed to a semi-definite program. In this paper, the effect of sampling widths is considered for the maximum power density calculation. The results show that when the sampling distance is less than a half wavelength, the sampling rate should be higher than the Nyquist rate.

articleTitle: Space Transformation for Vortex Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An all-dielectric oblate cylindrical shaped reflecting lens is proposed. The plane wave emitted from a wave port can be transformed into a vortex wave after being transmitted through the proposed lens and reflected by a planar metallic surface. The space transformation concept is applied for theoretical design of the lens, which results in a graded permittivity distribution profile. The far-field patterns are numerically simulated and reported in order to validate the proposed microwave lens over a wide frequency range spanning from 8 GHz to 12 GHz. Such an all-dielectric microwave lens can be potentially fabricated by low-cost materials through three-dimensional (3D) printing technology.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation with Triply Primed Arrays Based on Fourth-Order Statistics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A triply-primed array (TPA) is configured with three mutually primed integers, which has the degree-of-freedom on the order of their product, in the estimation of direction-of-arrivals (DOAs) of multiple quasi-stationary signals. Simulation results verify that the proposed TPA can detect more incident signals with higher accuracy than its compatible counterparts.

articleTitle: Interference in Rotating Structures and Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using the formulation of electrodynamics in rotating media, we study the effect of rotation on complex interference and diffraction patterns of metamaterials and/or periodic structures, as observed in the rotating medium's rest-frame. The interference is generated by a set of electrically small scatterers. To observe the rotation footprint, we use Green's function theory in rotating medium. Semi-analytic approximations for the rotation-induced pattern distortion are derived. The potential use of metamaterials for enhancement of rotation effects is studied and discussed.

articleTitle: Fast Design Tuning of Linear Microstrip Antenna Array Apertures By Means Of Response Features
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An approach to a rapid design closure of linear antenna array apertures at the electromagnetic (EM)-simulation level is proposed. We exploit an underlying array factor (AF) model corrected by means of characteristic points (angles and levels) of the radiation pattern of the EM model of the array aperture. The surrogate model constructed this way is iteratively updated and re-optimized within the trust-region framework. The algorithm is demonstrated using 12 and 24-element microstrip antenna arrays with the optimum designs obtained at the cost of a few EM simulations of the respective structures.

articleTitle: Numerical Dispersion and Stability of the Time Domain Propagator Numerical Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The numerical dispersion and stability conditions for the full wave time domain propagator solution of Maxwell's equations are presented. The Propagator Method is a numerical integral operator technique for moving the electromagnetic field through a numerical space at successive time increments. A derivation of the numerical dispersion relation and stability condition in 1-, 2-, and 3-dimensions is presented. It is shown that the coefficients in the numerical equations in 2- and 3-D can be found based upon a dispersion and stability condition analysis.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Wireless Power and Data Transfer Through Broadband CSCMR
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband CSCMR with pintable PCB is designed. This wireless power transfer system is able to achieve 20 MHz bandwidth at the operating frequency of 115 MHz, while maintaining around 80% power transfer efficiency. Utilizing this large bandwidth, high data rate digital communication through the same link is also achieved using backscatter modulation. The whole system is able to deliver 20% power to a 47Ω load with a 41 % power conversion efficiency rectifier, while receiving 2 Mbps data from the data input.

articleTitle: RCS at High Frequency Band using Rational Functions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Numerical calculation of RCS at high frequency is quite challenging problem. In this correspondence, we apply the Cauchy method and the TLS theory to the RCS data at low frequency band and predict the RCS data at high frequency band. Using the error between the original and the predicted data, the result is judged and the RCS data prediction using the Cauchy method is confirmed.

articleTitle: Shape Synthesis of 3-Layer Transmitarray Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synthesis of 3-layer transmitarray elements whose conducting parts are shaped to give the desired transmission properties (in contrast to conductors with a predetermined set of feature dimensions which are altered), is described and examples given.

articleTitle: Dual-port Conformal PIFA Diversity Antenna for Small Cylindrical Groundplane Mounting
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents and characterizes a dual-feed PIFA diversity antenna wrapped around a small cylindrical groundplane (ka ~ 0.8). Two rotation-spaced coax cables feed the conformal PIFA from the cylinder. The envelope correlation coefficient is less than 0.1 and the total efficiency of both ports for a copper antenna and PEC structure is ~ 80% at 2.45 GHz. This design is suitable for MIMO applications on small frames such as found on unmanned aerial vehicles, drones, bicycles, and radio masts.

articleTitle: W-band High-Performance Cavity-backed Slot Antenna Array with Inverted Microstrip Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a W-band 1×4 slot antenna array fed by the inverted microstrip gap waveguide (IMGW)with wide impedance bandwidth and high gain performance. The proposed cavity-backed slot antenna array is composed of an IMGW feeding network, radiation slots, and cavity back-shorts on the metal ground. Firstly, a novel antenna unit with wide band and good radiation pattern performance is designed. The radiation cavity is realized by moving periodic pins around the extended IMGW, and a stepped IMGW transmission line is used for the cavity excitation. Then, a 1×4 linear array is designed with a four-way IMWG feeding network to verify the performance of the antenna. The simulated results indicate that the impedance bandwidth of the proposed back-short slot antenna is 20.6% ranging from 87-107 GHz frequency range. The maximum realized gain of the antenna array is 13.1 dBi over the frequency range.

articleTitle: Bistate Frequency Selective Surface based on Microfluidic Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable frequency selective surface has been presented for bistate (transmittance/reflectance) operations. The proposed structure is designed based on microfluidic technology, where liquid metal alloy (eutectic gallium indium, EGaIn) is encased within a flexible dielectric substrate. The novelty of the design lies in its switching characteristic from dual-polarized allpass to polarization-selective bandpass/ bandstop behavior, based on whether EGaIn is injected in the microchannels. The structure, being asymmetric in nature, exhibits bandpass behavior under vertical polarization, whereas it gives rise to bandstop response during orthogonal polarization. In addition, the design performs well under various angles of incidence for both the polarizations. The performances of the proposed structure is also validated by the measured responses of the fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: Low Cross Polarization Triangle Magnetic Dipole Antenna for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we proposed new magnetic dipole antenna in the shape of a triangle at 5.8 GHz. The proposed antenna has a compact size of 0.39λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.38λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.031λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The proposed antenna has wide half-power beam width (HPBW)and low cross polarization because of magnetic current distribution. The cross polarization of the proposed antenna is about -71 dB in the E-plane and -99.6 dB in the H-plane. The HPBW of proposed antenna is about 176.7° in the E-plane and 86.8° in the H-plane.

articleTitle: Broadband Low-Profile Dipole Antenna with Parasitic Patches and Folded Strips
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a broadband low-profile dipole antenna. The antenna structure consists of a radiating dipole with folded parasitic strips above four parasitic patches on a perfect electric conductor ground plane.
