The placement of folded parasitic strips in a circle around the dipole generates extra resonance and significantly improves the antenna's impedance and gain bandwidths. The overall dimensions of the antenna are 120 mm × 120 mm × 16.3 mm (0.66λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>× 0.66λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>× 0.09λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> at 1.66 GHz), and the antenna has a| S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1.46-1.87 GHz (24.6%), a broadside gain of 8.37-8.84 dBi, and a radiation efficiency> 98%.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Wide-Band V-Band Patch Antenna on FR4 PCB
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Cost-effective and easy-to-manufacture antennas are key factors for 5G wireless high data rate links. In this context, we present a patch antenna designed on FR4-PCB for WiGig and backhaul applications, operating in the 60 GHz unlicensed spectrum. Yielding 20% measured 10 dB impedance-bandwidth and a maximum measured gain of 6 dBi, it stands out as a very competitive antenna compared to V -band FR4 PCB antennas found in literature. Furthermore, this antenna is suitable for illuminating a high gain dielectric lens for mobile backhaul.

articleTitle: Application of the Cross-Entropy Method to Electromagnetic Optimisation Problems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Many real-world electromagnetic design problems are difficult, and their optimisation requires the algorithm to manipulate diverse types of variables and multiple constraints. The cross-entropy (CE) method is a flexible and fast optimisation technique that can be used for optimisation of electromagnetic design problems with mixed variables and multiple constraints. The paper demonstrates the application of the CE method to the design of all-dielectric compact resonant cavity antennas with high gain and wide 3-dB directivity bandwidth and microstrip lowpass filters with high selectivity and wide rejection bandwidth. Both designs incorporate the requirement of fitting the allocated space. The optimised aforementioned designs show further improvement in the performance as compared to the original ones.

articleTitle: A Multibeam Parabolic Reflectarray for Onboard Tx and Rx Satellite Antennas At the Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design and performance of a multi-fed reflectarray antenna built on a parabolic surface is addressed in this communication. The proposed design can be used as onboard satellite Tx and Rx antenna in Ka-band and it is able to reduce to half the required number of antennas due to the ability of the reflectarray to produce two beams per horn by polarization discrimination. An application example providing up to 108 beams by only two antennas is described.

articleTitle: Multimode Multi-Constellation GNSS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a multimode Multi-Constellation GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) Antenna solution for automotive applications. In designing a GNSS Antenna to cover global requirements, there are requirements to be considered in order to support multiple navigation satellite constellations. In addition to GPS, the GLONASS constellation is required to support ERA-GLONASS in Russia, the Galileo constellation is required to support eCall in Europe. Also, there is the BeiDou constellation being deployed by China. Given the constellations have varying bandwidths and carrier frequencies, it is a challenge to design and integrate an antenna solution to support global coverage. In this paper, a single multimode multi-band patch antenna is designed and result shows the potential applications.

articleTitle: Transverse Permittivity Gradient (TPG) Superstrates or Lens: A Critical Perspective
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a quantitative comparison of superstrates with transverse permittivity gradient (STPG) when used in RCAs, as compared to stand-alone lens configurations. RCAs with TPG superstrates are often compared with lens antennas, considering the apparent structural similarity between the two. However, these two classes of antennas present inherent differences in terms of characteristics as well as principle of operation. Detailed comparisons are carried out using full-wave simulations. It was found that nearly 50% reduction in 3dB bandwidth was observed when a TPG superstrate was used as a lens antenna, as opposed to in an RCA.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Experimental Microwave Radar-Based Images: Evaluation Criteria
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave imaging has seen an increasing amount of clinical trials in the last two years, including ongoing and planned commercial development. The rapidly increasing number of studies with patient imaging is encouraging researchers to focus on the challenges of translating microwave imaging algorithms to clinical use. A large number of imaging algorithms have been proposed for radar-based imaging, however few detailed comparisons of these algorithms using realistic experimental or patient data have been published. This paper looks at two leading radar-based algorithms in experimental phantoms with and without tumours present. It shows that although some algorithms improve image quality when the tumour is present, the algorithms can also increase false positives in breast phantoms containing glandular structures.

articleTitle: UWB to C and WLAN Band Reconfigurable Yagi-Yuda Antena
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: UWB to C and WLAN Band Reconfigurable Yagi-Yuda Antenna is presented. Three different frequency standard bands can be obtained by controlling the states of the ideal switches. These switches are used to control the length of the resonators inserted in ground plane to achieve the reconfigu ration, maintaining unchanged the original size. Simulated results of the antenna system showed a good performance in terms of bandwidth control and gain diversity.

articleTitle: Compact Circular Polarization Antenna Based on Slot Structure for UHF RFID Handheld Reader
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact planar slot antenna with right hand circular polarization for radio frequency identification (RFID) handheld reader in the UHF band. The dimension of overall antenna is 70mm × 70mm × 9mm. Simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna has a peak gain of 4.1 dBi and an axial ratio under 2dB with in the band of 920-925 MHz. The antenna is suitable for China UHF RFID system.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Metamaterial Superstrate for Antenna Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual-band anisotropic zero-index metamaterial (ZIM)superstrate which can be used with antennas to enhance their gain in two frequency bands. The unit cell of proposed design consists of two capacitively loaded loops (CLL)which are nested to achieve dual-band operation. The extracted parameters of the resulting periodic structure show that permeability of the metamaterial is close to zero at 2.4 GHz and 3.5 GHz respectively. Used as a superstrate to a printed monopole antenna, the ZIM enhances its gain by 2.8 dB and 3.8 dB at 2.4 GHz and 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Integration of Antennas for Launching RF Signals in Metallic Tubular Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we report on finite element modeling of three types of antennas for launching the dominant waveguide mode into a cylindrical pipe. We show that a patch antenna on the inner surface located at any position can successfully launch the TE 11 mode into the pipes. The other two antenna types considered, a quarter wave probe and an inductive loop antenna, are not practical in this application.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Pin Circularly Polarized Antenna for 2.45 GHz and 5.2 GHz WiFi Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the development and characterization of a dual band antenna optimized for operation at 2.45 GHz at 5.2 GHz in Circular Polarization, hence suitable for WiFi communication in the S and C bands according to the IEEE 802.11/n protocol. The antenna is composed of two disc-based patches arranged in a concentric single-layer structure. The CP operation is enabled by the degeneration principle applied to the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode of either the internal and external disc. Each operative frequency is controlled with an independent coaxial connector, to ensure the maximum flexibility.

articleTitle: Differential Fed Bilateral Slotline Dipole on Flexible PCB for mm-Wave 5G Mobile Terminal
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a low-profile flexible antenna for mm-wave 5G mobile terminals at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna structure is fed through a differential stripline. It consists of a bilateral slotline and a bilateral dipole symmetrically arranged on the top and bottom ground planes. Since the proposed structure is flexible, it can be inserted into the package of the terminal in a curved shape. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna has good performance suitable for 5G mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Ku band Metal-Strip-Loaded Dielectric Rod Antenna with Narrowband Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metal grated pattern was implemented on a dielectric rod antenna (DRA) with rectangular cross-section to increase the antenna gain in a narrowband. The DRA is formed by a high permittivity core that is cut into shape using laser machining. The metal strip loading is added using micro-dispending of silver paste. The proposed design was characterized from 12.4 to 18 GHz, a peak gain increment of 2 dB was measured at 13 GHz and a half power beamwidth (HPBW) reduction of 12 degrees was obtained with metal strip length of 0.27 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>. An improvement that yields ~ 50% reduction in body gradient size when compared to a non-loaded antenna. Simulated data shows the inverse relationship between the end fire peak gain frequency and the strip length.

articleTitle: Structural Analysis of U-Slot Loaded Microstrip Patch using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The empirical design technique DIResF has been reported to give optimal bandwidth without probe optimization as compared to other existing design techniques (i.e. resonant frequency method (ResF) and dimensional invariance (DI)) [1]. This paper presents the comparative structural analysis of the above mentioned design techniques without feed excitation. This investigation reveals the salient feature of CMA that is uniquely helpful in antenna performance analysis namely the unique physical insight that is furnished from the radiation behavior of the currents residing on the antenna structure. The resonance frequency of modes, as well as their radiating behavior, can be determined from the information provided by the eigenvalues associated with the characteristic modes. In this paper, comparative analysis reveals the physical insight of DIResF's optimal behaviour than other two design techniques. DIResF's current modes give higher modal significance/ lower eigen value than other two design techniques which makes simultaneous excitation of participating current modes possible for wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: Complex Permittivity of Typical Construction Materials over 40–50 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Complex permittivity of construction material at millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) frequency band is a key parameter which impacts the propagation of mm-Wave greatly. Although measurements on permittivity of building materials have been performed at several specific frequencies in mm- Wave band, the wideband information over 40 GHz to 50 GHz is absent. This paper investigates the complex permittivity of four construction materials, which are granite, marble, wooden board and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) board, over 40 GHz to 50 GHz by free-space measurement. Complex permittivities are extracted from transmission coefficients and verified by reflection coefficients. The results of this work are especially useful in mm- Wave channel modeling for fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Simulation of High-Speed Graphene-Based Interconnects in Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: First-principles-based multiphysics simulation algorithms are developed to co-simulate Maxwells equations, equations characterizing graphene materials, and Boltzmann equation directly in time domain. Numerical experiments have validated the proposed multiphysics simulation of high-speed graphene-based interconnects, and demonstrated the importance of a cosimulation as compared to a decoupled analysis.

articleTitle: On the Dielectric Permittivity of 3-D Printed Biocomposite Cubes Using Two Different Coaxial Probe Measurement Methods
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The volume of electronic (e-)waste is at a new high with the ever-increasing use of traditional printed circuit boards (PCBs) worldwide. A possible solution to tackle such a challenge is to use biocomposite materials for manufacturing printed circuit boards. However, knowledge on the dielectric profile of such biocomposite materials is required for designing a radio frequency (RF) circuit. For this work, the permittivity was determined from 1 GHz to 6 GHz for three unique industrially available biocomposite materials. Specifically, two different types of industrial standard coaxial probes were used to measure the dielectric constants of three biocomposite materials, Buzzed, Entwined, and WoundUp. The measured data was presented and validated using a comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Polarization Control of a Metal-Only Transmitarray Unit-Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a metal-only transmitarray unit-cell exhibiting polarization twisting which allows reducing side lobe level of transmitarray radiation. This dominant capability is proposed and illustrated by two versions of a metal-only unit-cell consisting of four or three identical layers separated by quarter-wavelength spacers at 18.75 GHz (4 mm). The unit-cell is based on C-shaped slot, and the phase variation is achieved by varying the inner radius of the slot. The linear polarization is twisted by gradually rotating consecutively each layer with the same rotation angle.

articleTitle: CASPER West Evaporation Duct Height Inversion Using LATPROP-Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Refractive atmospheric conditions at low altitudes can have a significant impact on electromagnetic signal propagation in many maritime environments. For air-sea interaction research, it is crucial to characterize atmosphere boundary layer properties, specifically in this work, by utilizing radar clutter returns caused by electromagnetic ducting phenomena. Refractivity from clutter (RFC) is a technique that refers to the estimation of an atmospheric refractivity profile from radar clutter returns. The RFC algorithm works by obtaining the environment in which the simulated clutter pattern matches the measured radar data. The environments are simulated by a parabolic wave equation (PWE) algorithm and the data was collected using a commercial Koden MDS-63R marine radar architecture that was converted to enable increased sensitivity to radar clutter returns. The radar was deployed in Southern California at Pt. Mugu from September-October 2017 as part of the Coupled Air-Sea Processes and EM Ducting Research (CASPER) West Campaign.

articleTitle: On the Design of Wideband Monostatic STAR Systems With Spherically Stratified Lenses
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work the feasibility of a monostatic Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) system consisting of a spherical 2-layer lens fed by a quad-ridge horn is evaluated. It is seen that a lens in close proximity to the antenna aperture produces no significant degradation of an antenna-OMT system with an isolation of 30 dB between the ports. The dual-polarized system is analyzed in beamformer-based monostatic STAR configuration and is found to yield increased isolation as compared to the stand-alone circulators.

articleTitle: Phase Retrieval in Frequency-Diverse Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate a phaseless computational frequency-diverse imaging system at K-band frequencies. The integration of the phase retrieval concept with computational frequency-diverse imaging is achieved by leveraging a gradient-descent based Wirtinger Flow algorithm. Using the developed phaseless imaging system, imaging of complex-shaped targets, such as the letters of the word “DUKE”, is shown, and it is observed that the phaseless reconstructed images are on par with the complex-based reconstructions.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Unequal Filtering Power Divider Using Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband unequal power divider with filtering response is proposed based on the ring resonator. The first two resonant modes of ring are excited to form a dividing passband. After installing an open stub along the ring resonator and two coupled lines at two output ports, one additional transmission pole and three transmission zeros can be generated to improve the passband skirt and out-of-band rejection. Then, the isolation resistor is loaded to achieve the good in-band isolation. To obtain the unequal power division, the branch lines are designed to be with different characteristic impedances. Finally, a prototype with 1:2 power dividing ratio is designed and fabricated. The measured results show a 20-dB isolation and 42% fractional bandwidth, which have a good agreement with those obtained from simulation.

articleTitle: Time-varying metamaterial Doppler cloak: applications to invisibility and antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Doppler cloak is a cover to be placed in front or wrapped around a moving object to restore the source illumination frequency, as if it were not in motion, bringing the object to operate again in the standard static conditions. This feature is useful in narrowband applications, such as invisibility cloaks and highly resonant antennas, where a small detuning from the design operation frequency is sufficient for losing the invisibility effect or the communication link, respectively. Here, we show some results on the application of Doppler cloaks in these two scenarios. First, we consider the simple case of a cloaked cylindrical metallic scatterer in motion and, then, an antenna system composed of two antennas that are moving with respect to each other. Our preliminary results show that the Doppler cloak can shift the band of the propagating signal within the operative band of the cloak and of the receiving antenna, restoring the operative conditions for both cases.

articleTitle: A Multi-Band SRR and Strip Loaded Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact slot antenna suitable for penta-band applications is proposed. The different resonances are obtained by loading the slot on the top layer with an array of copper strips of equal length and with a Split Ring Resonator (SRR) at the bottom layer. The antenna prototype is fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement. The antenna is found to resonate at frequencies of 1.51 GHz, 2.35 GHz, 2.9 GHz, 3.66 GHz and 5.6 GHz. Also, a gain higher that 2.4 dBi and a bandwidth of at least 80MHz are obtained for all the bands.

articleTitle: Balanaced Loaded Transmission Lines Applied to Hybrid Couplers Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel compact hybrid coupler based on the concept of artificial transmission lines i.e. transmission lines loaded with reactive loads at both ends. A combination of longer and shorter lines are used, in order to balance the reactive loading, effectively allowing for their mutual cancellation. This mechanism is applied to the design of hybrid couplers with different aspect ratios, with respect to the classical square one.

articleTitle: Pulse Sequence Optimization for Harmonic-Diversity Exploitation of Time-Modulated Arrays in Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an unconventional time-modulated array (TMA) having its elements controlled by variable gains amplifiers (VGAs) is used as a receiver in a multi-point-to-point communications scenario. Taking advantage from its intrinsic multi-beam radiation features, the TMA is exploited to receive multiple narrowband signals through independent channels. An evolutionary algorithm is employed to define the parameters of the sum-of-weighted-cosine (SWC) pulse sequences aimed at properly shaping the multiple beams while maximizing the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at the receiver. A preliminary comparative assessment with classical TMAs using radio-frequency (RF) switches is presented in order to show the potentialities of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis for Contribution of Engine Inlet Structure to Monostatic RCS of Aircraft in the VHF Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: RCS contribution of engine inlet structure to the overall RCS of an aircraft is mainly considered. Using MOM based full-wave numerical analysis method, RCS of target aircraft model is calculated for frequency and direction(horizontal, vertical angle) in monostatic condition. Related to the frequency characteristics of the engine inlet structure, RCS enhancements in front angular region can be seen at the specific frequency region.

articleTitle: Propagation Models: Large Scale and Site-Specific
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the differences between publicly available propagation models, International Telecommunication Union (ITU)-R P.452-15 and Irregular Terrain Model, that are utilized for large scale planning against a site-specific model, the Aerospace Radio Frequency Propagation Tool (ARPT). ARPT was developed under the Air Force Spectrum Transition Plan. The advantages and disadvantages of each propagation model and its methodology are discussed in greater detail.

articleTitle: A Magneto-Electric Dipole High-Efficiency 60GHz Ridge Gap Waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an 8⨯8 magneto-electric (ME)dipole high-efficiency waveguide slot array antenna based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW)feed network operating in V -band. The proposed 8⨯8 array antenna has three layers: ME dipole layer, backed cavity layer, and feed distribution network layer. A transition from standard V-band waveguide port to RGW transmission line is designed. Final dimensions including ME dipole patch, radiating slot, backed cavity layer, RGW feed network are designed and optimized in simulation software. Simulations of the whole 8⨯8 array antenna demonstrate that the reflection coefficient bandwidth (∣S11∣<-10dB)is 15% from 56.5GHz to 65.5GHz, meanwhile, antenna efficiency is above 90% in the whole frequency band with maximum gain 27dB.

articleTitle: Design of Thin Multilayer Magnetic Radar Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a practical method to design an optimized multilayer absorber by using a database of magnetic materials defined by the user. The methodology handles both the normal as well as oblique incidence cases, and incorporates the effects of resistive Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) for performance enhancement of the absorber.

articleTitle: Power Transfer by Electric Coupling between Rotating Bodies with Axis-symmetrical Long Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a slip ring without mechanical brushes, which utilizes electric coupling. The coupling capacitors are compensated with inserted inductances. In the application to a solar power satellite, the power transfer of 1 GW is shown to be feasible.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-layer Linearly Polarized Wideband Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel three-layer wideband linearly polarized transmitarray antenna working in 7~16 GHz is proposed in this paper. The array element, which consists of a split circular ring connected by a narrow strip and two orthogonal metallic polarizers, is capable of an independent control of the phase and amplitude of the electromagnetic (EM) waves scattered into the cross-polarization. Moreover, in the whole working band, the proposed element features a low-loss transmission and approximately linear phase curves. A 25×25-element transmitarray excited by a pyramid horn is designed. The simulated results show that a 41 % bandwidth for 0.5-dB gain drop and a 40.7% peak aperture efficiency are achieved, which confirm the feasibility of designing wideband transmitarrays.

articleTitle: Multiple Beam Forming using Spherical Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Spherical metasurfaces are particularly suited for the beam forming as they intrinsically cover the entire radiation space. We introduce here the possibility to realize multiple simultaneous and independent beam forming operations with a metasurface synthesized by Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs) combined with bianisotropic surface susceptibility tensors. Specifically, we demonstrate a spherical metasurface tilting upwards and downwards the radiation patterns of an electric dipole and a magnetic dipole, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband and Sparse Finite-Element Formulation Free of Low-Frequency Breakdown
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new full-wave finite-element (FE) formulation is developed, which is not only sparse, well conditioned, but also free of low-frequency breakdown by construction. We first analytically identify the nullspace of the stiffness matrix, denoted by Co, and its complementary space C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> in an arbitrary mesh. Both of Co and C h are found to be sparse. For problems involving loss, we further decompose Co into two subspaces, each of which is also analytically identified. One subspace is the nullspace of the transformed submatrix characterizing the loss, and the other is its complementary space. The FE system matrix transformed onto the new space is free of low-frequency breakdown for both lossless and general lossy problems, where dielectrics and conductors can be lossy and arbitrarily inhomogeneous. Furthermore, the new FE system of equations is sparse, and well-conditioned, thus facilitating efficient computation. Numerical results have validated the proposed formulation.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Dual-Band Subarray for 20/30 GHz Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-layer dual-band array antenna for K/Ka-band is proposed in the context of the so-called Gap Waveguide Technology. The challenge faced in this array is to host radiators of two quite separated bands in the same aperture. Half of the radiators work at 20 GHz and the other half at 30 GHz. The interesting features of the proposed antenna are that it is fully metallic, the radiators are fed corporately, and both radiators and network are hosted in just a single layer. Radiators are quite unconventional since they are based on slots backed by a particular realization of coaxial cavities, whose vertical size controls the working frequency, providing good compactness to the whole structure. Preliminary results are presented to demonstrate the viability of the idea.

articleTitle: Mechanical Tension Effects on Cylindrical Probe-Fed Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The experimental characterization of the mechanical tension effects on a 2. 2 GHz probe fed circularly polarized rectangular microstrip antenna conformed on a cylindrical surface is presented in this work. Two prototypes were designed and built for a metallic cylinder with a radius of 25 centimeters and height of 1. 5 meters. The first antenna was used to characterize the effects of mechanical tension, also considering permittivity uncertainty and the manufacture after etch stress relief effect. A comparison between numerical and experimental results from the first prototype showed that the conformed patch is elongated along the curvature of the metallic cylinder approximately by 0.15 millimeters. The patch elongation was compensated on the second prototype. Experimental measurements showed that the elongation was predicted accurately.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Cyclic Enhancement Mechanisms in a Discrete Random Halfspace
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wave-theoretic predictions can exhibit discrepancies from radiative transfer theory in random media where stable interference patterns arise from multiple-scatter effects. In unbounded media, these discrepancies are attributed to so-called cyclic scatter mechanisms where the correlation of forward and reversed multiple scatter sequences causes an enhancement in the backscattered intensity. In bounded media, similar pseudo-cyclic mechanisms involving boundary interactions give rise to backscatter and specular enhancements. Here, the lowest-order enhancement mechanisms for scalar waves in a discrete random halfspace are described in closed-form using the distorted Born approximation.

articleTitle: A Nested-Spring Metamaterial Unit Cell for Broadband Mechanically-Tunable Effective ∊
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel nested-spring metamaterial unit cell that achieves broadband mechanically-tunable effective permittivity using compression and expansion of the spring-based unit cell structures. These structures are shown in simulation to be capable of producing relative effective permittivities ranging from 1.06 to 7.04 at the low end of the frequency range, with variation less than 10% from 2 MHz to 106 MHz. At the upper end of this frequency range, the electrical size of the unit cells is λ/57.

articleTitle: Wideband Equivalent Circuit Model for Smartphone Antennas Based on Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an approach to model the impedance characteristic of a generic smartphone antenna with lumped circuit elements based on characteristic modes is shown. In contrast to a pure fit of simple RLC resonator circuits, a model based on characteristic modes can deliver an enhanced insight into the real physical behavior of the modeled antenna. To obtain such a model, each dominant mode is modeled with a separate circuit. The superposition of all these circuits yields the whole model. To obtain the circuit models, we use an approach based on high pass circuits of even order, which is extended so that it is valid for inductive modes, too.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of Vertically Oriented Metamaterials for Wideband Omnidirectional Perfect Absorption
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterials provide a means to tailor the spectral response of a surface. Given the periodic nature of the metamaterial, proper design of the unit cell requires intimate knowledge of the parameter space for each design variable. We present a detailed study of the parameter space surrounding vertical split-ring resonators and planar split-ring resonators, and demonstrate widening of the perfect absorption bandwidth based on the understanding of its parameter space.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Loaded with Frequency Selective Surface and Artificial Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A pattern reconfigurable antenna loaded with frequency selective surface (FSS)and artificial dielectric medium operating at 5.2 GHz is presented. In this design, a monopole is used as a radiating source and surrounded by four columns of FSS screens and artificial dielectric medium. The FSS unit cell comprises two metallic crosses connected by a pin diode, the transmission characteristics of which are investigated with different states of pin diode. By changing the states of the pin diodes in the FSS screens, beam switching can be achieved in azimuth plane at 5.2 GHz. The loaded artificial dielectric medium provides a higher refractive-index to tilt the beam in elevation plane. Moreover, a maximum gain enhancement of 3.7 dB is achieved when artificial dielectric medium is loaded.

articleTitle: High Gain Off-Body linear to circular polarization based on dielectric meander-line for Underground Mining Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A High Gain Off-Body wearable antenna with a linear to circular polarization converter is designed for underground mining communications. The structure is made of 4 layers, an AMC substrate, a planar monopole and a meander-line polarizer converter with a FSS superstrate. At 5.8 GHz, the design achieves a bandwidth of 1.93 GHz, a realized gain of 10.21 dBi over the entire ISM band and 0.74 dB purity polarization at the resonance frequency. These results are shown to be suitable for underground mining communications.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of One-Sided Directional Slot Antenna for 1 THz Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A highly one-sided directional slot antenna for waves of 1-THz frequency range has been designed and fabricated. The antenna is composed of a floating metal and coplanar-waveguide feed line. The antenna was fabricated on a quartz substrate by using the planar process technology. The antenna size was 290 J.1m × 200 J.1m. The measured peak gain was 5.57 dBi at 0.93 THz, which well agrees with the simulated peak gain of 5.96 dBi at 1 THz.

articleTitle: Using electrically-small HPEM antenna array elements to divide power and shape aperture fields
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate the development of feeding networks for use with arrays of electrically small EZ antennas for HPEM applications. We present a detailed examination of the antenna probe design for coaxial waveguide feed system, and we show how the parameters of the feeding structure can be used to tailor the coupling between the feed network and the radiating elements though numerical modeling, simple circuit analysis, and experimental verification.

articleTitle: Improving Reliability in Hybrid Mesh Networks with Tripolar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The work herein demonstrates how hybrid mesh network reliability can be improved by leveraging the channel diversity enabled by a compact, tripolar antenna. Specifically, through simulation, we show that a tripolar antenna can reduce packet drops to a third of that of when a single element antenna is used. These results were achieved assuming a slowly-varying, but highly-multipath, propagation environment such as those that may he exnected in industrial IoT settings.

articleTitle: Supercomputing for Full-Wave Tomographic Image Reconstruction in Near-Real Time
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates large full-wave inverse-scattering solutions on the Blue Waters supercomputing facility. The high computational complexity of the distorted-Born iterative method (DBIM) is reduced with the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). A hierarchical parallelization of DBIM and MLFMA provides scaling to thousands of computing nodes of the supercomputer. Furthermore, we obtain considerable speedup with modern CPU+GPU architectures over conventional CPU+CPU ones. Results obtained on 4,096 GPU nodes demonstrate a near-real-time tomographic reconstruction, which is crucial for real-life imaging applications.

articleTitle: K-Band Cross-Aperture Coupled Circularly Polarized Dual Frequency Microstrip Patch Antenna with Single Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents the design, modeling, simulation, and characterization of a K-band cross-aperture coupled CP microstrip patch antenna element with a single feed for dual frequency operation. The patch element can be used as a building block for a larger planar array for SATCOM.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Square-Aperture Horn Antenna with a Linear Spline Profile
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The geometrical efficiency within an array cell of a square-aperture horn is supposed to be higher compared to a circular horn resulting in its suitability for array applications. In this article, the electromagnetic characterization of an HFSS-simulated horn antenna design is presented. The present work demonstrates a square-aperture horn antenna incorporated inside a rectangular parallelepiped metallic structure. The proposed horn consists of a rectangular waveguide segment, a linearly spline-profiled section, and a square aperture-with a loaded polyethylene dielectric lens-directed to free space. At 10 GHz, aperture efficiency is improved to 95.4 % and the design produces nearly equal 3 dB and 10 dB beamwidth patterns in both H- and E-planes. The generation of higher order mode coefficients was analyzed while VSWR and radiation pattern were also simulated across the X-band.

articleTitle: New AMC Ground Plane for 28 GHz Broadband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC)ground plane is proposed to operate at 28 GHz. The hybrid structure of the proposed antenna has 3 layers composed of AMC, Patch antenna with FSS reflector substrate to improve the gain and directivity on millimeter (mm)wavebands. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has good performance especially in terms of a wide bandwidth of about 5.4 GHz with good matching, an overall realized gain improvement of about 25 dB and a directivity of 28.4°. This broadband antenna is suitable for underground wireless communication system.

articleTitle: A Wide Bandwidth Low-Profile Top-Loaded Pyramidal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile wideband antenna is presented that uses a square pyramidal monopole radiator top-loaded with an etched copper-cladded dielectric. The proposed top-loading configuration along with a pair of shorting strips enables input impedance matching at reduced frequencies while maintaining a very low-profile (0.063 λ at the lowest operational frequency of 900 MHz). The measured impedance bandwidth is 900 MHz to 13.6 GHz for a 3:1 VSWR, and monopole-like radiation patterns are obtained from 900 MHz to 11 GHz. The proposed design is relatively easy to fabricate, is low-cost, and has a very wide bandwidth for its size.

articleTitle: Linear to Circular FSS Transformer for Dual-Polarized Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) placed in front of an array of circular apertures. The FSS is aimed at reducing the grating lobes of the apertures' radiation pattern, and transforming the linearly-polarized pattern of the apertures into a circularly-polarized pattern. To do so, the FSS incorporates 45° stubs capable of exciting two orthogonal modes with a 90° phase shift. Results show an axial ratio below 1 dB at the central frequency, and a reduction of 16.46 dB in the grating lobes level. The symmetric configuration of the FSS allows a dual-polarized (LHCP/RHCP) operation in a single structure by just feeding the aperture with an appropriate linear mode (V/H).

articleTitle: Methodology for Quantifying Metamaterial Stored Energy Using Theory of Characteristic Mode
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterials are artificial materials tailored to mold the flow of waves. Selecting a metamaterial for practical application is dependent on its effective parameter which classifies it as being electric or magnetic. This paper presents a theory of characteristic modes based quantitative approach for classifying metamaterial unit cell by means of stored energy. The presented results are promising for systematic design approaches for association of metamaterial unit cell to antennas such as in the design of metamaterial-inspired antennas.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Wideband Antenna Useful in MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband multi-beam antenna for MIMO applications at 5.8 GHz is presented. The main goal is to obtain a cheap multi beam antenna without using a beamforming network. Four compact antennas with unidirectional radiation pattern are connected with each order to form the side walls of a metallic cube. Each individual compact antenna is analyzed and optimized using the Theory of Characteristics Modes. Simulated results show that the four-port antenna provides four independent beams at 5.8 GHz. The available impedance bandwidth for the multi-beam antenna is 30% and the isolation between ports is below -15dB.

articleTitle: Extreme Aperture Antennas: Radiating and Electrical Performance Enhanced by Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we present the design of metamaterials-based flat lens and metamaterial-inspired particles, which have been successfully used to enhance the performance or to add new functionalities to aperture horn antennas. The metamaterial-based flat lens is designed to restore the gain performance of shortened optimum horn antennas. The lens consists of a proper combination of conventional epsilon-positive and epsilon-near-zero materials, in order to achieve the optimum field distribution on the aperture for maximizing the gain over a broad frequency range. The metamaterial-inspired particles are designed for integration directly inside horn antennas in order to provide additional functionalities or simple signal conditioning ability to the radiating element. Among them, filtering operations with a pass-band or a notched-band behavior, combination and splitting capabilities of signals with different carrier or polarization states, polarization conversion properties, and magnet-less non-reciprocity by exploiting spatiotemporal modulation of the particle have been verified both numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: RF-based Breast Surface Estimation - Registration with Reference Imaging Modality
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, two estimation problems are tackled. Firstly, the robust estimation of the external contour of the breast, using data from a Radio-Frequency (RF) Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) scan. Secondly, the registration between the RF breast scan and the breast scan using a 3D stereographic infrared camera. The bi-modality data registration is meant for controlled patient positioning and breast deformation during the RF breast examination.

articleTitle: Total Attenuation of Satellite Signal on Earth-Space Link in West Africa
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study examines the consequence of total attenuation impairments on fixed satellite communication link on earth-space path in West Africa for 0.01 % unavailability of an average year. The International Telecommunication Union Radio Propagation Recommendation (ITU-RP 618, 2012) procedure and study group 3 data bank base was used for the computation of total attenuation for seventeen (17) West Africa countries for both uplink and downlink frequencies. The results reveal lowest value at C-band which gradually increases at Ku and Ka bands while the highest values of total attenuation are experienced at v- band for all the locations. Both uplink and downlink results at v-bands show constantly that total attenuation is more severe (more than 100 dB) in countries like Togo (139.64 dB), Liberia (138.55 dB), Ghana (138.20 dB), Benin (134.19 dB), Ivory Coast (132.75 dB), and Nigeria (122.42 dB). It should be noted that all stations are in the tropical region of West Africa where rainfall is very high and therefore will experience more signal loss due to the presence of rain, cloud, oxygen, and water vapor even in clear-sky or none rainy conditions. The overall results will be helpful for system planning and better performance of satellite communication link in West Africa region.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Dielectric Rod Antenna Advancements Through Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Modern sensors require an increasingly small package which presents unique design challenges for antennas and arrays. One option is to install apertures conformally. This, however, limits aperture performance, especially for forward looking antennas with horizontal polarization. An ultrawideband antenna is proposed for embedded installations, permitting a polarization and frequency independent forward field of regard. A scaled version of the design is designed, fabricated, and measured.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhanced Low-VHF Communications with a Miniature Non-Foster Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate low-frequency communications with a highly miniature bandwidth-enhanced antenna. To achieve improved bandwidth while maintaining a small form factor, a non-Foster matching technique is applied to a λ/50 low-VHF antenna. The practical use of existing non-Foster matched antennas has been hindered due to their sensitivity to small system induced variations as well as nearby scatterers. We carry out software defined radio based wireless data transmission experiments with varying data rates to investigate the performance of our proposed antenna for practical applications in indoor environments. Experimental results show the non-Foster matched antenna enables transmitting data with rates three times higher than the same antenna matched with passive elements. We present communication quality measures by transmitting several packets and computing the signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR), the symbol error rate, and cross-correlation between transmitted and received pulses.

articleTitle: Chassis Diversity Antenna Comparison
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Chassis models comprising a conducting plate on a PCB are often used for cellphone-type terminals, and the diversity elements are usually inverted-F antennas (IFAs). This paper investigates different chassis-mounted IFA configurations for diversity performance. The IFAs are normally mounted in the corners of a rectangular chassis, but here we include a pair of colinear IFAs on the long edge to clarify the impact of pure spacing (no element rotation). The various configurations have different matching levels and we compare the diversity performance in terms of their isolation rather than their matching. It is shown how rotating the elements (including angular spacing, or polarization diversity, to the linear spacing) gives better overall diversity performance without any introducing extra techniques (cutting slots on the groundplane, de-coupling networks, etc). The use of the electromagnetic isolation reveals the effect of structural isolation on the performance because it effectively eliminates the mismatch factor and the antennas can remain unmatched for a diversity performance comparison.

articleTitle: Achieving Range Resolution in Holographic Imaging Using Single Frequency Microwave Data
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In direct microwave holographic imaging, conventionally, wideband data is required to obtain range resolution. However, acquisition of wideband data requires large antennas and complex electronic circuitry. Besides, in wideband imaging, the results are prone to errors due to the dispersive properties of the media. In this paper, we demonstrate the possibility of using single frequency microwave data and an array of receivers to achieve range resolution. This paves the way towards developing 3D holographic microwave or millimeter wave imaging systems using single frequency data.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of a Bent Umbrella-Shaped Transmission Line Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A bent umbrella-shaped transmission line antenna (BUMTA) is analyzed using the method of moments (MoM). Investigations are directed to omnidirectional beam formation in the azimuth plane. The effects on the directivity of the distance between the bottom end of the BUMTA bent arm section and the ground plane are investigated.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Simulation of General Composite Material Bodies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Modal analysis of general material bodies is very useful for designing novel material antennas, such as dielectric resonator antennas. Theory of characteristic modes (TCM) can be used to carry out mode analysis of material bodies with clear physical meaning. This paper focuses on how to apply two proposed finite element-boundary integral (FE-BI) formulations to determine the characteristic modes of general composite material bodies. Two FE-BI based generalized Hermitian eigenvalue (GHE) equations are examined through the simulation of the characteristic modes of material bodies. Numerical results show that the FE-BI based GHE equations are accurate for the solution of characteristic modes for general composite material bodies and the results obtained can be adopted as benchmark for the development of other modal analysis methods.

articleTitle: Ray Model Analysis with antenna for Predicting Indoor Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Understanding radio channel path characteristics such as path loss and delay spread is crucial for determining the coverage and for planning interference reduction strategies in indoor wireless communication systems. Ray tracing with uniform theory of diffraction is widely applied to a site-specified radio propagation estimation for wireless applications. It is therefore useful to evaluate the channel propagation properties of millimeter wave within an indoor environment. This paper studies the effects for both line of sight and non line of sight conditions with the influence of the antenna on indoor signal propagation at 28 GHz. The effects of different antenna type and beam pointing has the most significant effect on the received electric field strength and will provide insight in wireless radio system design.

articleTitle: RCS Investigation of Tetrahedral Aligned Sphere Targets for Radar Positioning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This contribution presents the investigation of tetrahedral aligned sphere targets and their effect on radar measurements via sinograms. Here, the radar cross section (RCS) is evaluated in order to determine the distance and angle between radar and target for precise 3D industrial robot positioning. Therefore, the sinograms are simulated by a shooting and bouncing ray approach with CST Microwave Studio. Two different targets are investigated: One with equally sized and and one with differently sized spheres. While the former has ambiguities, which only allow an angle estimation within a certain range, the latter reduces these ambiguousness towards zero.

articleTitle: Design of Flat Dielectric Reflectarrays Using State-of-the-Art Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dielectric reflectarray antennas consisting of a solid and flat ceramic with spatial variation of dielectric constant are proposed for mm-wave applications. Additive manufacturing is used to tailor the dielectric constant to achieve the desirable reflection phase on the reflectarray aperture. The complete design process is outlined, and a Ka-band dielectric reflectarray with a gain of 33.1 dB and desirable radiation characteristics is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Innovative CTS antenna architecture for beam reconfiguration in E-plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a high gain, low profile and reconfigurable Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS)antenna fed by two pillbox systems and a 3dB 180° coupler. The antenna system contains 16 radiating slots divided into two 8-slot sub-arrays. Such an architecture provides for the first time beam reconfiguration in E-plane. These concepts are validated experimentally in E-band (71-86GHz). The antenna module has been fabricated in Printed Circuit Board (PCB)technology; it is very compact and exhibits very good performance over the whole bandwidth with a maximum gain of 21.8dBi, a gain variation lower than 1.5dB, and an input matching level better than -18dB.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Selective Paper for Crack Detection of Concrete Building Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a frequency selective paper with X-band reflection characteristics is designed for the crack detection of concrete building structures and the change of resonant frequency characteristics according to cracks are investigated. Based on the crossed dipole unit cell known to have narrow-band reflection characteristics, a frequency selective paper operating in the X-band was designed and the frequency characteristics of the frequency selective paper unit structure including cracks were observed. As the crack width increased by 0.2mm, the resonance frequency tended to move to the higher band by about 90MHz. It was confirmed through simulation that the existence and the width of the crack can be predicted. Designed frequency selective paper was fabricated and frequency reflection characteristics were measured for six types of cracks. From the measurement result, the existence of cracks and the shape of cracks can be predicted according to the polarization of the incident angle.

articleTitle: A Beam-Scanning Array Antenna for LPWAN Base Station
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a beam-scanning array antenna for LPWAN base station. The two-element array of the pattern reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antennas is designed at the 2.4 GHz ISM band to provide 360° beam-scanning. The characteristics of the array are simulated using the 4NEC2 simulator. By using the pattern reconfigurable elements and with non-uniform amplitude excitation, the simulated results show that the array provides 16 beams covering 360° with 7 dBi gain. Also, the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> bandwidth of the array is satisfied to the desired operating frequency.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Reduction of a Narrow Wall Slotted Waveguide Array for Ku-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method to reduce cross-polarization (X-pol) of narrow wall slotted waveguide is presented. A 10 inclined slot array cut in the narrow wall of a rectangular waveguide with the element spacing of d = 0.64Aμ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>operating in Ku-band is employed. The proposed slotted waveguide antenna consists of a perforated-metallic plate which acts as a polarization filter. The polarization filter reduces the maximum cross-polarization level by 10 dB at the design frequency of 14 GHz and 5 dB over the frequency band 12 GHz to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Inductive and Resonant Transmitter for Dual-mode Wireless Charging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As wireless charging becomes popular, a transmitter that can support multi-mode operation seems to be essential for broad and rapid deployment. In this paper, a dual-mode transmitter is proposed to accommodate the tightly inductive coupled and loosely magnetic resonant coupled charging technologies. The challenge is to meet charging distance requirements, as they have opposite characteristic with respect to coupling coefficients. When two different coils are stacked on top of each other, proximity effect due to the nearby two sets of coils should also be mitigated. The coexistence issue is resolved by stacking and separating the different types of coils on top of each other and by making use of the tightly inductive charging coils to extend the charging distance of the magnetic resonant charging, allowing a further physical separation between the two sets of coils. The details of design stackup, prototype, and measurement result are presented.

articleTitle: A Broadband SIW Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel broadband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna is designed at V-band (60 GHz) for high gain 5G applications. The antenna consists of a truncated square patch having tiny square slots along upper and lower edge of the patch. The antenna size is 5.2×5.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. By putting via-through-holes along the four sides of the truncated patch, an SIW cavity is achieved. This cavity helps to obtain a wide impedance bandwidth and high gain by suppressing the surface waves. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 15% (56.2-65.2 GHz) and simulated peak gain of 7.76 dBi is achieved.

articleTitle: A Wideband Antenna for Buried RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a wide-band bow-tie antenna for underground buried RFID application. A narrowband antenna is not suitable for proper functioning of buried RFID tag as the soil can alter the resonance frequency under typical conditions. The bow-tie antenna was designed to be compatible with the commercial RFID IC Alien H-3. Design and simulation results are presented for the development of the tag.

articleTitle: Flexible Reconfigurable I-shaped Folded Slot Antenna for Wireless Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel I-shaped folded slot antenna that miniaturizes the overall size (40% reduction) of a conventional folded slot antenna designed at 1.4 GHz. The antenna is designed and simulated using HFSS on a flexible thin substrate so it can be used for conformal applications. It is also reconfigurable and two p-i-n diodes are used to redirect and redistribute the current resulting in a frequency reconfigurable antenna. When the diodes are ON, the I -shaped folded slot antenna behaves as conventional folded slot antenna at 3 GHz. However, when the diodes are OFF, the current is redirected on the entire I -shaped slot and it is resonating at a lower frequency 1.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Performance Characterization of Monolithically Integrated mmW Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present initial characterization of a novel, mono-lithically integrated multilayer mmW phased array architecture that can be seamlessly incorporated with large-scale fabrication of transceiver chipsets. Exhibiting an estimated radiation efficiency over 60% for the impedance bandwidth covering 35-75 GHz band, the ultra-wideband array topology offers a cost-effective realization with much improved on-chip performance. Moreover, the proposed array is an ideal candidate for conformal and mobile applications thanks to its low profile with the overall height of 500 μm and on-chip footprint of 7mm×3mm, exhibiting 5 dB realized gain.

articleTitle: Earth-Space Path Cloud Attenuation Distribution Study
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study investigates the impact of cloud attenuation at C, Ku, Ka, and V- bands in West Africa. Cloud attenuation statistics deducted from extracted data obtained from ITU-R study group data bank for the seventeen countries in the region, were used to determine the average satellite link margin for the region. Analysis of their cloud attenuation contour maps shows the average cloud attenuation for uplink and downlink: at the c-band are 0.17 dB and 0.095 dB; at Ku-band are 0.875 dB and 0.665 dB; at Ka-band 3.75 dB and 1.775 dB; and at V-band are 9.25 dB and 6.6 dB respectively in the tropical wet/dry climatic part of the region, while those for the tropical wet and tropical semi-arid climatic parts of the region are relatively higher and substantially lower respectively. Hence a margin of 1.8 dB and 3.8 dB; 6.3 dB and 9 dB for cloud attenuation in the uplink and downlink at Ka and V-band respectively are recommended.

articleTitle: Human Body Shadowing at 26.4 and 66.5 GHz in an Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We measured the fluctuation of propagation loss at 26.4 and 66.5 GHz when indoors in cases of 2 and of 5 people moving randomly. The 1% and 10% values of the cumulative distribution function (CDF) increase as the frequency increases. The probability (Ph) of propagation loss variation occurring due to human body shadowing increases as the transmitting (Tx) antenna height decreases. As the number of human bodies present decreases, Ph also decreases. We also found that Ph of 26.4 GHz is higher than that of 66.5 GHz. This is because the Fresnel radius of 26.4 GHz is larger than that of 66.5 GHz; this difference in probability seems to be because the frequency is easily affected by the human body.

articleTitle: Impact of Rain on Earth-Space Communication Link in West-Africa
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The impairment of radio signal at Ku band and above by rain is a key factor in satellite communication and radar remote sensing modelling. The major effect of rain on electromagnetic signals is by absorption and scattering. This effect is noticed both on the uplink and downlink at 0.01 % unavailability in an average year. The data bank used for the computation of the rain attenuation for a link to Nigeria Communication satellite (NigComsat II) for selected locations in West Africa was obtained from the International Telecommunication Union Radio Propagation Recommendation [10]. The input parameters obtained from ITU-R study group 3 data base were used in this study. The various results of the rain attenuation values at C, Ku, Ka, and V bands were presented on contour map. The results reveal lowest value is at C-band which gradually increases at Ku and Ka bands while the highest values of total attenuation are experienced at V-band for all the locations. Both uplink and downlink results at V-bands show constantly that total attenuation is more severe in countries like Togo, Liberia, Ghana, Benin, Ivory Coast, and Nigeria. It should be noted that all these countries are in the tropical region of West Africa where rain accumulation and rain rate is very high.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Antenna with High Gain and Low Side-Lobe for Automotive Anti-Collision Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized 4 ⨯ 8 microstrip antenna array with high gain, low side-lobe is proposed in this paper. The S-shaped delay line is applied in the feed network to achieve the miniaturization of antenna array. Furthermore, to acquire the low side-lobe, Taylor series amplitude weighting is used in the current amplitude distributions of feed network. The results of simulation show that the antenna array has a gain of 18.24 dBi, the bandwidth is from 23.65 GHz to 24.34 GHz while VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio)is less than 1.5, the side-lobe level in E plane (yoz)and H plane (xoz)are 25.61 dB and 33.12 dB respectively.

articleTitle: An Ultra-thin Dual-Band Smart-watch Antenna Compatible with Several Wireless Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a small ultra-thin multiband antenna for wireless handsets is introduced. The suggested antenna with two widebands is able to cover the Galileo/GPS/Glonass/DCSIPCS/UMTS/LTE2400/LTE2500/WLAN (2.4-5.2-5.8 GHz) and WiMAX(2.5-5.5 GHz) bands. Consisting of a driving element on top of the substrate, and a parasitic ground at bottom of the substrate, the proposed antenna has a simple configuration. The wide dual-band operation of the antenna is achieved by coupling between the driven element and parasitic ground. By inserting a strip on the driven element and cutting some slots at the parasitic ground, the operating bands of the antenna have been optimized and widened. Considering the fact that the antenna has a planar and simple configuration, the fabrication of antenna in mass production would be cost effective. The proposed antenna with the small active element size of 9.5 mm × 16.5 mm, and the total size of 30 mm × 30 mm × 0.5 mm, can be a good choice for portable devices, such as smart-watches.

articleTitle: RIME-Dipole Accommodation aboard JUICE
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The goal of the mission JUICE (JUpiter ICy moon Explorer) is the exploration of Jupiter and three of its moons. In the year 2030 the spacecraft (S/C) will arrive in the Jovian system and investigate the celestial bodies by RIME (Radar for Icy Moons Exploration) and other instruments aboard JUICE. The paper investigates the impact of mutual coupling between antenna and solar panels as well as the effect of an incorrect deployment of the antenna on the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Multi-beam Radiations from Phased Array of Antennas Excited by Modified Near-Field Focus Rotman Lens Beamformer for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of multi-beam phased array of antennas for near-field focus (NFF) RFID applications. The beamformer is designed by modifying Rotman lens architecture. Thus the trifocal points can create three phase sets to excite an antenna array to radiate electromagnetic fields focused at three designated points, respectively. Theoretic concept of the new NFF Rotman lens design will be first discussed. The multi-beam radiations at 2.4GHz band will be afterward shown to demonstrate the feasibility.

articleTitle: A Functional Understanding of the ROTAC Using the Cavity Green's Function
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The cavity Green's function expressed using the Ewald summation is used to explain the perturbations of analytic cavity modes when many antennas are placed within an over-moded resonant cavity. Simulation results demonstrate that away from the antennas, the fields can be expressed in terms of the analytical modes, which has implications for efficiently characterizing the fields in reconfigurable over-the-air chambers used for wireless device performance testing.

articleTitle: Phase Discretization Influence on the Performance of Focusing Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the effect of phase discretization on the electromagnetic performance of a planar focusing metasurface. Under the same focusing parameter settings, metasurfaces with different phase discrete levels approximating the ideally constant phase profile to be compensated by the metasurface are constructed. Their beam qualities, such as individual beam shape and focusing efficiency, are comparatively analyzed. It is demonstrated that the metasurface with the limit fine phase map can obtain higher focusing efficiency, more compact and symmetric focal spot shape, and smaller side lobe level.

articleTitle: Direct Methods for Unsymmetric Blockwise Sparse Matrices: Application to Domain Decomposition Global Preconditioning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A memory and time efficient block-wise sparse LU factorization and forward/backward(F/B) substitution for the application of the W-FETI (Woodbury-FETI) global algebraic Domain Decomposition preconditioner is presented. The proposed direct solver exploits inherited block-wise sparsity (sparse collection of dense block submatrices) of the unsymmetric W-FETI matrix, reducing memory and attaining high degree of cache coherency and maximal BLAS Level 3 performance. Comparisons with state-of-the-art sparse direct solvers on various electrically large problems suggest up to 3 times less memory and run-time complexity for the factorization and for the multiple rhs F/B substitution part, while maintaining the same accuracy.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Based on a Microstrip Magnetic Dipole for K Band Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wide-angle scanning phased array based on a novel microstrip magnetic dipole is proposed. The proposed antenna has a low profile of 0.04λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> denotes the wavelength in free space corresponding to the center operating frequency). The reflection coefficient is lower than -10 dB within the frequency range from 23.8 to 24.3 GHz, which covers the 24.05-24.25 GHz ISM band. The half-power beamwidth of the single element is about 150° in the E-plane and 50° in the H-plane, which has a good potential for wide angle scanning phased array. The simulated results show that the main beam can scan from -60° to 60° with 3 dB gain fluctuation in the E-plane. The proposed array can be used to improve the detection performance of K band radar systems.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Supression in Modulated Surface Reactance Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a method for suppressing the sidelobe of a modulated surface antenna in a given direction. It is based on synthesizing two beams, one pointing at the desired direction, and the other at the interfering direction, so that this second has the same amplitude as the sidelobe that must be suppressed and it presents a 180° phase shift. A one-dimension modulated surface reactance antenna is designed and sidelobe reductions of 14.5 dB and above 8 dB are shown in simulations and measurements, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Fixed Physical Length Planar Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton-mode Delay Lines for a 3-bit 360° Phase Shifter for Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present the design and simulations of a group of fixed physical length spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton based delay lines to compose a 3-bit 360° phase shifter at 0.3 THz. The design is based on corrugated planar Goubau line (CPGL) delay sections with different corrugation depths varying between 19.25 μm and 44.5 μm, The simulations result in average phase error, insertion loss, and return loss of 3.265°, -2.82 dB, and -26 dB at 0.3 THz through a delay section of 1.0575 mm and 1.5635 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Electronically Polarization-Reconfigurable Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) using modified cross-slot feed to obtain switchable polarization is proposed. The proposed antenna employs electronically changing the lengths of slots to generate and alter left/right handed circular polarizations and vertical linear polarizations, respectively. By designing the structure parameters of the DRA properly, wide bandwidth can be obtained under certain state for the resonance fusion of slot and DR. Simulation results are presented for the combination of switches on and off, while maintaining a reasonable impedance match, which successfully demonstrates polarization agility.

articleTitle: Synthetic aperture radar imaging of the interior of comets using time-domain back-projection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
