abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging is commonly used today for topographic and tomographic imaging of planetary surfaces and sub-surfaces. We describe SAR imaging of the interior of comets using time-domain back-projection and a simple ray-bending solution that accounts for the bulk dielectric property of the icy interior of the comet.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Fermi Tapered Slot Antenna with Waveguide-Microstrip Transition Device
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to solve the feeding problem of W-band printed antenna and improve the gain of the array antenna element, a waveguide-microstrip transition feed device is designed to feed the Fermi tapered slot antenna. This transition device of four steps gradient method is used in the waveguide to achieve impedance transformation between waveguide and microstrip antenna. The simulation results of CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">·</sup> show that the reflection coefficient is lower than -10dB in the frequency range of 75.7 GHz to 110 GHz, the gain at the typical frequency of 94 GHz reaches 16.7 dB. The measurement results are in good agreement with the simulation results. The antenna can be applied to the antenna array of passive millimeter wave imaging system.

articleTitle: HEM12δ Mode Based Advanced Cylindrical DRA using a New Feeding with Non-Metallic Base
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new concept of realizing the HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12δ</sub>mode in CDRA has been investigated. Excitation of lone HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12δ</sub>mode is the salient feature of the proposed design. A planar feed with non-metallic base ensuring a modified boundary condition has been realized and experimentally verified. The antenna promises of an attractive gain of 11 dBi with more than 35 dB co-cross polar isolation.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna with AMC for Long Range Automotive Radar Applications at 77 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces an antenna for Automotive Radar to operate at 77 GHz. The proposed antenna consists of a hybrid radiator and dielectric resonator. The hybrid radiator is a circular patch that feed by aperture method and the dielectric resonator is ring that feed by the circular patch to operate at 77 GHz with high gain 12 dB for one element. The EBG structure is implemented on the top layer to widens the proposed band, gives high gain and to reduce surface waves. The compact size of one element 3.5mm×3.5mm×l.16mm to operate from 75.3 GHz to 80 GHz with gain 12.3 dB.

articleTitle: Study on 12/21-GHz Dual-circularly Polarized Receiving Antenna for Satellite Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In December 2018, satellite broadcasting of ultra-high-definition television (UHDTV) will begin in Japan. For broadcasting UHDTV, BSAT-4a satellite was successfully launched. The satellite has not only 12-GHz-band right- and lefthand circular polarization transponders but also a 21-GHz-band experimental transponder. To receive services provided over these two frequency bands and with dual-polarization, we designed a dual-circularly polarized parabolic reflector antenna fed by 12- and 21-GHz-band microstrip antenna arrays with a multilayer structure. Finally, we confirmed through simulation that the designed antenna satisfies our requirements.

articleTitle: Full Wave Solutions of Multiple Scattering Using Vector Spheroidal Waves and Addition Theorem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop a hybrid method to calculate the multiple scattering of arbitrary-shape objects, based on the rigorous solutions of Maxwell equations in the form of Foldy-Lax multiple scattering equations (FL). The hybrid method includes three steps: (1) calculating the T matrix of each single object using vector spheroidal waves, (2) vector spheroidal wave transformations, and (3) solving FL for all the objects. We utilize the commercial software HFSS to calculate the T matrix of a single object. From the numerical integration of the scattered fields from HFSS with the vector spheroidal waves, the T matrix is obtained. To perform wave transformations (i.e. addition theorem) for vector spheroidal waves, we develop robust numerical methods. In solving FL, the coherent wave interactions among the objects are considered and the multiple scattering of all the objects is calculated. The hybrid method is applicable for full wave simulations of objects with arbitrary shapes, such as trees with arbitrary-shape branches and leaves.

articleTitle: Predicting RF Propagation with Numerical Models
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) propagation is highly dependent upon the vertical distribution of moisture along the transmission path. The U.S. Navy employs high-resolution numerical weather prediction (NWP) models to forecast these gradient structures and their mesoscale variability. In this research we explore the fidelity of propagation loss predictions obtained using an NWP with measured data collected during the Tropical Air-sea Propagation Study (TAPS) [1]. We demonstrate good agreement with Ka-Band path loss prediction to those received by a ship mounted MIMO system for ranges up to 40-45 km from the shore-based transmitter and investigate possible sources for the stronger signals observed at longer ranges.

articleTitle: Switched Folded Slot Phased Array Antenna for mm Wave 5G Mobile in Metal Bezel Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a switched folded slot phased array antenna for metal bezel design mobile application operating millimeter-wave (mmWave) 5G communication at 28GHz. The proposed antenna is 4×2 folded slot antenna array implemented on the corner of metal bezel of mobile device. The 4xl antenna array consists of folded slot antennas designed for beam steering in xy-plane. In addition, the 2-array subsets operate as array _1 mode, array _2 mode, and array_total mode for beam steering in yz-plane. Each mode has 10.7dBi, 10.6dBi and 11.7dBi of maximum gain, respectively. Beam steering angle is 140 degrees at xy-plane and 60 degrees at yz-plane. The detail of the design methodologies, simulation and measurement results are presented and discussed in relation to the targeted mm Wave 5G mobile application.

articleTitle: Accelerated Design Optimization of Antenna Structures Using Adaptive Response Scaling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Low-cost and reliable design optimization of antenna structures using adaptive response scaling (ARS) is presented. Our approach involves variable-fidelity electromagnetic (EM) simulation models. Nonlinear frequency and amplitude correction is applied to the low-fidelity model to create a fast surrogate which is iteratively rebuilt and optimized within the trust region framework. By exploiting correlations between the EM models of various fidelities considerable reduction of the design optimization cost is achieved. A demonstration example of a dual-band patch antenna is provided. The ARS performance is favorably compared to direct optimization of the high-fidelity EM model.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Dual-Band Leaky Wave Antennas Design Methodology with Directivity Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new design methodology for dual band leaky-wave antennas is presented in the paper. The proposed methodology is based on the use of a single partial reflective surface (PRS) made with a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) that fulfills the resonant condition at two different frequencies. This allows the design of a dual band leaky wave antenna including the control on the directivity at each one of the frequencies. Two examples of the application of this method (one with identical directivities at the two frequencies and the other one with different directivities) are presented.

articleTitle: Low-Loss Compact Re-configurable Reflectarray Element
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new design of a low loss compact, and X-band reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) element is investigated. The element is an aperture coupled element with a surface mounted varactor diode attached to the matching transmission line that makes the fabrication easier and results an adequate phase tuning range. The element is a square of length 15.6 mm (0.6 ×λ at 10.5 GHz). The equivalent circuit model is verified with the full-wave analysis. A biasing network is also designed to isolate the RF signal from DC. The proposed element provides amplitude losses under -2 dB for an applied voltage of 2-28 volts, and an adequate phase tuning range of 260° from a single varactor (@ 10.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Modeling Focused Ray Scattering by a Penetrable Dielectric Slab Over Skin Surface with a Finite Air Gap for Millimeter-Wave Person Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper details a model for a weak dielectric object on the human body with a small gap between the dielectric and body, as detected by a CW millimeter-wave security scanning system. This model is a refinement of the Virtual Source Model, focusing on the possibility that the dielectric is not directly against the skin. Seven primary scattering phenomena are considered in this model, more than in the Virtual Source model; later phenomena have negligible amplitude. Even a small gap can cause a significant difference in the return.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Classification of Buried Landmine Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new technique that is capable of detecting and classifying buried landmines at different depths in sandy soil with different soil conditions. Prony's method is used to extract the complex natural resonance (CNRs) frequencies from the reflected landmine signals. These CNRs are used as new features for detection and classification of buried landmines. Different classification methods are employed to investigate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Notch-Band UWB Antenna with RF-to-DC Rectifier for Dynamic Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dynamically reconfigurable UWB antenna with a notch band at 5.6 GHz is presented. The microstrip-fed monopole uses a J-shaped stub hosted inside a rectangular slot which is used for improved matching. The J-shaped stub can be connected or disconnected to the monopole using a PIN diode switch. In order to dynamically switch the PIN diode between “ON” and “OFF” states, a rectifier can be used to convert an RF signal at 5.6 GHz into a DC voltage that can be indirectly used to bias the PIN diode. The presence of an interfering signal at 5.6 GHz dynamically causes the biasing of the PIN diode and the creation of the notch that effectively filters out the interferer. Despite the rectifier's relatively high efficiency, the rectified DC power is not sufficient to bias the PIN diode, therefore, the RF-to-DC rectifier needs to be cascaded with a DC-to-DC power booster.

articleTitle: Empirical Analysis Formulae of Microstrip Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Empirical formulae are developed to estimate the effective dielectric constant and the effective width of the microstrip ridge gap waveguide (MRGW) technology are presented. The work is a step forward towards efficient modeling and design tools for the emerging ridge gap waveguide (RGW) technology. Inspired by the microstrip analysis formulae, curve fitting is used to fit the wave propagation parameters of the MRGW in a compact form. The developed formulae are applied to several MRGW configurations showing a promising agreement with the full-wave analysis.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Transparent Coplanar Patch Antenna for WLAN Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design for a dual-band transparent coplanar patch antenna for WLAN systems is described. The transparent coplanar patch antenna is constructed by using copper mesh of micron-sized linewidth. Measurement results show that the proposed antenna operates from 2.36 to 2.76 GHz and from 4.92 to 6 GHz covering the WLAN bands and it has a omnidirectional radiation pattern. Compared with other transparent antenna, the proposed antenna has a good total antenna efficiency of up to 45% using the copper mesh film. We also evaluate the transparency and have achieved a high transparency of 92%.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of Vector Parabolic Equation based Wireless Channel Models Using Polynomial Chaos Expansion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Vector parabolic equation (VPE) methods have been widely applied to model wave propagation in guiding structures with high accuracy and computational efficiency. A detailed specification of the modeled environment is required. However, considerable uncertainty can exist in the description of the environment. This paper presents a non-intrusive formulation of polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) method to quantify the uncertainties in VPE-based channel models for tunnel environments. The performance is validated against Monte Carlo simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Ridge Gap Waveguide Quasi-TEM Horn Antenna for Ka-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A ridge gap waveguide (RGW) fed (Transverse Electromagnetic) TEM horn antenna is presented. The design of a quasi TEM horn is achieved by exponentially tapering the plates adjoining the feed section. The feeding section is designed with the concept of half-height-pin RGW. To keep uniform field excitation, the H-plane is flared within the RGW only, and the E-plane is flared after the RGW launcher subsequently. The antenna S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>(10-dB) bandwidth is covering from 25-40 GHz. The radiation characteristics of the antenna are stable within the band having 8.19 dB gain at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: A Printed Conical Beam Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A linearly polarized antenna with conical beam is designed to operate in the unlicensed band of 60 GHz. The antenna is fed with substrate integrated waveguide and fabricated using the printed-circuit-board and plated-through hole-technologies. In order to generate a conical beam, two TM modes are excited within the cavity using two slots. Simulation results reveal that the proposed antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 12.9%, covers the frequency range of 56.8 to 64.6 GHz, and realizes a gain around 5dBi. The proposed antenna can be used for short-range wireless communications.

articleTitle: Interference rejection with Time Modulated Array for GPS application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we propose the Time Modulated Array (TMA) as a low-cost architecture to be employed as a GPS receiver with interference rejection capability. The controlling parameters of TMA for beamforming are investigated and are related to the weightings of a conventional phased array. Moreover, the capability of TMA to reject the interference signal is investigated using Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm as an adaptive algorithm. The performance of the array under different interference angles indicates that it can reduce the effect of interference significantly while providing sufficient gain for the desired signal.

articleTitle: ORCHESTRA: Optimizable RF Converged Hardware Expression of a Scalable Transmit/Receive Architecture
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The need for disruptive advances in warfighter capability, upgradability, and utilization drives sensor systems toward convergent RF functionality with shared resources. The reliance of modern federated RF systems on redundant hardware leads to underutilization and inefficient use of SWaP-C. In pursuit of affordable solutions to this shortfall, converged RF and heterogeneous digital signal processing combine with existing open standard system-of-systems platform concepts to enable the next generation of platform and mission capability, through a true digital array interface to the RF environment.

articleTitle: A Simple Aperture Coupled Circular Patch Antenna with CP Radiation and Frequency Agility
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An aperture coupled microstrip-line fed patch antenna with circularly polarized (CP) radiation is initially studied. To achieve better CP radiation at lower frequency and meanwhile able to yield good frequency agility, the technique of loading an inverted C-shaped slit into the circular patch is proposed. Furthermore, frequency agility can also be attained by simply tuning the air-gap distance between the upper layer circular patch and the lower layer cross-slot feeding structure. Further analyses have shown that the proposed antenna can achieve good CP frequency agility across the desired UHF (ultra-high frequency) RFID operating band (902-928 MHz).

articleTitle: A Cylindrical Luneberg Lens Antenna with Extremely Wide Fan-Beam
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cylindrical Luneberg lens antenna with extremely wide fan-beam at 60 GHz is designed by using dyadic Green's function (DGF) and differential evolution (DE) algorithm. The cylindrical Luneberg lens antenna is analysed by using the DGF of the cylindrically stratified media in parallel plates. The permittivity and radius of each layer are optimized by a DE algorithm. The optimal lens antenna is then simulated using commercial full-wave software. The designed lens antenna has an extremely wide fan-beam, where the 3-dB beam-width is about 120.3° and 4.7° in the E- and H-plane, respectively. Numerical results validate the proposed lens antenna and show the good agreement between the theoretical predictions and the full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Design of Planar Sparse Antenna Array with Rectangular boundary by Bi-linear Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A bi-linear approach is proposed to efficiently design planar sparse antenna arrays with rectangular boundary. On account of practical manufacturing and cost limitation, it deals with x-y de-coupled planar sparse arrays whose array factor could be decomposed into two linear array factors. Computational cost for both radiation pattern and array synthesis accordingly is significantly reduced. It is successfully applied to design an array with low sidelobe level.

articleTitle: Characterization of Multiple-Layer Anisotropic Metasurfaces Based on Generalized Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Scattering properties of multiple-layer anisotropic metasurfaces are characterized based on generalized boundary conditions. Once surface susceptibilities of all layers are determined, reflection and transmission coefficients could be readily derived for arbitrary incident angles and polarizations. The validity of this analytical method is demonstrated through comparison between computed results and full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Recent Advances of FEKO and WinProp
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes recent advances of the commercial CEM code FEKO, as well as the wave propagation and radio network planning tool WinProp. This includes the simulation of characterized surfaces (complex radomes, frequency-selective surfaces) with RL-GO, a direct solver for ACA (adaptive cross approximation), and supporting FEM (finite element method) and MoM (method of moments) with SEP (surface equivalence principle) in the same model.

articleTitle: Fully Printed VO2 Switch Based Reconfigurable PIFA Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Frequency reconfigurable antennas are attractive as they can cover multiple bands as well as different wireless standards in different countries. Typically., these antennas utilize complex subtractive fabrication processes which result in higher costs. For switching to different bands., generally semiconductor based devices such as PIN diode switches or MEMS switches., etc. are used., which add to the cost and pose integration and reliability issues. The ideal approach would be to use low-cost additive manufacturing techniques., such as inkjet printing. This work presents., a novel fully inkjet printed frequency reconfigurable PIFA antenna., where the switch (based on vanadium dioxide (V02)) has also been printed. The switch operates through thermal activation and reconfigures the frequency band. In one mode of the switch., the antenna operates at 2.4 GHz band for WiFi., Bluetooth or Zigbee applications., and in the other mode., it operates at 3.5 GHz band for 5G communications. The antenna achieved 1.58 dBi gain at 3.5GHz.

articleTitle: Planar Quasi-Yagi Antenna for Future 5G and WiGig Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a planar quasi-Yagi antenna that covers the operating bandwidths of 28 GHz, 38 GHz, and 60 GHz. Experimental results show that the fabricated antenna can achieve a 10-dB impedance bandwidth from 25.8 GHz to 29.8 GHz and from 33.2 GHz to > 67 GHz, and can demonstrate consistent end-fire patterns and peak gain greater than 6 dBi over the entire bandwidths.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Voltage Doubler Rectifier Design for Harvesting ambient RF Energy
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The voltage-doubler (VD) rectifier circuits are the most used in the rectennas design. In this paper, a method of designing a highly efficient Schenkel VD is proposed. The choice of the rectifying diode is first established according to measurements of ambient power density carried over in the literature. By using the filter Design tool of the Advanced Design System (ADS) software, a band-pass filter is designed to ensure a good power transfer between the antenna and the rectifier circuit. The filter elements are then optimized by the gradient method search to achieve optimum performance in the GSM band. Especially for a power density of 39 nW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the designed circuit associated with a 10 dBi gain antenna shows a conversion efficiency of 55%.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Electromagnetic Scattering from Objects above Complex Rough Surface Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents how to apply a new scattering model to the prediction of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from objects in the presence of underlying rough surface. The newly developed scattering model is more consistent with the real scenario through the adoption of finite beam source, considering the perturbation from the illuminated rough surface with using hybrid shooting and bouncing rays-physical optics (SBR-PO) method, and taking into account infinite environment effects using half-space Green's function. Numerical results obtained validate the proposed method and its implementation.

articleTitle: Phased Antenna Array Design using Shuffled Frog-Leaping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a new meta-heuristic approach (memetic algorithm) to address multi-objective problems in planar phased arrays. Memetic algorithms are hybrid algorithms that combine the benefits of a global search evolutionary algorithm with a local search method. The Shuffled Frog-Leaping Algorithm (SFLA) consists of a virtual population of frogs partitioned into different memeplexes. It performs a memetic evolution within the memeplex (local search) and a shuffling mix process between memeplexes (global search) to deliver optimum solutions in optimization problems. Derived results show improved characteristics of the antenna array.

articleTitle: A Class of Cavity-Based UWB Multi-Beamformers With Applications to Sub-6 GHz 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new class of cavity-based, true-time delay multibeam former is proposed. Rotman lens optics are implemented for broadband and low phase-error response. The proposed topology offers markedly improved efficiency over microstrip based designs, while operating inside a sealed, metal cavity. A prototype design is presented which operates at Stein's theoretical efficiency limit for passive RF beamforming over the UWB frequency band (3.1 to 10.6 GHz) with excellent multi-beam fidelity.

articleTitle: 3D Direction-of-Arrival Estimation using a Wideband Vector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication, direction finding performances of a reconfigurable wideband vector antenna are predicted. The accurate estimation of the direction of arrivals across the 3D half-space of incoming electromagnetic fields is obtained over a 1.7:1 frequency range from only two colocated and orthogonal circular arrays of Vivaldi antennas.

articleTitle: Towards Embroidered Textile Antenna Systematic Design and Accurate Modeling: Rectangular Patch Antenna Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present the methodology of material characterization and detailed simulation strategies towards the accurate modeling of embroidery-based textile rectangular patch antennas. The effective conductivity of the conductive material and the permittivity of the substrate material are characterized by the resonant frequency matching and the four-micro-strip line methods, respectively. A detailed full-wave simulation model is demonstrated to account for the double-layer embroidery nature of the conductive pattern. An embroidered patch antenna operating at 2.5 G Hz is prototyped to compare with the full-wave simulation model results of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and radiation pattern. The proposed modeling strategies are proved to be effective in guiding the embroidered patch antenna design.

articleTitle: Beam Domain Formulation for Tomographic Inverse Scattering. Part II: The Inverse Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this two-part paper we present a local inverse scattering approach using pulsed-beam frame (PBF) processing. In Part I we explored the beam-domain representation of the scattered fields and demonstrated that within the Born approximation, the beam-domain data is proportional to the local Radon transform of the medium. In this Part II we use this result and present a local reconstruction algorithm using pulsed beam back-propagators.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gain Tunable Two Elements Antenna Array Based on Graphene
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a two-element circular monopole antenna array is designed and tuned through a graphene sheet. A CPW fed is used to feed the antenna array. The graphene sheet is added under a CPW fed network of the antenna array. Thanks to the graphene sheet, the antenna array is operated to serve more applications with enhanced gain. The antenna array with the graphene sheet is designed and simulated. Simulated results are discussed and illustrated in the following sections.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual UWB Quasi-Yagi based MIMO Antenna System Using a Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a dual ultra-wideband (UWB) 2-element Quasi-Yagi based multiple-input-multiple output (MIMO) antenna system is proposed based on loop excitation. A novel defected ground structure (DGS) acting as a parasitic reflector element is used to achieve 48% reduction in size without compromising other performance metrics. The center frequency of operation is 2 GHz. The proposed dual-band MIMO antenna system has a wide measured bandwidth of 1.72 GHz from 1.9-3.62 GHz and 1.70 GHz from 4.6-6.3 GHz covering the GSM/EDGE/LTE, WLAN, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and WiMAX bands. The proposed MIMO antenna system occupies a size of 80×120×0.76 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, The maximum measured realized gain and total radiation efficiency of the MIMO antenna system are found to be more than 5 dBi and 80%, respectively, within both bands. Aside from good Yagi-Uda performance, the proposed antenna system also shows excellent MIMO performance, with minimum measured isolation of 15 dB and measured envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) value of 0.0341 in both bands.

articleTitle: Emitter Location Using Power Difference of Arrival
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we show the implementation of a noncooperative emitter location system in real scenario, using the power Difference of Arrival Technique and a cloud based radio planning tool. We show the results for a FM radio station localization using six sensors positions in a non-optimum distribution.

articleTitle: Application of Convolutional Neural Network in Target Detection of Millimeter Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article focuses on the establishment of convolutional neural network model to achieve the detection of human concealment in millimeter wave images. The convolutional neural network is applied to the image data set for detection training, pictures are randomly selected for identification, and the target location is marked. This paper proves that convolutional neural network can be applied as a feasible general image detection technology to different detection problems.

articleTitle: A Parametric Amplifier Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Parametric amplifier utilizes nonlinear and/or time variant properties of reactive elements (capacitors and/or inductors) to amplify radio frequency signals. A new hybrid topology containing a parametric amplifier and an antenna is presented. A pair of varactor diodes, as nonlinear reactors, are incorporated in the structure of a slot antenna on the side wall of a rectangular cavity resonator to amplify the received signal. A hybrid simulation (full wave simulation by (HFSS) and circuit simulation by (ADS) software packages) is used to simulate the entire antenna structure including radiating element and nonlinear amplifying elements. The simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of the proposed parametric antenna.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Purely Textile Proximity Fed Microstrip Patch Antenna for On-Body Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Novel combinations of materials and construction techniques are key for the development of new textile antenna configurations for on-body applications. Stretchable, flexible and conformable features of textile antennas are one of the hot research topics nowadays. This work gives a step forward with new designs of purely textile proximity coupled microstrip patch antennas with flexible and robust features at 2.44GHz, on-body applications. Their performance is successfully validated in different materials, both simulated and constructed, and obtaining positive results.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Dual-polarized Microstrip Antenna Array with Wideband and High Isolation for Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a dual-band dual-polarized (DBDP)microstrip array with wideband, high isolation and low cross polarization working at 12.5 GHz and 14.25 GHz is described in this paper. Cross slots coupled multilayer antenna elements are employed to widen the bandwidth. The feed networks are placed on the opposite side to improve the isolation. Meanwhile, u-shaped delay lines are employed to obtain differential outputs to reduce the cross polarization. The simulation results show that the DBDP array exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 24.8% ranging from 11-14.1 GHz for Port Hand 21 % ranging from 12.7-15.7 GHz for Port V. The cross polarization level is better than −24 dB in E-plane (xoy)and −36 dB in H plane (yoz), and the isolation between ports is above 35 dB.

articleTitle: Towards Three-dimensional Millimeter-Wave Radar Imaging of On-the-move Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents our preliminary results for a three-dimensional (3D) imaging of an on-the-move target using a MIMO millimeter-wave (mm-wave) radar, which uses 9 transmitters and 12 receivers. The operating frequency of the mm-wave radar is from 70 GHz to 77 GHz. Experimental results show that the images can be created as the target under detection moves in front of the radar system, which is combined with 3D video to show the continuous movement of the target. This preliminary work paves the way towards a mm-wave imaging system that can be used at checkpoints; thus enabling on-the-move detection of potential threats, enhancing passenger's overall experience, and achieving a high scanning throughput.

articleTitle: Multilayer Circularly Polarized Planar Aperture-Coupled Antenna for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a single-fed circularly polarized (CP) aperture-coupled antenna with multilayer structure is proposed for satellite applications in Ku-band. It is composed of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity, aperture coupling slot, hollow cavity, and stacked patches. CP operation is realized by embedding a pair of L-shaped strips around the two opposite corners of the square radiation patch. Simulation results show an impedance bandwidth (IBW) with Sl1<;-10dB from 13.5 to 19 GHz (33.8%) and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) from 15.5 to 16.4 GHz (5.6%), and gain of 5.8 ± 0.2 dBi across the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth. The overall volume of the antenna is 0.47λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×.47λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.12λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 15.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Radiation Patterns of an RF Energy Harvesting Necklace on Human Body Phantom
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The far-field electromagnetic radiation patterns of different dipole antennas used for an RF energy harvesting necklace for smart jewelry are studied. Rigid Vee, V-shaped copper and flexible silver-ink dipoles are explored with and without a human body phantom. Measurements demonstrate the advantages of Vee or V-shaped dipoles for harvesting more RF energy at the sides of the human body compared to a straight dipole. The flexible RF energy harvesting necklace can produce 72.2 μW at 5.3 m from a 3 W EIRP 915 MHz RF transmitter when worn by a person.

articleTitle: Comparison of Antenna Patterns from Active and Passive Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Patterns are the most challenging antenna parameter to estimate. The pattern detail is critical for high gain satellite systems and also essential for evaluating low gain diversity antennas for MIMO systems. For small devices with integrated antennas, such as mobile phones and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, antenna pattern measurement is usually done by attaching a coaxial test cable directly to the antenna port (often through a matching network), bypassing the rest of the system making the measurement passive. The test cable must be carefully routed to best suppress the cable's structural scattering contribution. With present measurement systems, it is possible to estimate a pattern using active, over-the-air (OTA) tests. In this paper we compare the results from passive and active tests. Then, by computing the correlation between the measured patterns, we demonstrate the effect of the test cable. This study also demonstrates the potential of antenna pattern estimation from active testing, which is regarded as necessary at higher microwave and mm-wave frequencies where the test fixture can significantly modify the radiation characteristics making the passive measurement inaccurate and in some cases essentially useless.

articleTitle: A 300-GHz Step-profiled Corrugated Horn Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper studies a 300-GHz step-profiled corrugated horn antenna array integrated in low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC)technology. First, several identical step-profiled corrugate horn antennas were aligned into linear array in the immediate vicinity. Then, the mutual coupling among the elements was evaluated and discussed. Finally, the radiation performance of the antenna array was inspected with a comparison between the calculated and simulated results. It was found that the mutual coupling between the adjacent elements is rather weak, indicating such a step-profiled corrugated horn antenna array is attractive candidate for THz antenna array applications.

articleTitle: Ultra High Order Basis Functions in Analysis of Scattering from Large Metallic Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Polynomial higher order basis functions defined over quadrilaterals are regularly used with patches of maximum edge up to 2λ and expansion order up to n = 8. In this paper it is demonstrated that these limits can be significantly extended if max-ortho bases are implemented in a proper way. Numerical results demonstrate effective usage of patches up to 8λ and expansion orders up to n = 24.

articleTitle: 1 GHz charge pump with ultra-low power boost converter for increased output voltage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a two-stage RF -DC charge pump is designed for impedance matching at 1 GHz and integrated with a commercially available ultra-low power boost converter with a turn-on voltage of 0.3V. This circuit was tested, up to a maximum range of 5.5 meters, using log periodic UHF transmit and receive antennas with 28 dBm output power from the transmitter. The boosted voltage of 4.2V at the converter's output can enable a wider range of wireless sensors for Internet-of- Things applications.

articleTitle: Effect of Geometrical Parameters of a Width Modulated Microstrip Line Based Mantle-Cloak
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Mantle cloaking of a metallic cylinder through a width modulated microstrip line metasurface is presented. The considered unit cell consists of a sinusoidally shaped profile printed on a dielectric substrate. The maximum height of the profile within a constant footprint unit cell is varied aiming to examine its effect on the field scattered by the cylinder described in terms of the Radar Cross Section.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Thin Dielectric Objects Using the Impedance Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, characteristic mode analysis of thin dielectric objects is performed using the impedance boundary condition. An electric field integral equation formulation is provided for the computation. An FR-4 slab is calculated as an example and the results are compared with full-wave solutions. It is shown that this method is fairly accurate and computationally efficient, which may be extended for other surfaces.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Open-ended Waveguide with Squinted Beam for X-band Monopulse Antenna on A Small Diameter Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-polarized open-ended waveguide (OEWG) with squinted beam for X-band monopulse antenna which can be placed on a small diameter cylinder. The antenna consists of a quadruple-ridged feeding structure in a square OEWG and an inclined aperture to achieve dual-polarization and squinted beam characteristics, respectively. The bandwidth of the antenna is from 8 GHz to over 12 GHz in an aperture dimension of 22 mm×22 mm (width×height). Using four designed OEWG antennas, X-band monopulse antenna is designed and its sum (Σ) and difference (A) patterns are calculated. The (Δ) pattern gains of the antenna are 9.7 dB, 12.1 dB, and 14 dB for 8 GHz, 10 GHz, and 12 GHz, respectively. The null depths of the A patterns are under -30 dB within the operational frequency.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band MIMO Slot Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band dual-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for wireless local area network (WLAN) and Wireless-Fidelity (Wi-Fi) applications is presented in this report. The proposed antenna has a simple planar structure and occupies a small area of 13. S×32mm2. An L-shaped open-ended slot and an L-shaped micros trip line are used as quarter-wavelength and half wavelength radiators, respectively. The operating band of the proposed antenna are from 2.3-2.49 GHz and S.1-S.S6GHz. The wide slot in the middle of the ground is used to achieve good isolation at both bands.

articleTitle: Tx/Rx Antenna System for Full-Duplex Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of an antenna system consisting of a Tx and a Rx antenna close to each other for SISO, MISO or SIMOFull Duplex applications. The reduction of the self-interference or mutual coupling is obtained by combining a compact two patches array and a single patch placed to specific chosen positions determined thanks to parametric studies in order to obtain a diversity system. Thus, an isolation level better than 50 dB at 5.5 GHz is reached. A good agreement between measured and simulated results is also observed. This result, combined with analog and digital cancellation techniques, can satisfy the self-interference challenge of Full Duplex system.

articleTitle: A New Wide Band Antenna for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new wide band antenna is proposed for applications in wireless communication systems. The proposed antenna is a combination of a dipole and slot radiating elements and it is formed by two metal sheets of symmetrical shapes separated by a S-shape slot. The antenna can be located above a metal ground and it is fed by a 500hm transmission line at the middle of the slot. A case of the semi-circular metal shapes in free space and above the circular ground plane (reflector) with a Teflon ring to support the dipole shapes has been analyzed. It has been shown that the antenna bandwidth varies from 30% to 50%. The realized gain of the antenna with the reflector is 8dB across the operational band.

articleTitle: 3D MIMO Dual-Band Antenna on Paper Substrate for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a 3D MIMO antenna printed on a flexible paper substrate is presented in this paper. The MIMO scheme is 3*3 and the antenna is devoted for dual-band 2.4/5 GHz WLAN applications. The antenna is based on an innovative compact dipole antenna with integrated balun.

articleTitle: Beam Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Holographic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a beam reconfigurable antenna based on holographic metasurfaces is presented. Sinusoidally-modulated surface impedance is obtained on the holography metasurface to satisfy the requirement of the interference between the desired beam and the reference beam, and the surface impedance can be tuned by changing the bias voltage of varactor diodes loaded on the sub-wavelength unit cells, which directly results in the change of radiation angle. The simulation results shown that the radiation angle can cover the range from 32° to 67°, which is in accordance with theoretical results. The proposed holographic metasurfaces have great advantages in microwave devices due to the characteristics of beam steering and low-profile.

articleTitle: A Multipurpose Calibrator in Radar Cross Section Measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple calibration is an important way for uncertainty assurance in radar cross section (RCS) measurement. In this work, based on Wood's CAM design, a multipurpose calibrator called ECAM is proposed, where an ellipsoidal surface is added to the hull of CAM. ECAM can offer three “exact” RCS values through simple azimuth rotation, which are invariant of or linearly proportional to frequency with adequate RCS levels. Numerical analysis is performed on data calculated using the method of moments (MoM) to demonstrate the usefulness of ECAM.

articleTitle: Gain and Side Lobe Level Enhancement of Array Antennas Using Metasurface Superstrates
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a wide-band circularly polarized antenna, and a systematic procedure for designing antenna arrays comprising of crossed-bowtie (cloverleaf) radiating elements. We show gain improvements ranging from 6.87dB for a single element to 15.84dB for 3×3 and to 20.5dB for 5×5 with Side Lobe Level (SLL)-12.8dB and -11.5dB. The Metasurface Superstrate (MSS) further improves the gain to 18.6dB for 3×3 and 22.4dB for 5×5 and SLL to -20.9dB and -14.7dB. The optimum height for the MSS superstrate is λ/4 to realize the best gain and SLL performance. The realized return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) bandwidth of the single antenna element is 38.5%, and its 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 41.5 %. The proposed antenna arrays may be useful for C-band satellite communication.

articleTitle: High-Gain Beam Steering by Near-Field Phase Transformation - An Overview
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents an overview of a new high-gain beam-steering antenna method, which makes use of printed metasurfaces for near-field phase transformation. This beam-steering technology can play a vital role in a variety of space and ground systems where steering a high-gain beam is required. The concept of near-field phase transformation yields antenna systems with a very low profile (small height). In our systems, which can be manufactured at low cost, the base antenna and the RF connections are completely stationary; there are many choices for the base antenna depending on the application. These antenna systems are planar and can be concealed in shallow spaces in existing structures, unlike traditional mechanically steered high-gain antennas. The only moving parts are two very thin totally passive rotating metasurfaces, placed very close to the base antenna. They can be remotely operated using a pair of stepping motors, which may be powered by a solar panel. Contrary to phased arrays these antenna systems are extremely efficient even in millimeter-wave bands, can handle much higher power levels with negligible distortion and non-linearity. The unique features of these antennas mean that they are useful on both stationary and mobile platforms including trains, planes, and emergency vehicles.

articleTitle: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for Wide-Angle Coverage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs)is proposed in this paper. Two different work patterns - endfire pattern and side radiation pattern - are effectively realized by controlling the status of three PIN diodes. Simulated results show the max gain direction ranges from 45° to 84° in the operating band of 5.1 GHz to 5.8 GHz while the antenna works on the side ejection pattern. And the proposed antenna can also provide an endfire radiation beam within 5 GHz to 5.5 GHz while operating on the other pattern.

articleTitle: Low-cost Conformal UHF RFID Tag Antenna for Plastic Water Bottles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel conformal UHF RFID tag antenna for tagging plastic water bottles is presented. The proposed tag consists of nested-slots integrated with a dipole. This configuration provides a good impedance match with a chip on the surface of water bottles at the cost of reduced antenna gain as compared to gain in free space. However, the label-type tag can be readable up to 3 m in US RFID band, when mounted on water bottles. On the other hand, the tag has a read range of 2.5 m in free space. Moreover, the proposed tag is compact (40×14 mm'), low-cost and can be easily printed on the surface of bottles.

articleTitle: Tapered Low Profile UWB Directive Antenna for Radar and Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a minimized ground, electrically narrow very low profile, ENVELOP antenna for ground penetrating radar and low frequency communication applications. The basic geometry consists of two combined short inductive loop TEM horns optimized for the lower UHF band. Previous short monopole TEM horns require relatively large ground planes with respect to the antenna element. The proposed antenna introduces a ground plane and a double exponential taper to increase bandwidth while decreasing the required ground plane size. The exponential taper compensates for the loss of bandwidth from the minimized ground plane. The exponential structure maximizes the loop based current contributions for a given height and ground plane requirement of. 09 Ao and 0.6 Ao respectively, where Ao is the minimum wavelength. This structure utilizes dual feeds with phase differences to create directional variation. The perpendicular maximized directivity and wide bandwidth are important for ground penetrating radar applications. Two improvements to the structure are introduced with a stacked and coupled dipole to improve the frequency bandwidth and antenna matching performance.

articleTitle: Design of a 1-bit Reconfigurable Transmitarray Element Using an Equivalent Magnetic Dipole
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this letter, a novel linearly-polarized 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray element at 12.5 GHz is proposed. The element consists of a transmitting magnetic dipole patch, a receiving square patch, and a metallized via-hole between them. Two PIN diodes with opposite states are integrated on the magnetic dipole patch, thus achieving 1-bit phase tuning using the current reversal mechanism. Full-wave simulations show that the half-power beamwidth of the proposed element is 142°in the E-plane by exploiting the radiation of the equivalent magnetic dipole, and the insertion loss is 0.74 dB with a 1-dB transmission bandwidth of 8.0%. The excellent performance of the proposed element demonstrates its promising prospects in wide-angle scanning transmitarray designs.

articleTitle: A Multipart 5G Base-Station Antenna Using Series-Fed Patch Antenna Sub-Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel antenna architecture using multiport arrays for 5G base stations. The proposed antenna consists of multiple sub-arrays, performing baseband signal processing so that high gain and broad angular coverage can be achieved simultaneously. The sub-arrays are designed by using series feed networks and patch antenna elements. We arrange these sub-arrays steering to different directions with overlapped sub-array patterns. With the information of the pilot signals, the channel state of each subarray port can be estimated. The output of each sub-array port is combined and fed to a baseband processor, which synthesizes a pattern with high gain and broad angular coverage. The antenna sub-arrays are designed, fabricated, and tested. The system performance utilizing baseband signal processing is also evaluated. Our comparison shows that the proposed antenna overcomes the limitation of conventional array structures.

articleTitle: High Gain Slotted Waveguide fed Microstrip Antenna Array at Ka-band for High power Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, high gain slotted waveguide fed microstrip antenna array with high power handling capacity has been designed at Ka-band. It consists of slotted waveguide, which feeds linear microstrip antenna array. This type of feeding technique has an advantage that it reduces the losses from the microstrip feed network and can handle high power. Each linear microstrip antenna array has 27 elements and there are 26 such linear arrays which are placed on each slot of the waveguide. It gives a bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>≤ 10 dB) from 35.80-36 GHz and gain of 35.4 dBi. It gives side lobe level of 16.8 dB. Such an antenna can be used in high power millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: ACompact AMC-Based Novel Monopole Antenna for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel and compact AMC-based coplanar waveguide (CPW) antenna designed with hexagonal ring and patch elements for RFID applications. The AMC structure is designed with meander line that reflects the incident wave with 0° phase reflector. The AMC cell is designed using CST microwave studio. An AMC unit cell alone, monopole antenna and a monopole with AMC surface with electrical size of 0.02λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0, 0.</sub>2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and 0.37 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> are designed at 868 MHz (European band) used for RFID applications. The proposed monopole antenna with AMC reflecting surface provides an overall realized gain of 6.7 dBi. The simulated results are characterized in terms of return loss, gain and radiation pattern of the antenna with and without artificial magnetic conductor AMC.

articleTitle: Broadband Patch Antenna with Narrow Width Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar rectangular conducting patch is considered to increase its bandwidth compared with the conventional microstrip antenna. The thin substrate is the main reason for narrowing the microstrip antenna bandwidth due to its high Q-factor. Here, the ground plane of the conventional microstrip antenna is reduced along its width direction, but the ground plane length along the patch length is kept. As such, the patch resonance is kept close to the conventional microstrip, but the Q-factor is decreased increasing the new structure bandwidth. Now, strong coupling between the patch and the coaxial cable feeding influences the antenna performance. Both the simulated and the measured results present the validity of this design where the bandwidth is increased to be over 15%. Depending on this analytical method the corresponding bandwidth can be broadened again after continuously narrowing the width of the ground plane.

articleTitle: Multifunctional All-Dielectric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Cascaded dielectric metasurfaces that provide distinct polarization conversion/control at different bands are introduced. A step-by-step design approach is presented to realize a wide range of polarization transformations with metasurfaces employing simple geometries. The proposed metasurfaces consist of cascaded subwavelength gratings with varying orientations that are separated by isotropic spacers. These metasurfaces can be designed to function as broadband or multiband polarization filters, as well as multifunctional polarization converters that are compact (wavelength-scaled)and low-loss.

articleTitle: An Explicit MOT Scheme for solving the Nyström-Discretized TD-MFIE
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fully explicit marching-on-in-time scheme for solving the time domain magnetic field integral equation is proposed. The unknown current density induced on the surface of the scatterer is expanded using a higher-order Nyström method in space and Lagrange interpolation in time. The resulting system is cast in the form of an ordinary differential equation and integrated in time using a predictor-corrector scheme to obtain the unknown expansion coefficients. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed explicit scheme can use the same time step size as its implicit counterpart without sacrificing stability and is five times faster under low-frequency excitation (i.e., for large time step).

articleTitle: A New Way to Integrate Physics-Based Channel Models in Communication System Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wireless communication system design is traditionally carried out in a rather sequential manner. As a result, propagation modeling and network protocol design have largely evolved as independent areas. This conventional fragmented approach does not fully capitalize on potential efficiencies during the design of communication systems. This paper proposes an integrated approach for communication system design, which is illustrated using an example of optimizing access point locations in a curved rectangular tunnel. The simple yet insightful example demonstrates the benefits of co-developing the wireless channel models and network protocol design and hence paves the way for further develooment of this intearated aooroach.

articleTitle: On the Modeling of Antenna Arrays for Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for the modeling of large antenna arrays in base-stations of massive MIMO systems. The approach subdivides an MxN array into either M or N subarrays, each consisting of N or M elements, respectively. Analyses are presented for an array consisting of 3×5 dipole elements operating at 2.45GHz in WLAN propagation environments of various degree of multipath. The results show the differences and trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost.

articleTitle: A Microwave Reflection Method to Determine the Complex Permittivity of Time-Varying Plasma
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microwave reflection method is presented to determine the complex permittivity of time-varying plasma. Due to the existing of multiple solutions in the extraction of permittivity from reflection coefficient, a linear variation approximation is proposed with two unknown timing coefficients to be defined with the Simplex algorithm. At last, the measurement results of shock-tube excited plasma are presented.

articleTitle: Flatness enhancement of Gap Waveguide Slot Arrays using a Ribbed-Grid Plate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a useful and simple way to avoid possible assembly problems between the radiating layer and the feeding layer, especially tailored for high-gain and low-profile gap waveguide array antennas. This case is focused on an 8×8 array as demonstrator although it may be extended to larger antennas. The radiating layer, instead of being just a thin plate with slots cut on it, it includes a ribbed grid. These ribs provide improved robustness to the radiating layer without modifying the slot array performance.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Quadruple Band-notched UWB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quadruple band-notched ultrawideband (UWB) horseshoe-shaped microstrip-fed patch antenna on Rogers RT 5880 substrate is proposed. Notch stop bands are achieved around the WIMAX (3.3-3.7 GHz), C band (4.5-5 GHz), X band (7.2-7.7 GHz), ITU band (8-8.5 GHz), which suppresses the interference between narrow band systems and UWB systems. Quadruple band-notched characteristics could be realized by adding a T-shaped branch, a C-shaped branch, and etching a U-shaped slot on the patch, a pair of L-shaped slots on the ground plane. The proposed structures on band-notched characteristics can be explained by antenna surface current and equivalent circuit. This antenna can be used for ultrawideband (UWB) applications.

articleTitle: Compact 60GHz On-Chip Antenna in 65nm CMOS Technology with Circular and Linear Polarization for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, design and simulation of a compact on-chip antenna for 60 GHz band applications is presented. Antenna is designed in 65 nm TSMC technology. This technology consists of 9 metal layers. A 0.7 mm×0.7 mm patch with slots is located on 9th layer and first layer is used as ground plane. Total chip size is 0.8 mm x 0.8 mm. In order to enhance radiation efficiency and control axial ratio, four slots are adjusted on ground plane. Circular and linear polarizations are achievable by proper port excitation. Maximum efficiency of the antenna is about 60% at 59.6 GHz. Simulated antenna bandwidth ranges from 58.7 GHz as band start and 62.3 GHz as band stop. Peak gain values for circularly and linearly polarized modes are -0.6 dB and -0.9 dB at 0° respectively.

articleTitle: 6–10 GHz Circularly-Polarized Multistatic Array for Standoff Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A system for performing standoff microwave imaging has been developed for the evaluation of imager performance in the upper C- and lower X-bands. The imaging system aperture is based on a sparse multistatic topology compatible with fast imaging techniques. Details on the design and realization of the imaging aperture are presented, as well as experimental images formed with the fabricated imaging array.

articleTitle: Absorber/Reflector Switchable Metamaterial with Polarization-Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a switchable metamaterial absorber/reflector has been presented based on microfluidic technology. The proposed structure consists of a meandered pattern engraved in an elastomeric substrate, where the liquid metal alloy (eutectic gallium indium, EGaIn) can be injected through the microchannels. The novelty of the design lies in its switching response from perfect reflection to polarization-selective absorption, depending on the injection of EGaIn in the channels. The structure, with liquid metal alloy, exhibits narrow-band absorption at 5.92 GHz during vertical polarization, whereas the absorption is shifted to higher frequency range (15.09 GHz) under horizontal polarization. Surface current distribution of the geometry has been studied to explain the absorption mechanism for different polarizations. Finally, the structure has been fabricated and experimentally verified, thereby confirming the potential use of microfluidic technology based structures.

articleTitle: Innovative Multi-Feed-Per-Beam Reflector Antenna for Space-Borne Conical-Scan Radiometers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an antenna for use on conical-scan space-borne radiometers in C band and demonstrate that stringent radiometric requirements can be met. The antenna consists of as m offset reflector fed by a focal plane array in a multi-feed-per-beam configuration, so far never used in ocean observation missions. We use distinct element beams and two optimization routines for obtaining element excitation amplitudes and phases, and with either routine, and in both x- and y-polarization, compliant beams, with footprint <; 20 km, distance to coast <; 20 km and accuracy <; 0.25 K, are obtained. These results may pave the way for use of focal plane arrays with digital beamforming in future radiometric ocean observation missions.

articleTitle: Forward Derivation and Analysis for 3-D Scattering Center Position of Radar Target
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To better link the scattering center with the target structure, this paper forwardly deduces and analyses the component-level 3-D scattering center position of radar target under the mechanisms of single and double scattering. The ray equivalent position under the double scattering mechanism is especially deduced. This position derivation process is then applied on the models of SLICY and T72 tank to deduce and analyze their scattering center positions. The corresponding measured SAR images are used for contrast to prove the validity of the position derivation.

articleTitle: An Efficient Mode-Matching Solution for Open-Ended Coaxial Waveguides via Analytic Continuation of the Radial Space
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The mode-matching technique (MMT) is a very efficient method for modeling canonical waveguide junctions by using discrete modal fields. The treatment of open-ended waveguides, however, can not be easily handled in traditional MMT formulations without the introduction of tricky continuum of radiation modes. As an alternative, the method of moments (MoM) can be employed in conjunction with the MMT for solving the resultant (discretized) field integral equation numerically. The numerical calculations, however, make this hybrid approach less than ideal in terms of computational efficiency. In this paper, we present a mode-matching-based solution for modeling open-ended coaxial horns. Closed-form solutions are obtained by using the complex coordinate-stretching formulation of the perfectly matched layer (PML) and the invariance of Maxwell's equations under such analytic continuation. Numerical results presented show good agreement versus other well-established numerical techniques.

articleTitle: A Metamaterial Broadwall Waveguide Slot Filtering Antenna for SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel metamaterial waveguide slot antenna array with filtering performance is presented. The array is composed of longitudinal slots cut in the upper broadwall of a rectangular waveguide and a metamaterial surface instead of its bottom broadwall. The array shows a good performance in operating band and perfect filtering characteristics in interfering band. A 4-element array is simulated with perfect performances, verifying the design.

articleTitle: Robust Image Retrieval from Phaseless Data
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a robust method to reconstruct complex images from phaseless data. By approximating low-frequency coefficients of an unknown signal by spectral method, the proposed method dramatically reduces number of unknowns at the initialization stage. Consequently, the proposed method is able to reconstruct complex images with much fewer phaseless measurements, while keeping the dominant computational cost of each iteration unchanged. Further numerical simulations also show that the proposed method is stable to different initializations and noisy environments. It is expected that the proposed method will find applications in the fields where image reconstructions from phaseless measurements are needed, such as antenna diagnostics.

articleTitle: Stripline Fed Hollow Dielectric Resonator Antenna-in-Package with/without Metal Shielding
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an antenna-in-package (AiP) configuration is proposed with hollow dielectric resonator antenna fed by short-circuited stripline through an aperture. Two antenna prototypes without and with the four walls of hollow shielded are designed and the -10 dB bandwidths are 31.7% and 15.7%, respectively. An isolation over 60 dB is achieved between the antenna and the microstrip line packaged inside when the hollow region is completely shielded with metal layers, which is very suitable for the applications of AiP and RF system-in-package.

articleTitle: A Six-Octave Wideband and Low Profile Log-Period Monopole Endfire Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a six-octave wideband and low-profile log-period monopole endfire antenna for the flush-mounted applications. 24 monopoles with log-period rule are used to cover 2-12 GHz operating frequency band and those monopoles are printed on both side of a low-loss dielectric layer vertically placed over a wideband microstrip-to-slot line transition. The low-profile is realized by bending some of the long monopoles so the overall antenna size is obtained as 40 mm×100 mm×13.6 mm. The simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna can work at the whole 2-12 GHz band with very good endfire radiation pattern and stable gain performance.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Feeder for Combinational Switched-Beam Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reconfigurable feeder for switched-beam based on RF switch is proposed on this paper. The proposed reconfigurable switch network provides not only on/off-functionality but also distributive path by attaching combiner/splitter and SP4T switch. In addition to reconfigurable input/output paths, isolation of the switch network has improved. Two-port output reconfigurable feeder generates multi-beam and the number of output can be expanded by combining two-port output reconfigurable feeders.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement for Parallel Feeding Networks by Regulating Transmission Line Lengths
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here, an approach to enhance the impedance bandwidth of antenna arrays fed by a parallel feeding network is introduced and elaborated. Through regulating the lengths of each segment of the transmission lines between two adjacent T-junctions in the parallel feeding network, the bandwidth can be expanded, and the reflection can perform symmetrical response around the central frequency. A simplified and ideal circuit model for the analysis is illustrated, and recursive expressions are derived for the design. Based on the numerical results of the expressions, some concise and practicable rules are obtained and verified on a 4×4 array. In addition, aT-junction structure with flexible directions of branches is proposed as key components to exemplify the implementation of the microstrip feeding network.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction Between Two Closely Spaced PIFAs
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of two PIFAs antennas array with decoupling structure to enhance the isolation between the elements for MIMO applications. The array is built on flexible polyimide substrate with relative permittivity of 4.3 and thickness of 50 um. The decoupling structure is rectangular loop placed between the two PIFAs. The array resonant at 2.45 GHz. An isolation of 7 dB has been achieved between the two elements at 2.45 GHz with separation of 2 mm. The total realized gain of the two elements excited in the array has been increased to 1.4 dB. The array is suitable for MIMO applications where compact size and high isolation between elements are required.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Cloaking for Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we discuss the potential of electromagnetic invisibility for antenna arrays. We focus our attention on a popular and widely-used parasitic array, i.e., the Yagi-Vda antenna, and we will show how electromagnetic cloaking enables tailoring its radiation pattern in several unprecedented manners. In particular, we first show how cloaking allows interlacing more Yagi-Vda arrays making possible the design of extremely compact and directive dual-band antennas with opposite pointing directions. Then, we describe the case of a power-dependent Yagi-Vda antenna whose radiation pattern can be tailored by acting on the antenna input power.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Grid Array Antenna for Dual Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microstrip grid array antenna is presented for dual band applications at 2.27 GHz and 17.7 GHz. By designing the location of the feed point, the antenna can operate at the two modes. One mode is corresponding to the normal operating scheme of the grid array antenna in the high frequency band.
