The other mode is similar with the operating scheme of the patch antenna in the low frequency band. The simulated results of the antenna are given and discussed.

articleTitle: Metasurface Particle with Independent Transmission and Reflection Full Phase Coverage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metasurface particle with independent transmission and reflection full phase coverage for circularly polarized waves is introduced. This particle is constituted of two parts, one controlling the power splitting and the reflection phase, and the other one controlling the transmission phase, both leveraging the Pancharatnam-Berry phase principle. Given its unique flexibility, this particle may find various applications in metasurface technology.

articleTitle: Parallel plate VLF Mechanical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Darpa proposed a low-frequency (LF) transmitter operates by mechanically moving bound static charge. However, the bounding charge has a low carrier density and the existing high speed rotating technology limits the operate frequency. This paper introduces a parallel plate design to increase the density of charge density, by using mechanical amplification. The maximum displacement generated by the piezoelectric ceramic can be amplified. And the operation frequency can be extended to up to 100KHZ which covers most of the marine low frequency communication requirement.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna Backed with Miniaturized AMC Reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates a low profile circularly polarized (CP) slot antenna with unidirectional radiation. The antenna includes a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed square slot radiator loaded by two L-shaped strips around two diagonal corners, underneath which is an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) reflector with an air gap in between. The AMC reflector is polarization independent and miniaturized by using lumped capacitors to accommodate sufficient unit cells within restricted electrical dimension. The antenna was analyzed numerically, and the simulated 10-dB impedance bandwidth and 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth are 16.0% and 3.0%, respectively, relative to the center frequency of 2.68 GHz. The overall size of the antenna is 0.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.54λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.08λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with a maximum gain of 6.7 dBic.

articleTitle: Side Launched Dual Circularly Polarized Monopulse Tracking Feed Element for LEO Satellites
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual circularly polarized tracking element for LEO satellites. This tracking element constitutes a part of five element monopulse feed. Side launched configuration employs electrical coupling and provides superior performance in terms of impedance bandwidth and isolation between RHCP and LHCP port. The element provides a return loss better than 18 dB over the bandwidth of 7.8-8.5 GHz and isolation between RHCP and LHCP port is more than 20 dB in the mentioned frequency range. With side launched configuration, the element is easy to fabricate, compact and is used as tracking element of a five element monopulse feed.

articleTitle: TEM H-Plane Horn Antenna Based on TEM Printed Gap Waveguide Configuration
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A TEM H-plane horn antenna based on double-layer textured printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW)configuration is introduced. This configuration of the RGW is providing the horn aperture with almost uniform amplitude distribution because of realizing PMC-like boundary condition around the lateral edges of the H-plane horn aperture. Besides, the TEM-RGW enables the horn to have a double thickness of the radiating aperture and therefore improved impedance bandwidth as compared to the quasi-TEM-RGW configuration with the same bandgap.

articleTitle: Dual-Stub Loaded Microstrip Line-Fed Multi-Slot Printed Antenna for L TE Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual tuning stub loaded microstrip line-fed multi-slot antenna design is presented in this paper for operation in the LTE band. The slot antenna on a grounded dielectric slab is comprised of three wide slot sections: one horizontal slot, one vertical slot, and a circular slot joining both slots. These slots are excited by a microstrip feed line on the other side of the dielectric. This arrangement generates multiple modes that are combined to obtain a large bandwidth for covering most of the LTE band: from 850 MHz to 2600 MHz or beyond. Two similar slots and feed lines are placed on two corners of the ground plane for polarization diversity. The fabricated antenna shows an excellent agreement in terms of scattering parameters.

articleTitle: A Highly Isolated Dual-polarized Crossed Dipole Array Antenna for Multi-mission Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A crossed dipole antenna array with dual linear polarization capability is designed and fabricated. Practical techniques such as utilizing stripline structures for baluns contribute to high isolation between the two polarizations. A better than 50 dB broadside port isolation is achieved over the entire frequency range of 2.7-3 GHz. Additionally, the isolation remains below 40 dB in scanning up to ±45° in the principal planes. A very low cross-polarization level over -60 dB is achieved owing to an image configuration of elements in the array arrangement. These features along with matched copolar beams, simple structure, and ease of fabrication make the proposed antenna array an ideal candidate for multi-mission applications.

articleTitle: A Research for Miniaturized Circular Polarization Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new design of a miniaturized circular polarization antenna element is proposed and presented for antenna array. The antenna-size reduction is achieved by adding four centrosymmetric `P-shaped slots end to the edge of a octagonal patch at the corner. It is very slight also comparing with common patch antenna. In order to get a compact and facile design producing circular polarization electromagnetic wave, two L-shaped feed line with vertical coaxial line ends to a microstrip transmission line runs parallel to the patch is used. The structure of the antenna and feed is studied and simulated with HFSS on computer.

articleTitle: mm Wave Antenna Gain Switching to Mitigate Indoor Blockage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Indoor blockage in a millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless communication link introduces significant signal attenuation. Solving the indoor blockage problem is critical to effectively using the unlicensed 60 GHz band spectrum. This work used various V-band horn antennas to collect signal measurements in an indoor lab environment. As an object blocks the Tx- Rx line of sight (LOS) path, the signal fades deeply. Experimental results showed that switching to a wider beam with lower gain has the potential to partially restore or maintain a communicating link. Effective beam switching and coordinated beam steering can shorten deep fades which is crucial for mm Wave communication systems that are very sensitive to the spatial characteristics of the environment. The experimental results in this paper thus motivate the design of future indoor mm Wave antennas capable of beam switching and facilitate fast beam search.

articleTitle: A CoPrime Array of Patch Antennas for DOA Estimation in Mobile Handheld Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Coprime arrays are used in direction of arrival (DOA) estimation systems due to their increased degrees of freedom (DOF). This work studies the effect of using real antennas within coprime arrays for DOA estimation in small form factor mobile handheld devices at 5.7 GHz. A printed microstrip patch coprime array made of two uniform arrays of 2 and 3 elements with a fundamental interelement spacing of 0.5A was fabricated using 125 mm × 60 mm × 1.5 mm FR-4 substrate. The simulated radiation pattern was incorporated in a DOA estimation algorithm based on Compressive Sensing (CS). Monte Carlo simulations showed increased error due to the introduction of real antenna radiation patterns compared with ideal isotropic antennas.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multiband FarIR Notch Filter Employing Phase Change Material
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a reconfigurable multiband notch filter in the FarIR band of 7 to 17 μm (40-18 THz) utilizing phase change material. The use of the phase change material, VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, allows the cross shaped FSS to effectively change its resonant frequencies. The FSS unit cell is divided into four quadrants containing two different dimensions of cross dipoles. Dividing the unit cell in this method allows for multiple notches in the transmission response.

articleTitle: A Nobel 4G and 5G Antenna Solution for Future Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel integrated antenna solution is proposed for the current 4G and upcoming 5G systems. The proposed antenna configuration can be placed in a small space of the wireless handheld devices. The 5G antenna is a Yagi-Uda antenna array and the 4G antenna is an inverted L-shape antenna. Electromagnetic simulations reveal that both antennas show good performance. The proposed antenna design is expected to be applied to the next generation mobile terminals.

articleTitle: An Innovative Learning-by-Examples Method for Real-Time Electrical Impedance Tomography of the Human Chest
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A non-invasive diagnosis method for real-time human chest monitoring is presented. The developed technique is based on an innovative learning by examples (LBE) methodology to efficiently solve the electrical impedance tomography (EIT) inverse problem. Towards this end, the partial least squares (PLS) feature extraction is profitably combined with an output-space-filling (OSF) adaptive sampling to build a low-size but highly-informative training database, which is successively exploited to make accurate real-time predictions of the lungs conductivity through support vector regression (SVR). A preliminary numerical validation is shown to assess the potentialities of the proposed LBE inversion technique.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Aperture-Coupled Hybrid-Fed Microstrip Patch Antenna for MPAR Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high-performance dual-polarized aperture-coupled hybrid-fed microstrip patch antenna for multifunction application is designed. Input isolation better than 52 dB and cross-polarization level lower than -31 dB are achieved, and simulation results are presented. The embedded element pattern of the designed element is simulated and used for calculating the MPAR-sized cylindrical array antenna radiation pattern, and the results for both co- and cross-polarizations are presented.

articleTitle: A Multiscale Time Integration Method for Coupled Nonlinear Electrical-Thermal Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The simulation of a coupled nonlinear electrical-thermal response in a high-power microwave (HPM) operation represents a highly multiscale problem in time. To address the temporal multiscale issue and account for the mutual coupling between the nonlinear electromagnetic (EM) response and the thermal variation, a multiscale time integration method is developed in this work. By utilizing the quasi-periodicity of the EM responses in consecutive operational cycles, the EM fields and the dissipated power calculated on the small time scale in one cycle can be extrapolated to tens of cycles away, while the thermal response is solved on its large time scale. With such a multiscale time integration, both the electrical and the thermal breakdown phenomena during the HPM operation can be captured.

articleTitle: RF Propagation Measurements Using a Mobile Receiver System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A mobile receiver system was developed under the Air Force Spectrum Transition Plan<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> as part of an effort to model propagation loss accurately over a variety of terrain and environmental conditions. In this paper, we describe the mobile receiver system and discuss how it was used to measure received power spectra and transmit antenna radiation patterns from an Air Force Satellite Control Network (AFSCN) tracking station. The transmitter and receiver setup, along with the measurement methodology are discussed in further detail.

articleTitle: Spectral and Spatial Uplink Interference Filtering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two affordable interference protection techniques for uplink multiple beam antennas are described. Adaptive excision spectrally filters high level uplink interference to maintain system linearity. Adaptive spatial filtering applies amplitude monopulse techniques to excision data to locate interference and commands antenna pattern nulls aligned with interference using known antenna data.

articleTitle: The Scattering by Two Inverted Staggered PEC Half-Planes Loaded by a Dielectric Layer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by two inverted perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) half-planes loaded by a dielectric layer is studied by using the Wiener-Hopf technique in the spectral domain. The procedure to obtain the solution is based on the reduction of the factorization problem to Fredholm integral equations of second kind. The structure is of interest in antenna technologies, electromagnetic compatibility and electromagnetic shielding. The study of structural singularities allows also the estimation of surface waves and leaky waves for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Back-To-Back Magnetic Dipole Antennas with Pattern Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A pattern reconfigurable antenna capable of steering in the wide angle is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of back-to-back magnetic dipole (MD)antennas. Each antenna can be a driven element or a parasitic structure by switching the radiation mode. The 3-dB beam under varying four radiation modes can cover ± 72° in elevation angle. The spacing between two antennas is 0.23 wavelength (λo)to utilize as an array antenna, and the size of the antenna is 0.38λo X 0.38λo.

articleTitle: Backscatter model for low-frequency magnetoquasistatic fields in indoor environments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We provide a mathematical model to predict signal backscatter loss for low-frequency magnetoquasistatic fields in indoor environments. Experimental and deterministic theoretical data are shown to model magnetic field path loss and take into account induced eddy-currents from large nearby walls in the indoor environments.

articleTitle: Waveguide-fed Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna using an Antipodal Finline Transition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new waveguide-fed Antipodal Vi-valdi Antenna (AVA) for mm-wave imaging applications is presented. A waveguide-to-broadside coupled Antipodal finline transition is designed to couple the dominant mode of a WR-12 waveguide into the AVA. The transition provides a wideband and low insertion loss in the entire E - band. A dielectric lens is added in front of the AVA to increase the directivity in the endfire direction of the antenna. The performance of the designed antenna is evaluated in the E - band in terms of its return loss, gain, and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Topologically-Protected One-Way Leaky Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate the application of the concept of photonic topological insulators (PTIs)in radiating and scattering structures. The general properties of topologically-protected unidirectional leaky modes are analyzed for a stratified structure composed of a magnetically-biased plasma (a continuum model of topological materials)covered by topologically-trivial materials. We discuss how the propagation and radiation properties of these modes can be controlled by introducing a suitably designed coating layer on the biased plasma, resulting in highly-directive one-way leaky-wave radiation. The topological robustness of these leaky surface waves allows overcoming large defects, corners, and bends along the propagation path without any back-scattering and backward radiation. Our findings may be useful for future leaky-wave (nano)antenna generations and stealth technology based on topological concepts.

articleTitle: Effects of Electromagnetic Modeling Methods on Coverage Prediction of Anti-Jam GPS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Full-wave electromagnetic software may be employed to accurately simulate the reception pattern of antenna elements for use in a controlled reception pattern antenna (CRPA). The implementation of an in-situ anti-jam CRPA model utilizing full-wave element patterns requires more computation time than employing free space patterns, but includes coupling between elements and material effects in the environment. The added work associated with the in-situ model is justified by confirmation of the null-steering results using a non-radiating network in the full wave environment, and comparisons are made between an in-situ CRPA and a simple free space model that does not include coupling effects and dielectric losses.

articleTitle: A Very Simple Dual-band Dual-sense Circularly Polarized Square Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-wideband dual-sense circularly polarized (CP) square slot antenna is presented in this paper. The righth- and circular polarization (RHCP) in +z direction for the lower frequency is mainly realized by an inverted L-shaped strip (ILSS). And the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) in +z direction for the upper frequency is mainly achieved by an offset feed structure (OFS). The measured 10-dB return loss bandwidth is 114.7% (1.75-6.46 GHz). Its measured 3-dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidths in the broadside direction are 60.2 % (1.8-3.35 GHz) in the lower band and 32.7% (4.6-6.41 GHz) in the upper band, which can fully cover all the WLAN and Wi-Fi bands.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Ultra- Wideband Ridged Horn Antenna Based on Traveling Wave Current Model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to explain the working mechanism of the UWB ridged horn antenna, the equivalent traveling current model of the ridged horn antenna is established based on the surface current data obtained by simulating in CST Microwave Studio sottware<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, Based on the model, a ridged horn antenna with metal grids is analyzed, and the reason why the antenna has stable directional radiation characteristics under ultra wideband is explained. The patterns calculated by the equivalent model are in good agreement with those simulated in CST, which proves the correctness of the proposed model. The simulation results show that the radiation of the ridged horn antenna is mainly generated by the current on the ridges.

articleTitle: A Rigorous Macromodeling Approach to Efficiently Simulate Large Arrays of Complex Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel macromodeling approach that allows efficient simulation of large arrays of complex scatterers. In the proposed method, each array element is modeled by a macromodel that is made up of an equivalent electric current density introduced on a fictitious surface surrounding the element and a set of linear discrete operators. Compared to the standard surface integral equation formulations, the proposed method results in fewer unknowns and in a better conditioned linear system that leads to faster computations and lower memory consumption.

articleTitle: Manipulating Optical Chirality in the Near-Field of Plasmonic Metamaterials with Superchiral Light
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we show that the optical chirality of plasmonic chiral metamaterials can be manipulated by superchiral light. In particular, the handedness selective enhancement and switching effect of optical chirality, along with the delocalization of the corresponding chiral fields, are observed in the near-field regime of a gammadion nanostructure. Our results indicate that the interaction between superchiral light and planar chiral nanostructures can further improve accessibility for plasmonics based enantiomeric sensing and potentially enable chiroptical imaging systems that can be coherently controlled.

articleTitle: Resonance Sensitivity and Quality Factor of Implantable Loop Antenna Loaded with Interdigital Capacitor in the Cerebral Spinal Fluid
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of an implantable loop antenna loaded with an interdigital capacitor operating at 400 MHz is presented. The sensitivity of the resonance change due to the change of the dielectric constant of the implantation tissue is studied and assessed via numerical simulations. The perturbation of the electric field affects the capacitance and thereby the input impedance of the antenna. In this manner, the antenna can be used to sense the dielectric constant changes of the implantation tissue. Despite the adverse effect of the cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) on the quality factor (Q) of the implantable antenna, a resonance shift of 25.2 MHz is obtained when the dielectric constant is increased by 14% from the nominal values.

articleTitle: A Cavity-Integrated Self-Polarizing Method for Circularly Polarized Fabry-Perot Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a self-polarizing approach to realize circularly polarized (CP) Fabry-Perot antenna (FPA) using linearly polarized feed. The antenna configuration is simple, including a conventional single-cavity, dielectric-superstrate FPA and a specially designed all-dielectric structure integrated in the FPA cavity. This is a new design method of obtaining CP radiation for this class of antenna. The achieved wide common impedance and axial ratio bandwidth outperforms state-of-the-art designs.

articleTitle: Low Loss and High Electrical Insulation Near Field Antenna Coupler
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the simulation and measurement of a near field antenna coupler with low coupling loss and high galvanic insulation (safety insulation to electrical hazard) for metallic panelboard installations. The antenna coupler is formed by three parts: a monopole antenna, a coupling structure and an insulator. Transmission losses at 2.45 GHz are measured at 1.4 dB. When the coupling structure is taken off, the monopole is well matched and presents a gain of 1.21 dBi.

articleTitle: Use of a Digital Non-Foster Radio Architecture for Conventional Tuning of Electrically-Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prior investigations of digital non-Foster antenna tuning have pointed out the similarity between these systems and SDR (software-defined radio) systems, where the SDR receiver ADC (analog-to-digital converter) and SDR DAC (digital-to-analog converter) can serve corresponding digital non-Foster circuit roles. In previous investigations, the particular focus has been on using digital non-Foster antenna impedance matching methods to overcome Wheeler-Chu limits of electrically-small antennas. However, the digital non-Foster radio architecture can also provide digital implementation of conventional impedance matching of electrically-small antennas. The advantage is that the impedance matching is accomplished in software without the need for external matching circuitry, allowing digital tuning of the antenna to desired frequency bands. Although such conventional impedance matching would not provide the bandwidth enhancement of non-Foster matching, it may be useful in providing some degree of preselection filtering for narrowband applications. Simulation results illustrate the proposed digital impedance-matching approach, and are compared to a conventional passively-matched electrically -small antenna at 75 MHz.

articleTitle: Fast FDTD Method for Large-Scale Layout Extraction and Analysis of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a fast FDTD solver is developed to perform the layout extraction and analysis of integrated circuits. In this solver, the time step is not restricted by the small space step encountered in the IC layout. Instead, it can be chosen to be arbitrarily large, thus making the full-wave FDTD simulation from DC to high frequencies become feasible. Meanwhile, the computational cost at each time step is also minimized via analytical identifications of the column space that determines the field solution. Numerical experiments have validated its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Formulation of Surface-Volume-Surface-EFIE for Solution of 2D Scattering Problems on Composite Dielectric Objects under TM Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work generalizes the Surface-Volume-Surface Electric Field Integral Equation (SVS- EFIE) for the solution of the 2D scattering problems on the composite penetrable non-magnetic objects under TM polarization. The SVS-EFIE formulation for homogeneous scatterers features a single unknown surface current density on the boundary. In order to generalize SVS- EFIE to the case of composite scatterers, two independent electric surface current densities must be introduced on the joint boundaries between different dielectric materials. On each of the remaining boundaries between the scatterer and the background medium only a single unknown surface current density is introduced similarly with the original SVS- EFIE. To validate the new formulation its solution is compared against solution of the traditional Volume-EFIE (V-EFIE).

articleTitle: A Novel Passive RFID Temperature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel passive RFID temperature sensor is proposed in this paper. The sensor utilizes an integrated T -match network (TMN) for matching the antenna to the RFID IC. Furthermore., the sensor detects changes in temperature by shifting its operating frequency. The frequency shifts are accomplished by a 3D printed liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) array that can reversibly actuate depending on the temperature to move the antenna and change its distance from the ground plane.

articleTitle: Ultra-wide Band (10 MHz-26 GHz) Permeability Measurements Systems for Magnetic Films
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new rf magnetic measurement system is proposed to detect complex permeability of magnetic films, of which the measurable frequency range has been demonstrated but not limited to lOMHz-26GHz. The system is based on a simple microwave generator and lock-in detection set up. The signal to noise ratio is enhanced by the lock-in detection technique. Measurements of ferromagnetic resonance and complex permeability on a thick FeGaB film (30nm) and an ultra-thin NiFe (2nm) were presented to demonstrated the wider frequency capability and higher signal to noise ratio as compared with the best available permeameter.

articleTitle: Analysis of Waves Propagation on Magnetized Graphenes Using Surface Boundary Condition FDTD
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is presented to study the magnetically biased graphene. With the introduction of the surface resistivity, the biased graphene can be taken as a two-dimensional anisotropic surface with zero thickness, which avoids the tiny spatial cell in FDTD simulation. Because of gyrotropy of the material, we calculate the average electric field over the sheet and reconstruct the electric fields after every time-marching step. The derived difference equations result in easy programming. Numerical results are presented to show the accuracy of our approach.

articleTitle: A Structured Deterministic Sampling Strategy for Array Diagnosis from Far-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The aim of this conference paper is to introduced a novel structured deterministic sampling strategy for diagnosis of defective array elements from far-field measurements. Different from the existing one called structured random sampling strategy, the proposed method is designed according to a polynomial-based approach by deterministic selection of sampling locations among angles by Discrete Fourier Transformation. The merits of our strategy is that sampling positions are fixed and easy to construct while the measurement matrix also satisfy Restricted Isometry Property. Several numerical simulations are carried out and the results show that a higher successful rate of diagnosis is achieved by utilizing our method.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement of MIMO Antennas Using Bilateral CEBG Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents mutual coupling reduction between, typical 5.8 GHz microstrip, antenna elements in both longitudinal and lateral directions. A bilateral complementary electromagnetic band gab structure, engraved in the ground, is used for such purpose. Four, side by side with λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/2 separation, antennas were tested for lateral isolation before and after applying CEBG. 18 dB isolation, enhancement was achieved. For longitudinal isolation two opponent elements with O.06λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> separation were tested and 16dB enhancement was achieved.

articleTitle: Design of a Bifocal Dual Reflectarray System with Parabolic Main Surface for a Multifed Space Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This communication presents the design of a dual bifocal reflectarray (RA)system consisting of a parabolic main RA and a flat RA sub reflector. The concepts of path length shift and virtual normal are introduced to describe the synthesis procedure. An application example is presented for being used as multifed onboard antenna in satellite communications.

articleTitle: Pruned NUFFT-3 for far-field calculations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We deal with an approach based on Non-Uniform FFTs (NUFFTs) of type-3 and on a pruned FFT to efficiently computing the far-field radiated/scattered by volumetric sources/objects. The approach consists of three steps: 1) representation of “non-uniformly sampled” Fourier exponentials by a finite number of “uniformly sampled” ones, with such number controlling the accuracy; 2) “pruned” FFT; 3) interpolation, again with controlled accuracy, of the “uniformly sampled” exponentials onto the “non-uniformly sampled” ones corresponding to the relevant observation directions. The computational performance of the approach is sketched.

articleTitle: Studies on Numerical Evaluation of Sommerfeld Integrals for Multilayer Topologies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Sommerfeld integrals (SI) for a multilayer media are encountered in full-wave analysis of high-speed microstrip interconnects or patch antennas that are radiating on a PEC-backed dielectric substrate covered by a superstrate. The weighted average and asymptotic methods for calculating the SI are two different techniques whose comparative numerical assessment is presented in this investigation.

articleTitle: 6–15 GHz Wide Scanning Connected Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work we report on the design, manufacturing and testing of a dual-polarized array of connected slots radiating in the presence of an artificial dielectric superstrate. The prototype array consists of 512 elements, i.e. 16×16 connected slots for each of the two polarizations. The antenna array is realized with a single multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB) and thus is low-cost compared to the typical configuration based on multiple vertically arranged PCBs. The performance is investigated in terms of simulated and measured matching characteristics and radiation patterns. The proposed structure achieves active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) lower than 3.1 over about an octave bandwidth (6 to 15 GHz), within a wide scan range (±60° in the H-plane and ±80° in the E-plane).

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Characterization of Terahertz Photoconductive Antennas Using Time-Domain Spectroscopy System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the radiation pattern characterization of terahertz photoconductive antennas using a new technique. The proposed technique is implemented using a modified terahertz time domain spectroscopy by applying a full mapping of the THz beam. The proposed method was also compared with analytical methods and numerical solvers. The comparison of the measured results with that of the simulations shows a half-power beam width error of 1.5° and an optical path difference error of 8%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time terahertz time domain spectroscopy system is used to characterize the radiation pattern of terahertz photoconductive antennas.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Volume Scattering Approach Based on Shooting-and-Bouncing-Rays (SBR)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Traditionally, ray tracing is a surface-based approach, searching for ray-surface intersections in order to determine the relevant propagation paths. This scheme is extended by a stochastic volume scattering approach, which, e.g., enables modeling of rain clouds in meteorological propagation simulations and foliage scattering for scenarios in outdoor environments. The proposed approach can easily be combined with standard surface scattering models, such as Geometrical Optics (GO) and Physical Optics (PO), and consequently enables the electromagnetic modeling of more complex as well as more realistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Analyses of SAR Images from Moving Ships over a Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a procedure for the simulation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images from a moving ship over a random sea surface is studied. In the simulation, the time-varying characteristic of the sea surface and the generated wake by the ship is taken into consideration, as well as the motion of the ship. Then SAR echoes under different parameters are simulated according to the electromagnetic (EM) scattering model, based on which SAR images is able to be obtained. From the simulated results, one can see the similar features caused by ship's motion in real SAR images. That is to say the simulated SAR images are able to reveal the motion features of the ship on account of considering the dynamic change of the composite scene, and the effectiveness of the simulation approach is verified as well.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Compact Dual CP Eight Band Planar Log Periodic Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting through Ambient Sources
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For the first time, the design of a compact eight band frequency independent dual circularly polarized planar log periodic antenna, is presented here. The designed antenna covers eight bands within the frequency range from 650 MHz to 3500 MHz simultaneously for RF energy harvesting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first ever compact eight band designed antenna covering various wireless standards (Digital TV band, Cellular bands, Wi-Fi bands and WiMAX band) with highest gain of 7.7 dBi at 3.5 GHz and good axial ratio in almost all the bands.

articleTitle: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide Tapered Slot Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) tapered slot antenna used for millimeter-wave applications is proposed in this paper. In order to get the large bandwidth and simple structure, the novel antenna is composed of the microstrip-to-SIW feeding transition and the elliptical-edge tapered slot radiators. Simple structure, small size, high performances and convenient connection with RF-end channel are the typical characteristics of this design. It can be fed by 50Ω microstrip line located from bottom side of the antenna, and got the end-fire radiation performance at the top side. The simulated results of the antenna indicate that the frequency band with VSWR<;2 is from 32.8GHz to 36.7GHz, and the 3-dB beam widths in E-plane and H-plane of element are larger than 80° at 35GHz. The performances confirm that the proposed simple SIW tapered slot antenna is suitable for the millimeter-wave electronic systems with the requirements of small and low-profile antenna.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration and System Evaluation of OAM-like Spatial Diveristy from Two Linear Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing at radio has been proven as one of the multiple-in-multiple-out (MIMO) solution without further signal processing. In this paper, we show that at least 3-element uniform circular array (UCA) can be used to transmit/receive beams carrying OAM. Even though the 2-element phased array cannot be used to generate beams carrying OAM, it can be used to transmit/receive two beams carrying different phase patterns. In our digital communication test, using the proposed two linear antenna arrays we can transmit different digital data without further signal processing just like the OAM multiplexing does.

articleTitle: Dual-band Mushroom Antenna with Two Concentric Circles Composite Vias
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dual-band and low-profile mushroom antenna with vertically-polarized and omnidirectional radiation in the horizontal direction is proposed. The mushroom antenna has multiple vias forming coaxial double ring structure at the center between a ground plane and a metallic patch. The double ring structure of vias has two different parallel resonant frequencies. It is confirmed from the numerical simulation results that the proposed antenna shows omnidirectional radiation pattern at dual-band.

articleTitle: Planar SIW Horn Antenna with Improved Matching at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a planar substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) horn antenna at 94 GHz which is fed through a coplanar waveguide (CPW) structure using an inset feed technique. The dielectric slabs printed on the same substrate are introduced as a matching network between the air and the proposed structure. The overall size of the antenna is 40 × 20 × 0.59 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, The radiation efficiency of the simulated antenna is 77.25% having a gain up to 7.62 dBi at the desired frequency band.

articleTitle: Time Reflection and Refraction in Temporal Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In electromagnetism, dualities exist between time and space since they both contribute to the propagation of electromagnetic waves to some extent. Such dualities provide us with an alternative tool to manipulate the electromagnetic waves via temporal discontinuities in addition to spatially symmetry - breaking structures. In this work, we investigate the reflection and refraction of time-periodic structures, which can be regarded as a temporal analogy to the distributed Bragg reflector. The Fresnel-like coefficients are derived by imposing appropriate boundary conditions. It is suggested that such temporal modulated structures may pave the way for complementary manipulation of electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Source Effect on Near-Field Multi-Beam-Splitting in Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC)antenna systems can be designed to produce beam-splitting in the near-field as a means of increasing system gain. This paper will describe performance of FPC system when two unidirectional antenna designs are evaluated with frequency selective surface (FSS)design with a cross (i.e. FSS-Cross) to create quad beam-splitting. The cavity-backed slot design has gain that is ~1 dB higher than the patch design.

articleTitle: Flexible Antenna on High Permeability Substrate for Electromagnetic Head Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The performance assessment and analysis of a wearable microstrip antenna based on high permeability material substrate in head imaging system is presented. The antenna is designed on polymer RTV6166-iron oxide substrate with relative permittivity and relative permeability of 3 and 5, respectively. The antenna consists of an inset-fed microstrip rectangular patch with dimensions of 44×72 mm, connected to 50 Ω feed. To evaluate the effect of the permeability in electromagnetic head imagining, the antenna is benchmarked against another similarly geometrized polymer RTV6166 based with unity permeability. Numerical simulations using CST Microwave Studio for both antennas are performed in free space and on a 3D human head model. The simulations results show that the antenna with high permeability exhibits better reflection coefficient (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) and electromagnetic penetration inside the human head tissues which will result in improved detection and image resolution.

articleTitle: Investigation of Checkerboard Metasufaces on Flexible Curvilinear Structure for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Checkerboard metasurface is implemented on flexible curvilinear structure to investigate its performance for reducing radar cross section (RCS) of such structures. The flexible checkerboard metasurface is shaped to two different radii of cylindrical curvature for the investigation. Metasurface is evaluated under normal incidence for both polarizations (i.e. HH and VV polarizations). Simulation results are also compared with measurements of a fabricated prototype and good agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: Efficacy of Magnetic and Capacitive Hyperthermia on Hepatocellular Carcinoma
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Magnetoquasistatic (MQS) and electroquasistatic (EQS) formulations are applied to model magnetic and capacitive hyperthermia, respectively, on treating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Finite element method is used to compute the field distribution in the treated area, and a bio-heat equation is solved to compute the temperature distribution therein. The efficacy of magnetic and capacitive hyperthermia in treating HCC is analyzed and compared.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Direct Transition from IC-package to waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: New applications like 5G and car radar require higher operating frequencies. For higher frequencies the size of a typical packaged IC is of the same order of magnitude of one or more waveguide cross-sections, giving the opportunity to use the waveguide as an IC to waveguide interconnect. The excitation of an in-package waveguide needs to be modeled to design the interconnect. This paper shows that a simplified Method Of Moments (MOM) model is suitable for modeling a dipole excitation. Results for the MOM model shows good comparison with CST and an analytical model. Furthermore, the MOM model is converted into a circuit model for a direct integration with IC design tools.

articleTitle: Scattering Control and Camouflage Through Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the last years, there has been a strong interest in the design of invisibility devices able to reduce significantly the scattering of an object in a desired frequencies range. In particular, mantle cloaking has proven that electromagnetic invisibility can be achieved using patterned surfaces, also known as metasurfaces. The aim of this contribution is to show that metasurfaces can be used also for camouflaging purposes, i.e., for designing devices able to make an object appearing as it were either larger or thinner or composed by a different material. As an example, we present the analytical formulation and the numerical results of a cylindrical object made of an electric conductor whose scattering is made equal to the one of a dielectric cylinder. Finally, the bandwidth limitations of this technique, as well as a potential solution to improve the frequency response of the camouflaging devices, are discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of Radiation Pattern in the Performance of Bio-Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The bio-radar system can measure vital signals accurately, such as the respiratory signal, by using the Doppler effect principle that relates the received signal properties with the distance change between the radar antennas and the person's chest-wall. In this paper, the antenna radiation pattern influence on the quality of the received signal is analysed. Moreover, we show that the antenna with a narrow beam leads to a better signal to noise ratio.

articleTitle: Tip Diffraction of Wide- Angle Cones
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The scattering by semi-infinite circular cones has an exact spherical harmonics solution, but so far there was no explicit expression for the tip diffraction coefficient, except for Felsen's seminal solution for a narrow-angle cone. In the present work we derive the diffraction coefficient for a wide-angle cone with cone-angle approaching π/2, a problem which is particularly relevant for terrain and urban propagation. The result provides a cogent physical interpretation for the scattered field, and can also be applied for diffraction of complex-source beam by a wide-angle cone.

articleTitle: Impact of Data Selection on the Accuracy of Atmospheric Refractivity Evaporative Duct Inversions Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One alternate approach to directly measuring or forward modeling atmospheric conditions that lead to anomalous propagation is to use radar measurements to inversely determine the conditions. This preliminary study examines the impact of varying the quantity of propagation loss data as well as 3 different data location groupings on the accuracy of inversion solutions. The fraction of successful trials increases as the amount of data increases up to ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>grid cells with the largest improvement in accuracy for both duct height and the M -profile occurring between 10°and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> grid cells. Non-unique solutions are problematic with one or numerous (≥10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>) grid cells.

articleTitle: Analysis of Scattering on Arctic Sea Ice in C-Band with Layered Medium Formulation of Surface Volume Surface Electric Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Full-wave solution of 4.9GHz plane wave scattering on 17cm by 17cm area of Arctic sea ice rough surface situated atop air-sea-water half-space is demonstrated. The solution is performed via Method of Moment (MoM) discretization of the Surface-Volume-Surface Integral Equation (SVS-EFIE). To account for the presence of air-sea half-space recently proposed formulation of the SVS-EFIE including multilayered media Green's function is used. The Green's function of the air-sea half-space is numerically computed using the Discrete Complex Image Method (DCIM). Numerically obtained distribution of the electric field throughout the model of the ice rough surface is compared against independent reference solution of a commercial multilayered media MoM solver.

articleTitle: Complex Sources, Gaussian Beams, and Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We exploit complex transformation optics (CTO), which generalizes conventional transformation optics (TO) from real-value to complex-valued coordinate transformations, to produce Gaussian-like beams from point sources. In the paraxial region, a Gaussian beam can be recognized as the field produced by a complex-source-point (CSP) with imaginary displacement along the axial beam direction. A CSP is simply a hypothetical source that is located at a complex-valued coordinate point. CTO stipulates that any coordinate transformation that would displace the (real-valued) spatial coordinates of a point source to (equivalent) complex-valued spatial coordinates can be mimicked by properly chosen metamaterial parameters. The proposed methodology yields a direct mapping of electromagnetic structure (viz. engineered material constitutive parameters) to electromagnetic function (field synthesis). This mapping is predictive and parametric.

articleTitle: Study of an Accurate Phase-Based Localization Method for Semi-Passive RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a simulation model for a novel method of indoor localization that is based on the phase difference between elements in an antenna array. The localization system is used to identify the position of a semi-passive radio frequency identification (RFID) tag. For proof of concept, a set of experiments for phase measurements are designed using a commercially available transceiver. Results demonstrate that the proposed simulation model comparatively provides an accurate estimation as well as assessment tool of phase measurements for indoor localization application.

articleTitle: Current Rejection Characteristics of Choke Structure Composed of Composite Right/Left-Handed Coaxial Line
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current rejection characteristics of the choke structure composed of composite right/left-handed coaxial line (CRLH CL) is simulated and compared with that of the quarter-wavelength choke structure. Dispersion relations of the CRLH CL are also simulated and compared with the current rejection characteristics.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Security based on Time Reversal Technique for Urban Radio Channels
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents experimental characterization of feasibility of physical layer security based on time reversal technique for radio channels. The investigation is for outdoor urban microcellular radio channels for both scenarios of fixed and mobile receivers. The investigation is at frequency range of 2.4 GHz and bandwidth of measurement system is 100 MHz. A metric based on difference between strongest and 2nd strongest peak on power delay profile is proposed and presented as performance indicator.

articleTitle: A Domain Decomposition Method Based on Simplified Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel non-overlapping and non-conforming domain decomposition method (DDM) based on simplified volume-surface integral equation (S-VSIE) is proposed for the electromagnetic analysis of composite very thin dielectric/complex finite array objects. In this scheme, such composite objects are decomposed into multiple composite subdomains. To model efficiently subdomains involving very thin dielectric, the VSIE with simplified prism vector (SPV) basis functions, called as S-VSIE, is applied. Further, a discontinuous Galerkin volume integral equation method based on the SPV basis functions (DG-S-VIE) is proposed for conformal as well as non-conformal volume discretizations. Moreover, a additive non-overlapping DD preconditioner is designed for the fast iterative solution.

articleTitle: Comparison of roof top- and ground - to- ground urban propagation of wideband UHF signals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report the results of both rooftop-to-ground and ground-to-ground channel sounding in the small urban area of Concord, NH with a center frequency of 437 MHz. The goal of this research is to better understand and document the differences in channel characteristics as applicable to both military and first-responder scenarios, using omni-directional antennae at low elevations deep in urban terrain where access by vehicles is not always possible. Path losses for ground-to-ground links were approximately 18 dB larger than roof-to-ground links for equivalent distances, and path loss exponents were significantly different (3.86 and 2.85 respectively). Significant reflectors were identified both inside(<; 8μS delay time) and outside (up to 30μ S delay time) of the city, impacting time dispersion of roof-to-ground and ground-to-ground channels alike, despite the fact that these distant reflectors were not within line-of-sight of either transmitter or receiver. The RMS delay spread of ground-to-ground channels generally increased with distance for ground-to-ground links, while rooftop-to-ground link delay spreads appeared to be independent of separation distance.

articleTitle: Isolation Improvement of Cylindrical Millimeter-Wave Repeaters Using a Reactive Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design and implementation of reactive impedance surfaces (RIS`s) for cylindrical millimeter wave (mmW) repeaters are discussed in this paper. A specific consideration is for the enhancement of transmit-to-receive isolation between wideband dual-polarized antennas. Using Floquet analysis, a hexagonal mushroom unit cell is designed to have a capacitive reactance in 16-40GHz range for the TM mode, and an array of unit cells (RIS) is fabricated and mounted on a metallic cylinder. The RIS is seen to improve isolation by an average of 15 dB across a wide bandwidth in KiKa-bands.

articleTitle: A Novel NFC Antenna for Metal Cover Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized dual-loop near field communication antenna of size 15 mm×25 mm is proposed for metal cover smartphone applications. By embedded it with a small rectangular slot of size 8 mm×16 mm loaded metal cover, the direction of the eddy current induced on metal cover will be the same with the current flow the on the dual loop NFC antenna coil. It's worth noting that the proposed NFC antenna design was certified by the Europay, Mastercard and Visa (EMV) test.

articleTitle: Exploiting Inverse Scattering Methodologies to Design Artificial Materials
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The usual aim of an inverse scattering problem is to retrieve the location, the shape and the electromagnetic parameters of the scatterer by processing measurements of the scattered field. Interestingly, the inverse scattering problem can be turned into a synthesis problem, provided the starting data is no longer a collection of measurements but rather some field specifications arising from design constraints. In this contribution, some methodologies already available in the inverse scattering community for diagnosis applications are extended and modified for design purposes. In this respect, the synthesis of artificial materials is dealt.

articleTitle: Cavity-backed Slot Array for Multilayer PCB Implementation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Communications systems at millimeter-wavelength (mm Wave) frequencies are expected to become ubiquitous, with their antennas commonly integrated within printed circuit boards (PCBs.) This paper proposes a compact low-cost mmWave PCB antenna element that is amenable to multilayer PCB designs and scalable to large arrays. The V-band (60GHz) cavity-backed slot array design excites the TE330 mode within a PCB cavity formed from walls made of microvias. The cavity excites nine radiating slot elements to form a high-gain broadside beam, and is single slot-fed from a substrate-integrated waveguide. A summary of the performance and a breakdown of the loss mechanisms are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Matching Layers for Increasing the Electrical Field Penetration inside Human Tissue
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The interaction of electromagnetic fields with human tissues is of great interest for a wide range of applications spanning from medical treatments to sport activity tracking. In several cases the penetration of the electric field inside body is a key factor for the successful design of wearable devices. The multilayered structure of the tissue and the complex permittivity of its components pose numerous challenges to the propagation of the electric field which will be addressed in this work with the aim of providing guidelines for the design of a matching layer able to enhance the field penetration.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Dipole Probe Receiving Pattern Based on the Lorentz Reciprocity Theorem
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The anisotropic receiving pattern of a dipole probe results in near-field measurement error. The error can be compensated if the receiving pattern is known. Although the receiving pattern has the same shape as the radiation pattern, the values of radiated fields in transmission mode are different from the values of induced voltage in reception mode. Hence, the receiving pattern can not be directly calculated from the radiation pattern. This paper derives the relationship between the radiated field and the induced voltage based on the Lorentz reciprocity theorem, and the induced voltage is then calculated from the radiated field using the derived relationship. The proposed method allows the fast calculation of the receiving pattern, which is useful for compensating the near field measurement error due to the probe's anisotropy. Numerical results are presented to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Synthesis of non-broadside linear array with sparse Bayesian learning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a method based on the sparse Bayesian learning is applied to design the excitation coefficient and location of each element for the non-broadside linear array for the given desired radiation pattern. The fast marginal likelihood algorithm is considered to improve the efficiency, and the hyperparameter is estimated pairwise for the complex excitation coefficients.

articleTitle: Nonlocal Metasurfaces Performing Analog Mathematical Operations
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurfaces enable unusual manipulation of the impinging electromagnetic wavefront over a subwavelength thickness. One interesting opportunity that has been recently explored consists in the possibility of performing mathematical operations in the analog domain, with clear advantages in terms of speed and power consumption compared to digital approaches, and a footprint much smaller than classical analog computing approaches based on Fourier optics. In this context, multilayer structures and photonic crystals have been proposed in recent years, however, they are limited to narrow angular spectra or require exceptional material parameters, hence they are difficult to achieve in practice. Here, we propose a novel class of metasurfaces with a strong nonlocal response that can be engineered to realize various types of mathematical operations, including 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order derivatives, for electromagnetic signals with arbitrary angular spectrum, and also with largely relaxed fabrication requirements. We develop a rigorous theory for these nonlocal metasurfaces and propose practical designs at microwave frequencies. Our results open a path towards performing fast, efficient and low-energy analog signal processing at the subwavelength scale, with applications for edge detection and low-power computing.

articleTitle: Multi-Target FOCO for Head&Neck Hyperthermia Treatment Planning: A Feasibility Study
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Clinical studies have shown the benefit of hyperthermia as a strong adjuvant to conventional cancer treatments but a tight control of the administered heating still represents an open challenge. Planning the hyperthermia treatment is the way to deliver a target conformal specific absorption rate (SAR) deposition over the target area while keeping the SAR bounded in normal tissue. This task is even more challenging in case of large and irregularly shaped target volumes. Motivated by this need, the so-called multi-target focusing via constrained power optimization was developed. In the current study, we investigated the effective gain in terms of heating profile of the proposed approach using simulations of 3D clinical patient specific models. Results indicate an average median temperature gain of 0.8°C with respect to standard FOCO.

articleTitle: Contrast-enhanced Thermoacoustic Imaging for Breast Tumor Detection with Sparse Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work reports detection of breast tumors using sparse measurements based on contrast-enhanced thermoacoustic imaging. Results show that only nine acoustic sensors are capable of reconstructing an thermoacoustic image with the breast tumor clearly distinguishable. This technique can help to advance time-efficient detection and diagnosis of breast cancers.

articleTitle: Accuracy of Surface Current Approximation Using Legendre Polynomials for 2-D TM Scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The accuracy of approximation of surface currents at electrically large flat 2-D scatterers is investigated, in TM monostatic mode. Legendre polynomials, of order up to 250, are used as entire domain basis functions. Method of moments is used for numerical analysis with the involved integrals calculated to machine precision. Presented results show that 50 wavelength scatterer can be analyzed as a single (mesh) element.

articleTitle: Results of W/ V band propagation studies in Albuquerque, NM, over two years
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 71-76 GHz and 81-86 GHz are two regions in the electromagnetic spectrum of great interest because are allocated for communication generally and are currently sparsely used. These allocations are attractive to system designers because of the available bandwidth for future applications. The W/V-band Terrestrial Link Experiment (WTLE) was first established in Albuquerque, NM, in 2015 to investigate atmospheric propagation in this band. Two years of data collection now enables the comparison of W/ V band propagation across with yearly variation in seasons. This paper presents a statistical analysis of the WTLE measurements during this time.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Position of Antenna on a Scaled Vehicle by Using Characteristic Modes Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the position of the antenna on metallic vehicle is studied by using the theory of characteristic modes. In order to reach higher gain at the horizontal plane, the position of a monopole on the metallic vehicle is optimized according to the characteristic currents on the surface of the vehicle. Scaling size (40:1) metallic vehicle and the monopole antenna is designed and fabricated. Simulating frequency is around 1200 MHz. Simulated results of the model are presented to verify the design concept.

articleTitle: Design of a Multiband LTE MIMO Antenna System Integrated in its Real Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a multiband MIMO antenna system with four accesses, with very good performance despite the complex environment that surrounds it. This environment consists of a thick plastic radome protecting the antenna and an aluminum metallic radiator placed behind it, which is usually not recommended to not disturb the operation of any antenna. The antenna has been studied in its environment and it presents in simulation very good levels of impedance matching, isolation and efficiency. This last one almost exceeds 80 % on three LTE bands: [0.7-0.9], [1.71-1.88] and [2.5-2.69] GHz. This system was then realized and measured in free space. The comparison of simulated and measured results validates the good functioning of the MIMO system.

articleTitle: Multiband Split-Monopole Antenna Design Rules
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design rules for a multiband, split-monopole antenna are presented. The antenna consists of two split (U-shaped) monopole antennas fed by a microstrip line that produce three unique resonances of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> = 2.015 GHz, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 4.189 GHz, and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> = 5.554 GHz. The design procedure outlines the overall design of the antenna and how to tune f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> independently without changing the other resonances. Both simulated and measured results for multiple tuning designs are presented.

articleTitle: A Capacity-based Sensing Matrix Design Method for Block Compressive Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In many compressive imaging applications, it can be difficult to design sensing matrices with suitable reconstruction capabilities. In this paper, we presents a novel method, based upon capacity maximization, for designing sensing matrices with enhanced block-sparse signal reconstruction capabilities. Numerical results, which demonstrate the design method's capabilities in a practical imaging application, are presented.

articleTitle: Far-Field Equivalence Through Equivalent Current Distributions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accurate antenna manifolds are desired for many signal processing algorithms. In situ antenna measurements are the most accurate way to obtain antenna manifolds on the platform of interest, but are often impractical or impossible to obtain. Instead, combinations of simulations and measurements are used to estimate antenna manifolds on platforms. The antenna under test is measured on a ground plane, and measured data is imported into numerical EM codes to include platform scattering. However, the import of the measured antenna data has limited accuracy and/or can lead to large run time in numerical EM codes. We present a new method to represent measured antennas in EM codes through an aperture current distribution of cross-slots and monopoles. Example results show good agreement with truth data when placed on complex platforms.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Channel Measurements in High Multipath, Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems are being proposed for a variety of short-range applications where large bandwidths are required. This work presents an experimental characterization for a dual-polarized 28 GHz indoor channel. Power delay profiles (PDPs) were measured in an indoor environment to extract site-specific multipath details.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method of MLFMA-ACA Algorithm for Analysis of Dielectric Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hybrid method of multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) and adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm for analysis of dielectric electromagnetic scattering is presented. In order to resolve the low frequency (LF) break down, ACA is applied to accelerate matrix vector multiplication operations in the lowest levels, while MLFMA is applied in higher levels to maintain high efficiency. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the hybrid method which can deal with LF break down when conventional MLFMA failed.

articleTitle: Printed W-Band Luneburg Lens for Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel low-cost printed circuit board Luneburg lens realization in W-band is proposed. This lens is fabricated by using a low-cost printed circuit board process. Concentric circles of holes in a substrate, covered on both sides with a metal sheet, realize a graded refractive index material. The effective refractive index contrast, necessary to implement the lens, is achieved by embedding a high dielectric constant substrate in the lens center using the same fabrication process. The periodic structure is analyzed by eigenmode analysis of a unit cell to calculate the effective refractive index. Field distribution of the proposed lens at 77GHz, excited by open-ended substrate integrated waveguides at its circumference, validates the conversion of the incident cylindrical wave to equiphase planar wave using the proposed lens.

articleTitle: Multi-arm Dipole for Compact Wearable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Non-resonant antenna configurations are investigated to provide compact radiators suitable to be adopted in wearable electronics. The non-resonant radiator exhibiting a capacitive reactance and a non-negligible radiation resistance can be matched by using a suitable underneath surface which is also able to prevent the radiation toward human body. High Impedance Surface (HIS) have been proved to be a suitable configuration to provide these two features. The focus of this paper is on the selection of a suitable primary radiating element. A novel element based on a CPW-fed version of a multiple-arm dipole is proposed and compared with the standard CPW-fed monopole previously employed in similar designs.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Cost Beam Steering Method Using Dispersive Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Beam steering is widely used in highly directional antenna systems and is generally done by using phase shifters or by changing the antenna elements. In this paper, a different technique for beam steering is presented. An antenna with a dispersive superstrate is able to steer the beam effectively. With this system, beam is steered 17° within 52 MHz bandwidth. The system is analyzed using CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Fast Source Reconstruction via ADMM with Elastic Net Regularization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Norm-1 regularized optimization algorithms are commonly used for Compressive Sensing applications. In this paper, an optimization algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) together with the Elastic Net regularization is presented. This type of regularization is a linear combination of the norm-1 and norm-2 regularizations, allowing a solution between the sparsest and the minimum energy solutions, but still enforcing some sparsivity. The combination of these two regularizations and the distributive capabilities of the ADMM algorithm enables a fast sparse signal recovering with minimum error.
