articleTitle: Design of a High Efficiency Low Sidelobe Dual-Polarization Cavity Antenna Array at Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 16 × 4 dual-polarization antenna array with high efficiency and low sidelobe is designed. To achieve good radiation efficiency, cavity antenna is used in this work as the basic element and stripelines are utilized to form the feeding networks. The feeding circuits for exciting different polarizations are stacked and carefully weighted. The simulated results show that the bandwidths of VSWR <; 1.6 for both of the polarizations are about 7.89% (14.6GHz-15.8GHz) and the isolation between the two ports is better than 40dB. In addition, 63% radiation efficiency (center frequency) with higher than 25.5dB gain is achieved.

articleTitle: A Lensing Case for the 5G Handset Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach to a functional rim-fixture as a cover of the smart phone to increase the antenna gain of the 5G beamforming structure. The 5G antenna is put on the top side of the phone platform and under the covering fixture that prevents the input impedance match and radiation characteristics from degradation. The cover has three usable types of dielectrics and these are segmented and aligned in series. The acceptable antenna characteristics are presented with the different angles of the beam which remain unchanged after adopting the lensing cover.

articleTitle: A Statistical Method for the Project and Analysis of a Yagi Antenna Using the HFSS and the Unscented Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work investigates the use of statistical sensibility as a design tool for Yagi Uda antennas using the HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) software and the Unscented Transform (UT). The study is based on correlation, covariance and regression analysis of input and output parameters. The test scenario used a Yagi antenna with four elements with a half wavelength feeder. The data were obtained by means of simulation using the HFSS software. The correlation study used the UT among the involved variables in the process, basically, distances between the elements and the impact of these in the output parameters: VSWR and the Total Gain. The idea is to seek which combinations allow better antenna performance, while being robust to small variations of the input parameters.

articleTitle: The Effect of Locations on the 3-D Printing Bed Surface for Designing PC-ABS Based RF Circuits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In additive manufacturing, Poly Carbonate-Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (PC-ABS)composite has better mechanical durability and heat-resistance compared to PolyLactic Acid (PLA)thermoplastics. 3-D printed radio frequency (RF)circuits often require being deployed in extreme conditions and hence PC-ABS RF circuits are preferable over PLA RF circuits. In this paper, variations of measured dielectric constant at 1 GHz and 10 GHz were reported for PC-ABS sample cubes based on the printing region on the printing bed surface of a 3-D printer. Also, an error analysis was presented using the measured permittivity at 1 GHz and 10 GHz and the reported average permittivity of PC- ABS from a literature.

articleTitle: Block-Division Based Extrapolation for Resolution Enhanced Radar Imaging of Complex Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Parametric model based electromagnetic (EM) signal extrapolation is usually not directly applicable to radar image processing for large sized complex targets. In this paper, a block-division based extrapolation technique is proposed, which can be used to enhance the resolution of radar images for complex targets. The large sized complex target is first divided into small blocks in image domain. Each block is then equivalent to a small sized simple target, whose data can be extrapolated using the technique based on parametric model and two-dimensional state space algorithm (2-D SSA) directly. The final image can be reconstructed by integrating all resolution enhanced block images. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the feasibility and usefulness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Monopole with Stacked FSS Reflectors for Enhanced Gain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates an enhanced monopole antenna design for ultra-wideband (UWB)applications. The antenna is a co-planar waveguide (CPW)fed UWB monopole that maintains a good impedance match from 0.5 GHz to 5.0 GHz, with a realized gain of 3.0 dB to 4.0 dB. To enhance performance, three frequency selective surfaces (FSS)are used as resonant reflectors to increase the realized gain to 4.0 dB to 11.3 dB from 0.5 GHz to 2.65 GHz. The resulting antenna comes in a form factor of 8.1” × 8.1” × 3.1”, and maintains a wide beam width over most of the frequency band.

articleTitle: Deep Thinning of MoM Matrices with the Balanced Electromagnetic Absorber Method in 3 Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A balanced (Weston-type) absorber, characterized by both electric and magnetic loss mechanisms, can be placed within the null field inside the equivalent surface currents replacing a perfectly conducting or homogeneous scatterer. The absorber, referred to as the filler, substantially reduces interactions between pairs of opposing basis/testing functions. The resultant moment matrix, formulated with the filler Green's function, is thinned accordingly. Moreover, most annulled elements need not be computed at all, thereby reducing substantially the matrix fill time. The lossy nature of the Green's function also serves to eliminate spurious internal resonances and thus makes the electric or magnetic field integral equation matrix well conditioned without resorting to a combined field integral equation.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna ESPAR in H Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel frequency-reconfigurable cavity-backed slot antenna ESPAR in the H plane is presented in this paper. Similar to other ESPAR antennas, the two parasitic cavities lying in the H plane are fed by the center driven cavity through coupling irises and terminated with varactors to provide variable loading impedances. By properly designing the loading impedance, continuous beamscanning in the H plane can be realized. Additionally, a pair of varactors are placed in the center of the slot to achieve a 47.7% frequency tuning range, while preserving the beamscanning performance at each operating frequency. Therefore, the proposed ESPAR is able to provide frequency diversity in addition to spatial diversity inherent in a fixed-frequency ESPAR. It is shown that the proposed ESPAR can steer its beam from -26 to 26 degrees in the H plane. By properly adjusting the frequency tuning varactors, the ESPAR can operate from 4.22 to 6.82 GHz and the impedance matching is maintained for all beamscanning angles.

articleTitle: A Complete Set of Boundary Conditions on PEC -A Way to Increase the Physical Insight of Undergraduate Students
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a complete set of boundary conditions (BCs) for the tangential and normal components of both the electric and magnetic fields on perfect electric conductor. This work aims to enhance the physical understanding of undergraduate students regarding the operating principle of basic microwave components like waveguide, cavity resonator, etc. by simplifying the lengthy mathematical derivations wherever possible by means of using the complete set of BCs.

articleTitle: All-Directions Thorugh-the-Wall Imaging Using Omnidirectional Bi-Static FMCW Transceivers: Imaging Technique and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Through-the-wall imaging using wideband radars is a powerful tool for mapping buildings' interiors and detecting static and moving objects hidden behind the walls. However, the low mobility and limited field of view of conventional systems limit their imaging capability in real scenarios. All-direction through-the-wall imaging using omnidirectional bi-static transceivers has been recently proposed to address the limitations of currently available imaging systems. This paper introduces an image formation technique for all-directions through-the-wall imaging realized by a bi-static FMCW radar. It is shown that a FMCW radar architecture simplifies synchronization of bi-static transceivers and allows for correction of synchronization errors. Imaging through utilizing a previously fabricated radar system in conjunction with the proposed image formation technique shows that all-directions through-the-wall imaging method can provide high resolution, 360° images of building interiors and hidden objects with specular reflections.

articleTitle: A 94 GHz Array Antenna for 45° Linear Polarization in LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed a 94 GHz planar array antenna for 45° linear polarization (LP) in low temperature co-fired ceramic technology (LTCC). First, the antenna is aperture-fed through a slot cut on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Then the array is fed by the 1-to-4 microstrip divider to form 2 × 2 radiation units. Two prototype array antennas with rectangular and circular elements at 94 GHz are designed and fabricated, respectively. The prototype with rectangular elements achieves a 5.6% bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB) from 90.8 GHz to 96 GHz with a gain varied from 7.2 dBi to 8.8 dBi while the prototype with circular elements achieves a 4.5% bandwidth from 91.2 GHz to 95.4 GHz with a gain varied from 7.2 dBi to 9.4 dBi.

articleTitle: A Voltage Tunable Metamaterial for Phase Shifting at U-band Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Voltage tunable metamaterial of short cross type array based on liquid crystal (LC) is proposed to achieve phase shift at U-band frequencies. Simulation results show, by increasing bias voltage from 0 to 14V, the metamaterial presents 230°phase shifting at 52GHz. Moreover, the resonant frequency is continuously and reversibly shifted from 53.6GHz to 49.9GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Wearable Planar UHF RFID Tag Antenna Attached to Multilayered Human Body
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wearable radio-frequency identification (RFID) tag antenna which can be attached to multilayered human body is proposed. The antenna is designed to operate at a band from 860 MHz to 960 MHz and is etched on a cotton fabric occupying a small size with a length of 65 mm, width of 22 mm, and height of 0.656 mm. The maximum frontal gain of the antenna is -13.8 dBi when attached to a multilayered human body at 915 MHz. Also, the simulated maximum reading distance of the RFID antenna against different frequencies is about 4 meters, presenting a good agreement with the measured result.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Responses of Waveform-Selective Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report an analytical study on characterizing the time-domain responses of waveform-selective metasurfaces (WSMs), which vary their electromagnetic responses at the same frequency. Especially, this paper presents simplified equivalent circuit models to estimate the time constant of WSMs. Our study can contribute to clarifying an underlying mechanism of WSMs as well as to facilitating their design procedure by using the equivalent circuit models.

articleTitle: Unique Charactersitics and Applications of Systems with Exceptional Points of Degeneracy
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We explore the occurrence of exceptional points of degeneracy (EPDs), which represent the coalescence of eigenmodes (eigenvalues and eigenvectors) in coupled waveguides. We demonstrate the conditions that lead to observing EPDs of various orders in certain coupled systems, either uniform or periodic. Those EPDs are found in lossless structures as well as in others with gain-loss balance; and we investigate their potential applications in boosting the performance of various devices at microwave and optical frequencies.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Three-Quarter Wavelength Inverted L-Shaped Antenna in Forward Direction of Metallic Objects or Human Bodies
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The length of an inverted L shaped antenna (ILA) which is three-quarters of the wavelength is studied. The ILA is placed on metallic objects or human bodies. The desired direction of radiation is at right angles to the objects. The gain in this direction without matching loss is enhanced, where the antenna is bent at a point that is approximately a quarter of wavelength from the feeding point. Because the current vector reverses near this bending point, the offsetting of current vectors is avoided and the combined current vector of this bent antenna is longer than that of the unbent antenna and that of the one quarter of wavelength ILA. As a result, the gain of the optimized three-quarters of wavelength ILA is enhanced.

articleTitle: Novel Balanced Coupled-Line Leaky-Wave Antenna Without Equalization of Phase Velocities
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A composite right/left-handed coupled-line leaky-wave antenna has been proposed, in which the balance condition has been met without the need for equalization of coupled-line sections phase velocities. The proposed concept adapts the previously reported concept of a coupled-line leaky-wave antenna, however, the compensation of unequal phase velocities which might cause the introduction of stop-band within operational bandwidth are compensated in a more simpler manner, omitting the time-consuming design of the modulated shape of coupled-line sections. The exemplary 32-unit-cell leaky-wave antenna is developed to prove the usability of the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Constructive Analytical Phasing (CAP) for Arbitrarily Oriented Arrays of Linearly Polarized Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a near-optimal phasing method, referred to as Constructive Analytical Phasing (CAP) to perform beamforming for arbitrary oriented antenna arrays of linearly polarized elements. Also, we investigate the resulting electric far-field polarization using Monte Carlo simulations. This simple but efficient method enables us to direct the beam to any desired point in space. In addition, it can be utilized to speed up any further optimization goals for a variety of antenna performance parameters such as pattern synthesis and side lobe level (SLL) reduction.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Reflect Array for Near-field Millimeter-Wave Beam Focusing Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low cost millimeter-wave (mm-wave) electronically reconfigurable Reflect Array (RA) has been presented in this paper. Aperture-Coupled Patch (ACP) elements are used to form a 40×40 element reconfigurable RA operating in the 71-74 GHz range of the mm-wave band. A feeding network, integrated with Single-Pole, Single-Throw (SPST) switches is designed to adjust the phase of the reflected field for the ON/OFF state of the switch. The performance of the reconfigurable RA is evaluated by performing beam focusing at the near-field of the array.

articleTitle: Cellular Antenna Performance Impact on MIMO in Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses considerations for the performance of MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) Antennas to support LTE in an automotive environment. In the paper performance of roof mount antennas are measured as well as antennas located in the interior of the vehicle. The interior antenna performance is compared to a set of reference antennas located on the roof with a large separation for decorrelation to support a good MIMO antenna configuration. The antennas are characterized as a component and then assessed in a field test.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Planar Ultra-Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel miniaturized planar ultra-wideband (UWB)antenna is presented. The proposed antenna, which is fed by a notched microstrip line, can yield an ultra-wide 10-dB impedance bandwidth with satisfactory radiation properties. It also features a compact physical size of 37.4mm × 64mm (0.19λ × 0.32λ at 1.5 GHz). A good agreement is obtained between the simulation and the measurement. Keywords-Ultra-wideband (UWB); compact antenna; planar antenna; antenna miniaturization.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Monopulse Feed Cluster Implemented via 3-D Metal Printing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact wideband monopulse feed cluster for antenna tracking applications. The monopulse feed cluster is highly-integrated and developed to provide dual-polarization, wide operational bandwidth and high polarization isolation. The complete feed cluster consists of square-aperture horns for signal transceiving, orthomode transducers (OMTs) for generating dual-polarized signals and magic-tees for constructing a comparator network. All the components are integrated strategically to achieve a compact size. Such a design is extremely difficult to realize via conventional fabrication process, so a 3-D metal printing technique is applied while considering its versatile features in practical fabrication. Preliminary results show that the monopulse feed cluster can operate with polarization isolation higher than 50 dB throughout the operational bandwidth from 10.5 GHz to 14.5 GHz, as well as satisfactory sum- and difference-radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Refractive Index Engineering in 3D Printed Dielectric Substrates for Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 3D printing is used to realize index-gradient and index-modulated dielectric media. The engineered media are associated to uniform inductive and capacitive grids to realize partially reflecting surfaces with either phase gradient or phase modulation along the dielectric-metal structures. Fabry-Perot cavity antennas utilizing the phase-engineered partially reflecting surfaces are designed, fabricated and measured. Simulated and measured performances show that the radiated beam is steered from boresight to a desired off-normal direction.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Steerable Maximally Sparse Array Via Modified Perturbed Compressive Sampling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new method based on the modified perturbed compressive sampling for the synthesis of steerable maximally sparse arrays is proposed. By considering the impact of invisible space region in the synthesis progress, the deterioration of the sidelobe level (SLL) during the scanning of the sparse array is addressed. Simulation example demonstrate the improvement of the SLL performance. Then, the relations among the array sparsity, array aperture and scanning region are analyzed and discussed through a series of simulation examples. The curves describing the relations are given.

articleTitle: Understanding the Element-Gain Paradox for Receiving Arrays Using Poynting Streamlines
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Energy flow directions around receiving array antennas can be modeled by generating streamlines of Poynting vector fields near the antenna. The geometrical shape of array effective area can be calculated from the locus of Poynting streamlines that terminate on the array element loads. The decrease of array directivity due to mutual coupling effects, or the element-gain paradox, can be explained by the overlap of element effective area shapes leading to the decrease of array effective area shape. The critical element distance for the element gain paradox effect is equal to the width of the effective area shape for a single isolated array element. These results provide a new, intuitive, and visually oriented tool for understanding a variety of effects in the theory and design of receiving antennas and arrays.

articleTitle: Virtual Source Model for Ray-Based Analysis of Focused Wave Scattering of a Penetrable Slab on PEC Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We develop a Virtual Source Model which is an intuitive, non-iterative, forward model to analyze the differential scattering of a dielectric covered conductive ground plane. This simple model is well suited for focused beam, nearfield mm-wave sensing of body-worn explosives for person scanning security systems. Ray analysis using the method of images for multiple interfaces yields good, experimentally-validated results.

articleTitle: Wideband Beam Steering Using a 4-Arm Spiral Array for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate a wideband scanning 4-arm spiral antenna array with high transmit/receive isolation for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR). STAR increases a channel's spectral efficiency by transmitting and receiving across the full bandwidth of a channel. To our knowledge, this is the first STAR array to demonstrate scanning across GHz bandwidths. Each 4-arm spiral element is divided into two arms for transmit and two more for receive. To suppress grating lobes, the element spacing is kept at less than λ/2. A 3×3 array prototype was fabricated and measurements agree well with simulations.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Hexagonal Modified Sierpinski Carpet Fractal Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed planar fractal antenna for bandwidth enhancement is designed. The proposed antenna consists of two iterations modified Sierpinski square slots with hexagonal radiation patch and CPW feed line. The simulated results indicate an impedance bandwidth of 133.5% (over 2.86-14.36 GHz)and a maximum peak gain of 5.5 dBi with stable radiation pattern. This antenna is designed on Rogers RO4350B substrate with height of 1.524 mm and 26×25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>of size. The designed antenna has a good potential to be used for UWB applications with compact size and better performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Archimedean Spiral Antenna Fed by Hecken and Exponential Microstrip Baluns
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of an ultra-wideband planar two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna fed by tapered printed baluns with Hecken and exponential impedance profiles. Practical baluns often exhibit amplitude and phase unbalances that cause disturbances in the antenna responses. The analysis described here addresses the dependence of antenna's performance on the balun profile, which plays an important role in the spiral design, since most of its applications require stable characteristics over the entire operating frequency band. The proposed baluns and antenna designs were simulated and optimized using ANSYS HFSS. All balun's configurations have shown a reflection coefficient better than -10 dB over the 1-18 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: 5.2 GHz Textile Antenna for Biological Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, a biological information monitoring system that constantly monitors patient's information has been used in a hospital. However, these systems have a problem with patients' movement restrictions by sensor cables and transmitters. In addition, 2.4 GHz band congestion has occurred to increase the number of the devices using the wireless LAN in a hospital. This paper proposed a 5.2 GHz band textile antenna as transmitting antenna for biological information monitoring system. Proposed antenna was designed to transmit both polarizations, were confirmed to work well by experiment.

articleTitle: Analog Beamforming with Single-Sideband Sub- Time- Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Switched TMAs are especially attractive in terms of efficiency either to exploit the fundamental mode improving the sideband lobe level of a given static pattern while minimizing the sideband radiation, or to leverage the steering capacity of the first harmonic pattern in a single sideband configuration. Both techniques have been combined to propose a so-called sub- TMA architecture which may take advantage, as described below, of the small size of millimetre wave antennas. The proposed sub-TMA-based architecture accomplishes a multiple-beam analog beamforming while offering high levels of both efficiency and flexibility.

articleTitle: Cross-Correlation Green Function for Interaction Between Electric and Magnetic Current Sources
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new cross-correlation Green's function (CGF) is formulated, considering the mutual interaction between electric and magnetic source current distributions. This additional CGF is essential for complete analysis of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) for “hybrid” MIMO antenna systems that contain both dipoles (electric current source) and slots / patches (magnetic current source). Preliminary numerical analysis on the ECC of a system containing two infinitesimal dipoles (one electric and one magnetic) is carried out.

articleTitle: Impedance Matching Metamaterials Composed of ELC and NB-SRR
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electric-LC (ELC) resonator couples strongly to a uniform electric field and negligibly to a uniform magnetic field. In contrast, non-bianisotropic split ring resonator (NB-SRR) couples strongly to a uniform magnetic field and negligibly to a uniform electric field. The unit cell consists of ELC and NB-SRR can generate the strong response from both electric and magnetic field. By optimizing the parameters of ELC and NB-SRR, we seek to find a design which can achieve impedance matching to free space and customized refractive index. The concept of designing impedance matching metamaterials with relatively high refractive index may prove useful in creating magneto-dielectric material for use as the substrate in antenna applications.

articleTitle: An Eight-Port 5G/WLAN MIMO Antenna Array with Hexa-Band Operation for Mobile Handsets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna design composed of a 6×6 5G MIMO antenna array in the LTE bands 42/43 (3400-3600/3600-3800 MHz) and a 2×2 MIMO WLAN antenna array in the 2.4 GHz (2400-2484 MHz), 5.2 GHz (5150-5350 MHz), and 5.8 GHz (5725-5875 MHz) bands for mobile handsets. Printed planar inverted-F antennas (PIFA) is used as the 5G antenna element (with a size of 3 mm×11.6 mm), while multi-branch monopole is adopted to design the WLAN antenna (with a size of 10 mm×10 mm). Furthermore, the WLAN antenna covers a Chinese 5G band (4800-5000 MHz) as well. Results demonstrate that the proposed MIMO antenna array has good characteristics of impedance matching and correlation coefficients in the desired bands of interest. Detailed design considerations of the proposed antenna are described in this paper. The corresponding simulated results are also presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Antenna Placement Optimization for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) technology has the potential to significantly enhance driver safety. The type, placement, and orientation of V2V antennas all affect the performance of the communication system. Simulation software for high frequency electro magnetics can be used to analyze the far-field effects of various vehicle antenna configurations without the need to perform physical testing. We present a simulation-based method for optimizing the placement and orientation of a monopole antenna on a vehicle using a Global Response Surface Method (GRSM). The resulting antenna configuration emits a stronger and more uniform far-field pattern while insuring a minimal reflection coefficient. A full-wave method; namely, the Multi-Level Fast Multipole Method (MLFMM), is used to perform the analysis of the antenna mounted atop a vehicle. This process has the potential to improve the performance and reduce the cost and design time of V2V antenna systems.

articleTitle: Doppler cloaking based on time-varying metamaterials: Theory and design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we present and discuss the theoretical aspects, design and bandwidth limits of Doppler cloaking. Doppler cloaking is a new cloaking technique that allows moving scatterers to appear at rest for an external observer. It consists of a time-varying metamaterial whose refractive-index is properly modulated as a periodic function in both space and time, leading to a periodic profile of the refractive index that moves with a certain velocity. By properly choosing the modulation scheme and frequency, Doppler-cloaking results in a zero-apparent velocity for the moving object. Conversely, static scatterers can appear in motion creating an illusion effect. Here, we will focus on the analysis of the fields propagating in the Doppler cloak and derive the key formulas for the design of a Doppler cloak. Then, fundamental limits on the operational bandwidth are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Determining the Dielectric Permittivity and Thickness of a Penetrable Slab Affixed to the Human Body Using Focused CW Mm-Wave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a fast and accurate method of finding the thickness and dielectric permittivity of weak dielectric objects using a focused continuous-wave radar security scanning system, to characterize objects that may be explosive threats. Building on the previously developed ray-based Virtual Source model for sensing scattering from slabs, this work presents an inversion algorithm using two observable CW millimeter wave probe parameters by considering expected small variations of dielectric slab thickness over its surface. The determination works reasonably well with a simulated dielectric covered conductive ground plane as a representation of body worn explosives.

articleTitle: A Proposed Long Wavelength Infra-red Metamaterial Absorber for THz Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A long wavelength infrared metamaterial absorber using electric field driven LC (ELC) resonating structure is reported in this paper. The structure shows an absorption peak of 96.2% at 30 THz (10.00 µm), The structure is studied for oblique incidences under TE and TM polarizations. The structure behaves as an absorber for both TE and TM polarizations so long as the angle of incidence is within 60°. All the results are obtained using Ansys HFSS, based on Finite Element Method (FEM). The absorption characteristics is simultaneously verified using COMSOL-Multiphysics simulation software and they are found to be in good agreement. The proposed ultra-thin (~λ/30) metamaterial absorber structure is expected to find potential application in THz spectroscopy, imaging techniques and sensing.

articleTitle: Roll-to-Roll Printed Transparent Applique Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present recent advancements in optically transparent antennas that are fabricated using large scale, roll-to-roll manufacturing processes. A CPW-fed Long Term Evolution (LTE) antenna was printed on a 125μm PET base substrate with predefined dimensions of copper micro-wire mesh, which had a sheet resistance of ~0.4 ohm/square, ~77% optical transmission, and~1.1% haze. The measured linear average gain (LAG) of the transparent antenna dropped about 2dB when compared to a solid metal counterpart. However measured 2×2 MIMO throughput with both antennas was found to have comparable performance during a vehicle drive test. Furthermore, it was found that the windshield mounted transparent antenna outperformed a roof mounted “Sharkfin” antenna by as much as 50% in the MIMO throughput.

articleTitle: Challenges in Terahertz Imaging of Freshly Excised Human Breast Tumors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Pulsed terahertz is investigated to image excised breast human tissue. Images of normal tissues obtained from breast reduction surgery are presented in addition to images of breast cancer tumors. Breast reduction tissue includes fat and fibroglandular regions, while malignant tumors include fat, fibroglandular and infiltrating ductal carcinoma regions. Breast tissue was received within 24 hours of surgery and was immersed in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium solution, defined here as fresh tissue. The bulk tissue of the same tumor is then fixed in formalin and embedded in paraffin to be scanned on the terahertz system. Histopathology images of 3-4 μm hematoxylin and eosin stained sections sliced from the top of the fixed tissue block are presented for comparison with terahertz images. Results demonstrate good agreement between terahertz and pathology images, particularly for fixed tissues.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz Yagi-Uda circular array antenna with omni-direcitional pattern for millimeter-wave WBAN applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 60GHz Yagi-Uda circular array antenna with omni-directional pattern for millimeter-wave WBAN applications is proposed. Center fed octagonal plates is used for feeding 8 Yagi-U da antennas located at the vertices of top and bottom octagonal plates. In order to improve the gain, each arm of dipole element is bent. The simulated 10-dB return loss bandwidth is 4085 MHz (57.17 GHz - 62.02 GHz) which covers a potential frequency band of 5G communication. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has an omni-directional radiation pattern toward the body surface with the maximum gain of 2.86 dBi at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Array Strategies for Improving the Performances of Chipless RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We consider array configurations of chipless tags for radio-frequency-identification (RFID) applications. The drawbacks of chipless RFID tags, e.g., short reading range, can be mitigated by arranging multiple tags in array configurations. However, the strategy for arrangements of individual tags can be critical, especially to avoid destructive electromagnetic coupling between them. Using a numerical implementation, we investigate different strategies and array configurations in order improve the performances of chipless RFID systems in terms of readability and reliability. This paper presents initial results to demonstrate the importance of array configurations.

articleTitle: 2.5 Dimensional Miniaturized Dual-band Frequency Selective Surface Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel dual-band frequency selective surface based on combined element of 2.5 dimensional spiral ring and crossed dipole is proposed. The simulation results indicate that the dual-bandstop frequency selective surface operates at the frequency of 2.3GHz and 5.9GHz, and is independent of incident angle and polarization. The whole dimension of the miniaturized unit cell is 0.051 × 0.051 (λ is free space wavelength on first resonant band). Its resonance mechanism is analyzed by the current distributions of the element at the two resonance frequencies.

articleTitle: A Uni-Planar Feeding Network for Monopulse Tracking Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a planar feeding network based on a novel 180° couplers is presented for monopulse tracking radar. The new 180° coupler is designed to feature symmetrical ports allocation between Σ/Δ ports and input ports by re-structuring the conventional rat race coupler and inventing novel compact crossover. It is the first time that a cost-effective planar monopulse comparator is investigated to untether it from complex multilayer designs or expensive waveguide solutions. To prove the concept, a comparator network operating at 5.8GHz is designed, and it shows that the full-wave electromagnetic simulation agrees well with ideal circuit simulation.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarized Null-Steering in Over-the-Horizon Radar with Planar Monopole Array on Finite Radial Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Other-the-horizon radar (OTHR) research is active in Canada at Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC) and planar monopole arrays are under study for mitigating the adverse effects of the auroral clutter in OTHR using null-steering techniques. Unfortunately, the ground system for the monopoles is made of radials and is limited in size. This introduces cross-polarized radiation that potentially reduces the OTHR performance if not accounted for. This performance reduction is evaluated in this paper, and straightforward joint co-polarized and cross-polarized null-steering is demonstrated.

articleTitle: PCB Based UWB mm-Wave Smart Capped Bowtie Array for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the preliminary development of a new antenna technology - the UWB capped Bowtie array antenna aiming to the applications in 5G wireless communication systems. The capped Bowtie antenna has not only the ultra-wideband active reflection coefficient performance but also a UWB stable radiation functions of the array element. A novel solution to the aggregation for tightly coupled capped Bowtie array is also presented briefly in the paper.

articleTitle: Microstrip-to-Probe Fed Microstrip Antenna Transition
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an accurate and simple method to model the transition between a probe-fed microstrip antenna and a microstrip circuit, assembled in a back-to-back configuration. With the aid of a full-wave electromagnetic simulation tool the two-port S-parameter matrix of the transition is calculated. This information is used to determine the antenna input impedance (Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub>) that enforces a given impedance (Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub>) after the transition. To showcase the applicability and validate the proposed method a co-designed GPS active integrated antenna was designed and manufactured.

articleTitle: AMC Packaged - Butler Matrix for Millimeter Wave Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband 4×4 microstrip line (MSL) Butler matrix design is presented for millimeter wave (MMW) applications. The MSL beamforming network (BFN) design is inverted over the metamaterial surface that is an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC), realized by the array of electromagnetic band gap (EBG) mushroom shaped unit cells. The purpose is to suppress the radiation losses from the discontinuities in the BFN s. The main components of BFN, i.e., the crossover and the hybrid couplers are designed with wideband characteristics. The results are presented for the 30 % impedance bandwidth around 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual Polarization, Dual Resonant Reflectarray Element for Beamsteering Applications at X Band
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual resonant, electronically-reconfigurable, phase-agile reflectarray element is presented. The element operates at X band and supports two linear polarizations. Reconfigurability is enabled through the symmetric placement of varactors across gaps in both resonant elements. The use of a dual resonant structure creates a phase range in excess of 450 degrees with an average loss of 2.7 dB.

articleTitle: Tunable Piezo-Actuated Metasurfaces for Millimeter-wave and THz Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a new class of low loss dynamically reconfigurable metasurfaces and their applications in the design of a beam steered high gain antenna at millimeter-wave (mm-wave)frequencies. A new tuning technology is applied to multilayer metasurfaces and the advantages of the proposed technology in terms of low loss, high switching speed and overall antenna performance is demonstrated. The proposed technology is scalable to higher mm-wave and THz frequencies using innovative micromachining processes.

articleTitle: Tunable Folded- Patch UHF RFID Tag Antenna Design using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a tunable ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) tag antenna is proposed using characteristic modes analysis. The proposed tag consists of a folded-patch and a feeding loop stacked on two substrate layers. The folded patch wrapped around 2 mm thick FR4 substrate and is optimized using characteristic modes to resonate around 915 MHz. The inductive feeding loop provides matching with RFID chip. This tag covers American RFID band form 905 MHz to 928 MHz with 10 dB return loss and can be tunable to European band by adding copper strips. Moreover, the proposed design is low cost, because it does not require any via or shorting pin. Furthermore, the measured read range of this tag is 3.5 m and 5 m in free space and above 200×200 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metal plate respectively.

articleTitle: Tri-band Reconfigurable Origami Helical Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable origami helical array that operates in three reconfigurable frequency bands centered at 2.07 GHz, 3 GHz and 4.45 GHz. Compared to previous work on origami QHA with foldable reflector, this helical array has a simplified feeding method with circular polarization (CP) achieved at all the 3 states (measured AR<;1.5 dB) by serially connecting a smaller helix on top of each uniform monofilar element. Also, one common reflector is applied at the 3 states to simplify the reconfiguration process with a smaller aperture area for each single element. Moreover, compared to the performance of the single element, this 7-element helical array has an increased simulated gain of 4.7 dB at state 1 at 2.07 GHz. Measured realized gains of 9.7 dB, 13 dB and 14.7 dB are achieved respectively at 2.07 GHz, 3 GHz and 4.45 GHz at 3 reconfigurable states. Therefore, this design can be applied in various scenarios, such as satellite radio and WiMax.

articleTitle: Dual-Layer Circularly Polarized Split Ring Resonator Inspired Antenna for Wearable UHF RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a circularly polarized antenna for wearable passive UHF RFID tag. The antenna consists of two layers without a physical connection. The upper layer is for achieving circular polarization by two orthogonal meandering dipoles connected to a split ring. The lower layer is a split ring resonator structure to achieve complex conjugate impedance matching with the RFID IC. The antenna has the maximum dimension of π×22<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and it provided a 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth of 23 MHz (905-928 MHz) in the simulation. The estimated maximum attainable read range of the tag exceeds two metres.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual Circularly-Polarized Waveguide Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel dual circularly polarized (CP) waveguide slot antenna array is presented. The RHCP and LHCP antenna array share a same aperture and adjacent wall. The radiating element is composed of a pair of tilted slots cut in the narrow walls of a ridge waveguide and a longitudinal slot in bottom of the U-shaped wall, which radiate a couple of orthogonal electromagnetic fields. The quarter of wave length depth of the ridge offers 90° phase difference for the two polarized fields. The difference of the RHCP and LHCP is the longitudinal slot offset. The dual CP antenna array obtains high efficiency and simple structure. A simple planar array is simulated to verify the design.

articleTitle: Plane Wave Synthesis in a Reconfigurable Over-the-air Chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work explores the accuracy with which a reconfigurable over-the-air chamber is able to synthesize a plane wave, as a basic component of a multipath field, in a test zone in which a wireless device under test is to be placed for performance evaluation. The excitations and reflection coefficients required to synthesize the plane wave are determined from a gradient descent optimization seeded with a convex optimization of a linear approximation of the problem. Results show that the chamber is able to synthesize a plane wave with high fidelity over a test zone circle whose diameter is approximately 40 % of the chamber side dimension.

articleTitle: A Wide-Band Dual-Polarized Frequency-Reconfigurable Slot-Ring Antenna Element Using a Diagonal Feeding Method for Array Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable slot-ring antenna that can switch between S- and C-band is presented. By turning on the eight PIN-diode switches, an S-band slot-ring antenna can be reconfigured into a 2×2 C-band slot-ring antenna array. This antenna operates from 2.75 to 4.1 GHz in the S-band state and from 5.5 to 8.1 GHz in the C-band state. In the C-band state, a diagonal feeding method is used to excite the 2×2 array and is able to provide either vertical or horizontal polarization; this feeding method can avoid the mutual coupling between two ports for V- and H-polarization.

articleTitle: A Selective Rectifier for RF Energy Harvesting for IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper study the performance of a rectifier circuit, dedicated to RF energy harvesting in actual propagation environments. The random behavior of the amount of the recoverable power is considered by the selectivity of the relevant conversion system. The most efficient rectifying diode and topology are selected according to the input power level. The DC output voltage and conversion efficiency are used to analyze performances. The obtained results show that the Single Series Diode (SSD) topology based on a Schottky diode SMS 7630 is the most efficient circuit for an input power levels less than - 20 dBm.

articleTitle: Antipodal UWB Vivaldi Antenna with Pseudoelement and Notched Flares for 2.5-57 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Novel methods of improving directivity and decreasing sidelobe radiation via the addition of an elliptical pseudoelement and irregularly-spaced notches in the tapered slot antenna are presented in this paper. This antenna has been shown to be functional over the C, X, Ku, K., Ka, and portions of the Sand V bands covering 2.5 - 57 (22.8:1 bandwidth) GHz. Minimum and maximum realized gains of 5.2 and 15.2 dBi were achieved at 2.5 and 32 GHz., respectively. As compared to other Vivaldi antennas reported in the past, the proposed design offers a larger bandwidth while providing 3-4 dBi higher gain in the majority of the band.

articleTitle: AFrequency-Tunable Varactor-Loaded Single-Layer Shorted Ring Microstrip Antenna fed by an L-probe
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a frequency-tunable varactor-loaded single-layer shorted ring microstrip antenna fed by an L-probe. In order to miniaturize a frequency-tunable ring microstrip antenna, two varactor diodes are mounted on a shorted ring patch antenna near the shorted vias. An L-shaped feeding probe, which is arranged in the same layer as the patch, is used to excite the shorted patch. Thus, the antenna structure is composed of a single-layer dielectric substrate and the patch area of the proposed antenna is reduced to a half in comparison with the conventional one. Resonant frequencies of the proposed antenna can be tuned by DC bias voltage applied to the varactor diodes. The bias circuit is arranged on the backside of the ground plane of the shorted patch with another thin dielectric substrate. In order to demonstrate the basic operation of the proposed antenna, a prototype antenna is fabricated and measured. Fractional bandwidth of a tunable range of the resonant frequency is around 5.7% under the condition of more than 3 dBi gain. The stable radiation pattern is observed over the frequency-tunable range. The antenna structure can be extended to multiband design more than dual-band easily by adding more shorted patches.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Properties of Metal Mesh Optically Transparent Touch Sensor Panels
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We design and characterize several optically transparent capacitive touch sensor panels, using a coarse metal-mesh as their trace material. These sensors form periodic patterns on a glass substrate and hence, they can also be considered as finite periodic structures with interesting electromagnetic properties, such as spatial filtering and frequency selectivity. These properties have been largely ignored, despite the fact that they offer many opportunities to integrate multiple functions into touch sensors. The present paper considers three popular touch sensor panel topologies as frequency selective surfaces and absorbers. Without any modification of the geometry, these panels present several pass-bands and stop-bands that can be further tuned to target frequency bands of interest.

articleTitle: Integration of Wireless Sensor Networks in Intelligent Transportation Systems within Smart City Context
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The use of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks has been exponentially growing in the last few years. Because of that, it is highly important to conduct previous radio propagation analysis when deploying vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) or vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) networks in urban scenarios, for Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) applications. In this work, the radio wave characterization for an urban infrastructure wireless communication system has been assessed for different frequencies. Two different realistic scenarios in which traffic lights, vehicles, people, buildings, vegetation and urban environment, have been implemented in an in-house 3D Ray Launching code. Results provide radio planning information before the deployment of Wireless Sensor Networks in terms of coverage, capacity and energy efficiency of the network.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Switched-Beam Antenna Using Cylindrical Bow Tie FSS Window
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The present paper relates to the design and implementation of a 2.45 GHz reconfigurable switched-beam antenna based on frequency selective surface (FSS). High frequency PIN diodes are accurately incorporated in the discontinuous Strip to reconfigure the electromagnetic (EM) wave. The switching window is created to electromagnetically emulate a transparent / opaque cylindrical surface. This surface is used to implement a reconfigurable antenna with a directive beam covering all azimuth angles plane by 6 equidistant angle. The simulated results confirm that this antenna can operate efficiently over a bandwidth of 130 MHz with a narrow beam width up to 30°. In addition, the level reached for the realized gain is about 13.8 dB at the frequency of 2.45 GHz. The proposed reconfigurable antenna is suitable for wireless sensor systems.

articleTitle: “Electromagnetic Vision”: Machine Intelligence Models of Radiowave Propagation in Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We explore the possibility of building learned models that can recognize the large-scale path loss characteristics of an environment by processing its geometry alone. These machine intelligence models can be trained by physics-based propagation analysis techniques such as ray-tracing or the parabolic equation method, to eventually develop an “electromagnetic vision”: the ability to provide the propagation properties of a channel based on a formally defined input file (or a sequence of images) that contains the channel's geometric specification. As a first step towards realizing this objective, we train a model to recognize the path loss exponent (PLE) in rectangular tunnels and show good correspondence of model predictions with measured and simulated data.

articleTitle: Effects of Tapering the Near-Field Distribution of Circularly Polarised Radial Line Slot Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we investigated the effect of tapering the electric near-field distributions of circularly polarised radial line slot array (CP-RLSA) antennas. Two CP-RLSA antennas were designed; the first one has a tapered amplitude distribution and the second one has a uniform amplitude distribution. Each of the antennas has several thousands of radiating slots on the top surface. The two field distributions were obtained by manipulating the slot lengths based on a slot coupling analysis. The RLSA antenna with a nearly uniform amplitude distribution has a gain of 34.5 dBic and 3-dB gain bandwidth of 8%, whereas the RLSA with the tapered amplitude distribution has a lower sidelobe level of -26 dB.

articleTitle: A Wideband Directional mm-Wave Antenna for Micro-Deformation Monitoring Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband mm-wave antenna is proposed with a directional radiation pattern for micro-deformation monitoring radar applications. The devised antenna consists of a coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding, a dipole-like radiating patch, a parasitic strip setting at the front of the radiating patch and a rounded ground plane with slots at the left and the right sides of the antenna. The parasitic strip is to enhance the bandwidth of the antenna, and it also used for improving the directional characteristic of the proposed antenna. The antenna is well designed and analyzed by using the HFSS, and the obtained results show that the antenna has a wideband bandwidth and good directional radiation patterns, making it suitable for micro-deformation monitoring radar applications.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Wideband 3-D Printed Interdigital Bandpass Filter Free of Post Fabrication Tuning
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a Ku -band wideband 3-D printed and connectorized eighth-order interdigital bandpass filter. The filter's cavity is prototyped with a ceramic-filled resin using stereolithography apparatus. The entire surface of the cavity is metallized with a conductive layer of electroless plated copper. Under circumstance of a high-quality surface metallization, the filter's RF performance can be well achieved without post fabrication tuning. The filter prototype demonstrates in the passband of 13.6-18 GHz an average insertion loss of around 2.2 dB and an average return loss of around 10 dB.

articleTitle: Tightly Coupled Dipole Array with Wideband Differential Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Differential RF front-end components provide greater immunity to ground noise and distortion by suppressing external interference. Recent advancements in differential RF front-end components offer high dynamic range, high input linearity, and low noise in the transceiver chain. However, differential phased arrays are not inherently ultra-wideband (UWB). To create a wideband differentially fed array for chip-integrated transceivers, a novel approach was taken on the well-established UWB Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA). This differential TCDA (D-TCDA) is proposed for S-Ku band (3-18 GHz) communications with emphasis on dual linear polarization and wide-angle scanning. The array achieves 6:1 bandwidth for VSWR <; 3 at broadside with scanning down to 45° from boresight in both E and H planes. The array exhibits very low cross-polarization, on the order of 70 dB.

articleTitle: Metal Only Spiral Slot Reflectarray Element Operating at 66 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metal-only reflectarray element operating in V-band (50-75 GHz) is proposed in this paper. By utilizing slots into the design, the dielectric substrate can be removed and replaced with an air gap. A slot based reflectarray element typically have a very limited phase curve. In contrast, in this paper, we show that multiple slots can result in a desirable phase range of 360°. The designed element consists of a square slot in the center of the unit cell with straight slots extending from its four corners to form resonators. The maximum loss of the element was less than 0.6 dB at the design frequency of 66 GHz.

articleTitle: UAV-based antenna measurement and diagnostics for circularly polarized antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The main goal of this contribution is to present the application of an Unmanned Aerial System for Antenna Measurement (UASAM) for analyzing circularly polarized antenna arrays. UASAM can be used for in-situ antenna measurement and diagnostics. It makes use of a power detector onboard an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) with a cm-level accuracy positioning system, which allows to acquire measurements in the near field region. Thus, it overcomes practical drawbacks of other UAV-based antenna measurement systems that work in the far field region. Its performance for providing antenna diagnostics of an array composed by two circularly polarized antennas with reverse handedness is analyzed, comparing it with anechoic chamber results.

articleTitle: Solution of Potential Integral Equations with NSPWMLFMA
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we present a numerical implementation of recently developed potential integral equations (PIEs) by using nondirective stable plane wave multilevel fast multipole algorithm (NSPWMLFMA). The proposed method is efficient and accurate to solve large scattering problems involving perfectly conducting bodies with geometrical details, which require dense discretizations with respect to the operating wavelength. Numerical results in the form of scattered field from various objects are provided to assess the accuracy and efficiency of PIEs solved using NSPWMLFMA.

articleTitle: Low Scan Loss Bifocal Ka-band Transparent Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new bifocal design of transparent transmitarray antenna (TTA)is proposed to reach low scan loss at Ka-band (27.5 − 29.5 GHz), using meshed metal unit-cells and transparent substrates (polymethylmethacrylate, PMMA)to allow total integration in dense urban environment. Thanks to the excellent performance of the meshed double-circle rings unit-cell under oblique incidence, wide field of view (±30°)with low scanning loss (lower than 0.53 dB)and low side lobe level (below −17.7 dB)are obtained by moving the feed along the focal plane of the TTA.

articleTitle: High-Gain Patch-Fed 3D-Printing Fresnel Zone Plate Lens Antenna for 60-GHz Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain Fresnel zone plate lens antenna designed for 60-GHz systems. Manufactured with the 3D printing technology and fed by a simple patch on the substrate, the proposed Fresnel lens antenna allows for low-cost fabrication and easy integration with planar circuitry. Experimental results show that the prototype antenna can achieve a 10-dB impedance bandwidth from 56.6 GHz to > 67 GHz and the peak gain of 14~20 dBi across the bandwidth, corresponding to gain enhancement of 9.2~10.9 dB.

articleTitle: Preliminary results on Conformal Transmitarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication some results of a preliminary study on Conformal Transmitarray Antennas (CTAs) are presented. In particular, the peculiarities of such a configuration are reported, and the radiation features of a small-medium size structure are shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of Three Sampling Methods for Shooting-Bouncing Ray Tracing Using a simple Waveguide Model
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses shooting-bouncing rays (SBR) ray-tracing techniques and their applications in computational electromagnetics. It specifically discusses uniform random, low-discrepancy deterministic, and uniform sampling techniques for the standard SBR formulation and compares their effects for a simple waveguide model.

articleTitle: Interpretation of Antenna Scattering Phenomena with the Aid of Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article is a study of electromagnetic (EM) antenna scattering phenomena from the Characteristic Mode (CM) standpoint and aims to shed some light on scattering from antennas. Using CM theory, the modes can be classified to yield two different sets of modes. One set is orthogonal with the localized antenna's source field in the vicinity of the feed point and this set of modes are referred to as the short circuit “Scattered Modes”. The other set includes the modes that can be excited by the antenna's source at the feed point and this set forms the so-called re-radiated fields or “Antenna Modes”. These modes are studied to determine the effect of each set on the overall scattering by an antenna within these scattering/re-radiation environments. This analysis provides additional physical insight as well as a new and different approach that can be used in various antenna applications.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Slot Antenna Design for 5G Smartphone with Metal Casing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable slot antenna has been proposed for the fifth-generation (5G) smartphone applications to cover a wide bandwidth of 824-960 MHz, 1710-2690 MHz, 3300-3600MHz and 4800-5000 MHz. The antenna is placed at the bottom of the phone, and is designed for metal casing. The folding slot structure is used to realize the miniaturization and narrow ground clearance of the antenna. The PIN diodes are used to achieve three different working states, so as to bring about good frequency coverage and antenna miniaturization. The proposed antenna has achieved the good impedance bandwidth and acceptable total efficiency throughout the required bands. The result shows that the proposed antenna is good candidate for a 5G smartphone with metal casing.

articleTitle: Coupled Half-Mode Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for IR-UWB in Air-Filled SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coupled half-mode cavity-backed slot antenna for high-precision impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) localization applications in the [3.7740; 4.7424] GHz frequency band of the IEEE 802.15.4a-2011 standard is designed and implemented in air-filled substrate-integrated-waveguide (AFSIW) technology. The antenna is matched to 50Ω in the [3.6400; 4.8300] GHz frequency band, yielding a bandwidth of 1.19 GHz or 28.1%. Furthermore, a total antenna efficiency higher than 91.0% and a system fidelity factor (SFF) higher than 98% is achieved within the 3dB-beamwidth of the antenna, making it suitable for high-precision IR-UWB localization.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Slot Loading in Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work explores the impacts of slot loading in a microstrip patch antenna from modal viewpoint. Slots are found to be effective in reducing nearest higher order modes. Closed-form expressions have been reported to account for the change in impedance properties. Further scopes of the present work have been highlighted from physical perspective.

articleTitle: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slot Array with Voltage-Controlled Liquid Crystal Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide slot array antenna with a reconfigurable liquid crystal phase shifter for operation at X-band and Ku-band is proposed. The frequency range of operation for a VSWR better than 2 is from 11.85 GHz to 12.25 GHz with a realized gain around 18 dB. Using a liquid crystal phase shifter makes it possible to carry signals with higher power than conventional phase shifters. Moreover, continuous phase shifting as well as wideband operation are among the advantages of using a liquid crystal phase shifter. The proposed antenna can be used in satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized and Multi-Beam Cross-Mesh Array Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cross-mesh array antenna is presented for RF power harvesting in this paper. To enhance the reliability of harvester, producing multiple polarizations and multiple beams is an effective method in rectenna designs. Benefited from the ability of tilting beam angle of cross-mesh array antenna, four differently tilted beams with two linear polarizations can be simply generated by four isolated feed points without any beamforming network design. To demonstrate it, a prototype operating around 6 GHz is fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Investigation of rough surfaces for propagation modeling in caves
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Making wireless communications available in caves is important, it will benefit several activities that are caves-related such as volcanology, speleo-biology, speleo-archeology, hydrology, military reconnaissance, and cave exploration. Besides, it will also enhance the safety of the operation of show caves like the tourist caves and furthermore, may assist in the search and rescue operation in caves. In this paper, we study the behavior of radio waves on a random rough surface using ray tracing technique that incorporates a special twist to the Fresnel reflection coefficient to account for the scattering effects arising from that rough surface. The findings of our work lays a foundation for further investigation to be conducted in actual cave environment, since the ground surface inside a cave is definitely not smooth but rough.

articleTitle: Design of an UHF RFID Tag Antenna with a Paper Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the well-known high frequency structure simulator (HFSS)is used to design an ultra-high-frequency (UHF)radio-frequency-identification (RFID)tag antenna with a paper substrate. With the continuous development of RFID technology, various factors of designing RFID tags have been investigated such as the substrate material, tag shape, working frequency band, and impedance matching. In the design of passive tag antenna, the impedance matching, broadband, and miniaturization are the main difficulties. We use a special structure to improve the performance of passive tag antenna and an UHF RFID tag antenna with a paper substrate is proposed for near-field applications. The tag antenna uses a matching network to achieve the impedance matching and employs a first-order Hilbert fractal structure to reduce the size. The overall size of the antenna is 63.6mm × 25mm and the operation band is from 881.9 MHz to 962.2 MHz which can cover the UHF RFID bands of many countries. Its good performance is verified by HFSS simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Target Detection and Tracking Algorithm Simulation for Automotive Millimeterwave Radar Based on Systematic Softeware-based Radar System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the increasing complexity of modern radar system and the increasing number of devices used in the radar system, it would be highly desirable to model the complete radar system including hardware and software by a single tool. This paper presents a novel software-based simulation method for modern radar system which here is automotive radar application. The method provides target detection and tracking algorithm simulator and the simulation results are compared with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Multibeam Array Antenna Based on E-Plane Butler Matrix for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized multibeam array antenna fed by a compact beam-forming network (BFN) in multi-layer substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is addressed. As the BFN, an E-plane 4 × 4 Butler matrix (BM) is designed. It is stacked with basic components in the vertical direction so that the dimension can be significantly reduced. Furthermore, some modifications of the BM have been made to obtain further miniaturization. The total occupied area of the designed antenna, including the BFN, is merely 3.8 1 × 0.5 1, which provides an attractive alternative for future 5G applications.

articleTitle: Overview of Hybrid Solver in HFSS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the hybrid solver in ANSYS HFSS for electrically large radiation and scattering problems. In HFSS v12, a domain decomposition solver was adopted to serve as an effective and parallelizable finite element preconditioner. Since then the framework has been extensively and systematically extended to incorporate multiple numerical solvers into a powerful hybrid solver. These technologies are illustrated via numerical simulations of some real-life problems.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Finite Element and Boundary Integral Method

articleTitle: Supershaped CPW-fed Monopole Antenna With Parasitic Strips for Unidirectional Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a supershaped CPW-fed monopole antenna with parasitic strips for unidirectional pattern is proposed. A Gielis curve based patch with planar reflector and parasitic strips are used to enhance the directivity. The characteristics of the antenna such as return loss, realized gain and radiation pattern are simulated and the return loss is compared with the measured results. The -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the designed antenna is from 2 GHz to around 10 GHz with the peak gain around 4 dB or above for most of the frequency range.

articleTitle: Computational Millimeter-wave Spotlight Imaging using Holographic Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a spotlight imaging system integrated with a frequency-diverse aperture is presented for security-screening applications. The spotlight imager consists of holographic metasurface antennas that can dynamically be tuned to radiate spotlight patterns allowing the extraction of high-resolution images from a constrained field-of-view (FOV). The spotlight aperture operates at a single frequency, 75 GHz, within the W-band frequency regime (75 - 110 GHz)and is used for the identification of threat objects while the frequency-diverse aperture operates at K-band frequencies (17.5 - 26.5 GHz)and is used for detection purposes, determining the constrained FOV to be imaged using the spotlight imager at high resolution.

articleTitle: Leaky Wave Antenna Array using Complementary Dual-Stub Radiating Elements for Consistent Gain
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a 16 element Leaky Wave Antenna (LWA) array in the X-band for obtaining pencil beam radiation pattern with consistent gain. The design uses complementary dual-stub configuration in microstrip line technology to obtain linearly polarized beam in the propagation direction. The unit cell of the antenna is chosen with transversal and longitudinal asymmetry to achieve consistent gain while scanning through the broadside direction. First, a single LWA element is designed with 90% radiation efficiency. The main beam scans from -22° at 8 GHz to +41°at 12 GHz about the broadside direction with gain variation less than 0.6 dB. Next, the array is designed using this element and the individual elements are fed in phase using wideband multi-section Wilkinson power dividers.
