Measured peak gain of 28 dBi is obtained in the broadside direction at 9.25 GHz. The 3 dB beamwidth measured in the broadside direction in the two orthogonal planes are 3.2°and 7°, respectively.

articleTitle: Wide-angle mechanical scanning Transmit-arrays for Satellite Ka-band user terminals
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The antenna design for broadband satellite communications is particularly challenging, new cost-effective solutions are still needed. An overview of recent contributions from the authors on planar transmit-arrays (TAs)for satellite Ka-band user terminals is presented. We tackle several design problems: how to improve the scanning coverage using low cost mechanical beam steering, how to choose the type of unit cells that compose the TA, how to devise a single aperture with high gain that operates simultaneous at two widely separate frequency bands. Different prototypes are used to conduct these studies. All these TAs provide wide beam zenith scanning, [-50°,50°] with less that 3dB of scan loss, good circular polarization performance and low beam distortions. The prototypes have the same aperture size, 195 × 145 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, that provide gains up to 29 dBi for 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband Array for Vehicle to Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-waves (mm-wave) provide opportunities for wide bandwidth, required for future high speed and vehicle to vehicle (V2V) communications. In this paper, we present a mm-wave phased array based on tightly coupled dipole elements, operating from 17.7GHz to 32.8GHz for V2V applications. The proposed array is low profile with unit cell dimension of 5mm × 5mm. Full wave simulations, assuming infinite array, show that the single element achieves a gain of 4.09dBi at 28GHz. In addition, a link budget analysis to study the communication range among vehicles is provided by considering different finite array dimensions. The estimated link budget shows that for a 4 × 4 and 8 × 8 element arrays, the maximum range to transmit signals at a speed of 1Gbps is 170m and 700m, respectively.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Dual-Frequency Dual-Polarization Feed System for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design of a high-gain dual-frequency dual-polarization feed system for 5G communication is presented. The feed system operating at 28 GHz and 60 GHz is composed of a dual-band coaxial horn, a coaxial orthomode transducer (Coaxial OMT) for 28 GHz, and an orthomode transducer (OMT) for 60GHz. The simulation results show that the reflection coefficient is less than -10 dB in the frequency range of 27.7-28.3 GHz and 59-61 GHz. Simulated gains at 28GHz and 60GHz are both 17dB and the radiation patterns are basically rotationally symmetrical. Besides, the feed system possesses a near constant phase center over the high and low frequencies. The proposed feed system can be used to illuminate the reflector antenna or reflectarray.

articleTitle: New Generation of WIPL-D in-Core Multi-GPU Solver
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Acceleration of in-core LU decomposition by using multiple GPUs in parallel and comparison of performance of two different GPU types, is presented in this paper. The presented algorithm for LU decomposition enables highly efficient utilization of an arbitrary number of GPUs. Comparison of performance of up to 8 GTX 680 GPUs and up to 4 GTX 1080 Ti GPUs is shown. The results presented show that a dense MoM matrix with 100 000 complex unknowns in single precision can be LU decomposed in 3.7 minutes, on a personal computer equipped with 4 GTX 1080 Ti GPUs.

articleTitle: Printed Quasi Yagi Antenna with Closely Spaced and Thick Directors for Triple ISM-Band/Wideband Applications at UHF
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study, a printed quasi Yagi antenna realized for almost whole UHF band is given. Within overall UHF band, the performances of three well-known ISM frequencies of 433, 866 and 915 MHz, which are used in many wireless applications such as LoRa, IoT, M2M, M-bus, and RFID, are desired to be kept relatively better. The proposed antenna includes a printed feed dipole with reflector and two director elements. The directors are quite thick and closely spaced to feed dipole, which provides significant enhancement in the bandwidth. According to gathered results, the antenna has more than 80% bandwidth for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; -6.5 dB between 407 and 955 MHz where return loss values are higher than 10 dB in the bands 417-493 MHz and 700-920 MHz covering three mentioned UHF ISM bands. Additionally, it has more than 10 dB front-to-back ratio and 4 dBi realized gain for the frequencies lower than 500 MHz and higher than 850 MHz, which again includes 433/866/915 MHz bands; while the gain values in the remaining band are relatively low as being 3.5 dBi on the average.

articleTitle: A Compact Ultra-wideband Single Element Planar Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a planar, single element ultra-wideband Yagi-Uda antenna. To feed the radiating element, a tapered microstrip balun is designed. The proposed antenna covers a wide frequency band of (1.2 GHz - 2.16 GHz), achieving a fractional bandwidth of 60%. The gain of the antenna lies above 5.2 dBi throughout the band, having a maximum gain of 7.23 dBi, within the smallest form factor (0.4λo x 0.54λo) reported so far for this frequency range. The antenna is fabricated on a low-cost FR4 substrate (1.5mm) and the measured results are in accordance with the simulations.

articleTitle: Simultaneously Matching a N-Port Network
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The concept of simultaneously matching a N-port network is investigated in this letter. Multi-port network impedance matching has been raised in various problems including phased arrays and MIMO antennas. A formulation based on an iterative method is introduced to find the matching impedances to simultaneously match a N-port network. An antenna array is presented as an example to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Modified Aperture-Coupled Millimeter-Wave Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A modified aperture-coupled patch antenna element is presented in this paper to improve the operating frequency bandwidth of a Ka-band reflectarray. The proposed antenna consists of four metallic layers and three dielectric substrates. Ultra-wideband frequency bandwidth can be achieved when both the patch and the slot are excited for radiation. Simulation results show that the proposed reflectarray unit-cell operates over the frequency band (29-40 GHz)~ 32% with a low reflection loss less than 0.5 dB for both normal and 45° incident angles.

articleTitle: Monolithic 3-D Printed Spherical-Resonator-Based Olympic-Topology Bandpass Filters
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents RF design and implementation of millimeter-wave bandpass filters (BPFs)based on high-quality-factor spherical resonators that are configured in an Olympic-shape coupling topology. This type of filtering topology is superior in an improved high-side out-of-band rejection due to the suppression of higher order modes of the spherical resonator. Fifth-order Olympic-topology BPFs are demonstrated at Ku and Ka bands by using direct-metal-laser-sintering and stereolithography (SLA)3-D printing techniques, respectively. Electroless copper/silver plating is employed for the surface metallization of the SLA-printed filter.

articleTitle: L-band Patch Antenna with Integrated Ka-band SIW Slot Array
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel shared-aperture dual-band antenna concept that has a microstrip patch antenna with an integrated SIW slot array in the patch metallization. The dual-band antenna is intended for an UAV application. The microstrip patch operates at 1.42 GHz and the slot array operates at 34.7 GHz. Each band is fed independently, and the patch provides a gain of 9.5 dB, with an impedance bandwidth of 50 MHz. The slot array provides a gain of 5.4 dB, with a bandwidth of 312.3 MHz. The antenna shows a very high isolation between ports at both bands.

articleTitle: Gain and Efficiency Enhancement of a 77 GHz On-Chip Antenna through AMC and Superstrate Package
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: On-chip antennas present an excellent solution for higher integration levels with the lower number of off-chip components and lower cost, however, their efficiencies are much lower due to lossy Si substrates. In this paper, we present a novel combination of Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) surface and a package which acts as a superstrate as well to enhance the on-chip antenna efficiency. Designed in standard 0.18 μm CMOS technology at 77GHz frequency band, the CPW-fed on-chip monopole antenna is a good candidate for automotive radar systems. Since the package of the chip acts a superstrate, it is not a mere protector of the chip but also provides functionality, qualifying this design as System-on-Package (SoP). The combination of the optimized AMC surface and superstrate package enhance the radiation efficiency of the antenna to 54.37% and the gain to 2.4dBi, achieving 22.1% efficiency enhancement and 9.1 dB gain enhancement as compared to the standalone on-chip antenna.

articleTitle: On the Optimization of Distributed Magnetic Traps in MRI Coils Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A systematic procedure for the design of printed filters aimed at decoupling Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) loops is presented. The filter (distributed magnetic trap) consists of spiral resonators, it is passive and conformal to the geometry of the antennas to be decoupled. The proposed design method begins from the estimation of the analytical mutual coupling between the MRI loops under the magneto-static approximation. From such analysis, a criterion for optimizing the distributed magnetic trap in terms of number of spiral resonators is proposed and applied at higher frequency. A Dual Tuned coil is employed as test case.

articleTitle: Simple Transmission Line Model from RET Results for Propagation Through Vegetation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: RET theory is widely used for modelling propagation through vegetation at microwave frequencies. The parameters of the model are determined from a limited amount of measured data via curve fitting. The propagation model is therefore essentially empirical and is characterized from a few types of trees at a few densities, using specific antennas at specific separations, and at a few frequencies. The resulting model is mathematically complex, has a large number of parameters, and is slow to compute. A simpler and faster-to-compute model is required, and given the empirical nature of the RET-based vegetation propagation model, it is a straightforward task to reduce the parameters and greatly simplify the model. This paper presents the simplest transmission line model that tightly fits established RET -based results.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Lazy Ant Colony Optimization for Frequency Selective Surface Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, 3D Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) designs have become popular due to their enhanced performance at oblique incidence angles as compared to planar designs. While planar FSS design has been successfully performed using discrete nature-inspired evolutionary optimization algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), these algorithms are not suited for the problem of 3D FSS design, due to the generation of non-contiguous structures, making manufacturing difficult. One alternative to these algorithms is the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) technique, which guarantees contiguous segments are generated. However, traditional ACO methods require meanders to continue until they are trapped, potentially generating a PEC unit cell. In this paper, a Multi-Objective Lazy Ant Colony Optimization (MOLACO) algorithm will be applied to the problem of FSS design. The introduction of lazy ants allows exploration of solutions previously inaccessible by traditional implementations of ACO. Simulated results will show that it is well suited to the problem of 3D FSS design.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small On-Chip Antenna Scaled down to One-Twentyfifth by One-Fiftieth of Wavelength
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically small on-chip antenna for RFID tags operating at 5.8 GHz is presented. The proposed antenna has dimensions of 2.1 mm (λ/25) by 1.2 mm (λ/50), implemented in a 0.18 μm pure CMOS technology. The antenna consists of two loops. By changing the size of the inner loop, we can manage the antenna impedance while maintaining its gain. The antenna has a gain and a bandwidth of -22.21 dBi and 4.9 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna Used for Structural Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) in civil engineering requires robust sensors but the connection line and power supply in traditional sensors remain a significant challenge to the practical implementation of SHM. In this paper, we propose a rectangular microstrip antenna which can be used as a strain sensor. The antenna is a wireless and passive sensor which can fully overcome the drawbacks of traditional sensors. It is found that the resonant frequency of antenna will change regularly with the change of strain. Also, the resonant frequency will vary linearly when the size of antenna changes in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. With these characteristics, the antenna can be an ideal sensor for the SHM applications.

articleTitle: Performance of a Spiral Antenna System for Wideband Sensing and Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design of a wideband two-arm spiral antenna system is presented. By squinting the elements off boresight, spectrum sensing and direction finding over a wide range of angles and frequencies can be achieved. With a 10 turn spiral element fed by stripline balun and squint angle of 30°, a minimum gain of -6 dBic, maximum axial ratio of 5 dB and minimum DFF slope of 0.1 dB/o is seen over the field of view of ± 60°.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Antenna Design Using Hexagonal Shape Unit Cells for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reflectarray antenna design using hexagonal shape unit cells for 5th Generation (5G) application is presented. The hexagonal shape has been proposed to design the unit cells with a 0°-360° reflection phase range. Moreover, the reflectarray is designed on a single layer topology, to make the design easy, more compact and low-cost fabrication. The obtained results show a good level of gain (27 dBi) at operating frequency of 28 GHz (5G band).

articleTitle: Multi-Antenna SAR Estimation in Linear Time
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is a measure used by regulatory agencies for determining the exposure safety compliance of portable wireless transmitting devices. For devices with multiple transmitter chains operating at a single frequency, determining compliance is complicated by the fact that testing needs to cover all possible combinations of transmissions from all antennas. We give a compliance test of multi-antenna devices with measurement time which is linear in the number of antennas N. The proposed test requires 7N -12 measurements per probe location for N ≥ 3, independently of the number and type of transmitted signals. We evaluate the performance of the proposed test for noisy SAR measurements.

articleTitle: Study of Diffraction at 30 GHz, 140 GHz, and 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents comparison between measurements and modeling of diffraction in indoor obstructed propagation environments at 30 GHz, 140 GHz, and 300 GHz. The results show that all three frequency bands experience diffraction in obstructed environment. Furthermore, the good agreement between measurements and modeling shows that diffraction at mm-wave and THz frequencies can be modeled by using Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD). Finally, the results show that diffraction becomes more dominant as frequencies increase from mm-wave to THz frequencies.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication and Measurement of a Millimeter Wave Fresnel Lens using Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design, fabrication and measurement of a 3D-printed Fresnel lens is presented. A dielectric characterization of polylactic acid material prior to simulation and fabrication of the lens is introduced. A full-wave simulation is used to design and optimize the gain of the lens. The focal length of the lens is chosen to be 40 mm. Fused deposition modeling is adopted to manufacture the lens. The final fabricated model is composed of 4 full-wave zones with 3 subzones and 1 supporting layer. The structure has 16 annular rings with maximum radius of 69.3 mm. Also., it has the thickness of 11.8 mm. The gain pattern measurements are performed in an anechoic chamber. The results show that the lens achieves a gain enhancement of 9 dB at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement by Position Perturbations in Stacked Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the effect of position perturbations on the bandwidth of an aperture coupled dielectric resonator antenna (DRA), is presented. Two combinations of stacked DRA's are considered for the analysis: larger over smaller (LOS), and smaller over larger (SOL). Different position perturbations on transmission line (TL), LOS, and SOL are applied to widen the matching bandwidth of the antenna. The performance of the proposed antenna are compared with the conventional antenna designed with no perturbations. The proposed antenna not only provides 5:1 ultra-wide matching bandwidth (from 2.7 GHz to 13.6 GHz), but also result in a highest gain of 9 dBi, which is 2 dBi more than the antenna designed with conventional method with no perturbation.

articleTitle: Additive-Manufacturing-Enabled Air-Filled Substrate Integrated Waveguide Microwave Components
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3D-printed air-filled substrate integrated waveguide topology is proposed to mitigate the problems limiting the performance of dielectric-filled substrate integrated waveguide based components while maintaining its most interesting features. The proposed topology is showcased through the design of a 3D-printed coaxial-to-AFSIW transition and a power divider/combiner. Measurement results validate the excellent performance in terms of impedance matching and bandwidth.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Multiband Antenna for Various Wireless Communications Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a quad-band antenna for the global system for mobile (GSM), wireless area network (WLAN), and worldwide interoperability for microwave access (WiMAX) is presented. The antenna is coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed rectangular monopole loaded with double E-shaped stubs. The multiband monopole antenna is designed and analyzed using computer simulation technology (CST) full wave simulation. For verification of simulation results, the antenna is fabricated with photolithographic technique and measured using vector network analyzer. There is a good agreement between simulated and measured results. The designed antenna operates at the frequency bands from 0.8 to 1.037 GHz for the GSM system, 2.329-2.575 GHz for the IEEE 802.11b&g WLAN systems, 3.459-3.549 GHz for the WiMAX system, and 4.93-5.64 GHz for the IEEE 802.11a WLAN system.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Circularly-Polarized Planar Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present the design and analysis of a K-band radially-periodic leaky-wave antenna radiating a circularly polarized broadside pencil beam. The structure is constituted by a metallic strip grating printed on top of a single-layer grounded dielectric slab, and is fed on the bottom by means of a square array of printed surface-wave launchers. The structure is optimized to support the fast n = -1 spatial harmonic, whose behavior has been accurately characterized through a full-wave dispersive analysis developed by means of an in-house method-of-moments (MoM) code. By proper phasing the four independent feeding points, linear or circularly polarized pencil beams can be obtained by exciting a dominant but weakly-attenuated, cylindrical TM leaky-wave mode. In this way, highly-directional broadside pencil beams showing good polarization purity can be obtained. The proposed design is of interest for modern satellite and terrestrial point-to-point communications.

articleTitle: Extending Waveguide Mode Theory Based Propagation Models to Arched Rough Wall Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio wave propagation modeling in tunnels plays an important role in designing reliable wireless communication systems. The roughness condition of tunnel walls, which is often disregarded, can be a source of significant path loss. However, current modeling techniques are either computationally intensive or limited to canonical tunnel geometries. This paper presents a highly efficient approach to model wave propagation in general tunnel geometries with rough surface walls. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated by comparing to numerical simulation models and measurement data in practical cases of railway tunnels.

articleTitle: Microstrip Time Domain Transmission (TDT)Application for Moisture Soil Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describe the work in progress of an impulse-based time domain transmission (TDT)technique using microstrip transmission lines for a soil moisture sensor implementation in agriculture.

articleTitle: THz Near Field Focusing using Cassegranian Configuration for EM Side-channel Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents near field focusing at THz frequencies using cassegranian antenna configuration used for the electromagnetic side-channel detection. The antenna is designed to produce the focused beam 30cm away from the aperture. The focusing is done in the near field region by moving the sub-reflector from the focal point along the axis. It is observed in the simulations and measurements that the subreflector position has to shift approximately 11 wavelengths along the axis to create the focus at the required location. The 3dB focus width of the antenna is ~4 mm. Finally, simulation results of near field gain are compared with measurements and good agreement is observed.

articleTitle: Novel Compact Hybrid Monopole ASA Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact hybrid monopole- Annular Slot Antenna (ASA). The proposed antenna combines the advantages of an ASA with the broadband feature of a wideband monopole. The antenna simulated performance is thoroughly analyzed and validated via measurements.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Hybrid Rigid-Flex Coaxial-Like Transmission Line Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a new rigid-flex hybrid technology is introduced which combines flexible Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP)film with 3D printed metal coated plastic rigid shells to form novel microwave and millimeter wave components. Hollow membrane like structures can be formed which leads to low-loss designs. A simple coax-like transmission line and a novel low-loss bandpass filter are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A 12.5:1 Bandwidth Dual-Polarized Tightly Coupled Dipole Phased Array with Compact Balun
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband dual-polarized tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) with compact perforated Marchand balun. Equivalent circuit model (ECM) is employed to determine preliminary design parameters for TCDA. In order to feed the array, a wideband and compact perforated Marchand balun is developed based on its ECM. A resistive loop is carefully designed and integrated in the array to further improve the impedance bandwidth of the TCDA. The phased array gives a 12.5:1 bandwidth (0.8-10 GHz, VSWR <; 2.7), and ±45° scanning angles in both of the E-plane and H-plane. In addition, it is observed that the array delivers a 10.5:1 (0.86-9 GHz, VSWR <; 3.3) bandwidth and a scanning range of ±60° in both of the E-plane and H-plane. The cross polarization level of the array in both of the two polarizations is below -20 dB, which outperforms those of reported TCDAs designed with the state of the art.

articleTitle: Simple High Gain 60 GHz Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain, low profile, and low-cost antenna at 60 GHz is presented. The antenna 10-dB return loss matching bandwidth covers the 60 GHz ISM band (57-64 GHz). The boresight antenna gain is 11-dB. The proposed antenna structure is suitable for short range, low power wireless communication applications. The proposed antenna is vialess. The design simplicity eases and relaxes any fabrication process requirements.

articleTitle: Brute-Force GPU Accelerated Evaluation of Dipole-Dipole Interactions
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A brute-force computation of interactions between elementary dipoles using graphics processing units (GPUs) is presented. The embarrassing parallelism of this problem allows for efficient utilization of the available hardware. Storing the geometrical arrangement of the dipoles only, keeps the memory requirements at a minimum. Despite its quadratic computational complexity, the GPU algorithm is shown to solve a synthetic nearfield far-field transformation problem with millions of unknowns in reasonable time.

articleTitle: Null-Steering Sensitivity to Ground Properties in Over-the-Horizon Radar with Planar Monopole Array on Finite Radial Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The use of planar arrays of monopoles is being considered by Defence Research and Development Canada for over-the-horizon radar to mitigate the impact of auroral clutter prevalent at northern latitudes. This is done by steering nulls towards the auroral clutter, but the null-steering performance in transmission turns out to be very sensitive to the properties of the ground. The average soil model seems to be a good choice when dealing with uncertainty about these properties for calibrating the array using theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: UWB Monopole Antenna with Reconfigurable Notch Bands based on Metamaterials Resonators
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new design of ultra-wideband (UWB) circular monopole antenna with reconfigurable bands rejection. The proposed approach is based on loading dual pairs of Split Ring Resonator (SRR) and Rectangular Spiral Resonator (RSR) on the CPW fed monopole antenna. According to the ON/OFF PIN diode states, a notch band is created in the UWB antenna. The proposed antenna was successfully designed and simulated using Ansoft HFSS. The simulated results showed good results in terms of reconfigurability in several rejection bands. This reconfigurable UWB antenna is suitable for isolation with coexistences narrowband standards (WIFI, WIMAX and satellite service) in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Beam Tilting Antenna Using FSS Layer for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new design of tilted beam antenna by utilizing a frequency selective surface (FSS) for 5G applications is presented. The method is applied to an end-fire Vivaldi antenna as a radiating source, which is designed to resonate at 28 GHz. One layer consists of 10×10 array of FSS unit cells is mounted bellow the printed Vivaldi antenna at specified locations to achieve a beam tilt-angle of -28 degrees in the H-plane. In addition, obtained results show a gain enhancement of 3.5 dBi compared with the unloaded case at 28 GHz and the reflection coefficient remained under -10 dB across its frequency band.
